title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention
summary: Softmax attention in Transformers suffers from quadratic complexity in sequence length, making it impractical for long-context applications. Linear attention alleviates this issue by replacing the exponential kernel with alternative functions that enable linear-time computation. Among existing linear attention approaches, recent studies have shown that polynomial kernels are particularly effective, as they exhibit sparse and spiky behavior similar to softmax attention, which emphasizes large dot products while suppressing irrelevant interactions. However, the exact computation of high-degree polynomial kernels is infeasible for high-dimensional representations. As a result, prior work relies on approximate polynomial kernels. This introduces a non-negligible approximation error. In this paper, we show that, from the perspective of polynomial kernel approximation, existing linear attention methods are still suboptimal. We propose \textbf{L}earnable \textbf{Lo}w-Rank \textbf{P}olynomial \textbf{S}ketch (LLoPS), a principled and flexible framework for approximating polynomial kernels with linear attention. Our method learns a low-rank polynomial sketch that provably achieves a strictly smaller approximation error than existing approaches. Experiment results show that LLoPS achieves the highest performance across extensive benchmarks, comparing with various linear attention baselines.

title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
summary: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. Harnessing-level recursion then extracts experience from these edits to update a continual improvement harness, enabling the agent to better adapt to future tasks. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, a single step consistently improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, yielding gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB, with further gains as the task-level recursion budget increases.

title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT
summary:
Purpose : To develop and evaluate CAPTOR, a deep-learning vision-language foundation model for oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT interpretation.
  Materials & Methods : CAPTOR (Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis foundaTion model for Oncologic Radiology) is a contrastive vision-language model, trained using a pretraining strategy for oncologic CAP CT (in single- or multiple-series acquisitions), on a multicenter retrospective dataset from North America, Europe and Asia, predominantly from tumor lesion examinations. CAPTOR was compared with state-of-the-art CT foundation models on three downstream tasks: disease detection, survival prediction using TumorImagingBench and image retrieval. Classification and retrieval were both evaluated on held-out internal and public test sets, stratified by anatomical coverage and indication. Bootstrap resampling was used to estimate confidence intervals, and pairwise comparisons were performed using permutation tests.
  Results : CAPTOR was trained and tested on 25,512 and 10,794 CT-report pairs respectively. TumorImagingBench datasets comprised between 134 and 421 studies each. CAPTOR outperformed all baseline models, on the classification task, on the CAP subset (AUC 0.767, 95%CI: 0.734-0.793, vs. 0.695, 95%CI: 0.645-0.736 for the next-best, p<0.001) and oncologic subset (AUC 0.784, 95%CI: 0.759-0.805, vs. 0.734, 95%CI: 0.703-0.767 p<0.001), ranked first on three of the four oncologic prognostic benchmarks, and achieved superior retrieval performance on CAP and oncologic subsets.
  Conclusion : A foundation model trained on oncology-enriched CAP CT data outperformed relevant state-of-the-art models in its target clinical context, underscoring the importance of clinically aligned pretraining.
  We release our preprocessing, training and inference code : https://github.com/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR and model weights : https://huggingface.co/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR

title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
summary: Pixel-space world models have recently emerged as a promising approach for GUI agents, predicting future screens prior to execution and subsequently re-perceiving them for action selection. However, this two-stage paradigm faces two key challenges in GUI environments: (L1) the high computational cost of pixel reconstruction and (L2) the need to reconstruct large and diverse appearance-level details beyond what is required for action selection. In practice, this screen-generation objective can induce an identity shortcut problem, where future-state prediction largely preserves the current state rather than capturing action-induced changes. In this work, we reformulate GUI world modeling by shifting the prediction target from full-screen reconstruction to action-induced future information in latent space. Concretely, we leverage a large multimodal model as the latent world model, whose shared representations support two dedicated heads for both action selection and predictive transition modeling. The action head directly translates these latent representations into action selection, while the transition head captures action-conditioned future information. To mitigate the identity shortcut, we further introduce an action-aware contrastive objective that encourages the transition representations to capture discriminative action-induced changes. Extensive experiments across offline and online GUI settings show that our method achieves up to 31.9% and 40.6% relative gains in success rate over pixel-space world models, respectively, while substantially reducing inference latency by up to 98.9%. Our code is available at https://github.com/sjyu001/latent2world.

title: Who Guides Whom? Negotiating Care, Religious Authority, and Technology in Bangladeshi Muslim Families
summary: Digital technologies are reshaping how families negotiate care, authority, and responsibility, yet these dynamics remain understudied in religiously situated family life. Through interviews with 38 adult members of Bangladeshi Muslim families, we examine how family members guide one another across religious, digital, and AI-mediated contexts. We find that authority did not simply follow age or family hierarchy: older members often remained sources of religious and familial guidance, while younger members increasingly provided expertise around digital risks, information credibility, and AI. Families also actively shaped digital environments and negotiated the role AI could occupy in everyday relationships. We develop the concepts of household epistemic governance, counter-curation, and domain-dependent authority to explain these shifting relations of knowledge and responsibility. Our findings suggest opportunities for family technologies that support negotiated boundaries, credible information practices, and culturally situated forms of care.

title: An Availability Management Framework for Microservice-Based Safety-Critical CIoT Systems: Architecture and End-to-End Evaluation
summary: Safety-critical Cellular Internet of Things (CIoT) systems increasingly rely on microservice architectures orchestrated across heterogeneous edge and cloud platforms. Although this paradigm improves modularity and scalability, the fault-tolerance mechanisms of contemporary orchestration platforms remain predominantly reactive, i.e., failed components are restarted or rescheduled only after an outage has already occurred. Such recovery can produce multi-second End to End Service Outage Time (E2E SOT), which can grow further under container restart backoff. This paper proposes an Availability Management Framework (AMF), a generic monitor-predict-recover loop that complements reactive recovery with machine learning-based anomaly detection and make-before-break switchover to a standby replica. Candidate ML models are evaluated offline under three protocols, including a change of operating regime, in order to select a model for live deployment. AMF is instantiated and evaluated on a three-tier tele-operated driving (ToD) testbed under a staged resource-exhaustion scenario. Relative to Kubernetes-only recovery, AMF completes switchover during the anomaly window, reduces E2E SOT, and avoids the tens-of-seconds outages associated with repeated in-place restarts under backoff. On this non-real-time testbed, residual E2E SOT lies inside healthy-path jitter and is therefore limited by path timing rather than by lateness of the recovery decision. The paper whows that coupling a validated ML based anomaly detector with proactive switchover can remove restart- and backoff-dominated outage from a critical path.

title: Defective, Amplified, Contested: Folk Conceptualizations of AI Slop
summary: AI slop has flooded social media feeds with overprocessed and derivative content--Jesus fusing with a shrimp, a humanoid orange chubby cat shoplifting, and a "hero" dog rescuing a human child after a plane crash. This might be no laughing matter, as waves of media coverage have taken a distinctly negative bent, emphasizing its low quality, ethical concerns, and threats to human creativity. Despite extensive attention from politicians and technologists, the perspectives of everyday users--the very audience most exposed to this phenomenon--remain largely unexplored. This descriptive work explored how Reddit users experience, conceptualize and contest AI slop. Inductive thematic analysis of posts and comments across six slop-related subreddits identified four themes covering constitutional defects, algorithmic overreach, user resistance, and entertainment outcomes--ranging from anxieties about eroding agency, moral norms, creativity, and existential questions to defensive distinctions between quality AI content and slop. We derive a user-driven definition: AI slop is audience-contested AI-generated content characterized by constitutional defects and enabled by platform logics. We operationalize slop through a facet-theoretical framework to inform future research into this fuzzy category.

title: Speech event detector: Timestamped detection of non-verbal vocalizations and background sounds for rich speech transcription
comments: Code is available at https://github.com/theboringai-work/surround-sound and pre-trained weights are hosted at https://huggingface.co/theboringai-work/surround-sound
summary: Automatic speech recognition produces words but drops the non-verbal content of a recording: the breaths, coughs, sighs and laughter of the speaker, and the horns, music or barking around them. We describe Speech Event Detector, a 5.8-million-parameter convolutional-Transformer model that outputs probabilities every 40 ms for 54 event classes (20 speaker vocalizations and 34 background sounds), together with post-processing that converts these probabilities into timestamped events and a procedure for merging the events into a Whisper transcript. The model is trained on material drawn from seven public datasets whose labels come in incompatible forms: single detected regions, free-text tags with timestamps, temporally strong ontology labels, symbols embedded in transcripts, isolated recordings and environmental recordings. We unify them using rule-based label mapping, recover timestamps for transcript-embedded labels through CTC forced alignment, locating 6,360 of 8,620 sounds, and combine about 168 hours of real annotated training recordings with synthetic mixtures and augmentation using real background noise. Per-class thresholds for two operating profiles are tuned on real held-out recordings, and performance is estimated using two-fold cross-validation. On whole held-out recordings from four datasets, considering the 48 classes with at least ten held-out events, the sensitive profile detects an average of 49 percent of a class's events, covering 67 percent of all 9,367 events, at a macro precision of 0.30. The balanced profile achieves a macro recall of 0.37 at a precision of 0.36, with macro event F1 scores of 0.32 and 0.33, respectively. The detector runs about 39 times faster than real time on eight CPU threads.
comment: Code is available at https://github.com/theboringai-work/surround-sound and pre-trained weights are hosted at https://huggingface.co/theboringai-work/surround-sound

title: Mapping Tire-Road Friction Coefficients Along Driven Trajectories
summary: Information of the tire-road friction coefficient is critical for intelligent vehicle systems, as friction establishes the limits at which the vehicle can be manoeuvred without loss of control. While there is extensive literature on online friction estimation, no previous studies have explored post-processing and mapping friction coefficients along a driven trajectory based on recorded sensor data. Mapped friction information could be shared by connected vehicles, enabling proactive measures in low-friction areas. This paper presents an offline post-processing method, FrictionMap, for mapping friction coefficients from recorded driving data. The method operates on commonly available on-board vehicle sensor information, and requires only a basic vehicle parameter set and a slip threshold as prior knowledge. FrictionMap runs an extended Kalman filter combined with a Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother to estimate vehicle dynamics. Data points where the friction limit is observable are identified by filtering points based on tire slip. A Gaussian process is fitted to these points to acquire a continuous estimate of the friction coefficient along the trajectory. FrictionMap is validated via a simulation study, and shown to outperform commonly used online friction estimation techniques. The code implementation and the simulation benchmark are released as open-source after paper acceptance to enable further research.

title: Composable Dynamics for Cooperative Humanoids: A RoboCompiler Extension
summary: Physically connected humanoids need consistent dynamics for internal actuator loops, inter-robot forces, and changing ground supports. We extend RoboCompiler with member-wise dynamics assembly, compiling reduced dynamics from rigid bodies, moving actuator parts, and reflected rotor inertias. Compiled body Jacobians and analytic constraint curvature yield an explicit Coriolis factor satisfying the power identity for floating-base quasi-velocities. A two-level reduction retains reusable robot models while composing their supports and hand connections; local inertial updates have rank at most six, and prescribed-acceleration constraint wrenches are affine in actuator efforts. These interfaces support actuator-aware tracking, coupled force allocation, payload updates, and support-mode switching for five hand-linked humanoids. Across 264 feasible states in eight humanoid configurations, normalised acceleration discrepancies remain within $1.6\!\times\!10^{-10}$ against a hard-constraint reference and $1.4\!\times\!10^{-10}$ against a compiler-independent reference; MuJoCo simulations achieve 0.73~mm root-mean-square (RMS) pelvis error in the ring dance and complete side steps through 20 support-mode changes.

title: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study
summary: LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. Can agents use experimental feedback to progressively improve strategies, and do the resulting strategies improve target-model performance on held-out data? We study how agents use experimental feedback to develop data-engineering strategies under fixed training and evaluation protocols. Our Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework lets agents pursue, revise, or combine research directions using cumulative findings. Strategies are selected by in-loop scores and evaluated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks-math and code data selection, math reward design, and math curriculum learning-selected strategies achieve absolute gains over generic baselines of up to 13.34% on AIME25 Pass@32 and 5.85% averaged across four held-out benchmarks under fixed training conditions. In-loop scores improve over successive experiments, while held-out trajectories show that later in-loop gains do not always improve generalization. Comparisons of research organization and feedback access favor combining evidence analysis with cumulative findings. Research trajectories show how earlier findings inform strategy revisions and combinations across research directions.

title: Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips
comments: Extended version of the paper titled "Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips'' to appear in MICRO 2026
summary:
We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips. Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant. Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop.
  Our results have important implications for HBM-based system design and validation. Relying solely on JEDEC- or vendor-specified test loops to bound HBM power could cause system failures and/or thermal throttling in real-world high-power AI/ML workloads. To improve 3D-stacked DRAM power modeling in open source architectural simulation infrastructures, we develop a new HBM power model. Our model predicts the power of 36 real HBM2 chips across diverse workloads (including a real LLM decode workload) with 7.6 -- 8.1% mean absolute percentage error, substantially more accurately than state-of-the-art HBM power models. The power consumption predicted by our model for a power-intensive microbenchmark closely matches (with 2.4% to 5.3% error across HBM3E's specified supply voltage range) the average HBM3E memory power consumed by three tested NVIDIA H200 GPUs. We publicly release our power model at https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power.
comment: Extended version of the paper titled "Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips'' to appear in MICRO 2026

title: From LLM Plans to Authorized Motion: Execution-Bound Authorization for Excavators
summary: An LLM-directed excavator can execute mechanically feasible motion whose destination or authority no longer matches the operator's approval. We propose execution-bound authorization for the approval--dispatch--execution interval. A one-use lease binds the action, generated motion, mission contract and admission tolerance; atomic dispatch rechecks current authority and measured joint drift. Periodic supervision detects revocation and requests a quintic stop with a carry-pitch endpoint, selected through sampled joint, stroke, flow and reference-acceleration checks. The framework connects exact motion identity to dispatch integrity and load-aware interruption. Evaluation combines a 672-case interface suite, four loaded digging cases in synchronous simulation, unloaded MuJoCo/Pinocchio transfers and two command-level LLM planners. The gateway admitted all 120 benign interface cases and produced zero unauthorized dispatches in the attack suite. Loaded dispatch-window tests produced zero unauthorized deposition. During simulated dump-phase revocation, maximum closed-site deposition decreased from 1.23 to 0.33\,m$^3$; loaded-slew stops used less than 75\% of nominal swing torque. These results demonstrate motion-bound authorization and quantify the retention and stopping behavior of supervised excavation skills.

title: Learning Non-Gaussian SEMs with Conditional Risk, and Why the Direction of Recursion Matters
summary: Variance-based methods recover a Gaussian linear structural equation model (SEM) with equal or suitably constrained error variances, either by recursively identifying the source nodes with smallest conditional variance (top-down method) or sink nodes with highest conditional variance (bottom-up method). We show that the use of conditional variance is incidental: replacing it with the conditional risk, i.e., the minimal expected loss of linear prediction under the negative log-likelihood of the noise distribution, extends both methods to non-Gaussian noise. Existing methods are the least-squares special case. This yields two main results. First, exploiting the noise distribution improves structure recovery: the matched-loss procedures recover the SEM more accurately than their least-squares counterparts and the LiNGAM methods, which are designed for non-Gaussianity. Second, the two methods, interchangeable in the Gaussian setting, separate under non-Gaussian noise: the top-down method is correct for every noise density with finite differential entropy, whereas the bottom-up method requires a regularity condition and can fail without it, for instance under mean-zero exponential or Cauchy noise. Simulations confirm both results.

title: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion
summary: Diffusion models provide expressive trajectory priors for multi-robot motion planning (MRMP), but scaling them to large teams requires coordinating individual motions without expensive joint computation. We introduce Akule, a sparse interaction diffusion framework that augments a frozen single-robot prior with three learned modules: a reusable pairwise correction model $R_φ$, a contextual selector $U_ψ$ that determines which corrections to evaluate, and a composer $G_ω$ that combines their effects through context-dependent signed weights. This decomposition separates which interactions merit computation from how their effects should be combined into coordinated denoising updates. We train $R_φ$ using matched pairwise trajectory optimizations, then learn $G_ω$ and $U_ψ$ from physically optimized joint trajectories without requiring a prescribed ground-truth interaction graph. The resulting joint proposals are passed to a downstream search-based planner for validation and repair. Across diverse MRMP benchmarks, Akule achieves competitive planning success, complete-planner speedups of up to $25\times$, zero-shot population transfer, and successful planning with up to $256$ robots. Ablations further demonstrate that learned selection and composition reduce pre-repair conflicts and downstream repair effort relative to heuristic selection and uniform summation.

title: Harvesting-Aware Routing for Low-Latency Reliable Transmission in Interference-Powered Networks
summary: We consider a multi-hop wireless network where energy-harvesting nodes rely solely on ambient radio-frequency interference as their power source. The goal is to deliver a packet from source to destination with minimum latency while guaranteeing a target end-to-end outage probability under Rayleigh fading. This gives rise to a joint routing and power allocation problem in which interference plays a dual role: it provides harvestable energy, but also impairs link reliability. We first transform the intricate, multiplicative end-to-end outage constraint into an additive form. Then, we propose two optimal algorithms. The first, HOPE, minimizes the bottleneck harvesting latency, i.e., the longest energy-accumulation time along the path, by reducing the problem to a least-cost path computation on a graph with interference-aware link weights. The second, THOPE, extends the objective to total end-to-end latency, adding the cumulative transmission delay, and likewise admits a closed-form least-cost path solution. Both algorithms are solved in polynomial time via Dijkstra's algorithm and yield explicit expressions for the optimal transmit powers. Extensive simulations reveal that HOPE and THOPE reduce the average total latency by up to an order of magnitude compared with shortest-path and minimum-energy benchmarks, while exhibiting sharply concentrated delay distributions that are largely insensitive to interferer density.

title: Adaptive-Depth Is a Finishing Stage
comments: Accepted for poster presentation at the AXIOM Workshop (Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning) at NeurIPS 2026. 9 pages, 8 figures
summary: Looped transformers reuse the same layer multiple times, allowing inference compute to be adjusted without changing the model. Recent adaptive-depth methods train the model across multiple loop depths from the beginning of training. We introduce fixed-first training, which varies model depth only during a short final phase of training. At 200M parameters, training a model of fixed-depth 2 for the first 67% of the run reduces modeled training compute by 45% while keeping mean negative log-likelihood (NLL) across inference depths within 0.5% of training across depths throughout. At 1B parameters, training initially at depth 4 reduces modeled compute by 31% to 37% and wall-clock time by 32% to 39%, while keeping final NLL within 0.8% and downstream differences within the observed seed variation. These results show that training over the full range of depths can be reserved for a short finishing phase with only small changes in performance.
comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the AXIOM Workshop (Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning) at NeurIPS 2026. 9 pages, 8 figures

title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing
summary: Slider-based control aims to give users continuous, fine-grained control over the intensity of individual edits in instruction-based image editing. However, existing approaches fail to deliver reliable continuous controllability: traversing a slider can produce abrupt visual jumps and non-monotonic changes, while jointly controlled sliders can interfere with one another. To systematically study these limitations, we introduce SlideBench, a comprehensive benchmark for continuous image editing spanning diverse editing categories and equipped with a unified suite of metrics quantifying monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and inter-slider disentanglement. Building on these observations, we propose SliderEdit++, which explicitly regularizes the intermediate editing trajectory rather than supervising only its endpoints. Our method combines velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control to encourage smooth, predictable slider traversal, together with a disentanglement objective that reduces interference between independently controlled edits. On SlideBench, SliderEdit++ achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline. At the same time, using a few-step editing backbone makes our method approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches, enabling substantially more responsive interactive editing.

title: Image Diffusion Models Are Good 3D Human Motion Generators
comments: 16 pages; under review. The first two authors contributed equally to this work
summary: Text-to-motion generation typically relies on dataset-specific skeletal representations, with models trained separately for benchmarks with different joint layouts. We investigate whether image diffusion architectures can model 3D human motion through a common image-compatible representation that accommodates heterogeneous skeletal layouts while preserving motion-specific kinematic structure. To this end, we organize root-centered joint trajectories into topology-informed joint--time images and model global root dynamics through a complementary latent stream. A motion autoencoder conditions local-motion decoding on the root latent, while a text-conditioned Scalable Interpolant Transformer (SiT) jointly generates both latent streams, with supervision on decoded 3D joint positions further constraining generation in motion space. In addition to dataset-specific models, we train a single motion autoencoder on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, followed by a single text-conditioned SiT shared across both datasets, preserving their respective skeletal definitions without skeleton retargeting to a common joint layout. Experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML show that our dataset-specific models achieve state-of-the-art performance, while shared training yields further gains on both benchmarks, demonstrating the benefits of shared modeling across heterogeneous skeletal layouts.
comment: 16 pages; under review. The first two authors contributed equally to this work

title: Simulate Before You Scale: High-Fidelity LLM Inference Planning Without GPUs
comments: This paper is accepted at ACM SIGMETRICS 2027
summary: Deploying large language model (LLM) inference at scale requires jointly selecting hardware layout, parallelism strategy, scheduling policy, admission control, and request routing to meet latency and throughput targets. These choices interact: a routing decision that improves cache locality can concentrate load, and an admission threshold that triggers only at saturation allows queues to grow deep enough to degrade critical-tier traffic. Evaluating candidates on GPU clusters is too expensive for iterative exploration, yet existing predictive tools either ignore batching and queueing dynamics or model only fragments of the pipeline. In this paper, we present BLIS, a deterministic, CPU-only discrete-event simulator that models the full inference serving pipeline (admission, routing, scheduling, prefill/decode execution, KV-cache management, and preemption). BLIS pairs analytical basis functions with learned scaling coefficients and overhead terms, fit once globally, to predict step latency without per-model or per-GPU profiling. Across 36 experiments spanning six models and three GPU types, BLIS achieves 6.7% median end-to-end error while running around 200 times faster than real execution. In a configuration search over 420 serving configurations for Llama-2-70B, BLIS identifies a 4-GPU deployment that meets a 300ms mean TTFT service-level objective (SLO), whereas competing tools either require double the GPUs or recommend configurations that fail under load. Two policies evolved entirely in simulation were validated on real hardware and merged into llm-d, a widely adopted open-source platform for distributed LLM serving: an admission policy that reduces critical-tier TTFT P90 by up to 82%, and a flow-control policy that reduces E2E P50 latency by 32-48% on overloaded workloads.

title: Do Artificial Neural Networks Need Dendritic Nanotubes? Two Reasons for Shrinking Importance Estimates in Continual Learning
comments: Github: https://github.com/Saurav-K-Aryal/Do-Artificial-Neural-Networks-Need-Dendritic-Nanotubes-.git 21 pages, 3 figures, 10 tables. Simulation and figure scripts are included as ancillary files
summary: Regularization-based continual learning protects each parameter in proportion to an estimate of its importance, yet these estimates come from finite samples and heuristics and are used as if they were exact. We report four studies that start from a biologically inspired mechanism and end with a statistical explanation of it. Motivated by dendritic nanotubes, we let transient lateral links diffuse importance tags between hidden units. Links between co-active units gave no significant gain, but random links with lifetimes of 25 or 200 steps raised final accuracy on 20-task Permuted MNIST by 1.5 to 2.6 points. We show that random diffusion implements linear shrinkage of importance toward the layer mean in expectation. A simulation of the link process alone predicts shrinkage weights of 0.23 and 0.52 for these lifetimes, and graph-free shrinkage at 0.25 and 0.5 reproduces both the accuracy and the dispersion of the consolidated importance, while every activity-dependent rule did worse than random links. A five-seed screen across EWC, SI, and MAS found nominal gains for SI and MAS on Permuted MNIST and losses on task-incremental Split CIFAR-100, where forgetting was small and shrinkage cost plasticity. Varying the number of importance samples then separates two mechanisms on Permuted MNIST. For EWC, the gain fell by about ten points per tenfold increase in samples, from 19.6 points with 10 samples to -0.4 with 1000, a variance effect. For MAS, a gain of about one point persisted at 1000 samples, consistent with a bias in the importance measure rather than noise. Shrinkage had no detectable effect for MAS on a domain-incremental CIFAR-100 benchmark. Finally, we show that a standard heteroscedastic empirical Bayes rule shrinks the largest Fisher-type estimates most, which may explain its poor results, and point to a log-scale alternative.

title: Variance Fingerprints: Component-Wise Identification of Content Factors by Augmentation Design
summary: Augmentation-based self-supervised learning can recover the content shared across views without separating its underlying factors into individual coordinates. We ask whether augmentations can be designed to make those factors identifiable. Our approach allows content factors to fluctuate across augmented views while preserving their mean for each source instance. Each instance receives a fixed, recorded set of augmentation strengths that controls how much its factors fluctuate. When factors respond differently to changes in these strengths, their patterns of variation provide information that distinguishes them. Under suitable decoder and support assumptions, we prove that these differences identify individual factors in a conditional Gaussian model, up to permutation, scaling, and translation. We then develop a learner that uses the recorded strengths to estimate these patterns jointly across instances, enabling learning from few views per instance. Synthetic experiments demonstrate near-perfect factor recovery through nonlinear mixing. Controlled dSprites experiments show improved coordinate alignment using augmentations that target known factors, even without telling the learner which augmentation corresponds to which representation coordinate. These results suggest a route to component identification in self-supervised learning: augmentation design can supply identifying information beyond shared content alone.

title: BigCell: Generating Gigapixel Whole-Slide Images
summary: Whole-slide images (WSIs) are gigapixel-scale digital scans of histopathology tissue and serve as the primary basis for cancer diagnosis. Existing histopathology generative models operate at the patch scale, producing fixed-size tiles of at most 1024$\times$1024 pixels which encompass only a small fraction of the WSI. In contrast, text reports for clinical diagnoses and slide-level diagnostic labels -- the supervision that exists at scale -- operate at the whole-slide level. We present BigCell, the first approach to generate coherent whole-slide histopathology images at native gigapixel resolution. BigCell trains a flow-matching transformer at 2048$\times$2048 pixels on over 120,000 publicly available WSIs spanning multiple organ types. Conditioning on embeddings from pathology foundation models and using an inference-time sliding-window pipeline, BigCell generates coherent images of up to 32,768$\times$32,768 pixels, outperforming prior tile generators on both tile-level and slide-level fidelity metrics. To make gigapixel synthesis practical, we introduce an adaptive scheduling strategy that prioritizes important slide regions, speeding up image generation by over 3\ttimes with minimal quality degradation. Furthermore, we propose the first text-to-image synthesis at 8k resolution by training a separate model that produces dense conditioning grids directly from pathology text reports. We demonstrate that augmenting with synthetic samples improves slide-level few-shot classification performance by up to $18 \%$ over baselines trained on real data.

title: Bipartite Carrier Compression and Machine-Certified Bounds in Schönhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
comments: 5 pages, self-contained. Lean 4 formal proofs, standalone certificate verifier, and full experimental artifacts openly available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23268580
summary: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-κ}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Schönhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles in h=25), reducing the global physical wire width by 377,890 wires from the reviewed baseline W = 177,284,805 down to W = 176,906,915. Evaluated over the exact 10^{-14} rational grid, this wire reduction certifies an improved second-moment coefficient AB = 5,164,059 / 125,000,000,000 and establishes the sharpened conditional exponent κ= 826,215,307 / 20,000,000,000,000 \approx 4.131076535 \times 10^{-5}, strictly surpassing the preceding record on this architecture (κ\approx 4.123864 \times 10^{-5}). All 47 polynomial constraints and 7 rational security margins are audited in exact Q-arithmetic with zero floating-point error, and the fundamental wire reduction identity is formally verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover without unproven axioms.

title: Large-Scale Data Center Integration in Power Systems: Uncertainty and Multi-Scale Variation
comments: Accepted for publication in Proceedings of the IEEE. Copyright 2026 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses
summary:
Hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centers are emerging as a structurally new class of electricity demand. Unlike conventional loads, they materialize as spatially concentrated, transmission-level point loads with rapid deployment timelines and converter-dominated dynamics. Their integration is governed by two defining properties: forecast uncertainty in load realization and multi-scale temporal variation spanning sub-seconds to planning horizons.
  We develop a unified framework that links reliability and affordability to these dimensions through a four-quadrant structure: (reliability, affordability) $\times$ (uncertainty, variation), which integrates probabilistic resource adequacy, generation and transmission expansion, operational security, and market design.
  Measured traces from a public generative-AI workload dataset show strongly tonal GPU power spectra rather than smooth broadband behavior: harmonic combs at the training-step cadence, and a distinct sub-second periodicity in inference. Across these traces the dominant variance band shifts with workload type (seconds for training and offline inference; tens of seconds and longer for online inference). We report this as a characterization of the measured workloads rather than a universal signature, and take it to indicate that such loads warrant a spectral description rather than a peak-demand one. These signatures directly affect reserve requirements, ramping products, voltage stability, ride-through performance, and harmonic interactions in converter-rich grids.
  Taken together, the analytical framework and empirical results establish a system-level basis for assessing the reliability and cost implications of large AI data center integration across planning and operational horizons.

title: Thinking with Images without Coordinates
summary: Recent advances in multi-modal large language models have shifted toward the "thinking with images" paradigm to improve reasoning faithfulness, yet existing methods rely heavily on explicit coordinate- based grounding. We identify two fundamental limitations in this approach, i.e., a semantic gap where sparse regressions miss high-dimensional latent structures, and a resolution gap due to the granularity mismatch between patch-level tokens and pixel-level coordinates. To address these, we propose TiCO (Thinking with images without COordinates). It reformulates visual reasoning as a semantic evidence discovery process within the latent space, and evidence is injected as token-level regions without pixel coordinates. Specifically, TiCO utilizes a dedicated probe token to estimate similarity distributions and performs importance sampling over spatially connected components to generate diverse, semantically dominant evidence rollouts. Extensive experiments across multiple high-resolution and general visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our TiCO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coordinate-based methods with significantly improved inference efficiency.

title: Learning to Sync at the Edge: Client-Side Adaptive Synchronization for Federated Learning
comments: 9 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables. Accepted to IEEE SEC 2026
summary: The scalability and performance of edge federated learning are fundamentally constrained by synchronization bottlenecks. Clients operate under heterogeneous compute, time-varying communication conditions, and, in some settings, privacy constraints, yet synchronization is often still handled with fixed schedules. However, synchronization decisions are often made outside the client, even though the client directly observes local progress, resource state, and communication conditions. We present a client-side reinforcement learning synchronization framework in which each client decides during training whether to upload, download, synchronize bidirectionally, or defer communication. The framework places a lightweight scheduler alongside the local model and formulates synchronization as a resource-aware control problem driven by local learning and system state. We study this framework on two representative edge workloads, spatiotemporal traffic forecasting and image classification. Across both settings, adaptive client-side synchronization improves the accuracy-cost trade-off, reducing system cost in traffic forecasting while maintaining competitive cost and improving final accuracy in image classification. We also consider privacy-constrained settings, where synchronization must account for not only latency and energy but also privacy expenditure. Overall, our results show that synchronization in edge federated learning is better treated as an adaptive client-side control problem than only as a server-side coordination mechanism.

title: RoboFake: Are Deepfake Detectors Ready for Humanoid Face Robots?
summary: Humanoid face robots can now move their lips in sync with speech and show detailed facial expressions. Give such a robot the face of a real person and drive it with generated speech, and you get a face forgery that happens in front of the camera: the camera records a real object, and no pixel is edited. We call this a RoboFake. In this paper we ask what current deepfake detectors do when they see a robot face. We test six public detectors trained on FaceForensics++ on video of a physical lip-syncing face robot, on a synthesized video of the same robot, and on rendered robot faces. All thresholds are fixed on FaceForensics++, and every result is compared with real human faces that went through the same processing as the robot videos. At a threshold that flags 5% of real faces, three detectors flag almost every physical robot frame, while two flag fewer than 7%. A matched human control and masking show that the response comes from the face, not from the processing or the background. However, it does not track synthesis: with only the face visible, three of the six detectors give the physical robot a higher fake score than its synthesized video. The response is also fragile, and light JPEG compression is enough to push most robot frames below the threshold for some detectors. Our results suggest that current detectors flag today's robots because their faces do not look human, not because they recognize a forgery. We release our evaluation protocol and code, and state three testable hypotheses about realistic, interactive RoboFakes.

title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
summary: Hybrid reasoning models such as the Qwen3 series switch between a THINK mode and a NO-THINK mode through a few chat-template tokens. A popular recipe trains such models with reinforcement learning in NO-THINK mode and reports improved reasoning performance. We provide evidence that much of this gain can be explained by thinking leakage: the gain comes largely from partially reactivating the reasoning abilities of the original model's THINK mode instead of learning enhanced reasoning behavior. We train Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B with GRPO in NO-THINK mode. As accuracy improves, responses become longer and more reflective, are increasingly judged by the original model to resemble its own thinking, and the model's internal activations shift toward its THINK mode. We then investigate at the level of weights, activations, and attention heads: scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches THINK-mode accuracy but does not exceed it; in Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace of the RL-trained model with its original-model value removes most of the RL gain, and the reverse exchange transfers a considerable fraction of the gain to the original model; and the RL-induced shift passes through the attention heads that read the empty think block. We further identify a possible mechanism in the GRPO training signal: responses favored by the advantage-weighted update are more THINK-like, and a gradient step computed from this signal moves the model toward its THINK state. Thus, gains in NO-THINK mode can largely reflect reactivation of reasoning abilities already present in the original model.

title: Solution of a system of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on a network
summary: We extend the study of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on networks from a single equation to a weakly coupled system of two equations on a star graph, and we develop a numerical scheme for it. Instead of prescribing the boundary values and imposing a junction condition, we compute the solution on each branch from its outer vertex toward the junction and determine the boundary values for which these branchwise solutions agree at the junction. On each branch, we replace the right-hand sides by their cell averages and solve the resulting problems exactly on every cell. This gives an iteration whose limits we compute in closed form. From these limits, the values of the discrete solution at the junction are affine functions of the boundary values on the branch, with a $2 \times 2$ matrix whose rows sum to one and whose determinant factors into explicit contributions of the cells. We use these formulas to characterize the boundary values that give solutions continuous at the junction and monotone on every branch: when the matrices are nonsingular, the admissible boundary values of one branch form a convex polygon, bounded by conditions on the difference of the two components and by positivity conditions, and the boundary values on the other branches follow from them. We also treat the singular case, and we illustrate the results with numerical experiments.

title: Inspect Any Crack: An Automated End-to-End Crack Segmentation and Severity Assessment Framework
summary: Image-based crack analysis is essential for automated infrastructure inspection to reduce the cost, subjectivity, and safety risks of manual surveys. Despite advances in visual crack detection, methods that translate predictions into physically meaningful and engineering-interpretable crack condition information remain limited. To bridge this gap, this study proposes Inspect Any Crack (IAC), an innovative end-to-end crack recognition and condition assessment framework that automatically derives physical geometric measurements and continuous severity scores from concrete-crack imagery. At its core, IAC introduces SACv2-Tiny, an efficient crack segmentation model adapted from a vision foundation model. Trained on the challenging OmniCrack30K dataset, SACv2-Tiny achieved a $62.49\%$ F1-score and $45.45\%$ IoU on the test set and a mean zero-shot F1-score of $69.89\%$ across three unseen datasets, demonstrating robust segmentation that enables downstream analysis with limited post-processing. IAC further processes the predicted masks to quantify physical crack width and affected area using ground-sampling-distance calibration. Validation at 41 caliper-referenced locations yielded a mean relative width error of $7.33\%$. Beyond geometric quantification, IAC introduces a novel continuous crack-condition metric, the Crack Severity Index (CSI), bounded on $[0,100]$, which combines maximum crack width and affected-area ratio into a unified, standards-informed severity measure. Through these developments, IAC advances crack inspection beyond pixel-level recognition toward interpretable and automated infrastructure condition assessment.

title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
summary: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.

title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory
summary: Learning long-range dependencies with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) is difficult because of the vanishing gradient problem. Gated recurrent neural networks like GRUs and LSTMs address this problem and are commonly explained by their ability to create additive copy paths through time. This explanation is correct, but incomplete: useful RNN gate values must themselves be learned, which is typically done with another RNN. We study this gate-learning problem through carefully controlled sequence classification tasks. Our analysis shows that gated architectures struggle when all training samples require long-range memory and thus equally suffer from the vanishing gradient problem. We intervene by adding short-dependency samples which let gated models learn solutions that capture long-dependency samples, but also generalize across different class labels. When properly learned, gated RNNs match or even exceed the test accuracy of modern architectures like Mamba and xLSTM. Overall, our results highlight gate learning as a central part of learning long-range memory and show how training data can support this process by exposing the same task over shorter dependencies.

title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
comments: Accepted at the 22nd European Conference on Computer Systems (EuroSys '27), April 19-23, 2027, Rabat, Morocco. 14 pages, 8 figures
summary:
Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior.
  In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. These data can be exported for visualization and analysis. Our approach demonstrates how instrumentation can be generalized beyond traditional hardware to support heterogeneous architectures, providing portability without modifying tool logic.
  By opening the black box of dataflow execution, DFIT establishes a foundation for new classes of performance analysis tools for AI accelerators. It provides a practical path toward reproducible, architecture-aware introspection across heterogeneous systems, bridging the long-standing visibility gap between compiler design, runtime scheduling, and hardware realization. Evaluation across Cerebras, SambaNova, and TPU shows practical overhead of 3.53%-13.62% across instrumentation modes with robust cross-platform portability.

title: TGSR: Text-Grounded Diffusion for Faithful Image Super-Resolution
summary: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image super-resolution (SR) by leveraging strong generative priors to enhance perceptual quality. However, for textual content, these priors often produce text hallucinations: non-existent or distorted text, which alter scene semantics and compromise model reliability. While recent methods focus on enhancing text generation, they do so indiscriminately, leaving hallucinations fundamentally unresolved. We argue the core problem is a lack of selective control. Therefore, we reformulate text SR as a selective generation problem: text is resolved only when reliable generation is expected, while other scene content is fully super-resolved. We introduce TGSR (Text-Grounded Super-Resolution), a test-time framework that progressively identifies and suppresses likely hallucinated text regions during generation. To enable this, we train dedicated detectors on a large-scale dataset curated from diverse diffusion-based SR outputs. TGSR consistently improves text fidelity across multiple backbones, increasing recognition precision by up to 17.68 points without degrading perceptual quality, underscoring the value of selective control in generative SR.

title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
summary: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.

AI.title_translation: 齐次超螺旋算法过零时间的下界研究
AI.tldr: 本文推导了齐次超螺旋算法滑模变量过零时间的理论下界，证明了非零振幅的过零偏移不会在有限时间内累积。
AI.motivation: 滑模控制中普遍存在高频切换和抖振问题。超螺旋算法虽能产生连续控制输入，但滑模变量在滑动流形附近仍可能反复过零，因此需要明确过零发生的速度上限以及其是否会在有限时间内累积（芝诺现象）。
AI.method: 针对标量齐次超螺旋算法，理论推导了滑模变量返回零点所需的两个时间下界以及完成一次完整偏移所需时间的界限，并结合数值仿真验证了结果。

AI.conclusion: 虽然标量齐次超螺旋算法中的过零点可能会在有限时间内累积，但对应偏移的振幅必须趋于零且满足可和性条件；因此，任何高于指定非零振幅的过零动作均无法在有限时间内无限累积。

AI.summary: 本文研究了标量齐次超螺旋算法在滑动流形附近的过零行为，推导了返回零点和完成完整偏移的时间下界。结果表明，任何大于预设非零振幅的偏移过零事件均无法在有限时间内累积，并进一步分析了齐次性缩放规律及通过数值仿真进行了验证。

title: Watermarking for Byzantine Robust LLM Training
summary: LLM watermarking has emerged as a promising approach for detecting downstream model misuse in centralized settings, but extending it to federated learning (FL) presents unique challenges. In particular, FL systems often rely on strong robust aggregators to defend against poisoning attacks. We empirically show that a malicious server can exploit these same aggregators as effective watermark-removal mechanisms during training, causing representative existing LLM watermarking methods to fail detection in the final model. To address this limitation, we formalize the problem as a constrained optimization task and propose CamoMark, an aggregator-agnostic watermarking scheme for embedding robust watermarks in FL. CamoMark optimizes watermarked updates to become inliers, maintaining bounded deviation from the distribution of clean updates, while preserving sufficient watermark signal for reliable detection. Evaluated on Qwen fine-tuned on the Alpaca dataset, CamoMark achieves a detection confidence of $p$-value $= 1.82\times10^{-2}$ using only 3.3% watermarked data. The watermark also remains robust to a range of post-training removal attacks, including continued fine-tuning on clean data, pruning, and model distillation. At higher watermark ratios, detection confidence improves substantially, reaching $p$-value $= 5.11\times10^{-11}$ at a 13.3% watermark ratio.

AI.title_translation: 拜占庭鲁棒LLM训练的水印技术
AI.tldr: 现有LLM水印在联邦学习中易被鲁棒聚合器移除，本文提出CamoMark，一种聚合器无关的水印方案，能在FL中嵌入鲁棒水印并成功检测，对多种攻击具有鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: 现有的LLM水印技术在联邦学习（FL）环境中，其水印信号容易被鲁棒聚合器在训练过程中移除，导致最终模型无法检测，限制了水印技术在FL中的应用。
AI.method: 本文将问题形式化为约束优化任务，并提出了CamoMark，这是一种聚合器无关的水印方案，用于在FL中嵌入鲁棒水印。CamoMark通过优化带水印的更新，使其成为内群点，在保持与干净更新分布的有限偏差的同时，保留足够的水印信号以实现可靠检测。
AI.result: CamoMark在Qwen模型上（Alpaca数据集微调）仅使用3.3%的水印数据即可达到$p$-value $= 1.82\times10^{-2}$的检测置信度。该水印对一系列训练后移除攻击（包括在干净数据上继续微调、剪枝和模型蒸馏）也保持鲁棒性。在更高的水印比例下（13.3%），检测置信度显著提高，达到$p$-value $= 5.11\times10^{-11}$。
AI.conclusion: CamoMark成功解决了联邦学习中LLM水印的鲁棒性问题，提供了一种聚合器无关的有效水印方案，能够抵御聚合器移除和多种后训练攻击，实现了在低水印数据比例下的高置信度检测。
AI.translation: LLM水印技术已成为集中式设置中检测下游模型滥用的一种有前景的方法，但将其扩展到联邦学习（FL）带来了独特的挑战。特别是，FL系统通常依赖强大的鲁棒聚合器来防御投毒攻击。我们凭经验表明，恶意服务器可以利用这些相同的聚合器作为训练期间有效的水印移除机制，导致现有代表性的LLM水印方法在最终模型中检测失败。为了解决这一限制，我们将问题形式化为约束优化任务，并提出了CamoMark，一种用于在FL中嵌入鲁棒水印的聚合器无关水印方案。CamoMark优化了带水印的更新，使其成为内群点，保持与干净更新分布的有限偏差，同时保留足够的水印信号以实现可靠检测。在对Alpaca数据集上微调的Qwen模型进行评估时，CamoMark仅使用3.3%的带水印数据即可实现$p$-value $= 1.82\times10^{-2}$的检测置信度。该水印对一系列训练后移除攻击也保持鲁棒性，包括在干净数据上继续微调、剪枝和模型蒸馏。在更高的水印比例下，检测置信度显著提高，在13.3%的水印比例下达到$p$-value $= 5.11\times10^{-11}$。
AI.summary: 本文研究了联邦学习（FL）中大型语言模型（LLM）水印的鲁棒性问题。现有水印方法在FL中易受鲁棒聚合器移除。为解决此问题，本文提出了CamoMark，一种聚合器无关的水印方案。CamoMark通过优化带水印更新，使其在保持与干净更新分布偏差有限的同时，嵌入鲁棒水印。实验表明，CamoMark在低水印比例下也能实现高置信度检测，并对多种后训练攻击具有鲁棒性。
AI.keywords: LLM水印, 联邦学习, 拜占庭鲁棒, CamoMark, 水印鲁棒性
AI.comments: 这项工作创新性地解决了联邦学习环境下LLM水印面临的独特挑战，特别是鲁棒聚合器可能成为水印移除机制的问题。CamoMark提出的聚合器无关设计，通过将水印更新优化为内群点，在保证水印检测能力的同时，维持了模型训练的正常进行。其对多种攻击的鲁棒性以及在低数据比例下的高效性，使其在实际应用中具有重要价值。

title: Layer-wise Input Recoverability in Deep Neural Networks
summary: The inner workings of deep neural networks are still not well understood. The information bottleneck framework, which characterizes deep networks by the mutual information between their hidden representations and the network's input, has been used to identify compression of input information with respect to an input image and output labels. We instead study how much of a layer's own input is recoverable from the layer's output in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). A convolutional layer applies its filters to one input patch at a time, so we evaluate recoverability on sampled input patches with a reconstruction-based probe and not on the entire feature map. The probe's size thus depends on channels and kernel size and not on feature map size, which lets our method scale to deep CNNs with wide feature maps. For each layer, we compare pretrained, random, and reconstruction-optimized encoders, using linear and linear-plus-residual-MLP decoders. We measure recoverability as $R^2$ between input patches and their reconstructions on a held-out set. Across nine ImageNet CNNs, recoverability generally decreases with depth but is more consistently predicted by the compression of the layer. Learning-attributed recoverability, the difference between pretrained and random encoders, is not uniform across architectures. We introduce single-property random controls, which transfer one pretrained property onto a random encoder, and find that each control changes recoverability with a consistent sign across models: copying pretrained singular vectors tends to raise recoverability, while copying the pretrained singular-value spectrum or activation sparsity lowers it.

AI.title_translation: 深度神经网络中的逐层输入可恢复性
AI.tldr: 该研究通过衡量卷积神经网络中每一层输入补丁从其输出中可恢复的程度，来理解深度神经网络的内部工作机制，发现可恢复性随深度减小，并受层压缩影响，且不同架构的学习归因可恢复性不同。
AI.motivation: 深度神经网络的内部工作机制尚不清楚。现有的信息瓶颈框架关注输入信息对输入图像和输出标签的压缩，但本研究旨在理解从层的输出中能恢复多少该层自身的输入。
AI.method: 研究评估了卷积神经网络中每一层输入补丁从其输出中的可恢复性，而不是整个特征图。使用基于重建的探针，其大小取决于通道和核大小。比较了预训练、随机和重建优化的编码器，并使用线性和线性加残差MLP解码器。测量可恢复性为输入补丁与其重建之间的R²。引入单属性随机控制来分析预训练属性的影响。
AI.result: 可恢复性通常随深度减小，但更一致地由层的压缩程度预测。学习归因可恢复性（预训练与随机编码器之间的差异）在不同架构中不一致。复制预训练的奇异向量倾向于提高可恢复性，而复制奇异值谱或激活稀疏性则会降低可恢复性。
AI.conclusion: 深度神经网络中层的输入可恢复性随深度减小，并受层压缩程度影响。预训练属性（如奇异向量、奇异值谱和激活稀疏性）对可恢复性有不同且一致的影响。
AI.translation: 深度神经网络的内部工作机制仍未被很好理解。信息瓶颈框架通过表征其隐藏表示与网络输入之间的互信息来描述深度网络，已被用于识别输入信息相对于输入图像和输出标签的压缩。我们转而研究在卷积神经网络（CNNs）中，从层的输出中能恢复多少该层自身的输入。卷积层一次将其滤波器应用于一个输入补丁，因此我们通过基于重建的探针评估采样输入补丁的可恢复性，而不是整个特征图。因此，探针的大小取决于通道和核大小，而不是特征图大小，这使得我们的方法可以扩展到具有宽特征图的深层CNN。对于每一层，我们比较了预训练的、随机的和重建优化的编码器，使用线性和线性加残差MLP解码器。我们将在保留集上输入补丁与其重建之间的R²作为可恢复性度量。在九个ImageNet CNN中，可恢复性通常随深度减小，但更一致地由层的压缩程度预测。学习归因可恢复性（预训练编码器和随机编码器之间的差异）在不同架构中并不均匀。我们引入了单属性随机控制，将一个预训练属性转移到随机编码器上，发现每个控制在模型中都以一致的符号改变可恢复性：复制预训练的奇异向量倾向于提高可恢复性，而复制预训练的奇异值谱或激活稀疏性则会降低可恢复性。
AI.summary: 本研究旨在理解深度神经网络中从层的输出中恢复其自身输入的能力。通过在卷积神经网络中，使用基于重建的探针评估逐层输入补丁的可恢复性，该方法可扩展至深层网络。研究发现，可恢复性通常随深度减小，并与层的压缩程度高度相关。此外，不同架构的学习归因可恢复性存在差异，且复制预训练模型的特定属性（如奇异向量、奇异值谱或激活稀疏性）对可恢复性有系统性的影响。
AI.keywords: 深度神经网络, 输入可恢复性, 卷积神经网络, 信息瓶颈, 模型解释性
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的方法来探究深度神经网络的内部信息流，通过“层级输入可恢复性”这一指标，提供了理解网络内部机制的新视角，与传统的信息瓶颈框架形成对比和补充。其方法论，特别是通过采样输入补丁而非整个特征图来评估可恢复性，使其能有效应用于深层CNN。对单一属性随机控制的引入，有助于解耦和理解预训练模型中不同属性对信息保留的影响，具有重要的理论意义。

title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation
summary: Video diffusion models increasingly serve as priors for 4D generation, but the generated videos often lack geometric consistency. Recent approaches address this through post-training by designing geometric rewards, yet this can degrade texture and fine detail, requiring auxiliary appearance rewards and careful reward balancing. To address this challenge, we propose GeoFix, a unified framework that improves geometric consistency and visual quality with a single geometric reward, applicable to both training and inference-time reward alignment. Our reward measures cross-view depth consistency in static scene regions, targeting structural inconsistencies without directly constraining appearance or penalizing valid object motion. Crucially, depth agreement increases with camera field-of-view overlap even in real videos and 4D datasets, allowing a smaller camera movement to be mistaken for better geometry. We account for this effect by calibrating the reward against the overlap-dependent trend. GeoFix achieves a 39% improvement in WorldScore 3D consistency and a 4% increase in VBench Quality Score.

AI.title_translation: GeoFix：用于4D一致性生成的几何修复
AI.tldr: GeoFix是一个统一框架，通过校准的单一几何奖励来提高视频扩散模型生成的4D内容在几何上的一致性和视觉质量，避免了现有方法的纹理退化问题。
AI.motivation: 视频扩散模型生成的4D内容常缺乏几何一致性。现有方法通过几何奖励在后训练中解决此问题，但这会导致纹理和细节退化，需要额外的外观奖励和复杂的奖励平衡。
AI.method: GeoFix是一个统一框架，使用单一的几何奖励来提高几何一致性和视觉质量。该奖励衡量静态场景区域的跨视图深度一致性，旨在解决结构不一致性，而不直接限制外观或惩罚有效物体运动。它通过根据视场重叠引起的深度一致性趋势进行校准，以避免将较小的相机移动误认为是更好的几何结构。
AI.result: GeoFix在WorldScore 3D一致性方面提升了39%，在VBench质量评分方面提升了4%。
AI.conclusion: GeoFix通过其创新的、经过校准的单一几何奖励，有效解决了4D生成中几何一致性不足的问题，同时保持了视觉质量，并在多个指标上取得了显著改进。
AI.translation: 视频扩散模型越来越多地用作4D生成的先验，但生成的视频通常缺乏几何一致性。最近的方法通过设计几何奖励在后训练中解决此问题，但这会降低纹理和精细细节，需要辅助外观奖励和仔细的奖励平衡。为了解决这一挑战，我们提出了GeoFix，一个统一的框架，它通过单一的几何奖励改善几何一致性和视觉质量，适用于训练和推理时的奖励对齐。我们的奖励衡量静态场景区域的跨视图深度一致性，旨在解决结构不一致性，而不直接限制外观或惩罚有效的物体运动。至关重要的是，即使在真实视频和4D数据集中，深度一致性也会随着相机视场重叠的增加而增加，这可能导致较小的相机移动被误认为是更好的几何结构。我们通过根据重叠依赖趋势校准奖励来解释这种效应。GeoFix在WorldScore 3D一致性方面实现了39%的改进，在VBench质量评分方面实现了4%的增长。
AI.summary: 本文提出了GeoFix，一个统一的框架，旨在解决视频扩散模型在4D生成中缺乏几何一致性的问题。现有方法常导致纹理和细节退化，并需要复杂的奖励平衡。GeoFix通过设计一个单一的、校准过的几何奖励来提高几何一致性和视觉质量，该奖励测量静态场景区域的跨视图深度一致性，并考虑了视场重叠对深度一致性的影响。实验结果表明，GeoFix在WorldScore 3D一致性上提升了39%，在VBench质量评分上提升了4%。
AI.keywords: 4D生成, 几何一致性, 视频扩散模型, 深度一致性, 几何奖励
AI.comments: GeoFix的创新之处在于其提出的单一几何奖励机制，该机制通过关注静态场景区域的跨视图深度一致性，并在奖励设计中考虑了相机视场重叠的影响进行校准，有效避免了现有方法中多奖励平衡的复杂性以及对纹理和细节的损害。这种方法在提高几何一致性的同时保持了视觉质量，具有重要的实际应用价值。

title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
comments: Accepted at the DynaFront workshop at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.
comment: Accepted at the DynaFront workshop at NeurIPS 2026

AI.title_translation: 可控多样性采样通过回拉方向
AI.tldr: 提出一种免训练方法，利用回拉几何学在条件扩散模型中引导采样方向，以在保持质量和对齐的同时，提高生成图像的多样性。
AI.motivation: 条件扩散模型生成的图像质量高但多样性不足，不同随机种子生成的图像视觉相似，限制了创意探索。现有方法增加多样性有额外开销或降低图像质量/对齐。
AI.method: 提出一种免训练方法，利用从条件嵌入空间到图像空间的映射所产生的局部回拉几何学，识别最大输出敏感性方向。通过沿着这些方向引导不同的采样轨迹，鼓励生成不同的图像，同时保持与条件信号的一致性。
AI.result: 在MS-COCO和BrushNet上的实验表明，该方法在提高提示条件图像生成和图像修复的多样性方面有效。
AI.conclusion: 该方法能够有效提高条件扩散模型生成图像的多样性，同时保持与条件信号的一致性，且无需额外训练或优化。
AI.translation: 条件扩散模型可以生成与给定提示高度对齐的高质量图像。然而，从不同随机种子生成的样本在视觉上可能仍然相似，这限制了创意探索。现有方法可以增加变异性，但通常需要额外的优化或采样开销，而更强的扰动可能会引入扭曲，从而降低图像质量或提示对齐。我们提出了一种免训练方法，该方法利用从条件嵌入空间到图像空间的映射所产生的局部回拉几何学来识别最大输出敏感性方向。通过沿着这些方向引导不同的采样轨迹，我们鼓励生成不同的图像，同时保持与条件信号的一致性。在MS-COCO和BrushNet上的实验表明，该方法在提高提示条件图像生成和图像修复的多样性方面有效。
AI.summary: 本文提出一种免训练方法，旨在解决条件扩散模型生成图像多样性不足的问题。通过利用从条件嵌入空间到图像空间的局部回拉几何学，该方法能够识别最大输出敏感性方向，并沿着这些方向引导采样轨迹，从而在保持图像质量和提示一致性的前提下，显著提升生成图像的多样性。实验证明其在图像生成和修复任务中均表现出有效性。
AI.keywords: 扩散模型, 多样性采样, 回拉方向, 条件生成, 图像生成
AI.comments: 该研究通过引入“回拉方向”这一几何概念，为扩散模型的多样性采样提供了一种新颖且高效的免训练方法。其创新之处在于无需额外训练或复杂优化，仅通过理解和利用模型内部的几何结构来引导生成过程，这在保持生成质量的同时有效解决了多样性不足的挑战，具有较高的理论和实践价值。

title: Diagnosing Generalization Boundaries in AI-Based Vulnerability Detection via Calibrated Embedding Distances
summary: High benchmark scores in learning-based vulnerability detection mask severe degradation under distribution shifts. This paper demonstrates that calibrated embedding geometry exposes these hidden generalization boundaries on syntactically similar vulnerable and patched code pairs. An evaluation of CodeBERT and Qwen2.5-Coder across pattern, project, and temporal shifts on a strictly paired dataset reveals three main findings. First, whitened intermediate-layer embeddings with local nearest-neighbour scoring separate unfamiliar samples with a mean out-of-distribution AUROC of 0.739 (RQ1). Second, distance scores reveal a shift-specific reliability gradient where accuracy drops by over 35 percentage points and cross-project shifts cause the sharpest degradation, even though temporal shifts drift geometrically farthest (RQ2). Third, false positives on patched code systematically correlate with geometric proximity to vulnerable training neighbourhoods, increasing from 9.4% in the lowest-risk decile to 58.8% in the highest (RQ3). These calibrated distances establish a diagnostic signal that maps representation geometry directly to model degradation without requiring auxiliary models.

AI.title_translation: 通过校准嵌入距离诊断基于AI的漏洞检测中的泛化边界
AI.tldr: AI漏洞检测在分布偏移下性能会严重下降，本研究发现校准嵌入距离可以揭示这些泛化边界，并提供了一个直接诊断模型退化的信号。
AI.motivation: 学习型漏洞检测在基准测试中取得的高分掩盖了在分布偏移下严重的性能下降，这些隐藏的泛化边界需要被揭示。
AI.method: 该研究通过校准嵌入几何学来暴露泛化边界，并在严格配对的数据集上，对CodeBERT和Qwen2.5-Coder在模式、项目和时间偏移下进行了评估。
AI.result: 1. 经过白化的中间层嵌入结合局部最近邻评分可以分离出不熟悉的样本，平均域外AUROC为0.739。2. 距离分数揭示了与偏移相关的可靠性梯度，准确率下降超过35个百分点，其中跨项目偏移导致最严重的退化，即使时间偏移在几何上漂移最远。3. 补丁代码上的误报与几何上接近易受攻击的训练邻域系统地相关，从最低风险的10%的9.4%增加到最高风险的10%的58.8%。
AI.conclusion: 校准后的距离建立了一种诊断信号，可以将表示几何直接映射到模型退化，而无需辅助模型。
AI.translation: 学习型漏洞检测在基准测试中取得的高分掩盖了在分布偏移下严重的性能下降。本文证明，校准的嵌入几何结构在语法相似的易受攻击和已打补丁的代码对上暴露了这些隐藏的泛化边界。对CodeBERT和Qwen2.5-Coder在严格配对数据集上进行模式、项目和时间偏移评估后，揭示了三个主要发现。首先，经过白化的中间层嵌入与局部最近邻评分相结合，可以分离出不熟悉的样本，平均域外AUROC为0.739（RQ1）。其次，距离分数揭示了与偏移相关的可靠性梯度，其中准确率下降超过35个百分点，并且跨项目偏移导致最严重的退化，即使时间偏移在几何上漂移最远（RQ2）。第三，已打补丁代码上的误报与几何上接近易受攻击的训练邻域系统地相关，从最低风险的十分之一的9.4%增加到最高风险的十分之一的58.8%（RQ3）。这些校准距离建立了一种诊断信号，可以将表示几何直接映射到模型退化，而无需辅助模型。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了基于AI的漏洞检测模型在分布偏移下的泛化问题。研究发现，通过校准的嵌入几何可以有效揭示模型在面对语法相似但未见过的数据时的性能退化边界。通过对CodeBERT和Qwen2.5-Coder在不同类型偏移下的评估，作者证明了嵌入距离可以作为一种无需辅助模型的诊断信号，直接反映模型性能下降，尤其指出跨项目偏移导致最严重的性能退化，并且误报与几何接近训练集中的脆弱代码区域相关。
AI.keywords: AI漏洞检测, 泛化边界, 嵌入距离, 分布偏移, 模型诊断
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于提出了使用校准嵌入距离作为一种直接诊断AI漏洞检测模型泛化边界的信号，而无需依赖额外的辅助模型。这对于理解和改进AI模型在实际部署中应对数据分布变化的鲁棒性具有重要意义，尤其是在安全领域。研究结果揭示了不同类型分布偏移对模型性能的影响程度，并量化了误报与嵌入空间中脆弱区域的关联，为未来的模型改进提供了方向。

title: ARMOR: Adversary Cost Amplification via a Schema-Preserving Password-Hardening Retrofit for Resource-Constrained Systems
comments: Submitted to IEEE Journal. 24 pages, 8 figures, 23 tables. Supplementary material included as appendices
summary: Internet of Things (IoT) gateways, edge authentication servers, and legacy systems need protection against offline password guessing after credential-database disclosure. Memory-hard key derivation functions (KDFs) are the preferred defense, but their resource requirements can exceed memory or latency budgets. ARMOR addresses this gap with a schema-preserving verifier-side transform for database-only (DB-only) compromise. Secret per-account chains of injective operations reside in an isolated Chain Registry. Fixed terminal escape encoding preserves distinct pre-hash values under each chain and moves outputs outside printable ASCII. We evaluate NAIVE adversaries using unmodified cracking tools and AWARE adversaries that enumerate chains. For the evaluated pre-hardened three-operation chains, NAIVE recovery is at most 0.10% on non-digit targets. Escape encoding yields zero recovery of digit-only targets under evaluated stock rule-based and non-rule attacks, closing a bypass permitting up to 45.3% recovery. Across 14.05 million eligible RockYou password entries, retaining duplicates, the median conditional guessing number is approximately 52 output-class tests at depth three and 317 at depth five. These values quantify the chain-search subproblem given the correct plaintext under a unit-cost model. A separate historical 14-operation AWARE evaluation matches all transformed targets at full dictionary coverage. Deployment measurements show microsecond-scale bare-metal transforms on three IoT boards, with protected storage dominating the measured TrustZone-M prototype components. Although an isolated high-entropy pepper provides stronger cryptographic protection, ARMOR combines compact per-account chain storage with low transform cost. When resources permit and the KDF accepts the complete transformed output, ARMOR composes as KDF(ARMOR(password)).
comment: Submitted to IEEE Journal. 24 pages, 8 figures, 23 tables. Supplementary material included as appendices

AI.title_translation: ARMOR：通过模式保留的密码强化改造为资源受限系统放大对手成本
AI.tldr: ARMOR为资源受限系统提供了一种模式保留的密码强化方案，以应对凭证数据库泄露后的离线密码猜测攻击，显著增加了对手的破解成本。
AI.motivation: 物联网 (IoT) 网关、边缘认证服务器和遗留系统在凭证数据库泄露后需要防止离线密码猜测。虽然内存密集型密钥派生函数 (KDF) 是首选防御措施，但其资源需求往往超出这些系统的内存或延迟预算，ARMOR旨在解决这一空白。
AI.method: ARMOR通过一个模式保留的验证器端转换来应对仅数据库 (DB-only) 泄露。它将秘密的、每个账户的注入操作链存储在独立的链注册表中。固定的终端转义编码保留了每个链下不同的预哈希值，并将输出移至可打印ASCII之外。当资源允许时，ARMOR可以与KDF组合使用，形式为KDF(ARMOR(password))。
AI.result: 对于预强化的三操作链，NAIVE攻击者在非数字目标上的恢复率最高为0.10%。转义编码在评估的基于规则和非规则攻击下，对纯数字目标实现了零恢复，堵塞了一个允许高达45.3%恢复的旁路。在1405万个RockYou密码条目中，中位数条件猜测数在深度三时约为52个输出类别测试，在深度五时约为317个。一项独立的14操作AWARE评估以完整的字典覆盖率匹配了所有转换后的目标。部署测量显示在三个IoT板上实现了微秒级的裸机转换，其中受保护存储在TrustZone-M原型组件中占主导地位。
AI.conclusion: ARMOR结合了紧凑的每个账户链存储和低转换成本，为资源受限系统提供了有效的离线密码猜测防御，填补了内存密集型KDF不适用的空白。
AI.translation: 物联网 (IoT) 网关、边缘认证服务器和遗留系统在凭证数据库泄露后需要防止离线密码猜测。内存密集型密钥派生函数 (KDF) 是首选防御措施，但其资源需求可能超出内存或延迟预算。ARMOR 通过针对仅数据库 (DB-only) 泄露的模式保留验证器端转换来解决这一空白。秘密的每个账户的注入操作链驻留在独立的链注册表中。固定的终端转义编码保留了每个链下不同的预哈希值，并将输出移至可打印 ASCII 之外。我们评估了使用未修改破解工具的 NAIVE 攻击者和枚举链的 AWARE 攻击者。对于评估的预强化三操作链，NAIVE 恢复在非数字目标上最多为 0.10%。在评估的基于规则和非规则攻击下，转义编码对纯数字目标实现了零恢复，堵塞了一个允许高达 45.3% 恢复的旁路。在 1405 万个符合条件的 RockYou 密码条目中（包含重复项），中位数条件猜测数在深度三时约为 52 个输出类别测试，在深度五时约为 317 个。这些值量化了在单位成本模型下给定正确明文的链搜索子问题。一项独立的、历史的 14 操作 AWARE 评估以完整的字典覆盖率匹配了所有转换后的目标。部署测量显示在三个 IoT 板上实现了微秒级的裸机转换，其中受保护存储在测量的 TrustZone-M 原型组件中占主导地位。尽管隔离的高熵 pepper 提供了更强的加密保护，但 ARMOR 将紧凑的每个账户链存储与低转换成本相结合。当资源允许且 KDF 接受完整的转换输出时，ARMOR 可以组合为 KDF(ARMOR(password))。
AI.summary: 本文提出了 ARMOR，一种为资源受限系统（如物联网设备和边缘服务器）设计的密码强化方案，以应对凭证数据库泄露后的离线密码猜测攻击。针对内存密集型密钥派生函数不适用的场景，ARMOR 采用模式保留的验证器端转换，通过秘密的、每个账户的注入操作链和转义编码来极大增加对手破解密码的成本。实验结果表明，ARMOR 能有效降低密码恢复率，并展现出极低的资源消耗，可与现有 KDF 结合使用。
AI.keywords: 密码强化, 资源受限系统, 离线密码猜测, 物联网安全, 密钥派生函数
AI.comments: ARMOR 的创新之处在于它在资源受限环境下提供了一种实用的密码强化方案，解决了传统内存密集型 KDF 的局限性。其模式保留和低成本转换特性使其在 IoT 和边缘计算领域具有重要应用潜力。然而，其安全性在面对能够枚举链的 AWARE 攻击者时的具体表现（尤其是历史评估结果匹配所有目标）以及对“高熵 pepper”的对比提及，可能需要进一步深入分析其在不同威胁模型下的鲁棒性。

title: Learning to See through Action: Predictive Curiosity for Robots
summary: Humans and animals do not learn vision from a fixed set of data: they move, interact, and learn from the visual consequences of their actions. Motivated by this developmental view, we study whether robots can improve visual learning by actively collecting experience through curiosity-driven interaction. We introduce DySCOVER, a self-supervised framework for active robot visual learning. A robot observes RGB frames, learns a visual autoencoder that encodes and reconstructs them, and trains a recurrent world model to predict the next visual latent state conditioned on the current state and action. The agent's policy is trained only with intrinsic rewards: reconstruction error encourages visually novel observations, while the world model's error encourages transitions whose consequences are not yet predictable. This prediction error biases the policy toward more intricate trajectories that enrich the agent's set of experiences with observations beyond those encouraged by visual novelty alone. Our experiments conducted with robotic arms as the embodied agents show that adding predictive curiosity improves the vision model over using visual curiosity alone. Across variations in initial conditions, experience capacity, embodiment, and scene content, adding predictive curiosity consistently improved visual learning. These results show that predictive curiosity can improve active visual learning beyond reconstruction-based curiosity alone.

AI.title_translation: 通过行动学习视觉：机器人的预测好奇心
AI.tldr: 本文提出DySCOVER框架，通过结合视觉新颖性和预测好奇心，使机器人能够主动收集经验，从而改善视觉学习。
AI.motivation: 受人类和动物通过行动和互动学习视觉的启发，研究机器人是否可以通过好奇心驱动的互动积极收集经验来改善视觉学习。
AI.method: 引入DySCOVER框架，一个用于主动机器人视觉学习的自监督框架。机器人观察RGB帧，学习一个视觉自编码器来编码和重建它们，并训练一个循环世界模型来预测下一个视觉潜在状态。智能体的策略仅通过内在奖励进行训练：重建误差鼓励视觉新颖的观察，而世界模型的误差鼓励那些结果尚不可预测的转换。这种预测误差使策略偏向更复杂的轨迹，从而丰富了智能体的经验集。
AI.result: 实验表明，与仅使用视觉好奇心相比，添加预测好奇心可以改善视觉模型。在初始条件、经验容量、具身性和场景内容的变化下，添加预测好奇心始终能改善视觉学习。
AI.conclusion: 预测好奇心可以超越单独基于重建的好奇心，改善主动视觉学习。
AI.translation: 人类和动物并非从固定的数据集中学习视觉：它们通过移动、互动，并从其行动的视觉结果中学习。受这种发展观点的启发，我们研究机器人是否可以通过好奇心驱动的互动积极收集经验来改善视觉学习。我们引入了DySCOVER，一个用于主动机器人视觉学习的自监督框架。机器人观察RGB帧，学习一个视觉自编码器来编码和重建它们，并训练一个循环世界模型来预测下一个视觉潜在状态，该状态以当前状态和行动为条件。智能体的策略仅通过内在奖励进行训练：重建误差鼓励视觉新颖的观察，而世界模型的误差鼓励那些结果尚不可预测的转换。这种预测误差使策略偏向更复杂的轨迹，从而用超出仅由视觉新颖性鼓励的观察来丰富智能体的经验集。我们使用机械臂作为具身智能体进行的实验表明，与仅使用视觉好奇心相比，添加预测好奇心可以改善视觉模型。在初始条件、经验容量、具身性和场景内容的变化下，添加预测好奇心始终能改善视觉学习。这些结果表明，预测好奇心可以超越单独基于重建的好奇心，改善主动视觉学习。
AI.summary: 本文提出了DySCOVER，一个自监督框架，旨在通过好奇心驱动的互动提升机器人的主动视觉学习能力。该框架结合了视觉自编码器和循环世界模型，利用内在奖励机制，包括重建误差和世界模型预测误差，促使机器人探索视觉新颖且结果不可预测的轨迹。实验证明，加入预测好奇心能显著优于单纯基于重建的好奇心，从而在多种条件下持续改善机器人的视觉学习效果。
AI.keywords: 预测好奇心, 机器人视觉学习, 自监督, DySCOVER, 世界模型
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于提出了“预测好奇心”的概念，并将其与传统的“视觉新颖性”相结合，鼓励机器人探索更复杂、更具挑战性的环境，从而更有效地学习视觉。这种方法模拟了生物体通过主动探索和预测来学习的机制，对机器人自主学习和具身智能领域具有重要意义。它超越了被动数据收集，强调了主动互动在视觉学习中的关键作用。

title: Plottery: A Code-Integrated GUI for Matplotlib
comments: Preprint. Final version is published in the proceedings of the 2026 IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages and Human-Centric Computing (VL/HCC 2026)
summary: Scientists have many tools to author plots: graphical direct manipulation apps like a spreadsheet's chart builder, text-based programming tools like Matplotlib and ggplot2, or AI chat interfaces.
