In our framework, the outcomes are images (what ad to show) and each bidder expresses their preferences over outcomes by declaring their value per unit of alignment between the image chosen by the mechanism and a textual description of their desired image. Our proposed mechanism combines the advertisers' bids and textual descriptions into a score that drives the reverse process of a diffusion model. This is used to sample a set of candidate images from which the welfare maximizing one is eventually chosen. Extensive experimentation evaluates our proposed mechanism around the following axes: (1) efficiency improvements of our allocation rule relative to the single-winner allocation rule; (2) monotonicity of our allocation rule; and (3) approximate incentive compatibility when combining our allocation rule with Myerson lemma-based or Clarke rule-based payments. Improvements along all these axes are shown with the number of Monte Carlo samples. Meanwhile, these benefits are attained while preserving the image quality.

AI.title_translation: 基于扩散模型的多赢家横幅广告拍卖
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于扩散模型的横幅广告拍卖新框架，允许多个竞标者共同赢得单个横幅广告机会，并根据其出价强度影响所显示的广告，从而实现比标准单赢家横幅广告拍卖更丰富的产出空间。
AI.motivation: 标准横幅广告拍卖是单一赢家模式，导致产出空间有限。本文旨在提出一种新的框架，允许多个竞标者共同赢得广告机会并影响广告显示，从而实现更丰富的产出空间。
AI.method: 我们提出了一个利用扩散模型的新框架，允许多个竞标者共同赢得单个横幅广告机会。每个竞标者通过声明其对机制选择的图像与期望图像的文本描述之间对齐程度的每单位价值来表达其偏好。我们提出的机制将广告商的出价和文本描述结合成一个分数，该分数驱动扩散模型的逆过程。这用于从一组候选图像中采样，最终选择福利最大化的图像。
AI.result: 实验结果表明，与单赢家分配规则相比，我们的分配规则在以下方面有所改进：(1) 分配规则的效率；(2) 分配规则的单调性；以及 (3) 当将我们的分配规则与基于Myerson引理或Clarke规则的支付结合时，近似激励兼容性。所有这些方面的改进都随着蒙特卡洛样本数量的增加而显示出来。同时，这些益处在保持图像质量的同时获得。
AI.conclusion: 本文提出的基于扩散模型的拍卖框架显著提高了多赢家横幅广告拍卖的效率、单调性和近似激励兼容性，同时保持了图像质量，并提供了比传统单赢家拍卖更丰富的产出空间。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一种新的横幅广告拍卖框架，利用扩散模型允许多个竞标者共同赢得单个横幅广告机会，并且根据其出价强度影响横幅上显示的广告，与标准的单赢家横幅广告拍卖相比，这实现了远更丰富的产出空间，在标准拍卖中只有一个赢家显示其广告。在我们的框架中，产出是图像（显示哪个广告），每个竞标者通过声明其对机制选择的图像与他们期望图像的文本描述之间对齐程度的每单位价值来表达其偏好。我们提出的机制将广告商的出价和文本描述结合成一个分数，该分数驱动扩散模型的逆过程。这用于从一组候选图像中采样，最终选择福利最大化的图像。广泛的实验围绕以下轴线评估了我们提出的机制：(1) 我们的分配规则相对于单赢家分配规则的效率改进；(2) 我们的分配规则的单调性；以及 (3) 当将我们的分配规则与基于Myerson引理或Clarke规则的支付结合时，近似激励兼容性。所有这些方面的改进都随着蒙特卡洛样本数量的增加而显示出来。同时，这些益处在保持图像质量的同时获得。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种新颖的基于扩散模型的横幅广告拍卖框架，允许多个竞标者共同赢得并根据其出价和文本偏好影响所显示的广告。该机制将出价和描述整合为一个分数，驱动扩散模型的逆过程，从而采样图像并选择福利最大化的图像。实验证明，与单赢家拍卖相比，该框架在效率、单调性和近似激励兼容性方面均有提升，同时保持了图像质量。
AI.keywords: 扩散模型, 横幅广告, 多赢家拍卖, 机制设计, 广告拍卖
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新之处在于将通常用于图像生成的扩散模型应用于广告拍卖领域，以创建“多赢家”场景。这显著扩展了传统单赢家模式的产出空间，可能带来更高效和灵活的广告解决方案。将文本描述融入偏好表达也是一个新颖的方面。

title: RES-MR: Risk-Aware Reasoning for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation
summary: Medication recommendations seek to deliver personalized drug combinations based on patients' clinical information, where ensuring transparent decision-making and personalized safety are of paramount importance. However, existing approaches predominantly operate as ``black boxes'', offering limited interpretability and hindering clinician trust. Furthermore, they typically rely on fixed, patient-agnostic safety constraints, neglecting the heterogeneity of risk tolerance across individuals, which poses significant risks to vulnerable populations. To address these gaps, we propose \textbf{RES-MR}, a novel Risk-aware Reasoning framework for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation using LLMs. RES-MR follows a two-stage training paradigm: (1) an explainable clinical reasoning distillation stage to elicit diagnostic capabilities by fine-tuning on synthesized reasoning trajectories, grounded in patient-specific knowledge from graph retrieval; and (2) a risk-aware policy optimization stage to dynamically balance therapeutic efficacy with personalized safety. This stage employs disentangled drug factors to construct patient-specific reference prototypes that capture desired therapeutic drug features and risk features to avoid. These prototypes enable risk boundary calibration and guide the model toward safe recommendations via reward shaping and clipping. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RES-MR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of accuracy, safety, and explainability. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/wangcong2001/RES-MR.

AI.title_translation: RES-MR: 用于可解释和安全药物推荐的风险感知推理
AI.tldr: RES-MR是一个利用大型语言模型（LLMs）进行可解释且安全的药物推荐框架，通过两阶段训练范式平衡疗效和个性化安全，并显著优于现有基线。
AI.motivation: 现有药物推荐方法多为“黑箱”操作，解释性差，难以获得临床医生信任。此外，它们依赖固定的、与患者无关的安全约束，忽视个体风险承受能力的异质性，对弱势群体构成重大风险。
AI.method: 本文提出了RES-MR，一个用于可解释和安全药物推荐的风险感知推理框架，它利用大型语言模型（LLMs）。RES-MR遵循两阶段训练范式：(1) 可解释的临床推理蒸馏阶段，通过在合成推理轨迹上进行微调，并基于图检索的患者特定知识，以激发诊断能力；(2) 风险感知策略优化阶段，动态平衡治疗效果与个性化安全。此阶段使用解耦的药物因子构建患者特定的参考原型，捕捉期望的治疗药物特征和要避免的风险特征。这些原型通过奖励塑造和剪裁实现风险边界校准并引导模型进行安全推荐。
AI.result: 在基准数据集上的大量实验表明，RES-MR在准确性、安全性和可解释性方面显著优于最先进的基线方法。
AI.conclusion: RES-MR通过风险感知推理和两阶段训练范式，成功解决了现有药物推荐方法在解释性和个性化安全方面的不足，显著提升了药物推荐的准确性、安全性和可解释性。
AI.translation: 药物推荐旨在根据患者的临床信息提供个性化的药物组合，其中确保决策透明化和个性化安全至关重要。然而，现有方法主要作为“黑箱”运行，解释性有限，阻碍了临床医生的信任。此外，它们通常依赖固定的、与患者无关的安全约束，忽视了个体风险承受能力的异质性，这对弱势群体构成了重大风险。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了RES-MR，一个新颖的、利用大型语言模型（LLMs）进行可解释和安全药物推荐的风险感知推理框架。RES-MR遵循两阶段训练范式：(1) 可解释的临床推理蒸馏阶段，通过在合成推理轨迹上进行微调，并基于图检索的患者特定知识，以激发诊断能力；(2) 风险感知策略优化阶段，动态平衡治疗效果与个性化安全。此阶段使用解耦的药物因子构建患者特定的参考原型，捕捉期望的治疗药物特征和要避免的风险特征。这些原型通过奖励塑造和剪裁实现风险边界校准并引导模型进行安全推荐。在基准数据集上的大量实验表明，RES-MR在准确性、安全性和可解释性方面显著优于最先进的基线方法。我们的代码和数据可在https://github.com/wangcong2001/RES-MR获取。
AI.summary: 本文提出了RES-MR，一个基于大型语言模型（LLMs）的风险感知推理框架，旨在解决现有药物推荐系统在解释性和个性化安全方面的不足。RES-MR采用两阶段训练范式：首先通过合成推理轨迹和图检索进行临床推理蒸馏，然后通过风险感知策略优化平衡疗效与个性化安全，利用患者特定原型进行风险边界校准。实验证明，RES-MR在准确性、安全性和可解释性方面均优于现有基线。
AI.keywords: 药物推荐, 风险感知, 可解释性, LLMs, 个性化安全
AI.comments: RES-MR的创新之处在于其结合了LLMs的推理能力与风险感知策略优化，解决了药物推荐领域长期存在的“黑箱”问题和个性化安全挑战。两阶段训练范式，特别是引入患者特定原型进行风险边界校准，是其核心贡献。这对于提高临床医生对AI推荐系统的信任和保障患者安全具有重要意义。然而，合成推理轨迹的质量和LLMs在真实临床场景中的泛化能力可能需要进一步验证。

title: EdgeLLM-Nano: Auditing Polar-Guided Key-Cache Compression and Consistency-Anchored Pruning on a 33.6 MB On-Device Language Model
summary: Deploying language models (LMs) on the edge presents unique memory, latency, and power challenges absent in high-performance computing. KV-cache compression emerges as a promising approach to address these challenges. However, the effectiveness of current KV-cache compression methods has not been thoroughly examined on edge devices. Moreover, we show that existing evaluation methods do not always involve the KV-cache under test. We propose EdgeLLM-Nano, a measurement study of KV-cache compression using a nano-scale decoder-only LM (transformer) testbed that has 8.39M parameters, i.e., 33.6 MB, to enable end-to-end examination of each backend, seed, and power sample. Our results give a negative verdict for a polar-guided key-cache quantizer (round-to-nearest (RTN) control causes an order of magnitude less damage), as well as a consistency-anchored progressive weight pruner (one-shot magnitude-based pruning performs as well as, if not better). We also introduce Long-Context Decode Fidelity (LCDF) evaluation, a token-by-token examination of teacher-forced log-losses using the KV-cache under test. Unlike perplexity that gives the same 5.461 score to all methods, LCDF distinguishes different KV-cache compression backends thanks to its paired statistics across seeds and effect sizes. Our companion Raspberry Pi 5 measurement shows all compression backends we tested to be less energy-efficient per token compared to uncompressed FP16 inference. Except for KIVI that is close to lossless in terms of LCDF, our findings indicate KV-cache compression can be improved. LCDF offers a simple and effective way of shedding light on KV-cache compression methods, whose negative impacts have been overlooked by perplexity.

AI.title_translation: 边缘LLM-Nano：在33.6MB的设备端语言模型上审计极性引导的关键缓存压缩和一致性锚定剪枝
AI.tldr: 该研究评估了在内存和功耗受限的边缘设备上使用KV缓存压缩技术，发现现有方法效果不佳，并提出了一种新的评估方法LCDF。
AI.motivation: 在边缘设备上部署语言模型面临内存、延迟和功耗挑战，KV缓存压缩被认为是潜在解决方案，但现有方法在边缘设备的有效性未经充分评估，且评估方法可能未包含KV缓存本身。
AI.method: 提出EdgeLLM-Nano，一个在小型（33.6MB）语言模型上进行KV缓存压缩的测量研究。引入了LCDF评估方法，对教师强制的逐token对数损失进行检查。在树莓派5上进行了能效测量。
AI.result: 极性引导的关键缓存量化器（RTN控制）效果较差。一致性锚定的渐进式权重剪枝器（一次性基于幅度修剪）效果与现有方法相当甚至更好。LCDF评估能区分不同的KV缓存压缩后端，而困惑度得分相同。大多数压缩后端比未压缩的FP16推理能效更低。KIVI接近无损，但总体而言KV缓存压缩仍有改进空间。
AI.conclusion: 现有KV缓存压缩方法在边缘设备上的效果不佳，甚至可能降低能效。LCDF是一种比困惑度更有效的评估方法，可以揭示KV缓存压缩的负面影响。KV缓存压缩技术仍有待改进。
AI.translation: 在高性能计算中不存在内存、延迟和功耗的挑战。KV缓存压缩被认为是一种有前途的解决方案，可以解决这些挑战。然而，现有的KV缓存压缩方法在边缘设备上的有效性尚未得到充分检验。此外，我们表明现有的评估方法并不总是包含被测的KV缓存。我们提出了EdgeLLM-Nano，一个使用纳米级解码器仅Transformer测试平台（具有839万个参数，即33.6MB）的KV缓存压缩测量研究，以实现对每个后端、种子和电源样本的端到端检查。我们的结果对极性引导的关键缓存量化器（舍入到最近（RTN）控制造成的损害要小一个数量级）以及一致性锚定的渐进式权重剪枝器（一次性基于幅度修剪的效果与此相当，甚至更好）给出了否定的评价。我们还引入了长上下文解码保真度（LCDF）评估，一种使用被测KV缓存的教师强制对数损失的逐token检查。与为所有方法提供相同5.461分数的困惑度不同，LCDF区分了不同的KV缓存压缩后端，这得益于其跨种子和效应大小的配对统计数据。我们配套的树莓派5测量显示，与未压缩的FP16推理相比，我们测试的所有压缩后端每个token的能效都较低。除了KIVI在LCDF方面接近无损外，我们的发现表明KV缓存压缩仍有改进空间。LCDF提供了一种简单有效的方法来阐明KV缓存压缩方法，其负面影响已被困惑度所忽视。
AI.summary: EdgeLLM-Nano 研究了在资源受限的边缘设备上部署大型语言模型时，KV缓存压缩和权重剪枝技术的有效性。研究人员发现，现有的KV缓存压缩方法在边缘设备上的效果不佳，甚至可能降低能效，并且传统的评估方法（如困惑度）无法准确反映其性能。为此，他们提出了一种新的评估指标LCDF（长上下文解码保真度），能够更精确地评估KV缓存压缩的效果。研究结果表明，某些压缩技术（如极性引导量化）效果不佳，而另一些（如一致性锚定剪枝）则表现良好。总体而言，该研究强调了在边缘设备上优化语言模型部署的挑战，并为未来改进KV缓存压缩技术提供了方向。
AI.keywords: KV缓存压缩, 边缘计算, 语言模型, LCDF评估, 模型剪枝
AI.comments: 该研究在边缘设备上对KV缓存压缩和模型剪枝进行了深入的测量研究，并提出了一种新的评估方法LCDF，克服了传统评估方法的局限性。研究结果具有实际意义，指出了当前KV缓存压缩技术的不足，并为未来的研究和优化提供了方向。然而，研究的局限性在于仅使用了单一的 nano-scale decoder-only LM 测试平台，未来可以扩展到更多不同架构和规模的模型上进行验证。

title: Scale, Drivers, and Limits of Representational Alignment Across Large Language Models
summary: Comparing large language models can reveal shared representational structure and systematic differences between them. However, aggregate similarity measures can obscure how agreement varies across geometric scales and which linguistic properties support it. We introduce two complementary methods to resolve where models agree and what supports that agreement. Standard representational similarity analysis (RSA) summarizes similarity across all stimulus pairs, potentially obscuring differences in alignment between nearby and distant inputs. Neighborhood-Weighted RSA (NW-RSA) addresses this limitation by weighting stimulus pairs according to their proximity in representational space, placing alignment from local neighborhoods to global geometry on a common scale. Counterfactual RSA (CF-RSA) tests which linguistic properties support alignment by comparing intact representations in one model with representations under controlled linguistic perturbations in another. Across diverse language models, we find strong agreement in coarse representational geometry but substantial divergence in local neighborhoods. Alignment is observed both across broadly sampled natural text and within linguistic equivalence classes that preserve particular aspects of meaning or structure. Counterfactual analyses reveal selective sensitivity: changes to logical scope reduce alignment substantially more than the tested changes to hierarchical syntax, event roles, or discourse structure. Alignment also decreases when sentence structure or lexical meaning is disrupted in word lists and jabberwocky sentences, suggesting that the regularities of natural language support stronger convergence. These findings refine claims of representational universality by showing that strong overall similarity need not imply agreement in how models represent finer linguistic distinctions.

AI.title_translation: 大型语言模型中的表征一致性的规模、驱动因素和限制
AI.tldr: 研究发现，大型语言模型在粗粒度的表征几何结构上存在显著一致性，但在局部邻域上存在较大差异。通过引入邻域加权RSA和反事实RSA方法，分析了不同模型在不同尺度和不同语言属性下的表征一致性。结果表明，粗粒度的几何结构一致性较强，而局部邻域的一致性较弱。逻辑范围的变化比句法、事件角色或话语结构的变化更能显著降低模型间的一致性。自然语言的规律性有助于增强模型间的一致性。
AI.motivation: 为了更深入地理解大型语言模型之间的表征一致性，探究这种一致性在不同几何尺度上的变化，以及哪些语言属性对其有支持作用，从而克服现有聚合相似性度量可能掩盖局部差异的局限性。
AI.method: 引入两种互补方法：邻域加权RSA（NW-RSA）通过对表征空间中邻近的刺激对进行加权，来评估不同尺度下的表征一致性；反事实RSA（CF-RSA）通过比较一个模型中的完整表征与另一个模型中经过语言扰动后的表征，来测试哪些语言属性支持表征一致性。
AI.result: 在不同的大型语言模型中，发现粗粒度的表征几何结构上存在强的一致性，但在局部邻域上存在显著差异。这种一致性存在于广泛抽样的自然文本以及保留特定意义或结构的语言等价类中。反事实分析表明，模型对逻辑范围的变化比对句法、事件角色或话语结构的变化更敏感，这些变化能更显著地降低一致性。当句子结构或词汇意义在单词列表和假想句中被破坏时，一致性也会降低，这表明自然语言的规律性有助于增强模型间的一致性。
AI.conclusion: 大型语言模型在整体表征上可能表现出高度相似性，但这并不意味着它们在表征细微的语言学区分上也能达成一致。研究结果强调了在分析模型表征一致性时，需要考虑几何尺度和具体的语言属性。
AI.translation: 比较大型语言模型可以揭示它们之间共享的表征结构和系统性差异。然而，聚合相似性度量可能会掩盖在不同几何尺度上一致性的变化以及支持这种一致性的语言属性。我们引入了两种互补的方法来解决模型在何处达成一致以及什么支持这种一致性。标准的表征相似性分析（RSA）总结了所有刺激对之间的相似性，可能会掩盖邻近和遥远输入之间一致性的差异。邻域加权RSA（NW-RSA）通过根据刺激对在表征空间中的邻近性对它们进行加权来解决这一局限性，将从局部邻域到全局几何的一致性置于共同的尺度上。反事实RSA（CF-RSA）通过比较一个模型中的完整表征与另一个模型中经过受控语言扰动后的表征来测试哪些语言属性支持一致性。在各种语言模型中，我们发现粗粒度的表征几何结构存在强的一致性，但在局部邻域上存在显著差异。在广泛抽样的自然文本以及保留特定意义或结构的语言等价类中都观察到了一致性。反事实分析揭示了选择性敏感性：逻辑范围的变化比测试的层次句法、事件角色或话语结构的变化更能显著地降低一致性。当句子结构或词汇意义在单词列表和假想句中被破坏时，一致性也会降低，这表明自然语言的规律性有助于增强模型间的收敛性。这些发现通过表明强烈的整体相似性不一定意味着在如何表征更精细的语言学区分上达成一致，从而改进了对表征普遍性的论断。
AI.summary: 本研究通过引入邻域加权RSA（NW-RSA）和反事实RSA（CF-RSA）两种新方法，深入分析了大型语言模型（LLMs）在不同尺度和不同语言属性下的表征一致性。研究发现，LLMs在粗粒度的表征几何结构上表现出高度一致性，但在局部邻域的表征上存在显著差异。逻辑范围的变化对模型间一致性的影响最大，而句法、事件角色和话语结构的影响相对较小。自然语言的规律性，如句子结构和词汇意义，有助于增强模型间的一致性。该研究精细化了关于表征普遍性的观点，指出整体相似性不代表在细微语言学区分上的表征也一致。
AI.keywords: 表征一致性, 大型语言模型, 邻域加权RSA, 反事实RSA, 语言属性
AI.comments: 该研究巧妙地通过两种新颖的分析方法（NW-RSA和CF-RSA）解决了表征分析中的关键问题，即如何区分不同尺度下的一致性以及探究其背后的语言学驱动因素。研究结果揭示了LLMs表征的复杂性，即虽然存在宏观层面的共性，但在微观层面的差异同样显著，这对于理解和改进LLMs的泛化能力和鲁棒性具有重要意义。未来的研究可以进一步探索更多语言属性对表征一致性的影响，以及不同模型架构和训练数据如何影响这些发现。

title: What Counts as the Same Task? Executable Contracts for Robustness Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents
summary: Robustness tests for tool-using agents often change the agent's environment, for example by hiding a hostile note in an invoice, and then judge the agent by what it does. The result tells us about the original task only if the changed test case is still a valid test of that task. Many evaluations decide this with weak rules, such as accepting any well-formed edit or any edit that stays close to the original in embedding space. We propose executable task contracts. A contract states which facts define a task, which edits are allowed, and what finishing the task means, and it checks each changed test case before the agent runs. We compare validity rules by scoring the same 14,336 stored agent runs under each rule. Across four encoders, embedding thresholds allowed 75-100% of edits that changed the task, such as swapping the payee, yet rejected 24-45% of valid hostile notes. With a MiniLM cosine threshold, Mistral appeared vulnerable on all 64 tasks, but only 26 had a successful valid attack. Replaying a saved solution and allowing edits to benchmark fields fail in similar ways. Evaluations should state, and check, what counts as the same task.

AI.title_translation: 什么才算作同一个任务？用于工具使用代理鲁棒性评估的可执行合约
AI.tldr: 评估工具使用代理时，测试用例的有效性至关重要。传统的弱规则（如允许格式正确或与原嵌入空间接近的编辑）无法准确判断修改后的测试用例是否仍属于同一任务。本文提出了可执行任务合约，它明确定义了任务、允许的编辑以及任务完成的标准，并在代理运行前检查测试用例的有效性。实验表明，基于嵌入的阈值规则允许大量改变任务的编辑，同时错过了有效的攻击。因此，评估应明确并检查“同一任务”的定义。
AI.motivation: 传统的工具使用代理鲁棒性评估方法依赖于弱规则来判断修改后的测试用例是否仍然有效，这可能导致评估不准确，无法真实反映代理的鲁棒性。
AI.method: 提出并使用可执行任务合约来评估工具使用代理的鲁棒性。该合约明确定义了任务、允许的编辑以及任务完成的标准，并在代理运行前检查每个修改后的测试用例的有效性。通过比较不同有效性规则（包括嵌入阈值）的得分来评估其性能。
AI.result: 基于嵌入的阈值规则允许75%-100%的改变任务的编辑（如交换收款人），同时拒绝了24%-45%的有效攻击。使用MiniLM余弦阈值时，Mistral在所有64个任务中看似都存在漏洞，但只有26个任务存在成功的有效攻击。重放已保存的解决方案并允许编辑基准字段的失败方式类似。
AI.conclusion: 评估工具使用代理的鲁棒性时，应明确定义并检查“同一任务”的标准，以确保评估的准确性和有效性。可执行任务合约提供了一种更可靠的方法来实现这一点。
AI.translation: 鲁棒性测试通常会改变代理的环境，例如在发票中隐藏恶意注释，然后根据代理的行为进行判断。只有当修改后的测试用例仍然是该任务的有效测试时，结果才能告诉我们关于原始任务的信息。许多评估使用弱规则来决定这一点，例如接受任何格式正确或在嵌入空间中接近原始的编辑。我们提出了可执行的任务合约。合约规定了定义任务的事实、允许的编辑以及完成任务的含义，并在代理运行前检查每个修改后的测试用例。我们通过在每种规则下对相同的14,336次已存储的代理运行进行评分来比较有效性规则。在四个编码器上，嵌入阈值允许75%-100%的改变任务的编辑，例如交换收款人，但拒绝了24%-45%的有效恶意注释。使用MiniLM余弦阈值时，Mistral在所有64个任务中似乎都存在漏洞，但只有26个任务存在成功的有效攻击。重放已保存的解决方案并允许编辑基准字段的失败方式类似。评估应该陈述并检查“什么才算作同一个任务”。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为“可执行任务合约”的新方法，用于更准确地评估工具使用代理的鲁棒性。该方法通过明确定义任务、允许的编辑和任务完成标准，并在执行前验证测试用例的有效性，解决了传统评估方法中存在的“什么才算作同一个任务”的模糊性问题。实验结果表明，传统的基于嵌入相似性的规则在判断任务有效性方面存在严重缺陷，可能导致对代理鲁棒性的错误评估。因此，作者强调评估应明确并强制执行任务定义的标准。
AI.keywords: 可执行任务合约, 鲁棒性评估, 工具使用代理, 任务定义, 有效性检查
AI.comments: 该研究解决了工具使用代理评估中的一个关键问题：如何准确定义和判断一个修改后的测试用例是否仍然属于原始任务。提出的“可执行任务合约”方法具有创新性，通过形式化定义任务约束，提高了评估的严谨性和可靠性。然而，合约的复杂性和实际部署的开销可能是一个挑战。未来的工作可以关注如何简化合约的创建和验证过程，以及在更广泛的代理应用中验证该方法的有效性。

title: Shared-Control Teleoperation of Omnidirectional Aerial Robots for Continuous Valve Rotation
comments: 3 pages, 2 figures. Accepted to IROS 2025 Workshop on Advancements in Aerial Physical Interaction. Best Paper Award Candidate
summary: Omnidirectional aerial robots offer full 6-DoF independent control over position and orientation, making them popular for aerial manipulation. Although there have been advancements in robotic autonomy, human operation remains essential in complex aerial environments. Previously, we proposed an aerial teleoperation system that brings the rotational flexibility of human hands into the unbounded aerial workspace, which was evaluated through a vertically mounted valve-turning task. However, due to the limited range of human forearm's motion, the robot could not continuously rotate the valve, hindering its application in industry. In this work, we propose an approach to initiate continuous rotation when the forearm angle exceeds a threshold. This switch of control authority exemplifies the concept shared control from human-robot interaction, marking a further step in aerial teleoperation.
comment: 3 pages, 2 figures. Accepted to IROS 2025 Workshop on Advancements in Aerial Physical Interaction. Best Paper Award Candidate

AI.title_translation: 全向空中机器人的共享控制遥操作以实现连续阀门旋转
AI.tldr: 为了克服现有空中遥操作系统中因人类手臂运动范围有限而无法连续旋转阀门的缺点，本研究提出了一种在手臂角度超过阈值时启动连续旋转的方案，实现了控制权的切换，这是空中遥操作领域的一个新进展。
AI.motivation: 现有空中遥操作系统在执行连续阀门旋转任务时存在局限，因为人类手臂的运动范围有限，导致机器人无法实现连续旋转。
AI.method: 当操作者的手臂角度超过预设阈值时，系统会自动接管控制权，启动阀门的连续旋转。
AI.result: 提出了一种新的空中遥操作方法，能够实现对阀门的连续旋转，克服了以往因手臂运动范围限制而无法连续旋转的缺点。
AI.conclusion: 本研究提出了一种利用共享控制实现全向空中机器人连续阀门旋转的方法，克服了现有技术的局限性，是空中遥操作领域的一个重要进展。
AI.translation: 全向空中机器人提供对位置和方向完全独立的6自由度控制，使其在空中操作领域备受欢迎。尽管机器人自主性方面已有进展，但在复杂的空中环境中，人工操作仍然至关重要。此前，我们提出了一个空中遥操作系统，它将人类手的旋转灵活性引入到无界的空中工作空间中，并通过一个垂直安装的阀门转动任务进行了评估。然而，由于人类前臂运动范围的限制，机器人无法连续旋转阀门，阻碍了其在工业中的应用。在这项工作中，我们提出了一种在手臂角度超过阈值时启动连续旋转的方法。这种控制权切换的例子体现了人机交互中共享控制的概念，标志着空中遥操作向前迈出了重要一步。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种用于全向空中机器人的共享控制遥操作方法，以实现连续阀门旋转。该方法解决了以往因人类手臂运动范围限制而无法连续旋转阀门的问题，通过在操作者手臂角度超过阈值时自动接管控制权，实现了阀门的连续旋转，是空中遥操作领域的一项重要进展。
AI.keywords: 空中机器人,遥操作,共享控制,阀门旋转,连续旋转
AI.comments: 该研究有效地解决了空中遥操作中的一个实际问题，即如何克服操作者手臂运动限制以实现连续阀门旋转。通过引入共享控制的概念，该方法不仅提高了操作效率，也为未来更复杂的空中操作任务提供了借鉴。然而，需要进一步研究在不同环境和不同类型的阀门上该方法的鲁棒性和适应性。

title: AphaVoice: Text-to-Speech Model for Aphasia Patient Simulation
comments: Accepted at IEEE Spoken Language Technology (SLT) 2026
summary: While language therapy is the primary treatment for post-stroke aphasia, limited clinical resources often restrict patient access to proper care. Addressing this gap requires reliable training simulations for medical professionals. However, current AI efforts focus almost exclusively on speech processing, leaving speech generation largely unexplored. This study introduces AphaVoice, a novel text-to-speech (TTS) framework explicitly engineered to synthesize highly realistic aphasic speech. Evaluated against state-of-the-art TTS systems, AphaVoice demonstrates a superior ability to capture the clinical feature of dysfluency, outperforming existing models in temporal metrics while consistently maintaining speaker identity. By leveraging latent space shifting, the model also supports multi-speaker generation without sacrificing phonetic realism. Ultimately, AphaVoice provides a scalable, high-fidelity tool for medical training and clinical simulation related to aphasia.
comment: Accepted at IEEE Spoken Language Technology (SLT) 2026

AI.title_translation: 失语症患者模拟的文本到语音模型
AI.tldr: AphaVoice是一个新的文本到语音（TTS）框架，用于生成逼真的失语症患者语音，在捕捉语言不流畅性方面优于现有模型，并支持多说话人生成。
AI.motivation: 目前的AI研究主要集中在语音处理，而语音生成，特别是失语症患者的语音生成，却很少被探索，这限制了对医疗专业人员的培训模拟。现有的临床资源也有限，限制了患者获得适当的治疗。
AI.method: AphaVoice框架利用潜在空间移位技术来合成逼真的失语症语音，并支持多说话人生成。
AI.result: AphaVoice在捕捉语言不流畅性方面表现优于最先进的TTS系统，在时间指标上表现更好，同时保持说话人身份。该模型还支持多说话人生成，而不会牺牲语音的真实性。
AI.conclusion: AphaVoice提供了一个可扩展、高保真的工具，用于与失语症相关的医疗培训和临床模拟。
AI.translation: 虽然语言治疗是治疗中风后失语症的主要方法，但有限的临床资源常常限制了患者获得适当治疗的机会。弥合这一差距需要可靠的培训模拟，供医疗专业人员使用。然而，目前的人工智能研究几乎完全集中在语音处理方面，而语音生成方面却很少被探索。本研究介绍了AphaVoice，一个新颖的文本到语音（TTS）框架，专门用于合成高度逼真的失语症语音。与最先进的TTS系统相比，AphaVoice在捕捉语言不流畅性的临床特征方面表现出卓越的能力，在时间指标上优于现有模型，同时始终保持说话人身份。通过利用潜在空间移位，该模型还支持多说话人生成，而不会牺牲语音的真实性。最终，AphaVoice为与失语症相关的医疗培训和临床模拟提供了一个可扩展、高保真的工具。
AI.summary: AphaVoice是一个新颖的文本到语音（TTS）框架，旨在生成高度逼真的失语症患者语音，以解决医疗培训和临床模拟中对可靠模拟的需求。该模型在捕捉语言不流畅性方面优于现有技术，并在保持说话人身份的同时支持多说话人生成。
AI.keywords: 失语症, 文本到语音, 语音合成, 语言不流畅性, 医疗模拟
AI.comments: 该研究成功开发了一个专门用于模拟失语症患者语音的TTS框架，解决了现有研究的空白。其在捕捉语言不流畅性和支持多说话人生成方面的能力使其成为医疗培训的宝贵工具。然而，该模型在不同类型的失语症患者中的泛化能力以及对语音真实性的长期感知评估有待进一步研究。

title: Optimize Once, Execute Fast: Latency-Aware Multi-Agent Workflow Learning for Recurrent Queries
summary: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-based MAS) have shown remarkable success in solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents through multi-step workflows. To overcome the high cost and specificity of manually designed workflows, recent research has shifted toward learning them automatically. However, a key limitation remains: while agent calls introduce significant latency due to model inference time and service congestion, most automated methods optimize solely for downstream performance, ignoring execution time (makespan). This issue is amplified when workflows are reused across recurring queries, making latency accumulate over time. This limits deployment in recurrent applications such as AI customer support and AI cloud troubleshooting, where users expect fast responses. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new problem, termed latency-aware workflow generation, where the objective is to minimize workflow makespan while aiming to retain downstream performance. We propose LAWA (Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion), a novel framework that reduces makespan via theoretically grounded graph edits targeting critical-path bottlenecks. By unifying a graph generator with this graph-editing procedure, LAWA supports both de novo workflow generation and refinement of existing ones. Empirical results across seven benchmarks demonstrate that LAWA significantly reduces makespan while achieving competitive task performance, supporting efficient reuse of multi-agent workflows for recurrent queries.

AI.title_translation: 为递归查询优化一次、快速执行：延迟感知多代理工作流学习
AI.tldr: 现有的LLM多代理系统（MAS）工作流学习方法通常只关注下游性能，忽略了代理调用带来的延迟，这在递归查询场景下尤为严重。本文提出了LAWA（Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion）框架，通过图编辑方法识别和优化关键路径瓶颈，以最小化工作流执行时间（makespan），同时保持下游性能。实验表明，LAWA能显著降低延迟，并支持现有工作流的精炼和新工作流的从头生成。
AI.motivation: 现有的LLM多代理系统工作流学习方法主要关注下游性能，忽略了代理调用带来的显著延迟，尤其是在用户期望快速响应的递归查询场景下，这种延迟累积会严重影响用户体验。
AI.method: 提出LAWA（Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion）框架，通过理论指导的图编辑方法来识别和优化关键路径瓶颈，从而减少工作流的执行时间（makespan），并结合图生成器以支持从头生成和优化现有工作流。
AI.result: 在七个基准测试中的实验表明，LAWA能够显著降低工作流的执行时间（makespan），同时保持具有竞争力的任务性能。
AI.conclusion: LAWA框架能够有效地生成或优化多代理工作流，显著降低执行延迟，同时保持任务性能，特别适用于递归查询场景，解决了现有方法在延迟优化方面的不足。
AI.translation: 基于大型语言模型的多代理系统（LLM-based MAS）通过协调专门的代理并进行多步工作流，在解决复杂任务方面取得了显著的成功。为了克服手动设计工作流的高成本和特异性，最近的研究已转向自动学习工作流。然而，一个关键的限制仍然存在：由于模型推理时间和网络拥堵，代理调用会带来显著的延迟，而大多数自动化方法仅优化下游性能，忽略了执行时间（makespan）。当工作流在递归查询中被重复使用时，这个问题会被放大，导致延迟随时间累积。这限制了其在需要快速响应的递归应用中的部署，例如AI客户支持和AI云故障排除。为了弥合这一差距，我们提出了一个新问题，即延迟感知工作流生成，其目标是在保持下游性能的同时最小化工作流的makespan。我们提出了LAWA（Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion），一个新颖的框架，通过针对关键路径瓶颈的理论指导的图编辑来减少makespan。通过将图生成器与此图编辑过程相结合，LAWA支持从头生成工作流和精炼现有工作流。跨越七个基准的实证结果表明，LAWA显著降低了makespan，同时实现了具有竞争力的任务性能，支持多代理工作流在递归查询中的高效重用。
AI.summary: 本文针对LLM多代理系统（MAS）在处理递归查询时面临的工作流延迟问题，提出了LAWA框架。LAWA通过识别和优化关键路径瓶颈来最小化工作流执行时间（makespan），同时保持任务性能，解决了现有方法仅关注下游性能而忽略延迟的局限性。
AI.keywords: LLM多代理系统,工作流学习,延迟优化,makespan,递归查询
AI.comments: 该研究解决了LLM多代理系统在实际应用中，尤其是在需要快速响应的递归查询场景下的关键痛点——工作流执行延迟。通过提出延迟感知工作流生成问题和LAWA框架，该方法不仅在理论上进行了创新（图编辑优化关键路径），而且在实践中也显示出显著的优势（降低makespan同时保持性能）。然而，对于LAWA在处理极其复杂或大规模工作流时的可扩展性，以及在不同硬件和网络条件下的鲁棒性，可能还需要进一步的评估。

title: From Field to Planning: Learning Temporal Polar Gradient Fields for Vision-based AAV Trajectory Planning in Dynamic Environments
summary: Autonomous Aerial Vehicle (AAV) trajectory planning requires real-time and accurate safety gradient guidance, especially in dynamic environments. Existing methods typically rely on static maps and dynamic obstacle tracking to construct gradient fields, imposing heavy computational burdens and yielding conservative trajectories. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage Field-to-Planning (F2P) learning framework to provide accurate and efficient safety gradients for trajectory planning in dynamic environments. In the first stage, we introduce an Ego-centric Polar Occupancy (EPO) representation that naturally matches the geometry of the onboard camera frustum, while supporting unstructured scene modeling. Subsequently, we formulate a Temporal Polar Gradient Field (TPGF) via multi-kernel separable Gaussian convolution to provide unified safety gradients, without explicitly distinguishing between static and dynamic obstacles. To mitigate the inherent spatial ambiguity introduced by applying convolutions within the polar grid, we propose an ESDF-guided offline learning strategy that incorporates geometric priors into TPGF. In the second stage, we employ the calibrated TPGF to guide the trajectory planning policy in a self-supervised learning manner. Comparative results with other approaches demonstrate the superiority of our method. Extensive real-world experiments within various cluttered dynamic environments validate the real-time performance and robustness on resource-constrained onboard systems.

AI.title_translation: 从场地到规划：为动态环境中的视觉自主飞行器轨迹规划学习时序极坐标梯度场
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为F2P的两阶段学习框架，用于在动态环境中为自主飞行器（AAV）规划轨迹。该框架使用一种新的“以自身为中心的极坐标占用”（EPO）表示法和“时序极坐标梯度场”（TPGF）来计算安全梯度，无需区分静态和动态障碍物。通过引导式离线学习解决了极坐标卷积的空间模糊性问题。在第二阶段，TPGF用于指导轨迹规划策略。实验证明该方法在实时性和鲁棒性方面优于现有方法。
AI.motivation: 现有自主飞行器（AAV）轨迹规划方法在动态环境中需要实时准确的安全梯度，但通常依赖于静态地图和动态障碍物跟踪，计算负担重且轨迹保守。
AI.method: 提出一个两阶段的“场地到规划”（F2P）学习框架。第一阶段：引入“以自身为中心的极坐标占用”（EPO）表示法，并使用多核可分高斯卷积构建“时序极坐标梯度场”（TPGF），以提供统一的安全梯度。通过“ESDF引导的离线学习策略”来解决极坐标卷积的空间模糊性。第二阶段：使用校准后的TPGF以自监督学习方式指导轨迹规划策略。
AI.result: 与现有方法相比，该方法在轨迹规划方面表现出优越性。在各种复杂的动态环境中进行的真实世界实验验证了其在资源受限的机载系统上的实时性能和鲁棒性。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的F2P框架通过EPO表示和TPGF，能够为动态环境中的AAV轨迹规划提供高效且准确的安全梯度，并在真实世界实验中证明了其优越的实时性能和鲁棒性。
AI.translation: 自主飞行器（AAV）轨迹规划需要实时且准确的安全梯度引导，尤其是在动态环境中。现有方法通常依赖于静态地图和动态障碍物跟踪来构建梯度场，这会带来沉重的计算负担并产生保守的轨迹。为了解决这些限制，我们提出了一个两阶段的“场地到规划”（F2P）学习框架，为动态环境中的轨迹规划提供准确且高效的安全梯度。在第一阶段，我们引入了一种“以自身为中心的极坐标占用”（EPO）表示法，该表示法自然地匹配了机载摄像头视锥的几何形状，同时支持非结构化场景建模。随后，我们通过多核可分高斯卷积构建了一个“时序极坐标梯度场”（TPGF），用于提供统一的安全梯度，而无需明确区分静态和动态障碍物。为了减轻在极坐标网格内应用卷积所引入的空间模糊性，我们提出了一种“ESDF引导的离线学习策略”，将几何先验知识融入TPGF。在第二阶段，我们采用校准后的TPGF以自监督学习的方式指导轨迹规划策略。与其他方法的比较结果证明了我们方法的优越性。在各种复杂的动态环境中的大量真实世界实验验证了其在资源受限的机载系统上的实时性能和鲁棒性。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为F2P的两阶段学习框架，用于解决自主飞行器（AAV）在动态环境中的轨迹规划问题。该框架通过引入新的“以自身为中心的极坐标占用”（EPO）表示法和“时序极坐标梯度场”（TPGF）来克服现有方法的计算负担和保守性问题。TPGF能够统一处理静态和动态障碍物，并通过ESDF引导的离线学习策略解决了极坐标表示中的空间模糊性。实验结果表明，F2P框架在实时性、准确性和鲁棒性方面均优于现有方法，并成功应用于资源受限的机载系统。
AI.keywords: 自主飞行器, 轨迹规划, 动态环境, 极坐标梯度场, 学习框架, 安全梯度
AI.comments: 该研究提出的F2P框架在处理动态环境下的AAV轨迹规划方面取得了显著进展。EPO表示法与相机视锥的几何匹配以及TPGF对静态和动态障碍物的统一处理是其核心创新点。ESDF引导的离线学习策略有效地解决了极坐标表示的固有挑战。然而，该方法在复杂场景下的泛化能力以及对不同传感器输入的适应性仍有待进一步探索。模型的计算效率和实时性在资源受限的系统上得到了验证，但其在大规模或更高维度环境下的扩展性也值得关注。

title: TurboProm: Low Cost and High Performance Metrics Observability at Scale
summary:
Many large enterprise and cloud deployments rely on metrics observability solutions (e.g., Prometheus) to monitor key performance indicators of system health (e.g., CPU, memory, network, app-level statistics). Monitoring and analyzing these metrics presents a significant challenge in terms of cost-latency tradeoffs at scale. Ideally, system operators would like immediately deployable and backwards compatible solutions to improve the cost-latency tradeoffs without significant impact on the fidelity of their observability applications. Unfortunately, existing solutions including state-of-art timeseries databases and custom approximate querying solutions fail on one or more aspects.
  In this paper, we present the design and implementation of TurboProm, a backwards-compatible drop-in accelerator for metrics observability deployments. TurboProm recasts metrics analytics tasks using a semantic-preserving summary view rather than classical query-centric view. Instead of estimating query results on raw timeseries metrics data, TurboProm uses semantic-preserving summaries that enable high-fidelity analytics with significant cost-latency improvements. We present a practical implementation of TurboProm that can be retrofitted to any existing observability deployment. We evaluate TurboProm on diverse real and synthetic workloads against state-of-art solutions and show that it can provide significant reduction in query latency and cost. TurboProm is open-source at https://github.com/ProjectASAP/ASAPQuery.

AI.title_translation: TurboProm：大规模低成本高性能指标可观测性
AI.tldr: TurboProm是一个向后兼容的、即插即用的指标可观测性解决方案，它通过使用语义保留的摘要视图而不是传统的以查询为中心的视图来重构指标分析任务，从而在降低成本和延迟的同时保持高保真度。
AI.motivation: 在规模化部署中，现有指标可观测性解决方案在成本和延迟之间存在权衡，而现有解决方案（包括最先进的时间序列数据库和自定义近似查询解决方案）未能全面解决这些问题。
AI.method: TurboProm通过使用语义保留的摘要视图来重构指标分析任务，而不是传统的以查询为中心的视图。它不是在原始时间序列指标数据上估算查询结果，而是使用语义保留的摘要，从而实现高保真度分析，并显著改善成本和延迟。
AI.result: 与最先进的解决方案相比，TurboProm在实际和合成工作负载上显示出显著降低查询延迟和成本的能力。
AI.conclusion: TurboProm通过使用语义保留的摘要视图，在不影响可观测性应用保真度的情况下，为指标可观测性部署提供了显著的成本和延迟改进，并且可以向后兼容地集成到现有部署中。
AI.translation:
许多大型企业和云部署依赖指标可观测性解决方案（例如 Prometheus）来监控系统健康状况的关键性能指标（例如 CPU、内存、网络、应用程序级别统计信息）。大规模监控和分析这些指标在成本-延迟权衡方面带来了重大挑战。理想情况下，系统操作员希望有可立即部署且向后兼容的解决方案，以在不显著影响可观测性应用程序保真度的情况下，改善成本-延迟权衡。不幸的是，现有解决方案，包括最先进的时间序列数据库和自定义近似查询解决方案，在某一方面或多个方面都失败了。
  在本文中，我们提出了 TurboProm 的设计和实现，这是一个向后兼容的、即插即用的指标可观测性部署加速器。TurboProm 使用语义保留的摘要视图而不是传统的以查询为中心的视图来重构指标分析任务。TurboProm 不是在原始时间序列指标数据上估算查询结果，而是使用语义保留的摘要，从而实现高保真度分析，并显著改善成本和延迟。我们提出了 TurboProm 的实际实现，它可以向后兼容地集成到任何现有的可观测性部署中。我们在实际和合成工作负载上对 TurboProm 与最先进的解决方案进行了评估，结果表明它可以显著降低查询延迟和成本。TurboProm 是开源的，网址为 https://github.com/ProjectASAP/ASAPQuery。
AI.summary: TurboProm 是一种创新的、向后兼容的即插即用解决方案，旨在解决大规模指标可观测性中的成本-延迟挑战。它通过使用语义保留的摘要视图来替代传统的查询中心方法，从而在不牺牲数据保真度的情况下，显著提高查询性能并降低成本。
AI.keywords: 指标可观测性,成本优化,延迟降低,TurboProm,摘要视图
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种非常有前景的解决方案，以应对大规模可观测性数据处理中的关键挑战。TurboProm 的核心创新在于其从查询中心方法转向语义保留的摘要视图，这在理论上和实践中都具有显著的优势。向后兼容性和即插即用的设计进一步增加了其实用性，使其能够轻松集成到现有系统中。然而，论文可能需要进一步探讨在某些特定场景下，摘要视图可能带来的潜在信息损失，以及在构建和维护这些摘要时的额外开销。总体而言，这是一个重要且具有影响力的研究。

title: AlignPoison: Conditional Targeted Poisoning of Generative Recommenders via Decoding-Aligned Prefixes
summary: Generative recommendation models based on autoregressive decoding have been adopted as alternatives to classical ranking-based systems. While their modeling flexibility has been widely studied, their resilience to data poisoning remains largely unexplored. In this work, we ask: how susceptible are generative recommenders to conditional targeted poisoning? Under a realistic setting where an adversary can inject limited malicious interactions and query a recommendation API as a black box, our empirical study shows that generative recommenders are vulnerable: injecting fewer than 1% synthetic interactions significantly increases the likelihood of promoting malicious targets under the trigger. To characterize this vulnerability, we analyze the synthesis of malicious interactions from two perspectives: (i) decoding alignment and (ii) prefix popularity. We observe that short, context-aligned prefixes that are both common under the model's induced transition dynamics and strongly linked to a frequent trigger consistently amplify targeted promotion. Motivated by this analysis, we develop AlignPoison, a black-box framework that discovers and samples context-aligned prefixes from API outputs. We conduct experiments on benchmarks in unimodal and multimodal generative recommendation settings. Results show that these prefixes outperform competitive baselines, improving ASR lift by up to 16.3 percentage points and highlighting a decoding-dependent, context-sensitive poisoning vulnerability in generative recommendation models.

AI.title_translation: 生成式推荐器的条件定向投毒：通过解码对齐前缀
AI.tldr: 生成式推荐模型容易受到定向数据投毒攻击，攻击者可以利用解码对齐和前缀流行度来操纵推荐结果，即使只注入少量恶意数据。AlignPoison框架利用API输出来发现和采样这些有问题的上下文对齐前缀，并在实验中证明了其有效性。
AI.motivation: 研究生成式推荐模型在现实世界的定向数据投毒攻击下的脆弱性，特别是攻击者可以通过API查询进行有限的恶意交互注入。
AI.method: 分析了恶意交互的两个方面：解码对齐和前缀流行度。开发了一个名为AlignPoison的黑盒框架，该框架从API输出来发现和采样上下文对齐的前缀，以实现有针对性的投毒。
AI.result: 在单模态和多模态生成式推荐设置的基准测试中，AlignPoison框架发现的上下文对齐前缀比竞争性基线表现更好，将ASR提升了高达16.3个百分点，揭示了生成式推荐模型中一种依赖于解码、对上下文敏感的投毒漏洞。
AI.conclusion: 生成式推荐模型容易受到定向数据投毒攻击，攻击者可以利用解码对齐和前缀流行度来操纵推荐结果，即使只注入少量恶意数据。AlignPoison框架能够有效地利用这些漏洞。
AI.translation: 基于自回归解码的生成推荐模型已被用作经典排序系统的替代方案。虽然它们的建模灵活性已被广泛研究，但它们对数据投毒的抵抗力在很大程度上仍未被探索。在这项工作中，我们问：生成式推荐器在多大程度上容易受到条件定向投毒的影响？在现实场景中，攻击者可以注入有限的恶意交互并通过黑盒查询推荐API，我们的实证研究表明，生成式推荐器是脆弱的：注入少于1%的合成交互会显著增加在触发条件下推广恶意目标的可能性。为了表征这种脆弱性，我们从两个角度分析了恶意交互的合成：(i)解码对齐和(ii)前缀流行度。我们观察到，在模型的诱导转移动力学下普遍存在、并且与常见触发器密切相关的短的、与上下文对齐的前缀，能够持续地放大定向推广。受此分析的启发，我们开发了AlignPoison，一个黑盒框架，它从API输出来发现和采样与上下文对齐的前缀。我们在单模态和多模态生成式推荐设置的基准上进行了实验。结果表明，这些前缀的表现优于竞争性基线，将ASR提升了高达16.3个百分点，并突出了生成式推荐模型中一种依赖于解码、对上下文敏感的投毒漏洞。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了生成式推荐模型在面对定向数据投毒攻击时的脆弱性。研究人员发现，攻击者可以通过注入少量（少于1%）的合成交互，利用“解码对齐”和“前缀流行度”这两个关键因素来操纵模型，使其推广恶意目标。他们开发了一个名为AlignPoison的黑盒框架，该框架能够从模型API的输出来识别和利用这些上下文对齐的前缀，并在实验中证明了其有效性，显著提高了攻击成功率，揭示了生成式推荐模型中一种新颖的、依赖于解码过程的特定于上下文的投毒漏洞。
AI.keywords: 生成式推荐, 数据投毒, 解码对齐, 前缀流行度, AlignPoison
AI.comments: 这项研究首次揭示了生成式推荐模型在数据投毒方面的脆弱性，并提出了一个有效的攻击框架AlignPoison。研究分析了攻击的根源在于解码对齐和前缀流行度，为防御策略提供了理论基础。然而，该研究主要集中在黑盒攻击场景，未来可以进一步探索白盒场景下的攻击和防御。

title: Names Are Not Objects: Object-Bound Confinement for Compromised AI Coding Agents
comments: 21 pages, 4 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/dcommey/ztac
summary: Coding agents read repositories and web pages that anyone can write, and then act with their user's authority. Prompt-injection defenses make it less likely that the model is steered but do not prevent it, so the system around the model must contain an agent that is already compromised. Many exploits against deployed coding agents share one cause: a check approves a name, such as a path, an argument vector, or a directory, and a later step maps that name to a different object: the file behind a symlink, the behavior an option selects, or a repository that git discovers on its own. We present Zero-Trust Agent Cells (ZTAC). A cell runs the agent in a kernel sandbox whose only route to files, programs, and the network is a socket to a broker. The broker resolves each request to the object it will act on, decides on that object, and checks at use that it is acting on the object it authorized. Programs that the broker starts run in a sandbox compiled from the same policy, and approvals are bound to the resolved object and can be used once. Our macOS prototype has 3.2k lines of trusted Rust code, excluding dependencies. We evaluate it against 74 attacks with ground-truth oracles, including replays of 10 publicly disclosed incidents. A tool allowlist loses 66 of them, and an allowlist combined with the kind of command sandbox that deployed agents use loses 56. ZTAC loses 2, both of which encode a secret into traffic to an allowed endpoint, and holds 14 for review. It completes 43 of 46 benign operations, with 8 approval prompts, and 4 of 7 workflows. A no-op brokered request has a median latency of 4.0 ms, and the spawned programs we measured take 8.5 ms to 18.4 ms longer than without ZTAC.
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/dcommey/ztac

title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment
summary: Reusable wearable PPG representations should capture local pulse morphology and broader physiological regularities. Existing pretraining objectives, however, usually apply supervision at the recording or pair level, overlooking that different concepts become reliable over different scopes of waveform evidence. We propose HiPPT, a physiology-grounded framework that matches each supervision source to its appropriate evidence scope. We construct a PPG-Text corpus of over 4 million wrist-worn recordings from 202K users, pairing recordings with waveform-derived morphology and metadata-derived context descriptions. HiPPT combines record-level morphology alignment, which grounds individual recordings in pulse characteristics, with cross-recording context alignment, which aggregates recordings sharing the same metadata tuple to capture context-consistent regularities. Waveform-guided text modeling further recovers masked contextual concepts from PPG patch representations, providing fine-grained waveform-text supervision. Across six downstream tasks spanning blood pressure, vascular stiffness, physiological attributes, and cross-dataset heart-rate estimation, HiPPT achieves the best result on the primary linear-probing metrics. The aligned space also supports zero-shot profiling of age group, sex, and BMI category, individually and jointly, with performance improving as more recordings are aggregated. These results show that evidence-scope matching yields transferable and semantically accessible wearable PPG representations. Code and pretrained weights will be released.

title: Multi-modal Representation Fusion for Long-term Microsurgical Anastomosis Trajectory Anticipation
summary: Microsurgical anastomosis is one of the most challenging and sophisticated procedures for surgical robotics, requiring accurate manipulation of surgical instruments within a limited space to achieve precise operations. Accurate surgical trajectory anticipation is essential for surgical scene understanding, intraoperative planning, robotic manipulation, and reliable behaviour analysis. However, existing approaches mainly focus on features extracted from surgical videos and historical trajectories, while overlooking rich semantic and motion information that can provide more discriminative multi-modal representations for complex surgical instrument-tissue interactions. In this work, we propose a cross-modal feature fusion framework for long-term 2D and 3D microsurgical anastomosis trajectory anticipation. The proposed framework consists of a multi-modal representation extractor and a cross-modal feature fusion network. Semantic recognition of surgical objects and consecutive motion estimation are incorporated as multi-modal visual cues, providing complementary spatial and temporal guidance for instrument-tissue interaction characterization. A coarse-to-fine progressive fusion strategy with a long-short-term memory mechanism is introduced to capture temporal dependencies step by step. The training and evaluation are conducted on our established robotic platform and a comprehensive dataset containing both phantom and ex-vivo surgical scenarios is constructed. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing methods and exhibits improved robustness across different surgical scenes, highlighting its potential for both intelligent robot-assisted and autonomous surgical systems.

title: A Gated Catchment Hydrology Model (GCHM) for Physically-Interpretable Rainfall-Evapotranspiration-Runoff Simulation Across Diverse Hydroclimatic Regimes
summary:
Recent advances in machine learning have improved rainfall-runoff prediction, yet most data-driven models remain difficult to interpret and do not explicitly enforce physical conservation laws. We present the Gated Catchment Hydrology Model (GCHM), a mass-conserving architecture based on the Mass-Conserving Perceptron (MCP). GCHM uses five storage states representing canopy interception, snow, soil moisture, groundwater, and streamflow generation. Constrained gates govern precipitation partitioning, evapotranspiration, infiltration, seepage, runoff, and baseflow while learning context-dependent process relationships.
  We evaluate GCHM across 50 CAMELS catchments spanning snowmelt-dominated, recent-rainfall, historical-rainfall, and arid regimes, using NOAA AORC meteorological forcing and remotely sensed vegetation and land-surface data. Performance is assessed using the Jawad-Kling-Gupta Efficiency (JKGE) metric, which accounts for stationary and non-stationary hydrologic behavior. We compare the full architecture with ablated variants and recurrent neural network benchmarks.
  GCHM reproduces streamflow dynamics across diverse hydroclimatic regimes, including arid catchments, while maintaining interpretable states and fluxes. Ablation experiments show that simplified architectures may perform adequately under wet conditions but struggle to represent flow persistence and recession during dry periods, when groundwater storage sustains low flows. Learned gates recover hydrologically plausible relationships governing snowmelt, runoff, seepage, and evapotranspiration. GCHM combines competitive predictive performance with mass conservation and interpretability, providing a foundation for hydrologic modeling and counterfactual analysis.

title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
comments: 19 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Code, rules, lessons, data and evolve reports: https://github.com/agentic-loops-x/Reels-RSI
summary: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. A program can be read, diffed, tested and audited; pixels can only be watched. Reels-RSI is an open-source reel director for any agent harness; its self-improvement happens at the program level rather than in weights or prompts. Every revision pass is logged with a code snapshot; a retrospective pairs each check finding with the diff that fixed it and proposes lessons; a lesson that a static check can catch is compiled into a rule with a must-fail and a must-pass example, so the memory is unit-tested; and a rule learned today runs over everything made before it. A bounded, benchmark-gated step lets an agent rewrite the director's playbook, kept only when blind pairwise judgments on held-out topics prefer it; nothing enters memory without a human decision. Across 111 reels -- a field study, two playbook evolutions, a 2x2 memory ablation, a weaker director, a 48-reel learning curve and a judge-reliability study -- we find that the rule learned in the field caught four latent defects in frames authored before it existed and none after; that rules are an audit for a strong director (eight unguarded reels, no violation) and a guard for a weaker one (thirty violations unguarded versus five); that lessons shorten revision loops but do not compound or move the judge; and that the first rewrite's 11--1 verdict was a position bias in our vote design (judges pick the second-shown reel 62--81% of the time), masking scripts that traded thirteen facts for craft. We document four failure modes of the preference signal, which check caught each, and the fixes. Code, rules, lessons and data are public.
comment: 19 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Code, rules, lessons, data and evolve reports: https://github.com/agentic-loops-x/Reels-RSI

title: DEFT: Disentanglement-Enhanced Fine-Tuning for EEG Foundation Models
summary: EEG foundation models (EFMs) have improved EEG representation learning by transferring knowledge from large-scale multi-subject pretraining to downstream tasks. However, their pretrained embeddings often retain substantial subject-related variation, placing an additional burden on the downstream classifier, especially in cross-subject settings. To address this issue, we propose Disentangled EFM Fine-Tuning (DEFT), a plug-and-play adapter for EFM fine-tuning. DEFT encourages branch disentanglement of pretrained tokens into task-oriented content and subject-consistent style, then performs downstream prediction from the content branch. It instantiates this factorize-before-classify design with recursive Gaussian refinement, temporal-variance regularization, subject-aware contrastive learning, and reconstruction. Experiments across multiple EEG datasets and four EFM backbones show that DEFT improves matched fine-tuning baselines. Further ablations and analyses support the intended content/style branch organization.

title: DSR-Net: Learning Dynamic Skeletal Relations for 3D Human Pose Estimation
summary: 3D human pose estimation requires accurate modeling of motion-dependent skeletal structures and inter-joint dependencies. Existing methods typically rely on fixed skeletal topologies in Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) or implicitly capture joint relations through attention mechanisms, limiting their adaptability to diverse motion patterns. To address this issue,we proposeDSR-Net, a dynamic structural representation learning framework for 3D human pose estimation. Specifically, a Dynamic Skeletal Relation (DSR) module is introduced to learn adaptive inter-joint dependencies beyond predefined skeletal connections. Based on the learned relations, a hierarchical relation-aware fusion strategy is developed to facilitate effective interaction between structural and temporal representations. In addition, a lightweight Residual Skeletal Recalibration Module (RSRM) is designed to enhance the stability of structure-aware features with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP demonstrate that DSR-Net achieves MPJPEs of 37.9 mm and 14.9 mm, respectively, consistently improving over strong baselines. The results validate the effectiveness of dynamic skeletal relation modeling for robust 3D human pose estimation.

title: Rethinking Activation Functions: Reducing Bias Can Improve Learning
summary: Many widely used activation functions, including ReLU, GELU, Swish, and Sigmoid, produce predominantly positive outputs, resulting in a nonzero post-activation mean that we term activation bias. Despite its ubiquity, the effect of activation bias on learning dynamics remains poorly understood. Using controlled models, we show that activation bias accelerates initial loss reduction but is accompanied by overshooting, non-smooth trajectories, and a steeper loss landscape. This early advantage also coincides with the model's use of task-relevant information encoded in the activation bias component. In contrast, reducing activation bias slows initial learning but ultimately yields a lower final loss. Experiments on larger vision and language models exhibit a similar pattern: smaller activation bias is associated with better late-stage performance. Thus, this seemingly minor property can substantially redirect learning and warrants explicit consideration in future activation function design.

title: Encrypted collision avoidance maneuver via variational optimization
comments: 15 pages, 1 figure, extended abstract submited to AAS/AIAA Space Flight Mechanics Meeting
summary: We propose an encrypted collision avoidance maneuver (CAM) design protocol using homomorphic encryption (HE) that enables operators to outsource CAM design to an untrusted server without revealing their private covariance. To this end, we reformulate the constrained CAM optimization as a sampling based estimation problem via a variational approach, so that the private covariance dependent terms can be efficiently evaluated under HE. The protocol requires only a single round of communication, and experiments on six real-world conjunction data messages demonstrate improved feasibility and reduced fuel consumption compared with CAMs designed using public covariance.
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, extended abstract submited to AAS/AIAA Space Flight Mechanics Meeting

title: MontageFlow: Physically Valid High Fidelity EEG Generation
summary: Generative modeling offers a promising solution to the scarcity of labeled clinical electroencephalography (EEG) data under strict privacy constraints. Although recent generative models report substantial improvements in generation fidelity, we show that these gains conceal a categorical failure. EEG is not an arbitrary multichannel signal: each channel records the voltage difference between two scalp electrodes. So, real recordings satisfy exact linear identities among their channels. Current generators invariably violate these identities, yet this has gone unnoticed. We therefore propose MontageFlow, a flow-matching model that enforces these identities by restricting its output to signals that satisfy them. We find that ensuring validity improves fidelity too. Furthermore, to retain the EEG characteristics that oversmoothing washes out, we also condition the model on a physiological state vector encoded from the whole EEG window. For generation, this vector is drawn from a prior fitted in latent space. Across 3 large-scale benchmarks, our model improves TS-FID by 1.6-3.6$\times$ over the closest rival while ensuring validity.

title: PAG-Agent: Zero-Shot Personalized Music Album Generation via Aesthetic Profile Distillation
summary: Large Music Models (LMMs) can synthesize high-fidelity audio and support increasingly flexible prompt control, yet modeling the subjective preferences of an individual listener remains underexplored. We present PAG-Agent, a zero-shot multimodal framework that uses an explicit Personal Aesthetic Profile to bridge user preference inference and music generation control. A multimodal LLM distills favorite-song audio and contextual user information into this structured representation, which a planning LLM translates into generation instructions for existing music synthesizers. We further introduce PA-Eval, which evaluates personalization through the Aesthetic Consistency Score (ACS) for target-user alignment and the Aesthetic Specificity Index (ASI) for cross-user specificity. Experiments with Personal-100 on multiple MLLM and music-generation backbones show consistent improvements over generic and direct conditioning. A 50-participant follow-up study further shows a correlation $r=0.64$ between ACS and subjective preference.

title: EVISTA: Unified Multimodal Video Search with Evidence-Aware Temporal Path Optimization
summary: In the era of big data, precise event retrieval from large video collections has become increasingly important and challenging. In particular, locating multiple events from the same video in their temporal order is difficult when different events are described by different types of evidence, such as visual content, on-screen text, and spoken words. We develop EVISTA, a unified multimodal video retrieval system for the Ho Chi Minh City AI Challenge 2026, which integrates visual-semantic, OCR, ASR, object, and metadata search over a shared keyframe index, and propose TEMPO-P, an evidence-aware temporal path optimization method for ordered multi-event retrieval. Building EVISTA for this task reveals two limitations of independent event retrieval: a relevant video may be missed when one event is weakly retrieved, and independently retrieved event candidates may be temporally inconsistent or unable to represent events defined primarily by text or speech. TEMPO-P addresses these limitations by aggregating candidate videos across events and modalities, jointly scoring keyframes using visual, OCR, and ASR evidence, and selecting a compact temporally ordered path within each video through dynamic programming. On five organizer queries and 36 additional multi-event queries, TEMPO-P matches visual-only temporal alignment on visually described events (R@1 0.42 for both) and retrieves queries containing text-defined events, which visual-only alignment cannot represent (R@1 0.38). TEMPO-P is integrated into EVISTA as its ordered-event retrieval mode.

title: Spatiotemporal Recognition of Abdominal Wall Layers During Optical Trocar Entry
summary: Objective. To evaluate whether spatial context and temporal modeling improve tissue recognition during optical trocar entry, where multiple abdominal-wall tissues may be visible simultaneously. Methods. We retrospectively analyzed 71 recordings with 1,516 annotated keyframes and 29,151 clinician-annotated sectors. Each frame was divided into 28 polar-grid sectors assigned to nine tissue classes. Color, neighboring-sector, and positional features were used by a gradient-boosted emission classifier. The full pipeline added learned temporal smoothing, spatial regularization, an anatomically ordered hidden Markov model, and posterior blending. Five-fold cross-validation was grouped by recording, with cross-fitting to prevent within-recording leakage. Primary evaluation used clinician-derived targets; ablations assessed classification, probability quality, spatial consistency, and peritoneum-or-deeper onset timing. Results. The complete pipeline achieved accuracy 0.646, macro-F1 0.507, and macro-AUROC 0.882, versus 0.600, 0.440, and 0.861 for emissions alone. Macro-F1 improved by 0.066 across all five folds. Label changes decreased from 66.2 to 19.5 per sector-minute, and median onset error decreased from 15.58 to 2.45 seconds. Frames with a tissue-depth-code span of at least three decreased from 53% to 26%, versus 22% for clinician annotations. Performance remained limited for preperitoneal fat and bowel, and the full model retained a 44% premature-onset proportion. Conclusions. Combining appearance, spatial context, and temporal constraints improved retrospective tissue recognition and onset localization. Tissue-specific limitations, residual timing errors, and reliance on future observations warrant external validation and prospective evaluation of causal models before clinical use.

title: TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities
summary: Robotic platforms combine multi-modal sensors to operate across diverse conditions, but most dense correspondence methods are limited to RGB-RGB or a small set of modality pairs. Training a model for each modality pair scales poorly with the number of sensors and forgoes potential positive transfer across modality pairs. We introduce TartanMatch, a unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered pairs among RGB, event, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR. TartanMatch adapts an RGB-pretrained correspondence model to all modality pairs within one shared network using lightweight modality adaptation and a mixture of real and synthetic data. On zero-shot real-world benchmarks, TartanMatch reduces Endpoint Error (EPE) over the strongest baselines by 61.9% for cross-modal matching and 49.6% for same-modal matching. We further show that joint training across all modality pairs improves average matching accuracy over pair-specific training, especially on challenging cross-modal pairs. These results demonstrate that a single model achieves broad multi-modal coverage and state-of-the-art matching accuracy.

title: Compositional Concepts Erasing: Disentangling Object-Style via Domain Manifold Unlearning
summary: Diffusion models pose significant risks regarding the generation of illicit content and copyright violations. This has catalyzed the development of machine unlearning to erase harmful concepts or copyrighted styles from a model's generative repertoire without compromising its general performance. However, previous unlearning approaches on diffusion models have largely focused on either object-level or style-level removal and failed to address the challenge of object-style combination unlearning. At the same time, multiple unlearning requests often lead to catastrophic forgetting. To address these challenges, we propose Domain Manifold Unlearning (DMU), which uses an EMA-updated feature proxy extracted from intermediate diffusion features to represent the retained target-object direction. As a lightweight estimating representation of an object, DMU enables selective unlearning of domain-specific components in a specific object while preserving other semantic representations, thereby significantly enhancing robustness in multiple combination unlearning scenarios. Extensive experiments show that DMU significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods of batch unlearning and sequential unlearning.

title: SEPM: Self-Evolving Procedural Memory Grounded in Task Graphs for Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: Long-horizon multi-agent collaboration requires memory that preserves both successful actions and the coordination structure underlying them. Existing memory systems support information sharing or procedural reuse, but often leave the evolution of shared procedures disconnected from the task dependencies and execution states of collaborating agents. This coupling also limits the direct transfer of procedural memory designed for individual agents to team settings. We propose Self-Evolving Procedural Memory (SEPM), a framework that uses task dependency graphs as a common representation for online coordination and procedural memory evolution. During execution, a lightweight shared blackboard records structured evidence alongside task dependencies, supporting the detection of goal, plan, and world-state divergence and evidence-based realignment. After execution, verified actions and dependencies are distilled into reusable procedures, while recurring failures inform warnings and constraints. The shared procedure pool evolves through creation, refinement, specialization, and retirement, guided by success and cost utility and constrained by evidence and safety requirements. Together, these mechanisms preserve the collaborative structure and applicability conditions needed to reuse experience across tasks. Evaluations on ALFWorld, WebArena, and OfficeBench under AutoGen and DyLAN show that SEPM achieves the highest task scores among the compared methods in all six benchmark settings. Under AutoGen, it improves task scores over the no-added-memory baseline by 29.85, 25.86, and 13.00 percentage points, respectively. The codebase is available at https://github.com/cookieApril/SEPM.

title: We Have Been Interpreting Diffusion Transformer Backbone Behaviors Wrong
summary: During a network forward call, diffusion backbones naturally produce many intermediate activations. If we evaluate each activation against an identical downstream benchmarking protocol, we can plot an inverted-U-shaped curve as the depth profile: the activation's performance goes up first and then down as we go into deeper layers. This is common knowledge in the diffusion model community, which inspires many applications including the widely-adopted REPA. However, the common interpretation of this depth profile may be inaccurate and incomplete: (i) The cause of this curve has long been treated as signal granularity changing from coarse to fine, but there has been little evidence in DiT backbones. (ii) The community has been mainly studying this phenomenon in a static way, without investigating how it changes across different training setups. In this work, we show a different mechanism picture for the profile, where the prediction target (e.g., $ε$, $u$, $x_0$) sits at the center. The semantically meaningful signal is only an intermediate by-product for predicting the target, while the prediction target is the real goal for the backbone. Furthermore, the choice of prediction targets as part of the training setup can predictably affect the curve's shape. With this updated interpretation, many applications of this depth profile can be better grounded and predicted. As an example, we show how to predict the near-optimal placement of REPA based on the prediction target of the training setup. The code is at https://github.com/Darkbblue/dit-compare.

title: Query-Adaptive Neuron Steering for LLMs
summary: Effectively eliciting the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) at inference time remains an important challenge. Existing studies address this challenge through context engineering, which shapes user queries, or fixed steering, which directly intervenes in model computation. However, predefined contexts and fixed intervention strategies may not adequately accommodate the diverse knowledge and reasoning requirements of individual queries. This raises a natural question: Can internal steering in LLMs be made query-adaptive? In this work, we investigate whether query-induced internal activations can guide adaptive steering in LLMs. Our pilot studies reveal subject- and layer-dependent neuron activation patterns and show that amplifying subject-relevant neurons can improve model performance. Based on these findings, we propose Q-NeuS, a query-adaptive neuron steering framework that dynamically determines which neurons to modulate and by how much for each input. Specifically, Q-NeuS constructs a compact subject-guided candidate neuron space and employs a lightweight Query-Adaptive Gate to generate neuron-wise modulation coefficients. To learn effective intervention strategies, we introduce Neu-GRPO, which adapts group-relative optimization to train the Query-Adaptive Gate using the relative performance of multiple neuron intervention configurations. The base LLM remains frozen throughout training and inference, and no task or subject labels are required at inference time. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that Q-NeuS consistently improves model performance and exhibits broad applicability across model scales and strong cross-benchmark transferability.

title: Safety-Critical Quadrotor Navigation Using Fourth-Order Control Barrier Functions with Full Nonlinear Quadrotor Dynamics
summary: Safety-critical quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments typically relies on hierarchical architectures in which a high-level safety filter modifies position references that are then tracked by a separate attitude controller. However, this separation can create a mismatch between translational safety objectives and attitude evolution. To address this gap, we propose a safety controller based on fourth-order control barrier functions (CBFs) that explicitly incorporates the full nonlinear quadrotor dynamics, including attitude dynamics and torque-level actuation. Furthermore, we apply the integral high-order CBF technique to resolve the mixed-relative degree issue in the derived constraint formulation. The resulting formulation enforces obstacle-avoidance constraints while optimizing control torques, granting the safety layer direct authority over attitude behavior and eliminating the hierarchical disconnect inherent in reference-tracking safety filters. We validate the approaches in both high-fidelity simulation and real-world flight experiments, demonstrating reliable constraint satisfaction and successful obstacle avoidance. These results suggest that torque-level high-order CBFs provide a practical pathway to provably safer quadrotor navigation under full rigid-body dynamics.

title: ScienceBuddy-PV: A Verifier-Governed Recursive Improvement Protocol for Panvascular Intervention Research
comments: 17 pages, 17 figures, 19 references. Public-data component audit; recursive improvement is specified as a protocol and not experimentally demonstrated
summary: ScienceBuddy-PV adapts the ScienceBuddy recursive-in-recursive design to panvascular intervention research through a structured evidence ledger, device-vessel ontology, abstention contract and retained failure bank. Recursive harness optimization and outer-loop model learning, including reinforcement learning, are specified but not executed. We audit a fixed component, rather than the complete agent system, using separate ARCADE syntax and stenosis tasks (1,000 training, 200 validation and 300 test images per task). A shared task-masked convolutional model was trained once per representation setting; its parameters and the heuristic support gate were then held fixed, with the stenosis threshold selected on validation data. On the locked test sets, syntax Dice was 0.475 (95% CI 0.459-0.490) and stenosis Dice was 0.231 (95% CI 0.214-0.249). Stenosis pixel AUROC was 0.957 and AUPRC was 0.180 at prevalence 0.00975. The gate accepted 76.7% of stenosis-frame outputs versus 100% for a score-only comparator. In a constructed mask audit, it accepted 44.3% of reference candidates and rejected 55.7%, exposing the cost of abstention. Acceptance does not establish correctness or clinical safety. This public-data component audit makes support and abstention measurable and provides a reproducible protocol for future collaborative agent studies. It does not demonstrate recursive improvement, patient-level validity or clinical device recommendations.

title: Energy Ring: Stabilizing Feature Energy for Reliable Test-Time Discovery
summary: Test-Time Discovery (TTD) aims to recognize known classes and detect novel ones while the model is already deployed, operating directly on a continual unlabeled test-time stream. Existing TTD methods are overly conservative, making known and unknown features collapse together and difficult to separate during test-time adaptation. In this paper, we revisit TTD from an energy perspective and find that the natural energy gap between known and unknown classes is unstable and easily collapses. We therefore propose Energy Ring to stabilize this gap by anchoring the two types of classes on separate energy rings. A lightweight adapter enlarges the norm-based gap while preserving known-class directions, and a perturbation consistency module forms compact clusters for unknown classes. During testing, energy-guided confidence weighting improves prediction, and a stability-based rectification mechanism corrects unreliable updates. Experimental results show that Energy Ring significantly improves TTD performance against existing TTD methods.

title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation
summary: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. NeST-Bayes infers instantaneous trust evidence scores for robots and object hypotheses by reasoning over ego-centric relational graphs constructed from cross-robot observation consistency. These evidence scores are accumulated over time through Bayesian updates of Beta-distributed trust beliefs to maintain temporally consistent trust estimates. Extensive evaluations show that NeST-Bayes achieves the highest mean object precision and robot recall across all benchmark settings, and the highest robot precision and object recall in most settings, compared to trust-based methods. Under aggressive optimized attacks, it achieves 98.8\% robot precision with 93.8\% recall and 98.3\% object precision with 95.4\% recall. In an occlusion-rich Webots warehouse, it maintains 92.5\% robot precision with 92.0\% recall and 97.3\% object precision with 85.0\% recall. These results demonstrate joint improvements in the reliability and coverage of retained information.

title: LongHisDoc: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chinese Long Historical Document Understanding
summary: Chinese historical documents are invaluable cultural treasures, but their complexity poses significant comprehension challenges for non-specialists. Despite the success of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) in modern document tasks, their capabilities in Long (full-book) Historical Document understanding remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce LongHisDoc, the first benchmark tailored for long historical document understanding. LongHisDoc comprises 1,012 expert-annotated QA pairs derived from 101 PDF documents, with an average of 85.1 pages and 42,776.4 tokens per document. It spans 10 categories and features four QA types: single-page, cross-page, multi-hop, and unanswerable. Answering these questions requires integrating multimodal evidence from text, layout, and visual elements. Our evaluation reveals that the top-performing LVLM and LLM achieve only 62.9% and 69.9% accuracy, respectively, highlighting a substantial performance gap. Furthermore, we assess various modal retrievers and the end-to-end RAG performance to provide references for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. We believe that LongHisDoc serves as a comprehensive benchmark to catalyze future research in full-book historical document understanding. The benchmark and evaluation code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/qweq12433454/LongHisDoc and https://github.com/SCUT-DLVCLab/LongHisDoc.

title: GMM: Generalized OS Memory Management for Programmable XPUs
summary:
Since the AI boom, the fast evolving programmable XPU devices utilize high-bandwidth local memory to accelerate domain-specific tasks offloaded from the host CPU, resulting in a proliferation of XPU memory management systems implemented in proprietary drivers. However, existing OS core memory management (MM) continues to lack a high-level software abstraction, excluding the XPUs from leveraging OS advanced memory features. The XPU manufacturers have to reimplement independent XPU MM drivers, exacerbating the fragmented XPU software ecosystem.
  This paper presents GMM, generalized memory management that provides unified MM subsystems for XPUs. By adding an explicit logical mapping abstraction, GMM 1) provides universal NUMA-aware memory API for XPUs; 2) allows ease of XPU MM delegation; 3) enables sharing of advanced XPU memory features. Lightweight XPU MM drivers are implemented for two representative XPU manufacturers, Nvidia and Huawei. Both GMM-based drivers obtain competitive performance compared with their vendor-supplied drivers. GMM also obtains up to 41% higher fault-driven page migration throughput. Two real-world industrial case studies are exercised, where GMM reduces XPU memory utilization by 10% with up to 22.6x faster inference serving switch latency.

title: A Stateful Research Information Infrastructure for Scientific Discovery
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied to an expanding range of scientific activities, including literature analysis, hypothesis generation, software development and automated experimentation. Yet these capabilities rely on a more fundamental condition: scientific information must remain identifiable and traceable across systems and over time. In practice, different versions of a work and their associated records and files are often scattered across services and local directories. This fragmentation forces researchers to identify and contextualize the same work repeatedly, disrupting continuity from discovery to interpretation and reuse. Here we present Gewu Insight, a research information infrastructure that addresses this discontinuity by organizing scientific works as persistent, stateful research objects. It unifies venue-, topic- and author-based discovery records through a shared paper identity. Within a local library, metadata, versioned resources and research context can then accumulate around the same work. These capabilities are integrated into an iterative workflow for scientist-led, AI-assisted research, allowing earlier interpretations to be revisited and refined. A bounded evaluation showed high candidate precision across the three discovery modes, with paper identity, resource distinctions and research state preserved in controlled workflows. By making continuity an explicit property of research infrastructure, Gewu Insight can serve as an inspectable scientific memory layer shared by researchers and AI assistants, supporting human judgment and providing a foundation for future, more epistemically grounded scientific AI.

title: FDE-Bench: Evaluating End-to-End Delivery from Underspecified Real-World Business Requests
summary: Real-world business requests often leave key requirements unstated because frontline practitioners struggle to articulate rules they know from experience. Forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must elicit these requirements through dialogue and iteratively optimize solutions until they meet customer acceptance criteria. Existing optimization benchmarks typically start from explicit objectives, while clarification benchmarks often introduce information gaps into existing tasks. We introduce FDE-Bench, the first benchmark built from real customer projects to evaluate agents on end-to-end delivery tasks that require interactive requirement clarification and iterative optimization. Its 49 cases span combinatorial optimization and machine learning. Clarification targets are distilled from discussions between frontline practitioners and FDEs. Agents elicit missing requirements from a simulated customer, and case-specific evaluators assess final artifacts against acceptance criteria using customer-accepted FDE solutions as quality references. Across 18 agent configurations, the highest mean delivery score is only 0.5510, compared with an FDE reference of 1.0. The highest delivery success rate (DSR), defined as the fraction of planned runs reaching this reference, is only 6.12%. These results show that reliable FDE-level end-to-end delivery remains out of reach for the evaluated agents on underspecified real-world business tasks. The benchmark project page is available at https://baidubce.github.io/FM-Agent/FDE-Bench/.

title: GG-Nav: Goal-oriented Grounding Chain-of-Thought Elicits Reasoning in Navigation Foundation Models
summary: Emerging strong Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have advanced navigation foundation models. However, these models still have unsatisfactory performance on goal-oriented navigation settings. In this paper, we first conduct a motivating study revealing that the key issue lies in the insufficient utilization of streaming observations and imprecise target localization. To tackle these challenges, we propose GG-Nav, a simple yet effective navigation framework that learns a structured chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism via supervised fine-tuning to explicitly localize goal-relevant instances, accumulate grounding evidence, and support more reliable decision-making. Specifically, the structured CoT is designed with two key stages: (i) Observation-to-Evidence, which reasons over all intermediate frames between adjacent decision steps to retain useful goal-related evidence; and (ii) Evidence-to-Decision, which integrates the current observation with accumulated evidence to ground the target and support the generation of navigation actions or clarification questions. Extensive experiments show that GG-Nav outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of success rates on the HM3D ObjectNav, VL-LN, and CoIN benchmarks by 3.1%, 16.6%, and 5.3%, respectively. Ablation studies further show that accumulating evidence from intermediate observations reduces evidence-missing failures by 11.6%, while explicit grounding reduces stopping errors by 49.4%. We also deploy GG-Nav on a Unitree Go2 robot, demonstrating its zero-shot generalization capability in unseen real-world environments.

title: Are Multimodal Benchmarks Really Useful? Item-Level Multimodal Benchmark Diagnosis via Structure-Response Co-Calibration
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 34 pages, including appendices
summary: Multimodal benchmarks are central to evaluating whether models can reason over information from multiple modalities. However, existing literature has revealed that some benchmarks may contain shortcut items that can be answered from a single modality or from answer-option regularities alone, thus failing to reflect models' true cross-modal inference ability. Existing methods for assessing benchmarks typically rely either on intrinsic item structure or extrinsic model response behavior, which are not adequate for a comprehensive diagnosis. To fill in this gap, we propose SRCoD, a structure-response co-calibrated diagnosis framework for item-level diagnosis of modality dependence in multimodal benchmarks. SRCoD estimates sample-wise multimodal information structure from benchmark content and target answers, and uses this signal as a soft structural anchor for modality-conditioned item response modeling. The learned model produces a calibrated item-level diagnostic profile that reflects how strongly an item depends on different forms of modality evidence, enabling fine-grained benchmark analysis beyond aggregate accuracy. SRCoD also provides interpretable attribution of the diagnosis results. Extensive experiments under two complementary protocols, i.e., benchmark-refinement oriented validation and human-labeled item validation, demonstrate that SRCoD outperforms state-of-the-art benchmark diagnosis methods.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 34 pages, including appendices

title: Byzantine-linearizable Single-Writer Multi-Reader Register in the GPU-Inspired Shared Memory Model
summary: The construction of fault-tolerant atomic registers is a fundamental problem in distributed computing. GPUs, widely used in scientific computing and machine learning, face Byzantine thread behaviour, while their shared memory lacks access control, allowing any thread to modify shared objects. This raises the question of whether atomic register semantics can be maintained when any thread, including the designated writer, may behave Byzantine. We study this problem in the GPU-inspired shared-memory model of Georgiou et al. and present implementations of a Byzantine-linearizable single-writer multi-reader (SWMR) register. CAReg uses constant memory with a quantifiable probability of invalid reads, while SnapObject maintains a bounded window of authenticated writes, eliminating invalid reads and tolerating up to \(n-1\) Byzantine processes through lock-free and wait-free variants. Our results demonstrate how GPU phase-based, lock-step execution can partially compensate for the absence of access control.

title: InfraWorld: Motion-Aware World Modeling for Roadside 4D Occupancy Forecasting
summary: Roadside 4D occupancy forecasting predicts future semantic occupancy in a fixed infrastructure coordinate system. Roadside scenes are globally structured yet locally evolving, requiring comprehensive scene-level context while precisely modeling sparse localized motion. However, existing forecasting paradigms struggle to tackle both requirements. To address this limitation, we propose InfraWorld, a world model formulating roadside occupancy forecasting as selective state evolution. InfraWorld maintains a dense BEV state for the complete scene and persistent motion queries for moving regions, assigning complementary states to global context and local dynamics. Specifically, we propose Dynamic Query Initiation (DQI) to initialize queries in regions supported by motion in the observed history. During rollout, the dense state is updated through Long--Short Temporal Fusion (LST), which combines short-term adjacent-frame continuity with long-term motion trends to preserve stable context while capturing scene evolution. Motion-Aware Query Injection (MAQI) then refines the queries and injects confidence-weighted query information into corresponding BEV tokens, enabling targeted dynamic updates without perturbing global context. Together, InfraWorld concentrates predictive capacity on evolving traffic regions. Extensive experiments on the InfraOcc and Occ3D--nus datasets demonstrate that InfraWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance for roadside 4D occupancy forecasting while retaining its effectiveness under ego-centric settings. Code will be released.
