summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). However, ZO optimization suffers from high variance in high-dimensional parameter spaces. While recent methods restrict perturbations to random low-rank subspaces, these subspaces often misalign with task-specific descent directions. We propose AdaSub-ZO, a novel forward-only fine-tuning framework in learnable low-rank subspaces. Instead of relying on fixed random matrices, AdaSub-ZO iteratively learns layer-wise projection matrices directly from finite-difference feedback to track task-aware descent directions. Furthermore, AdaSub-ZO incorporates a subspace momentum acceleration mechanism to smooth noisy gradient estimates across evolving subspace bases. Extensive experiments on natural language understanding tasks demonstrate that AdaSub-ZO outperforms existing ZO baselines, substantially reducing gradient estimation variance and accelerating convergence.

AI.title_translation: LLM 的可学习低秩子空间中的零阶微调
AI.tldr: AdaSub-ZO 是一种新的前向模式微调框架，通过学习低秩子空间来解决零阶优化在 LLM 微调中的高方差问题，并在实验中表现优于现有方法。
AI.motivation: 零阶（ZO）优化虽然可以实现内存高效的 LLM 微调，但在高维参数空间中存在高方差问题。现有方法将扰动限制在随机低秩子空间，但这些子空间可能与任务特定的下降方向不一致。
AI.method: AdaSub-ZO 框架通过有限差分反馈，迭代学习层级投影矩阵，以跟踪任务感知的下降方向，并引入子空间动量加速机制来平滑梯度估计。
AI.result: AdaSub-ZO 在自然语言理解任务的广泛实验中，显著降低了梯度估计方差，加速了收敛，并优于现有的 ZO 基线。
AI.conclusion: AdaSub-ZO 通过学习低秩子空间来改进 LLM 的零阶微调，有效解决了现有方法的局限性，并在实验中取得了优于基线方法的性能。
AI.translation: 零阶（ZO）优化能够实现大型语言模型（LLM）的内存高效微调。然而，ZO 优化在高维参数空间中存在高方差。最近的方法将扰动限制在随机低秩子空间，但这些子空间经常与任务特定的下降方向不一致。我们提出了 AdaSub-ZO，一个在可学习低秩子空间中进行前向模式微调的新框架。AdaSub-ZO 不依赖于固定的随机矩阵，而是直接从有限差分反馈中迭代学习层级投影矩阵，以跟踪任务感知的下降方向。此外，AdaSub-ZO 包含一个子空间动量加速机制，以平滑跨越不断演变的子空间基的噪声梯度估计。在自然语言理解任务上的广泛实验表明，AdaSub-ZO 的性能优于现有的 ZO 基线，显著降低了梯度估计方差并加速了收敛。
AI.summary: AdaSub-ZO 是一种创新的零阶（ZO）微调框架，用于解决大型语言模型（LLM）在高维参数空间中微调时的高方差问题。该方法通过学习低秩子空间来替代固定的随机子空间，并利用有限差分反馈迭代地更新投影矩阵，以适应任务特定的下降方向。此外，AdaSub-ZO 还引入了子空间动量机制来稳定梯度估计。实验结果表明，AdaSub-ZO 在自然语言理解任务上能够有效降低梯度方差、加速收敛，并取得优于现有 ZO 方法的性能。
AI.keywords: 零阶优化, 大型语言模型, 低秩子空间, 微调, AdaSub-ZO
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的 AdaSub-ZO 框架，通过引入可学习的低秩子空间来解决零阶 LLM 微调中的高方差问题。该方法通过迭代学习投影矩阵和引入子空间动量，有效提高了优化效率和收敛速度。实验结果支持了该方法的有效性，但未来的工作可以进一步探索其在更大规模模型和更复杂任务上的泛化能力。

title: Understanding Unified VLMs: From Attention Probing to Guidance Tuning for Multimodal Generation
summary: Unified vision-language models (VLMs) perform both text-to-image (T2I) and image-to-text (I2T) generation with one shared Transformer backbone, yet how the backbone processes the condition in either direction remains poorly understood. We study this question from the perspective of conditional guidance: we probe every attention head to show the activation difference between two branches of classifier-free guidance (CFG) with different conditional guidance. On two unified VLMs of autoregressive and masked-diffusion paradigms, the probing reveals a subset of heads that are more sensitive to the change of condition while others are agnostic to it. This characteristic pattern holds in both T2I and I2T generation and is largely stable across data samples, demonstrating the internal mechanism of unified VLMs. Motivated by this, we propose a new inference-time intervention approach for unified multimodal generation, named \textit{HeadTuned-CFG}, which uses the probed condition-change awareness to select and tune the conditional guidance at the attention-head level. Experiments show consistent benefits in both multimodal generation directions of unified VLMs without additional training, and in particular substantial improvements over strong baselines in T2I generation. These results further support the key finding of our probing analysis: the observed pattern of functional specialization is an intrinsic property of unified VLMs.

AI.title_translation: 理解统一VLMs：从注意力探究到多模态生成的引导调优
AI.tldr: 该研究通过探究注意力头揭示了统一VLM中条件处理的内部机制，并提出了一种基于此机制的推理时干预方法HeadTuned-CFG，以改善多模态生成。
AI.motivation: 统一视觉语言模型（VLMs）虽然能够同时执行文本到图像（T2I）和图像到文本（I2T）生成，但其共享的Transformer骨干在处理任一方向的条件时如何工作仍知之甚少。
AI.method: 本研究从条件引导的角度出发，通过探究每个注意力头，分析在使用不同条件引导的无分类器引导（CFG）的两个分支之间的激活差异。在自回归和掩码扩散两种范式的统一VLM上进行探究后，提出了一种名为HeadTuned-CFG的推理时干预方法，该方法利用探究到的条件变化感知能力，在注意力头级别选择并调整条件引导。
AI.result: 研究发现，统一VLMs中存在一部分注意力头对条件变化更敏感，而其他头则不敏感。这种特征模式在T2I和I2T生成中均成立，且在不同数据样本间保持稳定。提出的HeadTuned-CFG方法在无需额外训练的情况下，在两种多模态生成方向上都带来了持续的性能提升，特别是在T2I生成中，相对于强基线有显著改进。这些结果支持了功能专业化是统一VLM内在属性的关键发现。
AI.conclusion: 统一VLMs内部存在功能专业化模式，其中部分注意力头对条件变化高度敏感。基于这一洞察，本文提出的HeadTuned-CFG方法能够有效提升多模态生成性能，证实了这种内在机制的重要性。
AI.translation: 统一视觉语言模型（VLMs）使用一个共享的Transformer骨干执行文本到图像（T2I）和图像到文本（I2T）生成，但骨干在任一方向上如何处理条件仍然知之甚少。我们从条件引导的角度研究这个问题：我们探究每个注意力头，以显示在使用不同条件引导的无分类器引导（CFG）的两个分支之间的激活差异。在自回归和掩码扩散两种范式的两个统一VLM上，探究揭示了一部分头对条件变化更敏感，而其他头则对此不敏感。这种特征模式在T2I和I2T生成中都成立，并且在数据样本之间基本稳定，这证明了统一VLM的内部机制。受此启发，我们提出了一种新的统一多模态生成推理时干预方法，名为HeadTuned-CFG，它利用探究到的条件变化感知能力，在注意力头级别选择和调整条件引导。实验表明，在统一VLM的两种多模态生成方向上都持续受益，无需额外训练，特别是在T2I生成中，相对于强基线有显著改进。这些结果进一步支持了我们探究分析的关键发现：观察到的功能专业化模式是统一VLM的内在属性。
AI.summary: 本文深入研究了统一视觉语言模型（VLMs）在文本到图像（T2I）和图像到文本（I2T）生成中共享Transformer骨干如何处理条件。通过探究注意力头在无分类器引导（CFG）下的激活差异，研究发现统一VLMs存在一种内在机制：一部分注意力头对条件变化高度敏感，而其他头则不敏感。基于这一发现，作者提出了一种新的推理时干预方法HeadTuned-CFG，该方法通过在注意力头级别调整条件引导，在无需额外训练的情况下显著提升了多模态生成性能，尤其在T2I生成中表现出色，验证了其探究分析的关键发现。
AI.keywords: 统一VLM, 注意力探究, 条件引导, 多模态生成, HeadTuned-CFG
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过深入探究统一VLMs的注意力机制，揭示了其内部功能专业化的特性，即某些注意力头对条件变化更敏感。这一发现具有创新性，因为它提供了对复杂模型内部工作原理的理解。在此基础上提出的HeadTuned-CFG方法，无需额外训练即可提升性能，展现了理论洞察指导实际优化的潜力。该研究为未来统一多模态模型的解释性研究和高效推理优化提供了新思路。

title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments
summary: Words are increasingly becoming an interface for action: large language models (LLMs) can now invoke tools, operate devices, and make decisions that affect the physical world. However, current benchmarks largely evaluate LLMs through static text responses, offline tool calls, or simulated tasks, leaving open the question of how well they can act in real physical environments. We present a benchmark for measuring LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction, where models control a harness system connected to real-world components including robotic arms, cameras, and sensors. In each task, the model must issue instructions, receive physical feedback from the environment, interpret the resulting state, and adapt its next action accordingly. This setting evaluates capabilities beyond language understanding, including grounded perception, action planning, tool selection, spatial reasoning, feedback-driven correction, and robustness to execution uncertainty. Through experiments with representative LLMs, we characterize their ability to translate linguistic reasoning into physical actions and identify common failure modes such as hallucinated state changes, poor recovery from unexpected outcomes, and unstable long-horizon plans. Our benchmark aims to provide a systematic foundation for evaluating LLMs as interactive agents that connect words, tools, and the physical world.

AI.title_translation: 言语到世界：交互式物理环境中的大型语言模型基准测试
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一个在真实物理环境中评估大型语言模型（LLM）能力的基准测试，该测试通过闭环交互来衡量LLM在感知、规划、执行和纠错方面的表现，并指出了现有LLM在物理世界交互中的局限性。
AI.motivation: 现有的大型语言模型基准测试主要评估离线任务和静态文本响应，未能充分衡量LLM在真实物理环境中的交互和行动能力。
AI.method: 提出了一个在真实物理环境中进行闭环交互的基准测试，其中LLM通过控制机器人手臂、摄像头和传感器等硬件来执行任务，并根据物理反馈进行调整。
AI.result: 通过对代表性LLM的实验，研究揭示了它们在将语言推理转化为物理行动方面的能力，并识别出常见的失败模式，如状态幻觉、对意外结果恢复能力差以及长期规划不稳定。
AI.conclusion: 该基准测试为评估LLM作为连接言语、工具和物理世界的交互式代理提供了系统性基础，旨在推动LLM在物理世界中的应用。
AI.translation: 言语正日益成为行动的接口：大型语言模型（LLM）现在可以调用工具、操作设备并做出影响物理世界的决策。然而，目前的基准测试主要通过静态文本响应、离线工具调用或模拟任务来评估LLM，这使得它们在真实物理环境中表现如何的问题悬而未决。我们提出了一个用于在闭环物理交互中测量LLM的基准测试，其中模型控制连接到机器人手臂、摄像头和传感器等真实世界组件的约束系统。在每个任务中，模型必须发出指令，接收来自环境的物理反馈，解释由此产生的状态，并相应地调整其下一个动作。这种设置评估了超越语言理解的能力，包括基础感知、动作规划、工具选择、空间推理、反馈驱动的校正以及对执行不确定性的鲁棒性。通过对代表性LLM的实验，我们对其将语言推理转化为物理行动的能力进行了表征，并识别出常见的失败模式，如状态幻觉、对意外结果恢复能力差以及不稳定的长时程规划。我们的基准测试旨在为评估LLM作为连接言语、工具和物理世界的交互式代理提供系统性基础。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了“Words to World”基准测试，用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）在真实物理环境中的交互能力。该基准测试通过闭环系统，让LLM控制机器人硬件，接收物理反馈并进行调整，从而衡量其在感知、规划、执行和纠错等方面的综合能力。实验结果揭示了当前LLM在物理世界交互中的局限性，并为未来LLM作为物理世界代理的发展奠定了基础。
AI.keywords: 大型语言模型, 物理环境, 交互式基准测试, 闭环控制, 具身智能
AI.comments: 这项研究解决了评估LLM在物理世界交互能力方面的一个关键空白。通过引入一个真实的、闭环的基准测试，研究人员能够量化LLM在将语言指令转化为实际物理行动方面的表现，并识别出关键的挑战。该基准测试的设计具有创新性，能够评估LLM的多种能力，如基础感知、规划和反馈驱动的校正，这对于开发更强大、更可靠的LLM代理至关重要。然而，真实世界实验的复杂性和成本可能限制了该基准测试的可扩展性。此外，如何有效地模拟或处理现实世界中的不确定性和意外情况，仍然是未来研究的一个重要方向。

title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring
summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models, particularly large language models (LLMs), are increasingly used in educational settings for tasks such as item generation, automated scoring, and feedback delivery. The quality of these outputs depends not only on the AI model but also on how users construct the prompts that guide model behaviors. Current prompt engineering practices are largely ad hoc, relying on trial and error rather than principled design. This lack of structure introduces validity threats including construct misrepresentation, construct-irrelevant variance, and limited reproducibility. We propose that Evidence-Centered Design (ECD), a framework in educational measurement for structuring valid inferences from observed performance, can serve as a principled foundation for prompt engineering in educational applications. We map the three core ECD models, the student model, the evidence model, and the task model, onto the components of educational prompt design, and describe a workflow for ECD-based prompt engineering. We derive five design principles from this mapping and present an empirical study contrasting ECD-designed prompts with state-of-the-art (SOTA) prompting baselines on an automated scoring task. Our empirical study demonstrates the usefulness of this framework on automated scoring. Results suggest that treating prompting as assessment design rather than informal instructions strengthens the validity, reliability, and fairness of AI-generated educational outputs.

AI.title_translation: 使用以证据为中心的设计来指导测量中的提示工程：以自动化论文评分为例
AI.tldr: 该研究提出使用以证据为中心的设计（ECD）框架来改进教育领域中生成式人工智能（GenAI）的提示工程，以解决当前提示工程的随意性问题，并以自动化论文评分为例进行了实证研究，结果表明这种方法能提高AI输出的有效性、可靠性和公平性。
AI.motivation: 当前生成式人工智能（GenAI）在教育领域的应用，如自动化评分，其输出质量很大程度上依赖于提示工程，但目前的方法多是随意试错，缺乏原则性，这可能导致构建误传、无关方差和可复现性差等有效性威胁。
AI.method: 研究将教育测量的以证据为中心的设计（ECD）框架（包括学生模型、证据模型和任务模型）应用于教育提示设计，提出了一种基于ECD的提示工程工作流程，并从中推导出五个设计原则。随后，通过一项实证研究，将ECD设计的提示与当前最先进（SOTA）的提示基线在自动化评分任务上进行了对比。
AI.result: 实证研究表明，将提示工程视为评估设计而非非正式指令，可以增强AI生成教育输出的有效性、可靠性和公平性。
AI.conclusion: 以证据为中心的设计（ECD）为教育领域的提示工程提供了一个有原则的基础，能够有效解决当前提示工程随意性带来的问题，并能提高AI生成教育输出的质量。
AI.translation: 生成式人工智能（GenAI）模型，特别是大型语言模型（LLM），越来越多地应用于教育领域，执行诸如试题生成、自动化评分和反馈提供等任务。这些输出的质量不仅取决于AI模型本身，还取决于用户如何构建指导模型行为的提示。目前的提示工程实践在很大程度上是临时的，依赖于反复试验而非原则性设计。这种缺乏结构的做法引入了有效性威胁，包括构建误传、构建无关方差和可复现性有限。我们提出，以证据为中心的设计（ECD）——一个在教育测量中用于指导从观察到的表现中进行有效推断的框架——可以作为教育应用中提示工程的原则性基础。我们将三个核心的ECD模型（学生模型、证据模型和任务模型）映射到教育提示设计的组成部分，并描述了一个基于ECD的提示工程工作流程。我们从这种映射中推导出了五个设计原则，并进行了一项实证研究，在自动化评分任务上，将ECD设计的提示与最先进（SOTA）的提示基线进行了对比。我们的实证研究证明了该框架在自动化评分方面的实用性。结果表明，将提示视为评估设计而非非正式指令，可以增强AI生成的教育输出的有效性、可靠性和公平性。
AI.summary: 本研究提出将教育测量中的以证据为中心的设计（ECD）框架应用于生成式人工智能（GenAI）的提示工程，以解决当前提示工程随意性带来的有效性问题。研究者将ECD的核心模型映射到提示设计组件，并提出了一种ECD驱动的提示工程工作流程和设计原则。通过在自动化论文评分任务上的实证研究，证明了该方法能够有效提升AI生成教育输出的有效性、可靠性和公平性，强调了将提示工程视为评估设计的重要性。
AI.keywords: 提示工程, 以证据为中心的设计, 自动化论文评分, 生成式人工智能, 教育测量
AI.comments: 这项研究巧妙地将教育测量领域的成熟框架（ECD）应用于新兴的AI提示工程领域，提供了一个非常有价值的、有原则的设计方法。通过实证研究验证了其有效性，尤其是在自动化评分方面，为提高AI在教育应用中的可靠性和有效性提供了实践指导。然而，该方法在其他教育任务中的普适性和可扩展性，以及在实际应用中推广的挑战，值得进一步探讨。

title: MoMaTune: Model, Match, Then Tune Language Models for Numerical Records
summary: Despite remarkable progress in language understanding and generation, decoder language models continue to exhibit striking failures on numerical data. Numerical examples are typically serialized as text by concatenating feature names with their values (e.g., fat:3.4), while conventional task adaptation applies loss only to the downstream prediction target. This leaves two structures weakly supervised: within-value sensitivity, where digit position determines numerical magnitude, because token cross-entropy contains no explicit numerical metric; and across-field structure, where measurements in the same record are statistically dependent, because target-only tuning provides no direct loss on the measurements or their dependencies. We introduce MoMaTune (Model, Match, then Tune), a two-stage post-training strategy organized around these supervision gaps. Stage 1 applies Model, ordinary next-token prediction densely over label-free serialized records, and optionally adds Match, a same-record consistency objective that aligns representations of different partial views of the same example. Stage 2 applies Tune, supervised fine-tuning for downstream target prediction. We evaluate MoMaTune on 169,285 records from eight public datasets, with 339 of 340 input fields numerical. At 1.5B parameters, Model raises the eight-dataset masked-value imputation aggregate from 0.106 to 0.401, while the three-dataset correct-context gain rises from 0.058 to 0.167. On diagnostics, Model also increases sensitivity to numerically consequential digit changes, while Match improves robustness to informative partial views. Adding Tune yields higher target-supervised embedding aggregates for each tested Stage-1 parent, and the two-stage recipes obtain higher aggregate scores than Tune alone. The same pattern is observed at 4B, 9.6B, and 27B parameters when model embeddings are used for downstream prediction.

AI.title_translation: MoMaTune：对数值记录进行建模、匹配，然后微调语言模型
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为MoMaTune的两阶段后训练策略，用于解决语言模型在处理数值数据时的不足。该策略首先通过“建模”（密集的下一词预测）和可选的“匹配”（同一记录一致性目标）来增强模型对数值数据内部结构和跨字段依赖性的理解，然后通过“微调”进行下游任务的监督学习。实验表明，MoMaTune在数值记录处理任务上显著优于仅使用监督微调的方法，并且在不同模型规模下均表现出色。
AI.motivation: 传统的语言模型在处理数值数据时存在不足，因为它们将数值序列化为文本，并且仅对下游预测目标进行监督，导致模型对数值的敏感性不足以及无法理解记录中不同字段之间的依赖关系。
AI.method: MoMaTune是一种两阶段的后训练策略。第一阶段包括“建模”，即对序列化的记录进行密集的下一词预测，并可选地加入“匹配”步骤，通过一致性目标来对同一记录的不同视图进行表示对齐。第二阶段是“微调”，即针对下游目标预测进行监督式微调。
AI.result: 在169,285条记录的八个公共数据集上评估，MoMaTune在掩码值填充任务上的平均得分从0.106提高到0.401，在正确上下文任务上的得分从0.058提高到0.167。此外，它还提高了模型对数值敏感的数字变化的敏感度，并增强了对信息性部分视图的鲁棒性。与单独的微调相比，MoMaTune的两阶段方法在不同模型规模下均取得了更高的得分。
AI.conclusion: MoMaTune通过其两阶段的“建模-匹配-微调”策略，有效地解决了语言模型在处理数值记录时的固有挑战，显著提高了模型在数值敏感性、跨字段依赖性以及下游任务预测方面的性能。
AI.translation: 尽管在语言理解和生成方面取得了显著的进步，但解码器语言模型在数值数据上仍然表现出惊人的缺陷。数值示例通常通过将特征名称与其值连接（例如，fat:3.4）来序列化为文本，而传统的任务适应仅对下游预测目标应用损失。这使得两个结构处于弱监督状态：值内敏感性，其中数字位置决定数值大小，因为令牌交叉熵不包含显式数值度量；跨字段结构，其中同一记录中的度量在统计上是相关的，因为仅目标调整不提供对度量或其依赖关系的直接损失。我们引入了MoMaTune（建模、匹配，然后微调），一种围绕这些监督空白组织的双阶段后训练策略。第一阶段应用“建模”，即对无标签的序列化记录进行普通的下一词预测，并可选地添加“匹配”，一个同一记录一致性目标，将同一示例的不同视图的表示对齐。第二阶段应用“微调”，即针对下游目标预测进行监督式微调。我们在来自八个公共数据集的169,285条记录上评估了MoMaTune，其中339个输入字段是数值字段。在1.5B参数下，“建模”将八个数据集的掩码值填充平均得分从0.106提高到0.401，而三个数据集的正确上下文增益从0.058提高到0.167。在诊断测试中，“建模”还提高了对数值上重要的数字变化的敏感性，而“匹配”提高了对信息性视图的鲁棒性。添加“微调”为每个测试的 Stage-1 父模型提供了更高的目标监督嵌入平均得分，并且与单独的“微调”相比，两阶段方法获得了更高的平均得分。当使用模型嵌入进行下游预测时，在4B、9.6B和27B参数下观察到相同的模式。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为MoMaTune的两阶段后训练策略，旨在解决语言模型在处理数值数据时的局限性。该策略通过“建模”（密集的下一词预测）和可选的“匹配”（同一记录一致性目标）来增强模型对数值数据内部结构和跨字段依赖性的理解，随后通过“微调”进行下游任务的监督学习。实验结果表明，MoMaTune在数值记录处理任务上显著优于仅使用监督微调的方法，并且在不同模型规模下均表现出色。
AI.keywords: 数值数据处理, 语言模型微调, MoMaTune, 后训练策略, 序列化数据
AI.comments: 这项研究有效地解决了大型语言模型在处理数值数据时存在的关键挑战。通过引入“建模”和“匹配”阶段，该方法弥合了传统序列化和目标导向微调之间的监督鸿沟，从而显著提高了模型对数值信息的理解和利用能力。实验结果令人信服，表明该方法在各种规模的模型上都具有良好的可扩展性。未来的工作可以探索将此方法应用于更广泛的数值密集型任务，并进一步研究“匹配”阶段中不同一致性目标的有效性。

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Heterogeneous Task Allocation Under Spatio-Temporal Environmental Uncertainty for Multi-Robot Teams
comments: The 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR 2026)
summary: Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) have been increasingly deployed to perform different kinds of maritime tasks in recent years, which motivates the need for a reliable task allocation policy that can adapt to heterogeneous tasks and maritime disturbances. In this work, we formulate a multi-robot task allocation problem in which a team of ASVs with heterogeneous capabilities needs to complete tasks of different types and appearance times under unknown stochastic spatio-temporal uncertainties from maritime disturbances. We propose a decentralized Reinforcement Learning (RL) based policy network that is trained to be robust towards uncertainty-induced observation deviations, and is able to perform individual decision making that leads to efficient execution behaviors toward heterogeneous task requirements. We evaluate the proposed policy and four baseline methods in simulated experiments with varied proportions of different tasks types, numbers of tasks, robot species and robots per species. Experiment results show that our proposed policy achieves the lowest makespan and can be deployed to address scenarios with 100 robots and 400 tasks.
comment: The 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR 2026)

AI.title_translation: 基于强化学习的多机器人异构任务分配在时空环境不确定性下
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种基于强化学习的去中心化策略，用于在存在时空不确定性的海洋环境中，分配异构任务给异构的自主水面载具（ASV）团队。实验结果表明，该策略能有效减少完成时间（makespan），并能扩展到包含100个机器人和400个任务的大规模场景。
AI.motivation: 随着自主水面载具（ASV）在海洋任务中的广泛应用，需要一种能够适应异构任务和海洋干扰的可靠任务分配策略。
AI.method: 提出了一种去中心化的、基于强化学习的策略网络，该网络经过训练能够对不确定性引起的观测偏差具有鲁棒性，并能进行个体决策，以实现高效的异构任务执行。
AI.result: 与四种基线方法相比，所提出的策略在模拟实验中实现了最短的完成时间（makespan），并且能够处理包含100个机器人和400个任务的场景。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的基于强化学习的去中心化策略能够有效应对时空不确定性，实现异构多机器人团队的高效任务分配。
AI.translation:
近年来，自主水面载具（ASV）被越来越多地用于执行各种海洋任务，这促使人们需要一种可靠的任务分配策略，该策略能够适应异构任务和海洋干扰。
在本研究中，我们将多机器人任务分配问题进行公式化，其中一个ASV团队需要完成具有不同类型和出现时间的任务，同时应对来自海洋干扰的未知随机时空不确定性。
我们提出了一种去中心化的、基于强化学习（RL）的策略网络，该网络经过训练，能够对不确定性引起的观测偏差具有鲁棒性，并且能够进行个体决策，从而实现针对异构任务需求的有效执行行为。
我们在包含不同任务类型比例、任务数量、机器人种类和每种机器人数量各异的模拟实验中，对所提出的策略和四种基线方法进行了评估。
实验结果表明，我们提出的策略实现了最短的完成时间（makespan），并且可以部署到包含100个机器人和400个任务的场景中。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种新颖的、基于强化学习的去中心化策略，用于解决在存在时空环境不确定性的海洋中，多机器人团队异构任务分配的问题。该策略能够使具有异构能力的自主水面载具（ASV）团队有效应对各种任务类型和海洋干扰，并做出个体决策以实现高效执行。模拟实验结果表明，该方法优于现有基线方法，显著缩短了任务完成时间，并能有效扩展至大规模应用场景。
AI.keywords: 强化学习, 异构任务分配, 多机器人系统, 时空不确定性, 自主水面载具
AI.comments: 该研究在处理海洋环境中固有的时空不确定性方面取得了显著进展，其去中心化的强化学习方法为解决复杂的多机器人任务分配问题提供了一个有前景的解决方案。然而，实际部署中的鲁棒性和可扩展性仍需进一步验证。

title: Localized Joule heating and carbonization process optimization of 3D printed polymer structures for lab-on-CMOS applications
summary: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. Such high temperature is detrimental to the CMOS sensor circuits, causing severe degradation. We present a novel solution of localized Joule heating of these polymer nanostructures to achieve complete carbonization of the electrodes. Both analytical and COMSOL simulations guided the experiments to characterize the carbonization process conditions. Partial carbonization was achieved at 500-600 °C of global temperature, and complete carbonization was achieved by localized Joule heating. Pyrolized nanostructures monolithic samples on a silica wafer were fabricated using standard material processing, such as 2-Photon Polymerization. Pyrolysis was achieved by Rapid Thermal Processing (RTP). Observations using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the feasibility of polymer carbonization within a CMOS compatible temperature window.

AI.title_translation: 用于片上CMOS应用的3D打印聚合物结构的局部焦耳加热和碳化工艺优化
AI.tldr: 通过局部焦耳加热优化3D打印聚合物结构的碳化过程，以适应CMOS兼容的温度窗口，解决了传统高温退火对CMOS传感器的损害问题。
AI.motivation: 传统高温（约950°C）热退火工艺会严重损害CMOS传感器电路，阻碍了集成碳电极在片上芯片、生物医学、环境和工业应用中的发展。
AI.method: 结合分析和COMSOL模拟，研究局部焦耳加热对3D打印聚合物纳米结构进行碳化的工艺条件。通过2-光子聚合和快速热处理（RTP）技术制备样品，并利用光学显微镜、扫描电子显微镜和拉曼光谱进行表征。
AI.result: 在500-600°C的全局温度下实现了部分碳化，而通过局部焦耳加热则实现了完全碳化。实验证明，该方法可在CMOS兼容的温度范围内实现聚合物碳化。
AI.conclusion: 局部焦耳加热是一种有效的碳化方法，可以在CMOS兼容的温度窗口内实现3D打印聚合物纳米结构的完全碳化，为将碳电极集成到CMOS传感器中开辟了新的可能性。
AI.translation: 使用与CMOS技术集成的碳电极在片上芯片、生物医学、环境和工业应用方面具有巨大潜力。一种开发碳电极的方法是在CMOS芯片上3D打印聚合物纳米结构，并使用高温（约950°C）热退火工艺将其热解成碳。如此高的温度对CMOS传感器电路有害，会导致严重退化。我们提出了一种通过局部焦耳加热这些聚合物纳米结构来实现电极完全碳化的新颖解决方案。分析和COMSOL模拟指导了表征碳化工艺条件的实验。在500-600°C的全局温度下实现了部分碳化，并通过局部焦耳加热实现了完全碳化。使用标准材料加工（如2光子聚合）在二氧化硅晶片上制备了解热解的纳米结构整体样品。通过快速热处理（RTP）实现了解热解。通过光学显微镜、扫描电子显微镜和拉曼光谱的观察证明了在CMOS兼容的温度窗口内实现聚合物碳化的可行性。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种局部焦耳加热方法，用于优化3D打印聚合物结构的碳化过程，以解决传统高温热处理对CMOS传感器的损害问题。通过结合分析和COMSOL模拟，研究人员确定了实现完全碳化的工艺条件，并在CMOS兼容的温度窗口内成功制备了碳化纳米结构。该方法通过光学显微镜、扫描电子显微镜和拉曼光谱进行了验证，证明了其在片上CMOS应用中的潜力。
AI.keywords: 局部焦耳加热, 碳化, 3D打印聚合物, CMOS兼容, 片上芯片
AI.comments: 这项研究提出的局部焦耳加热方法在解决CMOS兼容性问题方面具有重要意义，为开发更先进的片上系统提供了新的途径。然而，模拟与实验结果的精确匹配程度以及该方法在大规模生产中的可扩展性仍有待进一步研究。

title: ClinEdge: An Expert-Graded Benchmark of Real Patient Edge Cases Where Frontier Multimodal Models Fail
comments: 14 pages, 5 figures. 32 real, de-identified clinical cases; 224 expert-graded evaluations across seven frontier multimodal AI systems
summary:
Most benchmarks for large language models in medicine are built from licensing examinations and theoretical questions. The few that draw on real clinical data do so only in part, and rarely require a model to read a patient's own imaging. ClinEdge addresses this gap with 32 real, de-identified patient cases from active clinical practice, each evaluated across seven frontier systems for a total of 224 expert-graded evaluations. Each case pairs primary imaging with a short vignette, contains a feature known to defeat pattern-matched reasoning, and is scored against the patient's documented clinical course. The suite is built for depth rather than volume. Grading followed a two-stage expert process. First, a senior orthopaedic surgeon graded all 224 responses on a weighted rubric and a pass-or-fail verdict. Second, a panel of nineteen physicians, largely senior specialists at teaching medical colleges, independently reviewed every case and every one of the 224 grades. All seven production systems were evaluated through their public interfaces, and all 224 conversations are preserved as replayable links.
  Performance was poor across all systems, and the failures were shared: different vendors missed the same findings and converged on the same wrong plans. From the experts' notes we catalogue 18 recurring failure modes in five families. The models stop reading an image at the first finding. They give generic plans and lean toward over-treatment. They trust a misleading history over correct imaging. Their answers vary across systems and runs, and change with question format. Failing answers were delivered fluently and without any expressed uncertainty. Four cases are released in full; the remaining 28 are held out, and we invite frontier AI labs and healthcare AI companies to evaluate their models against them (research@futrbridge.com)
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. 32 real, de-identified clinical cases; 224 expert-graded evaluations across seven frontier multimodal AI systems

title: The Era of Vibe Tapeout: Dark Age or Golden Age for Analog Circuit Design?
summary: LLM agents now write their own schematic and layout generators, run EDA tools, read the results, and fix the design. This "vibe tapeout" is becoming practical for analog circuits as well. This paper measures how far it has come in two settings. (A) On an open PDK (SKY130), a cloud LLM agent designed an 11-bit, 5.12-MS/s SAR ADC from its specification. The agents produced DRC- and LVS-clean macros and met the specification after parasitic extraction (PEX). In particular, under the condition in which the agent received a sanitized reference design derived from our 65-nm design (vibe porting), it produced the best layout in the shortest time. Its area was 1/1.6 to 1/2.8 of that of the conditions without a reference. This condition reached signoff without human intervention. The agents also identified the causes of post-PEX degradation (CDAC wiring coupling and common-mode-dependent comparator offset) by their own experiments. On the other hand, agents sometimes reported false passes, and verification independent of the design agent was essential. (B) A commercial PDK is under NDA and cannot be given to a cloud LLM. We therefore evaluated local LLMs running on university servers with a six-task benchmark on a commercial 65-nm CMOS PDK. Kimi K3 passed five of the six tasks, while MiniMax M3 passed two. Neither solved the debugging task, which requires finding the cause from symptoms. Finally, we discuss the prospects for extending vibe tapeout from ADCs to entire SoCs, and ask whether vibe tapeout is a dark age or a golden age for analog design. Our answer is that it is a golden age for designers who know what to verify.

title: EvolvAttack: Backdooring self Evolving VLM Agents
summary: Self-evolving mechanisms let vision-language model (VLM) agents continually adapt through evolving memory, but they also allow malicious behavior to emerge only after deployment. We introduce a new attack surface, the self-evolving backdoor, whose payload stays dormant in the initial agent and is progressively activated as the agent evolves. Unlike conventional backdoors, which can be exposed by testing triggered inputs on a static model, our attack requires both a visual trigger and a sufficiently evolved memory state; static scanning with clean memory thus yields near-zero attack success and may deem the agent benign. We realize this through memory-aware backdoor training, which couples trigger activation with the agent's evolving memory while preserving benign behavior unless the trigger co-occurs with payload-related memory. Across three VLM backbones, four agent pipelines, and recency-, semantic-, and reward-based memory evolution, the attack preserves normal functionality and stays nearly inactive before evolution (0.5% attack success rate), yet exceeds 95% attack success within 100 interactions, revealing a stealthy threat unique to self-evolving agents.

title: ObsSpec: Accelerating Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation Speculation
summary: Tool-using agents alternate between model generation and tool execution, waiting for each tool call to complete before starting the next generation. This sequential execution is costly during agentic reinforcement learning (RL), which requires large batches of multi-turn rollouts. We introduce ObsSpec, an observation speculation pipeline for agentic RL that uses a small world model to predict tool outputs while the environment executes, allowing the policy to begin its next generation early. ObsSpec retains speculative work only when the predicted and actual observations match exactly, making rollout collection lossless, while co-training keeps the world model up to date as the policy learns. On terminal-use tasks, predictions from a 0.6B world model exactly match actual observations in 66.4% of attempts and arrive roughly 16 times faster. Using these predictions, ObsSpec reduces agent latency by 9.3% and 14.2% for 8B and 32B policies. Across controlled experiments, we characterize the regimes in which ObsSpec reduces agent latency under shared policy resources. Finally, because ObsSpec overlaps policy generation with tool execution, it is architecturally compatible with existing techniques for accelerating RL. Code is available at https://github.com/kylemontgomery1/verl-recipe/tree/obsspec/obsspec.

title: Correlation-Aware Reconstruction for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Reconstruction-based detectors for multivariate time series anomaly detection typically learn a single entangled representation of normal behavior and flag anomalies based on reconstruction error. However, real-world anomalies are not only isolated spikes in a single channel but also disruptions in the relationships between channels, where each sensor individually appears normal, but their joint behavior deviates from the norm. Because these models compress both temporal evolution and inter-channel structure into this single space, they lack an explicit mechanism to isolate such inter-channel dependencies from normal temporal dependencies, leading to lower detection rates for cross-channel anomalies. We propose CARMA (Correlation-Aware Reconstruction for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection), which is a reconstruction-based variational autoencoder with two complementary latent spaces: a temporal latent that captures sequential dynamics, and a correlation latent that is trained to reconstruct the window's pairwise Pearson correlations. Both representations are fused in the signal decoder, and anomalies are detected from the reconstruction error. We evaluate CARMA on the TSB-AD-M benchmark suite (17 datasets, 180 series) against 29 baseline methods, and show that it significantly outperforms all of them across multiple threshold-free and range-aware metrics, achieving a VUS-PR of 0.4929. Ablations show that removing the correlation branch degrades performance, that adding a second latent without supervision recovers only part of the gain, and that supervising the correlation latent with an explicit correlation target accounts for the rest and produces a sharper error response at anomalies.

title: Entropy/Length Profile Bounds for the Conversion of (Non)linear Codes in the Merge Regime
summary: Code conversion changes the parameters of encoded data while avoiding complete decoding and re-encoding. Existing general bounds largely rely on the algebraic structure of linear codes. This paper develops an information-theoretic framework for nonlinear code conversion in the merge regime. Using the entropy/length profile (ELP), we derive upper bounds on the number of unchanged symbols and lower bounds on the number of read symbols for arbitrary $(n,M)_q$ codes, without assuming linearity or requiring $\log_q M$ to be an integer. We also obtain joint bounds for multiple initial codes and consequences involving minimum distance. For linear codes, the proposed bounds reduce to the corresponding generalized Hamming weight (GHW) bounds. The construction based on Hamming codes converts Hamming codes of redundancy two into a Hamming code of any larger redundancy and simultaneously attains the general bounds on unchanged and read symbols. The construction based on quasigroups shows that new bounds remain tight for genuinely nonlinear codes of nonintegral dimension and at a nonintegral entropy threshold, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first construction of convertible codes for nonlinear codes.

title: Cascade: GPU-Accelerated Out-of-Core Suffix Array Construction for LLM Corpora
summary: Suffix arrays over LLM (pre)training corpora underpin deduplication, contamination testing, n-gram statistics, and training-data attribution, and every new corpus or tokenizer needs a new one. GPU constructors are fast but bounded by device memory, and out-of-core pipelines run at CPU speed, reaching trillions of tokens by building sharded indexes. Reach is bounded not by the size of the data but by what must stay resident, and in a partitioned construction that is the coupling between partitions. We present Cascade, which requires none of it to stay resident. Splitter K-grams sampled from the corpus fix every partition's range of the final suffix array before any sorting, so the GPU sorts and ranks partitions independently and never merges them. The partitions are still coupled: every round of the method needs ranks that other partitions hold, classically kept in a global rank array (the inverse suffix array) that must stay resident. We instead send each rank to the one partition that needs it, and maintain an invariant ensuring ranks are only ever compared within one partition, so no global rank array is needed. The text and a compact partition map, the only structures read at random, then stay in host memory by choice rather than necessity, one at a time when memory is short; every other structure becomes a stream that can be placed across device memory, host memory, and disk as it is written. On a single GPU node, Cascade builds exact suffix arrays of up to 238B tokens, 2.4-6.8x faster than infini-gram's pipeline and 5.9-10.9x faster than libsais.

title: Do Rollups Self-Organize? Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in the EIP-4844 Blob Fee Market
comments: 5 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings 2026)
summary: EIP-4844 gave Ethereum rollups a separate fee dimension for data, governed by a multiplicative update rule that targets three ``blobs'' per block. Whether this target is reached depends on how many independent, self-interested rollups choose to post data, a question that closed-form models address only for a single agent under exogenous prices or in a static equilibrium. We propose a calibrated multi-agent reinforcement learning environment for the blob fee market in which the blob base fee is endogenous, set by the EIP-4844 rule on the aggregated decisions of heterogeneous rollups fit to post-Dencun Ethereum data. After confirming that the environment reproduces the known single-agent analytical optimum, we show that independent learners, with no convergence guarantee, still settle near the target without coordination ($3.32\pm0.01$ blobs per block over five seeds). Over a fiftyfold demand range ($10\times$ to $500\times$), supply stays at the target from $10\times$ to $200\times$ and rises above it at higher demand, where the fee can no longer hold it. Posting frequency increases with rollup size, an emergent analog of the size threshold predicted by prior theory. A costless layer-1 calldata outside option pushes the fee down by roughly an order of magnitude while aggregate supply stays at the target, so the fee rule acts as a negative-feedback controller on decentralized supply.
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things (AIBThings 2026)

title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning
summary: We introduce Sequent-Prover, a family of verifier-using language-model agents, and the post-training framework that produces them. Agents reason in an executable SMT-LIB scratchpad: they write complete SMT-LIB programs, query Z3 across turns, inspect solver feedback, repair formalizations, and terminate with an explicit answer. Our recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps from a noisy teacher proposal policy by sampling multi-turn trajectories, retaining the successful tail that is correct, non-trivial, grounded, and executable, then applying supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level preference optimization. Because solver success alone does not guarantee semantic faithfulness, we evaluate task accuracy, k-sample reliability, and SMT program quality. Across 37 benchmarks and 7,254 problems per model family, post-training raises the 4B model's per-attempt accuracy from 85.6% to 97.0% and four-sample all-correct reliability (pass^4}) from 64.1% to 91.7%. It also reduces average SMT calls from 4.10 to 2.52 and tokens per attempt from 18.97k to 12.72k. Sequent-Prover agents give answers backed by executable formal artifacts.

title: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read
summary: Low-bit quantization reduces the cost of serving reasoning models but can substantially degrade long chains of thought. Each step reads cached keys and values spanning thousands of tokens, allowing quantization errors to accumulate along the trajectory. Standard calibration operates on short segments that omit the earlier context needed by later reasoning steps. Even when this context is retained, cache reconstruction error alone does not capture how quantization errors affect subsequent attention. We present RECAP, a post-training quantization method that calibrates reasoning models on the history they read. Dynamic-prefix calibration separates long historical context from short-block reconstruction. It regenerates prefix keys and values with the current quantizer and rotates the active block to supervise every position along the trajectory. Prefix read geometry further supervises historical cache errors according to their effects on attention outputs, weighting key and value errors asymmetrically. With both components applied only during calibration, RECAP outperforms the baseline across multiple reasoning models and quantization settings. Under W4A4KV4, RECAP improves accuracy over the baseline by 13.3 percentage points on MATH500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 15.8 points on AIME-120 with Qwen3-4B. These results highlight the importance of preserving historical dependencies during calibration for low-bit reasoning.

title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
summary:
To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it.
  For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehlé and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices.
  Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align}
  For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehlé, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption.
  For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight.
  Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.

title: LeHami: Symplectic Latent Dynamics for World Models
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models directly in latent space, but unconstrained autoregressive predictors may contract the latent distribution over long rollouts. We introduce Symplectic Hamiltonian JEPA (LeHami), which replaces the standard predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow over a structured latent state (q, p) integrated using an exactly symplectic leapfrog step. This construction preserves phase-space volume at every rollout step and rules out uniform contraction, asymptotically stable fixed points, and merging of distinct latent states, independently of the learned parameters or action sequence. We obtain the momentum-like component from temporal derivatives of the learned position-like representation, providing an explicit second-order state for prediction and control. On conservative and actuated visual pendulum environments, LeHami substantially improves long-horizon velocity prediction over an unconstrained JEPA world model and empirically maintains constant latent volume where the baseline contracts. The learned flow also supports accurate integration at unseen sub-frame step sizes and numerical time reversal. These results show how geometric structure can provide inference-time guarantees that are complementary to representation regularization in latent world models.

title: Embodiment-Aware Inference-Time Search for Human Reaction Selection in Humanoid Retargeting
summary:
Training humanoid robots to learn human behaviors requires expensive data collection, and human-robot interaction data can be even more difficult and costly to collect. Training a specialized reaction model for each humanoid embodiment can also be time-consuming and resource-intensive. Human-to-humanoid motion retargeting provides a more scalable alternative, allowing human-human reaction data to serve as a common motion representation for different humanoid embodiments. However, due to morphological and kinematic differences between humans and humanoid robots, a reaction preferred in human motion space may not be the most suitable one for execution on a particular robot embodiment.
  In this work, we propose an inference-time reaction search framework that leverages stochastic sampling from a generative reaction model and jointly considers reaction quality and humanoid embodiment feasibility. Given the observed interaction, our framework generates multiple plausible reaction candidates. Each candidate is retargeted to the target humanoid and evaluated using complementary interaction and embodiment-specific feasibility criteria, allowing candidate selection under the physical constraints of the target embodiment. Since the reaction generator remains frozen, the framework can adapt to different humanoid embodiments at inference time without retraining. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains overall human reaction quality while improving the feasibility of retargeted humanoid reactions across different embodiments. The proposed pipeline improves humanoid retargeting feasibility by 1.61%. Moreover, human-space and G1 best-candidate selections disagree in 78.98% of samples, demonstrating substantial embodiment dependence. Code will be released.

title: Do correct answers have stable latent knowledge support?
summary: Large language models are typically evaluated in terms of the correctness of their output. However, output correctness alone does not confirm whether the latent knowledge supporting an answer has stable internal representations. We therefore propose latent state stability (LSS) and knowledge topology stability (KTS) to investigate the stability of individual knowledge states and their relational structure, respectively. Specifically, we first separately average the model's internal representations of the same knowledge under each elicitation condition. Using the mean representation under the baseline condition as a reference, we remove shared shifts to obtain corrected representations. We then formulate LSS as the distance between each corrected representation and its reference representation, normalized against the typical distance between knowledge items of the same type. We formulate KTS as the cross-condition consistency of the ordered pairwise representation distances among knowledge items of the same type. Next, we construct EpiStableBench, which comprises 4,411 items spanning factual knowledge and mathematical reasoning, with 76,766 controlled queries. Across 16 LLMs from four families, representation stability varies substantially even among items answered correctly under the base condition. Within models, higher stability generally corresponds to higher accuracy under held-out elicitation conditions; across models, stability does not consistently increase with model size or overall accuracy. Meanwhile, we present LatentDPO to learn a knowledge-editing policy that accounts for the stability of latent knowledge. Experimental results show that integrating LatentDPO with multiple existing editing methods consistently improves editing success and generalization across different expressions.

title: GeoBridge: Evolving Transferable Decoder Topologies for Geometric Vision
summary: Depth estimation and Gaussian reconstruction share a need for multi-scale feature processing, yet use different prediction interfaces and training objectives. Whether a decoder's internal computation can be optimized once and reused across these systems remains a structural design question. Search over primitive configurations alone leaves the organization of transformations fixed. To address this gap, we propose GeoBridge, an evolutionary framework for transferable decoder topologies. First, GeoBridge makes stage-internal topology searchable through residual, sequential, and parallel composition of configurable primitives. Shape-preserving composition retains the stage interfaces of a fixed multi-scale scaffold. Second, a functional-tree encoding supports stage-aware crossover and hierarchical mutation, while a gradient sensitivity-alignment proxy evaluates candidates without training. Multi-objective evolution balances this proxy with computation and parameter cost. Third, selected topologies are instantiated and trained in target systems with task-specific prediction interfaces. A single source search takes approximately 12 GPU hours. GeoBridgeNet-A3 achieves the best depth accuracy among four adapted decoder baselines under a common encoder and training protocol on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI. The same topology reaches 27.11 dB PSNR in Gaussian novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K, and its refined representations support open-vocabulary segmentation on LERF. These results support decoder topology as a reusable design object across the evaluated geometric vision systems. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/EMI-Group/GeoBridge-NAS.

title: Imperfect Verifiers, Exact Targets: Inference-Time Scaling for Continuous Generation
summary: Verifier-guided inference-time scaling uses additional computation to score intermediate states and steer generation toward better outputs. However, imperfect intermediate verifiers can distort sampling, and repeated refinement alone does not ensure recovery of the desired reward-tilted distribution. We introduce Continuous-State Verifier-Guided Backtracking (CS-VGB), an inference-time scaling method for sampling from reward-tilted distributions with continuous generative models through repeated denoising and renoising. With correctly paired denoising and renoising transitions, the stationary distribution of CS-VGB at the clean checkpoint equals the desired reward-tilted target, even when intermediate verifiers are inaccurate. Under stated regularity conditions, CS-VGB converges exponentially to the target despite verifier error, and the expected number of updates needed to reach a clean sample grows only linearly with the number of checkpoints. In analytically tractable settings, we empirically demonstrate that CS-VGB recovers the desired reward-tilted distribution despite verifier error, whereas the compared verifier-based sampling methods fail to recover the target under the same verifier errors. We also instantiate the framework with diffusion models and one-step stochastic posterior maps. Across prompt-guided ImageNet generation, facial-attribute generation on CelebA, and multi-robot planning, recurrent CS-VGB search improves reward and task success as inference budgets grow, with image-generation rewards continuing beyond the observed plateaus of denoising-only baselines.

title: North or South? Diagnosing LLMs' Understanding of North Korean Language, Society, and Knowledge
comments: Accepted to AACL-IJCNLP 2026 (Main Conference). 19 pages, 1 figure, 11 tables
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made substantial progress in multilingual question answering, yet their ability to understand low-resource sociolinguistic contexts remains under-explored. We study North Korea as a unique testbed where decades of division have produced distinct differences from South Korea in vocabulary, orthography, norms, and ideological discourse. We introduce LENS (Language and sociocultural Evaluation for North Korean Society), a human-validated benchmark of 1,765 questions evaluating LLMs across three dimensions: linguistic robustness, sociocultural perspective alignment, and domain-specific knowledge. Evaluating diverse recent LLMs, we find a modest performance drop on North Korean language inputs, a larger gap in sociocultural perspective alignment, and severe limitations on domain-specific knowledge. Qualitative analysis reveals that models often conflate formal institutions with lived realities, project liberal-democratic assumptions, or rely on coarse stereotypes. Our results demonstrate that linguistic similarity alone does not guarantee sociocultural or domain-specific understanding, highlighting the critical need for grounded evaluation resources for underrepresented cultural and political contexts.
comment: Accepted to AACL-IJCNLP 2026 (Main Conference). 19 pages, 1 figure, 11 tables

title: FragFlex: Fragment-Based Flexible Molecular Generation for Exploring Vast Chemical Space
comments: 15 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap
summary: Drug discovery requires efficient exploration of an astronomically large chemical space. Molecular graph diffusion models offer a promising approach to this task, but many require graph size to be fixed before generation. Although atom-level insertion and deletion can enable flexible-size generation, jointly modeling molecular size, atom types, and bonds while maintaining chemical validity remains challenging. We introduce FragFlex, a flexible-length discrete diffusion model that performs node insertion and deletion at the fragment level. During denoising, FragFlex jointly learns the size, fragment identities, and inter-fragment connectivity of the fragment graph. A neural attachment-site predictor and valence-aware assembler then convert the generated fragment graph into an atom-level molecule. In large-scale experiments generating 10 million molecules, FragFlex achieves near-perfect chemical validity while maintaining high uniqueness, demonstrating a strong balance between the two.
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap

title: Retrieving Complementary Evidence for Multi-Hop RAG with Semantic Gain Graphs
summary: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires finding documents whose evidence is useful in combination. Query relevance and graph connectivity help locate related content, but neither directly measures the additional information one document contributes given another. We introduce SG$^2$RAG, a framework that represents this complementarity through semantic gain. Offline, a large language model assesses the relevant and nonredundant information contributed by one chunk given another within neighborhoods proposed by semantic similarity. These ordered assessments are aggregated into symmetric edge weights to construct a reusable Semantic Gain Graph. Online, controlled Personalized PageRank starts from query-relevant seeds and ranks complementary evidence beyond the initial retrieval set. Experiments on MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and HotpotQA with two language model backbones show that SG$^2$RAG achieves the best average EM, F1, and Recall@10 among the evaluated single-retrieval methods. Under identical candidate support and propagation, semantic gain improves average F1 and Recall@10 over similarity weighting by 4.08 and 4.31 points. Analyses of supporting documents and improvements in three iterative retrieval frameworks further support its effectiveness as a reusable retrieval component.

title: Protein Crystallization Segmentation and Classification Using Subordinate Color Channel in Fluorescence Microscopy Images
summary: The accuracy of detecting protein crystals for fluorescence microscopy images is very critical for high throughput and automated systems. Although the trace fluorescent labeling method could highlight protein crystals, reflection and emission from the fluorescence dye is not always due to crystal regions. Therefore, the analysis of the peak wavelength in the emission spectra of a fluorophore may not always yield effective results. In this paper, we show that using the subordinate color intensity corresponding to longer wavelengths than the peak wavelength of the emission spectra could improve the accuracy of protein crystal detection. Hence, we have built a segmentation method based on the percentile intensity of the subordinate color for trace fluorescently labeled (TFL'd) protein crystallization trial images. Compared to using the dominant color channel, our segmentation method on subordinate color channel was able to reduce the misclassification rate of likely-leads or crystals as non-crystals by the percentage of from 9.71% to 2.02% depending on the classifier. Similarly, the accuracy of classifiers were increased by the percentage of from 1.77% to 5.53%. Our method reached around 94% accuracy while keeping misclassification of likely-leads and crystals as non-crystals below 1%. Moreover, to evaluate the generalizability of our method, we have conducted new wet lab experiments on two proteins, Concanavalin A (Con A) and Ab inorganic pyrophosphate (AbIPPase), and the misclassification rate was below 1%. Our experiments show that using the subordinate channel may be more helpful for TFL'd protein trial image classification.

title: ASM-6D: Fast Certified Pose-Shape Inference with Complete Correspondence Flow Maps
summary: Category-level 6D pose and shape estimation requires recovering an object's pose and geometry from partial observations without an exact instance model. We present ASM-6D, which couples generative complete-geometry prediction with explicit category-level pose-shape inference through shared correspondences. Given an RGB-D image, ASM-6D generates alternative complete 3D correspondence hypotheses whose point identities are shared with a category-level Active Shape Model (ASM), including occluded points. Each hypothesis is fitted directly for rotation, translation, metric scale, and instance shape without a separate correspondence-assignment stage. We analytically eliminate translation and shape coefficients, reducing fitting to a nine-variable scaled-rotation optimization problem that enables efficient batched evaluation of multiple hypotheses in real time. ASM-6D achieves state-of-the-art performance on ROPE and HouseCat6D benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate the importance of generative correspondence prediction and active shape variation. The representation also supports shape completion, shape-dependent pose ambiguity, tracking, and robotic grasping at 6-38 Hz, depending on the inference budget.

title: Policy Improvement From Private Information For Decentralized LQG Teams
summary: Sharing of information in multiagent systems allow for improved coordination. Delays in communication can cause asymmetries in information, causing classical results to fail. We study the decentralized LQG problem with delayed information. In general, the optimal policies are not linear and are difficult to calculate. Restricting to linear policies, we analytically calculate the gradient descent for gains from private information. This naturally lends itself to a gradient descent algorithm which we apply to examples to show policy improvements.

title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation
summary: We present Co-DSL, a framework in which users and LLMs co-design reusable spatial concepts for layout generation. In the first stage, our system allows users to create a library of personalized operations. To add a concept, a user provides a description, which the LLM converts into an initial implementation. The user can then observe the concept's execution behavior over example scenarios and provide lightweight feedback to the LLM, which revises the concept's implementation logic. In the second stage, given a library, an LLM can author a layout program that meets a new layout request from a user. Executing a layout program instantiates a concept-graph, a declarative composition of library concepts. In this way, we require the LLM only to specify which concepts should hold, while we use a solver to search for a layout that satisfies them. Across five spatial layout domains, we find that Co-DSL libraries let LLMs capture layout patterns that are challenging for prior fixed-operation systems, and demonstrate that our concept-graph representation is needed for LLMs to reliably compose concepts together. We further find that Co-DSL lets LLMs author generative layout programs that expose high-level parametric controls users can manipulate to explore a distribution of related layouts without re-prompting.

title: OntoAR-HAR: Ontology-Guided Agentic RAG with Personalized Memory for Human Activity Recognition
summary: LLMs increasingly support sensor-based human activity recognition (HAR) by linking motion signals with activity semantics and physical knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds decisions in sensor examples and domain features, enabling training-free target-user inference with less dependence on raw numerical arrays. However, existing LLM/RAG-based HAR typically searches single-level activity spaces using static population knowledge. Consequently, they compare many unrelated candidates using the same static population evidence and overlook personalized motion patterns. We propose OntoAR-HAR, an ontology-guided agentic RAG framework combining static population and personalized knowledge. Its tree-structured activity ontology decomposes classification into local decisions among semantically related activities. The static store supplies node-constrained examples, while offline-discovered executable signal features provide numerical evidence for local distinctions. During inference, the personalized store collects selected user observations, which the LLM integrates with static knowledge and signal features while traversing the ontology to an activity label. Cross-subject and heterogeneous-sensing experiments show complementary gains from hierarchical retrieval and personalized memory across multiple LLM backbones, achieving state-of-the-art performance. By explicitly modeling hierarchical relations across activity granularities, OntoAR-HAR also addresses the long-overlooked semantic inclusion problem and avoids treating related labels as independent categories.

title: ProWorld: Multi-View World Model with Proprioceptive Feedback for Closed-Loop Policy Evaluation
summary: Evaluating robot manipulation policies through repeated physical trials is costly. We study whether an action-conditioned world model can serve as a closed-loop test environment whose policy success rates track those on real robots. Beyond realistic video, the model must return the camera views and proprioceptive state needed for the policy's next action and preserve failed-action outcomes to avoid overestimating policy capability. We introduce ProWorld, a world model that jointly predicts multi-view video and robot state, then feeds both back to a frozen policy for repeated interaction. ProWorld comprises a shared transformer for joint video-state flow prediction and Shared-Time View Encoding to distinguish cameras while preserving temporal synchronization. To reduce interaction hallucinations that turn missed grasps into successful lifts, we augment training with failed interactions collected in high-fidelity simulation, reducing inflated success rates in the generated environment. ProWorld achieves the highest overall TriWorldBench score among the compared methods. Across three policies and four local manipulation tasks, it attains a Pearson correlation of 0.95 and a Spearman correlation of 0.94 between generated and real success rates. These results support joint visual-proprioceptive feedback and failure-aware training as a basis for world-model-based policy evaluation.

title: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models
summary: Recently, AutoRegressive Visual Generation (ARVG) models have emerged as a competitive paradigm for high-quality image synthesis. However, their substantial computational and memory demands make them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices. Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) provides a promising solution to reduce the computational and memory costs of ARVG models, yet existing methods often suffer from substantial image quality degradation under low-bit quantization. In this paper, we propose a training-free PTQ framework for ARVG, consisting of Tail-Aware Bounded-init Grid Refinement (T-BGR) and Coarse-to-Fine Activation Precision Scheduling (CAPS). T-BGR introduces a tail-aware reconstruction objective for weight quantizer calibration, assigning greater importance to distribution-tail coefficients and preserving fine-grained information without introducing additional parameters or high-precision branches. CAPS performs coarse-to-fine activation precision scheduling by jointly considering the importance and computational cost of different generation stages, enabling efficient mixed-precision allocation under a given bit budget. Extensive experiments on multiple ARVG backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently improves robustness under aggressive low-bit quantization. Notably, on Infinity, our framework achieves near full-precision image generation quality at an effective W4A5.6 activation precision, while existing methods at W4A6 still exhibit noticeable quality degradation or inconsistent performance. Code is available at https://github.com/lxm-lc/HGA-Quant.

title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition
summary: Large language models (LLMs) offer a new approach to wearable-sensor-based human activity recognition. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further introduces similar motion examples and discriminative sensor knowledge, enabling decisions grounded in observations relevant to the current query. More evidence, however, does not necessarily mean better-organized evidence. When online prompts and LLM agents primarily orchestrate inference, decisions about which activities to compare and when to invoke discriminative knowledge remain concentrated at inference time. As the activity vocabulary grows, the model must repeatedly process more candidates and associated knowledge, whereas pruning candidates too early risks excluding the true activity. We propose confusion-hierarchy evidence-aware reasoning (CHEAR), which moves part of this knowledge organization offline. CHEAR constructs and validates an activity hierarchy from recurrent cross-subject retrieval errors and builds corresponding activity-pair knowledge. At inference time, the hierarchy orders candidate comparisons; the LLM retains candidates progressively, and local discriminative knowledge is accessed only for the remaining activities. Across eight datasets, CHEAR achieves 86.79\% mean cross-subject accuracy, a 75.91\% candidate reduction rate, and 96.44\% true-activity retention. Per-sample token use is 85.15\% lower on average than in a variant without the hierarchical structure. Mean accuracy across eight cross-dataset transfer directions is 88.81\%. These results show that organizing candidates and discriminative knowledge around observed activity confusions reduces online LLM input while maintaining recognition performance.

title: WisdomNet: trustable machine learning toward error-free classification
summary: Misclassification is a critical problem in many machine learning applications. Since even the classifier models with high accuracy (e.g., > 95%) still introduce some misclassification error, it may not be possible to rely on the output of a classifier. In this paper, we introduce trustable learning, which prompts the learning model to yield only the true output, thus avoiding misclassifications. Whenever the model cannot decide the output accurately, the learning model should indicate that there could be a misclassification error if it is forced to classify, and hence, it should reject to make a decision or defer it to a human expert. Therefore, we develop a methodology for trustable learning and apply it to artificial neural networks and show that it is possible to develop a classifier with 0% misclassification error. We propose a novel neural network architecture named WisdomNet that could provide zero prediction error by introducing an additional neuron named as conjugate neuron that would indicate whether the network is able to classify the data correctly or not. The WisdomNet architecture can be applied to any previously built model, and we have evaluated WisdomNet with several network architectures such as multilayer perceptron, convolutional neural network, and deep network on different data sets. The results show that the WisdomNet is able to reduce the classification error rate to 0%, while labeling the data is difficult to classify as `reject' at a low percentage of within around 10%.

title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
summary: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter's normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.

title: RM-WAM: Reliable Memory-Augmented World Action Models for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, yet most existing methods make decisions primarily from the current observation. This limits their reliability in long-horizon tasks, where visually similar states may correspond to different interaction histories and task stages. Moreover, directly incorporating historical observations can introduce stale, stage-mismatched, or error-contaminated information, leading to inaccurate world prediction and accumulated closed-loop errors. We propose RM-WAM, a reliable memory-augmented World Action Model that treats memory as a context-dependent predictive resource rather than universally useful historical context. RM-WAM represents history using complementary short-term visual state memory and latent event memory, which respectively capture recent interaction dynamics and longer-term state transitions. A counterfactual memory learning scheme varies the accessible history while keeping the current inputs and prediction targets fixed, enabling the model to learn a context-dependent utility estimate for historical memory. Based on this estimate, a utility-aware gating mechanism adaptively controls memory injection into the world-action backbone. Experiments demonstrate that RM-WAM highlights the importance of reliable and selective memory utilization in long-horizon tasks.

title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design
comments: This manuscript has been submitted to IEEE journal
summary: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.
comment: This manuscript has been submitted to IEEE journal

title: FENAS: A Few-Shot Meta-Ensembling Framework for Efficient Neural Architecture Search with Synergized Zero-Cost Proxies
summary: Efficient neural architecture search (NAS) requires accurate performance estimation under limited evaluation budgets. Existing zero-cost proxies (ZCPs) provide fast training-free signals, but each proxy usually captures only a partial property of an architecture, leading to unstable rankings across datasets and search spaces. In contrast, GNN-based predictors can improve accuracy, but often depend on labeled architectures, graph encoders, and costly representation learning, which makes them less suitable for extreme few-shot settings. We propose FENAS, a topology-agnostic few-shot prediction framework that turns complementary initialization priors into robust ranking signals. Its core component, CAST, is a feature pipeline that combines copula alignment and synergy transformation. CAST maps heterogeneous ZCPs into a compact feature manifold, enabling lightweight meta-learners to produce reliable rankings from scarce supervision. On NAS-Bench-201, with only 0.5% labeled samples, FENAS achieves a Kendall's Tau ($τ$) of 0.70, outperforming representative topology-based few-shot predictors in this low-label regime. In closed-domain search, FENAS evaluates the NAS-Bench-201 space in approximately 1138 seconds and achieves competitive test accuracy. By providing a fast, reliable, and structurally simple evaluation mechanism, FENAS supports the design of automated neural architectures under limited evaluation budgets.

title: An Open MuJoCo Simulation Framework for a Quadrotor Carrying a Tendon-Driven Soft Continuum Arm
summary: Combining aerial robots with soft continuum manipulators promises safe, compliant interaction with the environment, but the coupled dynamics of a free-flying base and a highly deformable, underactuated arm are difficult to study without a suitable simulator. This paper describes an open-source simulation framework, built on the MuJoCo physics engine, for a quadrotor that carries a tendon-driven soft continuum arm underneath its body. The arm is modelled as a pseudo-rigid-body chain of twelve segments joined by pairs of orthogonal compliant hinges. Three tendons, spaced \SI{120}{\degree} apart and routed through every segment, bend it in any direction. A geometric tracking controller on $SE(3)$ flies the vehicle; its rotor allocation matrix is generated directly from the model description. A closed-form tendon-tension allocation keeps every tension within its limits and gives the same bending moment in every direction. We report the full set of modelling choices and parameters, and we evaluate the framework in four simulated scenarios: a \SI{36}{\second} mission with a figure-eight and a tendon-driven tip sweep, an attitude-gain study, a quasi-static characterization of the bending workspace, and an impulsive disturbance applied to the arm tip. With the nominal gains the vehicle tracks the mission with \SI{3.1}{\centi\meter} RMS position error while the arm tip swings up to \SI{37}{\centi\meter} from the body axis. The gain study shows that a low-bandwidth attitude loop lets the arm excite sustained oscillations. The simulation runs about $15\times$ faster than real time on a laptop CPU. All models, controllers and scripts that reproduce the figures are released.

title: Cost-Aware Conflict Triage for xApp Control Conflicts in Open RAN
summary: Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN) enables multi-vendor deployments where concurrent RAN control applications (xApps) independently optimise mobility, load, coverage, and energy within the Near Real Time RAN Intelligent Controller (Near-RT RIC). When xApps act on overlapping control parameters, their isolated loops produce conflicting decisions that degrade the network Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Existing conflict-evaluation methods estimate severity but do not answer whether the intervention is cost-justified. This paper proposes a cost-aware conflict triage framework that pairs ECDF-based severity evaluation with an event-level decision layer. The framework groups detected conflict records into episodes, extracts nine features, estimates per-mechanism costs and benefits, and assigns one of three actions: tolerate, defer, or mitigate. Evaluated in a simulator-driven Open RAN setting over 30 Monte Carlo runs with four concurrent xApps, the framework defers 66.8 %, mitigates 19.8 %, and tolerates 13.4 % of detected episodes, achieving a mean net utility of 0.132 per intervention, 3.9x higher than an always-mitigate baseline, by avoiding low- value interventions through cost-aware selectivity.

title: Accuracy and Uncertainty in Machine Deception Detection (Research White Paper)
summary: A deception detector is only as useful as the trust its alarms deserve. Like a polygraph, detectors that read a language model's internal activations can catch deceptive responses that look honest. Yet current detectors depend on which layers they read, weaken on broader tests, and do not state how certain their alarms are. This white paper proposes the Machine Deception Detector, which targets both detection accuracy and the uncertainty of detector scores. The detector reads every layer of the language model, learns which tokens carry evidence of deception using only response labels, and calibrates its alarm threshold so that its false--positive rate stays below a prescribed level. An ensemble of such detectors measures the uncertainty of each score and raises an alarm only when its members agree, with a confidence level that sets how certain each alarm must be. The proposed evaluation trains on instructed honest and deceptive statements, tests on five unseen deceptive tasks of Liars' Bench read by six Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B parameters, and is designed to also show which layers carry the deception feature and how this changes with model size.

title: ArguScale: Evidence-Grounded Human-AI Sensemaking Across Concurrent Live Conversations
summary: Monitoring concurrent classroom collaborative reasoning discussions is challenging because instructors have to track collaboration-relevant behaviors across multiple ongoing conversations at once. Existing Human-AI conversational sensemaking systems can scale monitoring upward through summaries and visual abstractions, but these representations may distance users from underlying conversational evidence, e.g., relevant audio and transcript segments, needed to forage downward. Through our formative study, we developed ArguScale, an evidence-grounded Human-AI sensemaking system that organizes interactional signals into temporally aligned representations linked to transcript and audio evidence. A temporal signal-density view provides temporal context and supports rapid cross-group comparison, while selective evidence access allows instructors to inspect audio and transcript. We evaluated ArguScale in a mixed-design study with 20 participants. Compared to other conditions, ArguScale improved participants' ability to efficiently and accurately identify collaboration-relevant cues. We further identify strategies participants used to forage for and make sense of conversational evidence under live time constraints.

title: Channel Match: Calibrating Shape Latents for Few-Step 3D Generation
summary: Recent native 3D generators achieve high-quality asset creation by modeling structured 3D latents with flow-based transformers, but their high-resolution generation remains computationally expensive due to costly iterative sampling. In this work, we introduce a few-step distillation framework for native 3D generation, enabled by continuous self-consistency training with a custom JVP FlashAttention kernel and an analytic velocity regression objective for sparse structured 3D latents. To stabilize joint optimization, we further introduce an adaptive loss weighting strategy that automatically balances them without manual tuning. Beyond acceleration, we reveal a previously overlooked failure mode of few-step native 3D generation: sampling-induced latent distribution drift preserves geometric correctness but disrupts downstream PBR texture synthesis, causing texture artifacts on geometrically valid assets. To address this issue, we propose Channel Match, a training-free adaptive per-channel latent calibration method that restores the latent distribution without modifying either generator. We validate our approach on TRELLIS.2 at the $1024^3$ resolution setting. Our two-step model achieves $4.5\times$ faster geometry sampling while maintaining geometry quality comparable to the many-step teacher, and Channel Match further improves rendering quality by recovering the latent interface between geometry and appearance generation.

title: SuperAI: Merging Capabilities Across Heterogeneous Foundation Models
summary: Enabling the reuse and composition of knowledge and capabilities distributed across foundation models is an important step toward building scalable artificial intelligence (AI) systems. However, architectural differences and incompatible representations make it difficult to transfer and integrate these capabilities through a unified cross-model interface. To address this challenge, we propose SuperAI, a cross-architecture multi-model fusion framework that integrates complementary capabilities from multiple source models into a host model through orthogonal alignment of low-dimensional task-relevant representations.
