title: On Measures of Dissimilarity on the Majorization Simplex
summary: The majorization simplex $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of probability vectors of length $n$ whose entries are arranged in non-increasing order. Under the majorization order, $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a lattice, and it is the natural space for comparing distributions when the labels of the outcomes are not relevant. In this work, we study measures of dissimilarity (and, similarity) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. Our first set of results concerns the Rényi-entropy based distance $d_α(p,q)=H_α(p)+H_α(q)-2H_α(p\vee q)$ proposed by Yadav and Shkel (2026), which generalizes a metric of Cicalese, Gargano and Vaccaro (2013). We show that $d_α$ is a metric on $\mathcal{P}_n$ for $α\in[1,\infty)$, while for $α\in[0,1)\cup\{\infty\}$, $d_α$ is not a metric in general. Our main result in this part identifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in the triangle inequality of $d_α$ when $α>1$, for which we identify the equality conditions for the supermodularity of the Rényi entropy $H_α$. Our second set of results concerns the total variation distance and the Hellinger affinity (also called the Bhattacharyya coefficient) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. We obtain a number of bounds on these measures, along with some of their equality conditions. The resulting Hellinger affinity based upper bound on the total variation distance can be smaller than the bounds obtained from Pinsker's and the Bretagnolle--Huber inequalities.

title: EHR-Bench: A Chinese Multi-Task Benchmark for Recruitment AI
summary: Recruitment applications span diverse operations, from drafting job descriptions and interpreting queries to organizing profiles, assessing fit, and recommending candidates and jobs. Systematic LLM evaluation therefore requires task coverage that reflects this range of business needs. We introduce EHR-Bench, an open Chinese benchmark comprising twelve tasks across six capability families and five recruitment scenarios. The tasks cover generation, extraction, classification, retrieval, semantic similarity, and reciprocal ranking within one evaluation framework. An internal recruitment dataset guides task definitions, the occupation taxonomy and sampling targets, output requirements, and scoring protocols. Following these specifications, we construct 8,336 task instances from public materials and controlled augmentation, with source-aware expert review and documented provenance. We evaluate twelve LLMs through task-level, capability-level, and aggregate comparisons. Closely ranked models exhibit distinct task strengths, and performance varies across input sources, reference evidence, and candidate pools. Five shared models retain the same observed Overall ordering on a private operational reference, with variation in capability and task correspondence. EHR-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for systematic model assessment, task-specific model selection, and further research on LLMs for recruitment. The project repository is available at https://github.com/EhrBench/EHR-Bench.

title: StageBreaker: Shifting Video RL Post-Training Scheduling from Stages down to Data Dependencies
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has emerged as the key paradigm for improving autoregressive video models. Emerging vision-language reward models further strengthen post-training with accurate rewards, but their long chain-of-thought inference substantially raises the associated costs, while the pursuit of long videos prolongs policy training. Despite these rising costs, existing video RL systems still adopt coarse-grained stage-centric execution, which stalls policy training until all reward evaluation finishes, replays every trajectory twice due to a further barrier within policy training, and induces load imbalance across GPUs. To address the challenges, we propose StageBreaker, a fine-grained data-dependency-driven scheduling framework, which schedules the true dataflow of an RL step rather than its stages. Specifically, StageBreaker overlaps policy training with reward evaluation by exploiting reward-separable policy training, and merges the two trajectory replays into one by leveraging loss-independent back-propagation. It further balances GPU load by scheduling computation at the finer granularity. Our evaluation results show that StageBreaker achieves a speedup of up to 1.41$\times$ over stage-centric execution.

title: 3D-VITAL: Visibility-aware Identity Training from Artificial Liftings of 3D Reconstruction model for Cross-View Object Re-Identification
summary: We address the Cross-View Object Re-Identification (ReID) task, aiming to match identities across drastically different viewpoints. We focus on Single-View Aerial-Ground ReID (SV AG-ReID), where models train on one viewpoint and must generalize to another at inference. To bridge this viewpoint gap, related work employs generative models to synthesize novel views from source images as additional training data. We leverage recent advances in large-scale single-view 3D mesh reconstruction to lift source images into textured meshes and to render them from new viewpoints. However, this pipeline produces unreliable data in two distinct ways. First, the reconstruction may fail and produce geometrically incorrect meshes, resulting in severe corruption in rendered novel views. Second, even when the geometry is correct, the rendered novel views contain hallucinated textures in regions not visible in the source image. The reconstructed mesh carries a per-pixel partition between regions visible from the source view and regions that the reconstruction model had to hallucinate, available as a deterministic byproduct of rendering. We introduce this per-pixel visibility map and exploit it in a two-stage design. Cross-View Consistency Filtering (CVCF) discards geometrically incorrect meshes by ensuring multi-view consistency between source and novel views over visible patches. Visibility-Aware Attention Supervision (VAAS) leverages the visibility map to guide the model's attention toward reliable regions of the rendered view during training. Combined, these two components enable our method, 3D-VITAL, to better leverage the synthetic signal from single-view 3D mesh reconstruction. 3D-VITAL sets a new state-of-the-art on three SV AG-ReID benchmarks. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/TurtleSmoke/3D-VITAL.

title: Feature-Context Consistency: Unsupervised Adversarial Detection with Drift Stability on Attributed Graphs
summary: Adversarial detection on evolving attributed graphs faces two challenges: fraud labels arrive late or not at all, and natural distributional drift erodes any trained decision boundary. Modern detectors can reach strong detection rates when labels are available and the distribution is stationary; sustaining that quality without labels and under drift is the open problem. We identify feature-context consistency -- the alignment between a node's attributes and its aggregated neighborhood attributes -- as a single structural signal that addresses both. We formalize it as the Context Boost (CB) score within a Restricted Boltzmann Machine framework (CB-RBM) and prove two complementary worst-case guarantees: a strict separation between the expected CB of legitimate and adversarial nodes, with gap growing linearly in model capacity, whenever the adversary's context stays far enough from legitimate neighborhood context; and a Wasserstein-Lipschitz bound on how far the CB distribution moves under natural drift. We validate on XBlock Ethereum phishing (~153K nodes) and Reddit banned-user detection (~11K nodes), with two further datasets in the appendix spanning diverse domains. With zero labels, CB-RBM achieves AUROC >= 0.96 on four adversarial attacks and keeps FPR close to its calibrated 5% target under drift -- outperforming supervised GNNs (hundreds of labels), unsupervised graph-anomaly baselines, and a standard RBM whose FPR collapses to 89-100%. What typically requires separate mechanisms -- label-free operation and drift stability -- here follows from a single structural regularity of the data. Code: https://github.com/serval-uni-lu/CB-RBM.

title: Belief Space Planning for Risk Signal Temporal Logic via Mixed-Integer Convex Programming
summary: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifies robot tasks with spatio-temporal requirements, and its robustness semantics allow planning by trajectory optimization. In practice, robots estimate their state from noisy measurements, and when the information gained from a measurement depends on the state, the robot can actively reduce its uncertainty by planning in the belief space. The resulting problem is, however, generally non-convex, for which gradient-based methods are neither complete nor globally optimal. In this paper, we consider Risk STL (RiSTL) planning in Gaussian belief space and show that an information-form parameterization of the belief, together with a convex relaxation of the belief dynamics, yields a mixed-integer convex program (MICP). We prove that the MICP is sound and complete, and that the relaxation preserves the globally optimal input trajectories. We validate the effectiveness of our method in numerical simulations.

title: GQL Datatypes as an RDF Vocabulary
comments: 13 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for DMKG 2026 (2nd International Workshop on Data Management for Knowledge Graphs), Bari, Italy
summary: The ISO GQL standard introduces a rich value-type system for property graphs, including scalar, temporal, byte-string, list, record, and dynamic union datatypes. The vocabulary presented here additionally covers a vector extension. At the same time, RDF-based knowledge graph systems identify literal datatypes by IRIs and interpret typed literals through value spaces, lexical spaces, and lexical-to-value mappings. This paper presents the GQL Datatypes RDF Vocabulary, a lightweight RDF vocabulary that represents selected GQL datatypes and the vector extension as RDF datatype IRIs and describes their hierarchy, aliases, and selected constraints using RDF, RDFS, OWL, and XML Schema Datatypes vocabulary terms. The vocabulary is intended to support interoperability between GQL-oriented property graph systems and RDF-based knowledge graph systems. We describe its namespace and datatype model, summarize its datatype coverage, and show how the accompanying generator and validator use the vocabulary. In the reference implementation, RDF literals retain GQL datatype IRIs; XSD mappings declared in the vocabulary support scalar validation, while lists, records, and vectors are encoded directly as JSON lexical forms of vocabulary-typed literals.
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for DMKG 2026 (2nd International Workshop on Data Management for Knowledge Graphs), Bari, Italy

title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
summary: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
summary: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.

title: Attention-Graph Curvature for the Verification of Mathematical Reasoning
comments: Accepted at the 6th Workshop on Mathematical Reasoning and AI (MATH-AI), NeurIPS 2026
summary: Language models have recently solved open Erdős problems and achieved gold-medal level performance on International Mathematical Olympiad problems. But their solutions, written in natural language, cannot yet be verified by proof assistants. An erroneous reasoning step can invalidate every step that comes after, so it is advantageous to detect errors early. Several methods have been proposed to detect erroneous reasoning quickly based on the features of the forward pass of the language model that performs reasoning. In this work, we study whether the directed Forman curvature of that model's attention graph, a local quantity computed at an edge from the attention weights around it, carries information about a step's correctness. To do so, we evaluate four per-step verifiers on ProcessBench with and without the curvature appended to their input. Appending curvature values improves the overall mean performance of all four verifiers. ReProbe, the verifier that takes every token of a step as input, shows the largest improvement. Adding the curvature increases the time of the language model's forward pass by 18% on average.
comment: Accepted at the 6th Workshop on Mathematical Reasoning and AI (MATH-AI), NeurIPS 2026

title: Audit Before You Distill: A Controlled Workflow for Reasoning Transfer into Compact Medical Language Models
summary: Teacher rationales can help a smaller model answer health professions questions, but they can also reinforce errors. We examined when they help and how this evidence can guide training using Brazilian Portuguese questions from medical and multiprofessional residency examinations. First, we measured how a teacher rationale changed the student's probability of selecting the correct answer and compared this effect with rationales drawn from other questions. The complete rationale increased this probability by 21~p.p. when the teacher was correct and decreased it by 14~p.p. when the teacher was wrong. By intervening on the reasoning content, we showed that shuffled rationales did not produce the same pattern. Guided by this result, we trained only with rationales attached to correct teacher answers and compared answer-only training, step-by-step distillation, and our proposed Distill-SFT method. Distill-SFT showed a modest advantage over step-by-step distillation on previously missed questions under reasoning, while using fewer training instances by combining the answer and rationale into a single target. We also investigated catastrophic forgetting using the out-of-domain ENEM dataset. Answer-only training reduced reasoning accuracy by 12~p.p. relative to baseline, compared with approximately 4~p.p. for either rationale-based training method. Together, these findings support a workflow that audits rationale content before distillation, verifies teacher answers before supervision, and trains compact models efficiently for health professions question answering.

title: The Online Steinitz Problem
summary: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small. We first obtain deterministic prefix-discrepancy bounds of $O(\log T)$ for $d=1$ and $O(\sqrt T)$ for $d\ge2$. Our main contribution is a general reduction that converts deterministic and randomized online vector-balancing algorithms, which assign signs to arriving vectors, into online ordering algorithms. Combined with recent vector-balancing results, this yields a randomized algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log T+\sqrt{d\log T})$ and running time $O(dT\log T)$. The guarantee holds with high probability against an oblivious adversary. The reduction also gives bounds for sparse vectors and extends to inputs in arbitrary compact convex bodies. Finally, we prove matching lower bounds in both the deterministic and randomized cases.

title: What Is the "Self" of a Large Language Model?
summary: What could the "self" of a large language model be, if it is neither a particular word nor a single privileged layer? We propose a relational account: a functional self is an actor-centered organization of information that distinguishes the model's recorded actions from externally supplied material while content and reasoning operations change. Its representational candidate is a family of layer-specific source-binding components, rather than one unchanged vector throughout the network. Preliminary observations from a 27B BF16 model provide a geometric starting point. Across 150 matched message bodies, 450 role conditions, and a 75/75 discovery-held-out split, the combined Assistant-versus-external displacement transfers strongly across bodies and positions. Selected early components place User and System closer to one another than to Assistant, whereas this full-space distance relation does not persist throughout depth. These findings motivate a layered account: an early source-encoding candidate can be combined with role-specific information use and continuation preparation at later depths, without requiring monotonic overwriting of the common displacement. We connect this account to dynamic reasoning, historical continuity, and a computational model separating content operations, source binding, authority, and output. The reported evidence establishes a reproducible role-conditioned geometry; the proposed interpretation is that functional selfhood may reside in persistent relations among changing representations.

title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
summary: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

title: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents
comments: 25 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/ti-mm/LearnFromMove ; Benchmark and training data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/LatentGUIWorld
summary: Existing benchmarks for GUI agents primarily focus on increasing task difficulty by extending task horizons. Besides, enabling agents to explore unfamiliar environments and successfully complete tasks within them is also a critical yet challenging problem. We introduce LatentGUIWorld, a benchmark of six tasks in three matched pairs organized by the evidence needed for control: $I_0$ uses prior knowledge and available observations, $I_1$ requires interaction that directly reveals hidden semantics, and $I_2$ identifies dynamics from action-response relationships. Frontier models struggle especially on $I_2$ tasks. We introduce MOVE, which separates movement from button events and exposes intermediate visual feedback, together with demonstrations of iterative exploration and control. Ablations show that both action granularity and multi-step demonstrations improve performance. After SFT, LatentLearner-9B achieves 50.0% overall success on LatentGUIWorld, comparable to several frontier models. Joint RL further raises egocentric Drag and Ten-Choice success to 92.0% and 75.3%. Behavioral analysis reveals multi-step exploration. In egocentric Drag, RL increases Pearson correlation between error-normalized commands and ideal gain compensation from 0.610 to 0.803. Together, these behaviors show that models learn to explore through interaction and adapt their control to environment dynamics. The same format improves GUI grounding after RL, reaching 67.37% mean accuracy across five benchmarks versus 66.72% for conventional RL.
comment: 25 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/ti-mm/LearnFromMove ; Benchmark and training data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenMOSS-Team/LatentGUIWorld

title: Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
summary: Visual contrastive decoding corrects answers using the prediction difference between the original image and a reference condition, yet the same contrast also turns supported abstentions into incorrect answers. We find that abstentions are lost at two stages: contrastive decoding with candidate filtering can exclude the abstention token before any comparison takes place, and the reference branch's response to the abstention instruction is removed when the reference prediction is subtracted. We therefore propose instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the effect of the abstention instruction on the original-image prediction intact while leaving the contrast strength freely adjustable. Using a perturbed image and an image-free prediction as references, we obtain IP-VCD and IP-M3ID. On decision utility (DU), which credits both correct answers and supported abstentions, both methods outperform all compared non-IP baselines on every one of nine models on VizWiz, and IP-VCD also leads on eight of nine models on Food-101. Candidate measurements and paired per-question comparisons show that computing the instruction effect and the visual contrast term separately lets contrastive decoding support both correct answers and supported abstentions.

title: Matrix algebras with orthogonal Cauchy-like transforms and Toeplitz approximation: a negative result
summary: We consider newly designed matrix algebras associated with Cauchy orthogonal transforms. In this work, we are interested in checking the approximation of Toeplitz matrices using algebras of matrices, where each matrix is diagonalized by a fixed Cauchy orthogonal transform, in the spirit of fast algorithm based on preconditioning. We use the Korovkin theory for checking the Toeplitz approximability. Unfortunately and somehow surprisingly, the Korovkin test is negative, in contrast with the successful test for all the Fourier-like and trigonometric algebras, widely used in the relevant literature. More in detail, for the Cauchy algebras, the Frobenius optimal approximation fails to lead to the desired clustering, as also confirmed by ad hoc numerical experiments. It remains open to understand which kind of structured matrices can be approximated by these new algebras.

title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision
summary: Improving an LLM agent requires knowing what to change when it fails. Similar failures can require different fixes, and resolving one problem can expose another. We introduce Trace-to-Architecture (T2A), a framework that uses execution trajectories to determine what to change in an agent's harness and when those changes apply. A development agent diagnoses failures using execution evidence from successful and failed tasks, revises the corresponding harness components, and then checks whether target tasks improve, selected successful tasks remain successful, and the edits are actually triggered. New execution evidence guides subsequent diagnosis and revision. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld, T2A achieves the highest aggregate score for all three evaluated task agents, exceeding their respective strongest baselines by 6.2--30.3 points. We also integrate T2A's diagnosis and validation procedures into Meta-Harness, improving the resulting harnesses' mean ScienceWorld score by 21.6 points from the same starting harness.

title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service
summary: The rapid advancement of foundation models and edge intelligence is transforming wireless networks from data-oriented communication systems into artificial intelligence (AI)-native service platforms. Token communications (TokenCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm that directly transmits task-oriented AI representations. However, existing studies typically assume that generated tokens can be transmitted immediately, overlooking the queueing dynamics arising from the mismatch between token workload generation and time-varying wireless service capability. To address this limitation, we introduce Queue-Aware TokenCom, which explicitly incorporates token queues into the AI service pipeline. We present an end-to-end architecture integrating AI representation generation, token workload management, wireless transmission, and downstream task inference. We then discuss two key design directions: budget-aware token representation optimization and queue-aware token service optimization, with the token budget serving as a critical interface between AI performance and communication efficiency. Moreover, we investigate fixed and adaptive token budget strategies to characterize the fundamental tradeoff between AI performance and communication efficiency in dynamic wireless environments. Finally, we outline research directions toward closed-loop, task-aware, and scalable TokenCom systems.

title: PathPilot: An Adaptive Question-Conditioned Multi-Magnification Navigation Agent for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
summary: The diagnostic capability of WSI agents relies on effective slide navigation to identify diagnostically relevant regions and efficiently integrate evidence across the slide. While in clinical practice, pathologists dynamically examine slides across multiple scales, integrating global and cellular evidence in a sequential manner, existing AI navigation approaches mostly operate at a single fixed magnification or rely on predefined magnification traversal. This mismatch prevents existing methods from modeling cross-magnification interactions and adaptive magnification selection inherent to real diagnostic workflows. We propose PathPilot, a clinically consistent multi-magnification WSI navigation agent that explicitly models cross-magnification localization and evidence-adaptive exploration. Specifically, we introduce a CrossMagLoc that learns magnification-specific diagnostic localization from pathologist viewing behavior and integrates information from adjacent magnifications to identify the diagnostically most relevant region within the current ROI, thereby providing a diagnostically informed starting point for subsequent question-conditioned exploration. We further introduce an EviRegionSearch that starts question-conditioned exploration from this region, progressively accumulating question-relevant evidence and adaptively determining the next navigation action according to the remaining evidence requirement. Their iterative interaction enables PathPilot to sequentially explore across ROIs and magnifications until sufficient evidence is acquired. Extensive QA evaluations across five cohorts demonstrate consistent superiority over competing SOTA methods on inter/external cohorts, respectively, validating question-conditioned evidence acquisition across regions and magnifications that mirrors the sequential, knowledge-driven navigation of pathologists.

title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization
summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards commonly assigns one sequence advantage to an entire response. This outcome-level signal distinguishes overall response quality but leaves changes in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit. We introduce VAttnPO (Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization), which uses answer-conditioned visual attention to refine token-level credit while preserving the verifier-derived trajectory-mean advantage. A frozen old policy constructs a visual reference by teacher forcing the known correct answer and produces a visual distribution for each rollout token. VAttnPO measures their agreement in visual-attention space using Jensen--Shannon divergence, rather than reading guidance from teacher output-token distributions or introducing an attention-matching objective. Trajectory centering, relative-position weighting, and credit balancing turn this agreement into a zero-mean, position-aware correction to the GRPO sequence advantage. Token intervention, visual-index permutation, and trajectory analysis provide diagnostic evidence linking this signal to model behavior, visual correspondence, and generation position. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, VAttnPO raises six-task image AVE from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50 and scores higher on every reported structured, video, and MME metric. Gains over GRPO also hold on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3-8B-Instruct.

title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
summary: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.

title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
summary: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

title: Before Attention Sinks Form: Hidden-State Geometry Reveals and Modulates Their Formation
summary: Attention sinks are usually studied after they have formed. We ask whether a measurable hidden-state change appears beforehand and whether changing that geometry alters what happens later. To remove network depth as a shortcut, we compare prompts in the same model and at the same layer. When sink timing varies across prompts, simple spectral summaries of the hidden states add information beyond current attention, with the clearest prompt-specific signal in a short window about two to three layers before sink formation. The predictive strength varies across cohorts, so we treat the spectrum as a readout of a pre-sink state change rather than a universal warning statistic. The signal is broader than one measured extreme activation. We then modify only the singular values of the post-layer hidden states after current attention has already been computed. These interventions change later sink behavior in Qwen2.5, GLM-Z1, and GPT-OSS relative to norm-matched random spectral perturbations. In Qwen2.5, the immediate suppressive effect is accompanied by a reduction in next-layer query--key preference for position~0, and the learned spectral directions remain stable when estimated from substantially less training data. Together, the results show that attention sinks are preceded by a short spectral reorganization of hidden states, and directly perturbing this geometry can causally alter subsequent sink formation.

title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
summary: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/MTD upon publication.

title: NFMap: Topographic 2D Manifold Learning with Invertible Normalizing Flows
summary: We present NFMap, a dimensionality reduction method for 2D visualisation that extends Generative Topographic Mapping (GTM) with a bijective normalizing flow. Like GTM, NFMap places a fixed mixture grid prior over a 2D latent map, giving a parametric embedding, an explicit likelihood, and the ability to project new points onto an existing map; the likelihood is an effective out-of-distribution signal on chemical datasets. Unlike GTM, whose latent-to-data mapping is an RBF network of bounded flexibility, NFMap's mapping is a normalizing flow, and is therefore fully invertible: any location on the map can be carried back to data space. To alleviate map crowding on large datasets, NFMap additionally supports heavy-tailed Student-t mixture components. NFMap maps data to a latent space of the same dimension, split into a 2-dimensional navigable map and an off-manifold residual. Because the flow is bijective and its objective penalises volume contraction, variance squeezed out of the residual must reappear in the navigable map. The residual scale is the main control between local neighbourhood fidelity and global distance fidelity; its effect depends on the dimensionality of the data and is coupled to the extent of the latent grid.

title: The Multilingual Artificial Hivemind: Do All LLMs Think Alike in Every Language?
summary: Text generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) often remains limited in diversity compared to that produced by humans. Recent advances demonstrate the presence of inter- and intra-model collapse in open-ended generation of English text, raising concerns about the long-term homogenization of LLM, and more importantly, human thought. However, our understanding of whether this homogenization extends to languages beyond English is limited. In this work, we investigate the role of language on output diversity. Specifically, we aim to understand whether multilingual LLM-generated text is also homogeneous, and whether this homogeneity matches what we observe in humans. Across 23 open-weight models and 13 languages, we find that the artificial hivemind effect is pervasive but uneven in its extent. The intra-model effect holds in three different embedding spaces and under a lexical metric that uses no embedding model, so it is not an artifact of how diversity is measured. The size of the homogenization gap is associated with a model's competence in a language, measured on a held-out translation benchmark, robustly across embedding spaces. Thus, we demonstrate a performance-diversity tradeoff in multilingual LLMs.

title: Is the Platform Part of the Measurement? A Protocol and Simulation Study for Cross-Platform Equivalence of Machine-Labelled Policy Sentiment
comments: 25 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Includes an original 500-replication simulation study. Code: https://github.com/asadfix/platform-measurement (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23105129)
summary: Comparing machine-labelled sentiment across social media platforms is now routine: differences in classifier scores between platforms are read as differences in public opinion. These comparisons rest on an assumption that the classifier measures the same construct, on the same scale, on every platform. Some studies check a classifier's validity platform by platform, but to our knowledge none has modelled the platform as a facet of the classifier's measurement. We adapt the psychometric equivalence toolkit (generalizability theory, measurement invariance and differential item functioning, and score linking) to machine-labelled policy sentiment, treating the platform as a survey mode, and specify a six-step protocol with anchor events fixed in advance, an anchor-density audit, and a two-classifier convergence control. A simulation with known ground truth illustrates what the assumption can cost in one generating configuration fixed in advance: across 500 replications, because the platforms measure through different functions, a pooled index that takes platform scores at face value reports the wrong sign of aggregate sentiment on nearly a quarter of days, whereas an index adjusted with each platform's known measurement function does so on under one day in sixty on average. A case study of the instrument from the first author's MSc dissertation, a fine-tuned BERT classifier over 255,446 UK economic-policy comments from Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, and Quora, motivates the design and illustrates the instrument-dependence the protocol addresses. The full four-platform application, under fresh collection with the pre-specified design, is the designated follow-up study. The protocol lets a researcher test whether pooling platforms is defensible in a given corpus, or whether platform scores must be linked before any average is taken.
comment: 25 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Includes an original 500-replication simulation study. Code: https://github.com/asadfix/platform-measurement (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23105129)

title: Image Tokenizers Should Be Trained Between Images
summary: Latent diffusion models generate images as codes of an image tokenizer, whose decoder turns them into the pixel image. Recent tokenizers improve how well these codes reconstruct an image and how easily a generator learns them. Yet a generator does not reproduce the codes of training images, and when a generated code lands outside what the decoder expects, the decoded image contains imperfections. Current methods make the decoder more robust to generated codes by adding noise during training. However, generated codes lie between the training codes and resemble their mixture more than one of them plus noise. To improve generated images, decoders should therefore be trained on codes in the space between training samples. We propose InterpTok, which fine-tunes MAETok to decode mixtures of image codes into natural images. Since no target image exists between two training samples, a discriminator judges whether each decoded mixture looks as natural as its two sources. A mixing ratio loss requires the decoded mixture to keep the mixing ratio of the two codes. Together, they prevent collapse to a trivial solution and yield a sharp and natural composition of both images. InterpTok keeps MAETok's reconstruction quality and improves interpolation quality more than threefold, the best of all tokenizers in a recent benchmark. Beyond interpolation, InterpTok improves the generation FID of a matched diffusion transformer from 11.61 to 8.48 without guidance, and even reaches 8.11 at an eighth of the sampling steps, where the generator on MAETok's codes worsens. The generator trained on our tokenizer also reaches the final result of the one trained on MAETok at half the training steps. Our findings show that the space between image codes can and should be explicitly supervised rather than ignored.

title: Separating Prompt Harmfulness from Interaction Safety via Partial Generation
summary: LLM-based information systems need safety guardrails. Most guardrails classify the prompt alone. If the prompt looks harmful, the system rejects it before any answer is generated. This is costly. Many rejected prompts would have received a safe response. Users lose help they should have received from the information system. This cost grows as conversational and generative search becomes common. Prompt-level labels treat harm as a property of the query. But harm depends on what the model actually writes. Existing input-output guards do look at responses. But they judge a finished response, so the decision comes after full generation. However, we observe that safety of model interaction with the input prompt can be inferred early with only partial output. So the system can start generating, watch the partial response, and stop only if it turns harmful. We test this idea in three steps. First, we build a dataset of 41,944 prompt-response pairs with seven open weights LLMs from three families: Llama, Gemma, and Qwen. Second, we show that prompt harmfulness and interaction safety differ. Prompt labels and response labels agree on only 50.46\% of items (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.06). Of the prompts that make any model respond harmfully, only 3.5\% do so for all seven LLMs. Third, we show that partial responses carry most of the signal. Fine-tuned classifiers predict response-level harm well (best AUPRC 0.885, F1 0.807). About one third of the response tokens recover almost full-response AUPRC.

title: Towards Complementary Keypoint Detection via Mixture of Detectors
summary: Keypoint detection plays a central role in geometric vision pipelines. Existing detectors exhibit complementary strengths across different scene structures and keypoint budgets, and reliance on a single detector often results in suboptimal keypoint distributions. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Mixture of Detectors (MoD)} for dense matching pipelines, a unified framework for complementary keypoint detection through the adaptive composition of heterogeneous detectors. MoD first distills heterogeneous detectors into a unified model, allowing diverse detection maps to be predicted efficiently within a single forward pass. Detector selection is subsequently formulated as a patch-wise, budget-conditioned decision process, in which a lightweight router assigns the most suitable detector to each local region. To avoid heuristic supervision, the router is trained with task-driven rewards derived from downstream matching quality, jointly capturing both keypoint quantity and precision. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, ScanNet, and HPatches demonstrate that MoD consistently outperforms strong baselines across a wide range of keypoint budgets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving keypoint distribution and downstream geometric performance.

title: Relational Learning as World Modeling
summary: Relational learning typically predicts from a database state, but decision making asks a different question: how will that state change under an action? In operational systems, the answer depends on system-specific dynamics that may not be visible in the database itself. We view each such system as a relational "world" and ask whether a model can infer how it behaves from observed executions. We introduce TabWM (Tabular World Model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM uses them as context to predict the sparse structured edits caused by a new action without parameter updates. Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 rises from 0.016 with no observed executions to 0.685 with 64, where a correct edit must match its operation, relational location, and value. Because these predictions are explicit relational edits, they can be applied recursively to imagine candidate futures and compare actions before they are taken. Broader search over these predicted futures improves the realized return of selected action sequences. Together, these results suggest that relational dynamics can be learned in context, broadening relational learning from modeling system state to modeling how that state changes under action.

title: A note on Finiteness and Boundedness in Cartesian Products of Discrete and Well-Ordered Sets, Application to Transition Systems
summary: In this short note, we prove that any closed interval in a well-ordered and discrete space is finite. The coincidence between finiteness and boundedness can then be established for transition systems where the state space is well-ordered and discrete. Finally, this result is also proven when the state space is a Cartesian product of $d$ discrete and well-ordered sets.

title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models
summary: Geospatial reasoning links VLMs to real-world action and decision making. Reliable reasoning requires accurate spatial information and effective spatial representations. However, current VLMs obtain this information mainly from language and vision. At larger geographic scales, limited visual observations make it difficult to establish accurate spatial references and recover precise spatial relations. This leads to a bottleneck for VLM spatial perception and reasoning. This paper proposes that geospatial vector geometry can become a native spatial modality within a VLM and introduces GeoVec-VLM. First, we develop a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial structure and arrangement of vector objects, building an explicit spatial basis. Second, we introduce a geometry interaction strategy that brings this basis into multimodal computation, where it interacts with visual content and language references according to the queried spatial relations. Together, these designs allow perception and reasoning to operate on shared geometric references. Across five spatial reasoning tasks, GeoVec-VLM improves mean accuracy by about 11\% relative to the strongest baseline, maintains its gains under geographic transfer, and shows greater geometric consistency. Our results show that geospatial vector geometry offers a promising internal spatial basis for VLM spatial reasoning. https://github.com/TXFR/GeoVector-VLM

title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
summary: Digital Twin (DT) combined with reinforcement learning (RL) can support adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making by comparing expected and observed network behavior. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network. For each action, the same channel simulator is evaluated under an attack-free and an attacked configuration. Receiver-level residuals are combined with spatial jamming footprints and accumulated to form a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into an aggregated state, a belief-concentration reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. The BGQL scheme is compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random under matched attacker sets. Across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs in four configurations, with the number of active jammers supplied to every method, BGQL achieves mean aggregate full-band link-rate scores of approximately 437.4--564.2~Mbit/s and rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37--76.79~Mbit/J. Its detection accuracy is 100\% in one-jammer configurations and approximately 78\%--81\% in two-jammer configurations. BGQL requires approximately 80--130~s per run, compared with 5--14~s for SARSA, reflecting evaluation of 625 beam pairs during exploratory steps. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.

title: Game-Creation-Agents: Autonomous Game Production
summary: Game-Creation-Agents (GCA) turns a natural-language request into a runnable Phaser 4 browser game. The pipeline first builds a multimodal game design document that couples mechanics and scene contracts to grounded visual references. It then projects that document into a runtime scaffold, machine-readable contracts, and deterministic tests. Eight specialized agents next carry out production: scenes are implemented serially, assets are produced in parallel, and one reduced manifest joins the two branches into a single build. Build-linked real-UI checks and a code-blind critic then verify that build and decide whether the game may ship. Each blocker returns to the agent that owns the affected artifact for a bounded repair, and the game is released once all the gates pass. We evaluate finished games separately, through their rendered interfaces alone, over prompt-matched tasks run under a common protocol. GCA achieves stronger requirement satisfaction, core mechanics, content depth, and functional visuals than a comparable open pipeline. In a side-by-side human study, raters also score GCA's games higher on every dimension and prefer them overall.

title: DCCB-Capability-Aware Optimal Info-Power Flow for Transmission Switching in AC/MTDC Grids
summary: Transmission switching is an effective approach for restoring operational flexibility and improving the economic performance of AC/multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids following DC-side faults. Its practical implementation requires that the faulted branch be safely isolated and that the associated switching commands be successfully delivered through the communication network. However, conventional transmission switching models generally represent switching actions using binary variables, without considering the availability of communication resources or whether the corresponding DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) can interrupt the fault current affected by time delay. To address these issues, this paper develops an explicit optimal info--power flow (OIPF) formulation that incorporates information transmission into the post-fault transmission-switching optimization for AC/MTDC grids. The switching status of each DC branch is determined by the availability of its communication path and associated communication resources. In addition, binary switching decisions are supplemented by a DCCB feasibility constraint that limits the estimated delayed-interruption current to the DCCB breaking capability. The resulting problem is formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that can be efficiently solved using off-the-shelf optimization solvers. Numerical results reveal that limited communication capacity and additional routing costs may render electrically beneficial switching actions infeasible or uneconomical, while delay-aware DCCB interruption constraints may favor lower-delay communication routes despite their higher costs.

AI.title_translation: 面向交直流混联电网线路开断的考虑直流断路器能力的最优信息-潮流协同模型
AI.tldr: 本文提出了考虑通信资源与直流断路器时延开断能力的交直流电网故障后线路开断MISOCP优化模型。
AI.motivation: 传统输电开断模型通常仅用二元变量抽象表示开断动作，未考虑通信网络资源的可用性，也未计及通信时延对直流断路器（DCCB）能否有效开断故障电流的影响。
AI.method: 提出一种显式的最优信息-潮流（OIPF）模型，将信息传输过程嵌入故障后开断优化中；利用通信路径和通信资源可用性确定开断状态；引入DCCB可行性约束，将考虑时延估计的开断电流限制在DCCB自身开断能力范围内；整体优化问题被形式化为可高效求解的混合整数二阶锥规划（MISOCP）模型。
AI.result: 数值结果表明，有限的通信容量和额外的路由成本可能会导致在电气上有利的开断操作变得不可行或不具备经济性；同时，考虑时延的DCCB开断约束会促使优化选择时延更低但成本更高的通信路由。
AI.conclusion: 在交流/多端直流电网中实施故障后线路开断时，必须综合考虑通信网络资源限制与断路器受时延影响的开断能力，方可保证开断决策的实际可执行性与整体运行经济性。
AI.translation: 线路开断是交流/多端直流（MTDC）电网发生直流侧故障后恢复运行灵活性并提高经济性能的有效方法。其实际应用要求安全隔离故障支路，并通过通信网络成功下发相关的开断指令。然而，传统的线路开断模型通常仅使用二元变量表示开断动作，未考虑通信资源的可用性，也未考虑相应的直流断路器（DCCB）能否在受时延影响下成功开断故障电流。针对这些问题，本文提出了一种显式的最优信息-潮流（OIPF）模型，将信息传输纳入交流/MTDC电网的故障后线路开断优化中。每条直流支路的开断状态由其通信路径及相关通信资源的可用性决定。此外，二元开断决策还补充了DCCB可行性约束，将估计的时延开断电流限制在DCCB开断能力之内。由此产生的问题被构建为混合整数二阶锥规划（MISOCP）模型，可使用现成的优化求解器高效求解。数值结果表明，有限的通信容量和额外的路由成本可能会使在电气上有利的开断操作变得不可行或不经济，而考虑时延的DCCB开断约束可能会使系统倾向于选择时延更低但成本更高的通信路径。
AI.summary: 本文针对交直流混联电网故障后线路开断问题，提出了一种考虑直流断路器开断能力和通信资源约束的最优信息-潮流（OIPF）模型。研究将通信拓扑资源和时延开断限制转化为MISOCP模型，揭示了通信条件和断路器物理开断限制对开断决策可行性与经济性的显著影响。
AI.keywords: 线路开断, 交直流混联电网, 最优信息-潮流, 直流断路器, 混合整数二阶锥规划
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将信息通信网络特性（如通信时延、路由成本及信道资源）与物理侧直流断路器的耐受/开断极限深度融合，突破了传统输电开断优化将通信与控制假设为理想状态的局限，为信息物理交直流混合电网的协同优化与故障快速恢复提供了更加贴合工程实际的建模范式。

title: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents
summary: Cloud graphical user interface (GUI) agents send instructions and screenshots to remote planners, exposing personally identifiable information (PII). Existing placeholder defenses mask detected spans and reuse exact strings. Fragmented or changed forms can expose PII or break entity continuity across turns. PrivacyGuard addresses this private reference problem with source-linked sanitization (SAN) and a structured reference lifecycle (REF). SAN reconstructs fragmented or overlapping evidence and rewrites the complete source extent. REF links changed appearances to session entities and supports locally resolvable references without returning raw values to the upload path. In five-turn sessions scored against common gold, PrivacyGuard reduces audited source-value leakage by 33.55\%--82.60\% relative to the closest prior full-pipeline system in all four reader--language combinations. REF raises strict cross-form continuity from 0.04 under exact-value reuse to 0.81. In reference-required Android tasks, verified completion rises from 8/30 and 7/30 to 17/30 and 20/30. On AndroidLab, PrivacyGuard achieves the highest or tied-highest task-success point estimate among protection pipelines for all four planners. On PrivScreen, it reduces fixed-reader field exposure by 62.72\%--62.84\% relative to the same baseline. PrivacyGuard lowers upload exposure while preserving a locally resolvable task path.

AI.title_translation: PrivacyGuard：云GUI代理的源链接净化和本地可解析PII引用
AI.tldr: PrivacyGuard通过源链接净化和结构化引用生命周期解决云GUI代理中的PII泄露问题，显著降低数据泄露并提高任务完成率。
AI.motivation: 云图形用户界面（GUI）代理在向远程规划器发送指令和截图时会暴露个人身份信息（PII）。现有的占位符防御措施无法有效处理碎片化或变化的表单，导致PII泄露或实体连续性中断。
AI.method: PrivacyGuard引入了源链接净化（SAN）和结构化引用生命周期（REF）。SAN重建碎片化或重叠的证据并重写完整的源范围。REF将变化的外观链接到会话实体，并支持本地可解析引用，而无需将原始值返回到上传路径。
AI.result: 与最接近的现有完整管道系统相比，PrivacyGuard在所有四种阅读器-语言组合中，将审计的源值泄露减少了33.55%至82.60%。REF将严格的跨表单连续性从0.04提高到0.81。在需要引用的Android任务中，验证完成率从8/30和7/30分别提高到17/30和20/30。在AndroidLab上，PrivacyGuard在所有四个规划器中实现了最高或并列最高的任务成功点估计。在PrivScreen上，相对于同一基线，它将固定阅读器字段暴露减少了62.72%至62.84%。
AI.conclusion: PrivacyGuard在降低上传暴露的同时，保持了本地可解析的任务路径，有效解决了云GUI代理中的PII泄露问题。
AI.translation: 云图形用户界面（GUI）代理向远程规划器发送指令和截图，从而暴露个人身份信息（PII）。现有的占位符防御措施仅掩盖检测到的跨度并重用精确字符串。碎片化或变化的表单可能会暴露PII或破坏跨轮次的实体连续性。PrivacyGuard通过源链接净化（SAN）和结构化引用生命周期（REF）解决了这个私有引用问题。SAN重建碎片化或重叠的证据并重写完整的源范围。REF将变化的外观链接到会话实体，并支持本地可解析的引用，而无需将原始值返回到上传路径。在针对通用黄金标准评分的五轮会话中，PrivacyGuard在所有四种阅读器-语言组合中，相对于最接近的现有完整管道系统，将审计的源值泄露减少了33.55%--82.60%。REF将严格的跨表单连续性从精确值重用下的0.04提高到0.81。在需要引用的Android任务中，验证完成率从8/30和7/30分别提高到17/30和20/30。在AndroidLab上，PrivacyGuard在所有四个规划器中实现了保护管道中最高或并列最高的任务成功点估计。在PrivScreen上，相对于同一基线，它将固定阅读器字段暴露减少了62.72%--62.84%。PrivacyGuard降低了上传暴露，同时保留了本地可解析的任务路径。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了PrivacyGuard，一种用于云GUI代理的隐私保护系统，旨在解决因指令和截图传输导致的PII泄露问题。它通过源链接净化（SAN）重建并重写碎片化PII，以及结构化引用生命周期（REF）维护实体连续性并支持本地可解析引用。实验结果表明，PrivacyGuard显著降低了PII泄露，提高了跨表单连续性和任务完成率，优于现有方法。
AI.keywords: PII保护, 云GUI代理, 源链接净化, 本地可解析引用, 隐私
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入源链接净化和结构化引用生命周期，为云GUI代理中的PII保护提供了一个新颖且全面的解决方案。其创新之处在于能够处理碎片化和动态变化的PII数据，并保持实体连续性，这在现有方法中是一个显著的不足。该方法不仅降低了数据泄露风险，还通过本地可解析引用确保了任务路径的可用性，在实际应用中具有重要意义。

title: A Bethe-Ansatz Source of Early Token Correlations: A marginal-preserving construction for parallel proposals
comments: 5 pages, 2 tables. Ancillary files reproduce all numerical results
summary: Parallel token proposals in language-model decoding need a joint law, not merely accurate token marginals. We construct a family of coordinate-Bethe-ansatz laws from the periodic XXZ chain and compare each with its maximum-entropy pairwise projection at identical one- and two-site moments. In the eight-site, three-excitation sector, symmetry makes their entire probability-law difference one-dimensional, determined by a contiguous three-site moment. Along the Bethe branch, this gap varies with anisotropy, changes sign, and vanishes exactly at $Δ=(3+\sqrt{3})/2$, where the eigenstate law becomes exactly pairwise. A nonlinear readout transfers a nonzero gap into the first two token positions while preserving their separate marginals. At $Δ=1.5$ the deterministic binary token laws differ by 0.02654573 in total variation. Exact speculative verification then gives a strict accepted-prefix advantage for a constructed target and a neighborhood within targets sharing its first-token marginal. This is a mathematical existence result. It does not establish a language-model gain or wall-clock speedup.
comment: 5 pages, 2 tables. Ancillary files reproduce all numerical results

AI.title_translation: Bethe-Ansatz早期token相关性的来源：一种用于并行提议的边际保留构造
AI.tldr: 本文构建了基于Bethe-Ansatz的联合概率定律，用于语言模型解码中的并行token提议，发现在特定各向异性参数下，该定律变为精确的成对关系，并通过非线性读出将非零间隙转移到token位置，从而在推测性验证中获得严格的前缀优势。这是一个数学存在性结果。
AI.motivation: 语言模型解码中的并行token提议需要一个联合定律，而不仅仅是准确的token边际分布。
AI.method:
1. 从周期性XXZ链构建了一系列坐标Bethe-Ansatz定律。
2. 将其与相同的一阶和二阶矩下的最大熵成对投影进行比较。
3. 在八站点、三激发扇区中，利用对称性将概率定律差异简化为一维，由连续三站点矩确定。
4. 采用非线性读出将非零间隙转移到前两个token位置，同时保留其单独的边际分布。
5. 使用精确的推测性验证来评估接受前缀的优势。
AI.result:
1. 在八站点、三激发扇区中，对称性使得其整个概率定律差异是一维的，由一个连续的三站点矩决定。
2. 沿着Bethe分支，这个间隙随各向异性变化，改变符号，并在Δ=(3+√3)/2处精确消失，此时本征态定律变为精确的成对关系。
3. 非线性读出将一个非零间隙转移到前两个token位置，同时保留它们的独立边际分布。
4. 在Δ=1.5时，确定性二元token定律在总变差上相差0.02654573。
5. 精确的推测性验证为构建的目标和共享其第一个token边际的目标邻域提供了严格的接受前缀优势。
6. 这是一个数学存在性结果，它并未建立语言模型增益或挂钟时间加速。
AI.conclusion: 本文提供了一个数学存在性结果，表明Bethe-Ansatz可以是早期token相关性的来源，并且在特定条件下，通过非线性读出和推测性验证，可以获得严格的接受前缀优势。但它不代表语言模型的实际增益或速度提升。
AI.translation: 语言模型解码中的并行token提议需要一个联合定律，而不仅仅是准确的token边际分布。我们从周期性XXZ链构建了一系列坐标Bethe-Ansatz定律，并将每个定律与在相同的一阶和二阶矩下的最大熵成对投影进行比较。在八站点、三激发扇区中，对称性使得它们的整个概率定律差异是一维的，由一个连续的三站点矩决定。沿着Bethe分支，这个间隙随各向异性变化，改变符号，并在Δ=(3+√3)/2处精确消失，此时本征态定律变为精确的成对关系。非线性读出将一个非零间隙转移到前两个token位置，同时保留它们的独立边际分布。在Δ=1.5时，确定性二元token定律在总变差上相差0.02654573。精确的推测性验证为构建的目标和共享其第一个token边际的目标邻域提供了严格的接受前缀优势。这是一个数学存在性结果。它并未建立语言模型增益或挂钟时间加速。
AI.summary: 本文研究了语言模型解码中并行token提议所需的联合概率定律。通过从周期性XXZ链构建Bethe-Ansatz定律家族，并与最大熵成对投影进行比较，作者发现其概率定律差异在特定条件下由三站点矩决定。研究表明，在Δ=(3+√3)/2时，本征态定律变为精确的成对关系。通过非线性读出，可以将一个非零间隙转移到前两个token位置，同时保留它们的边际分布，并在推测性验证中展示了接受前缀的严格优势。这是一项数学存在性研究，不直接涉及语言模型性能提升或速度优化。
AI.keywords: Bethe-Ansatz, token相关性, 并行提议, 语言模型解码, XXZ链
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于将Bethe-Ansatz这种物理学中的精确可解模型引入到语言模型解码的理论分析中，为理解token之间的早期相关性提供了一个新颖的数学框架。它提供了一个重要的数学存在性证明，表明在特定条件下，通过精心设计的联合概率分布可以获得推测性验证的优势。然而，其主要局限性在于，它明确指出这仅仅是一个数学存在性结果，并未直接证明在实际语言模型中能带来性能增益或计算加速，这限制了其直接的工程应用价值。

title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
summary: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

AI.title_translation: LIBERO-Industry：工业过程约束下的机器人操作基准测试

title: InfoVis: Unified Slide Image Generation and Editing
summary: Generating and editing presentation slides requires models to combine accurate text rendering, instruction following, visual grounding, aesthetic design, and precise editing within one canvas. Existing work covers only subsets of these capabilities and lacks large-scale slide-native supervision and diagnostic evaluation. We formulate four slide-centric tasks and build a scalable data engine with over 13M continual-pretraining records and 1.9M supervised fine-tuning records. We also introduce VisSlideBench, a benchmark of 1,527 manually screened instances that covers all four tasks with task-specific, multidimensional evaluation. Its automatic rankings agree with blinded, dimension-wise human rankings. Using these resources, we train InfoVis, a unified 9B slide generation and editing model. On VisSlideBench, InfoVis leads every evaluated open-source model on all eleven metrics and scores 7.94 overall against 7.99 for Nano-Banana-2. Starting from FLUX.2-klein-base-9B, slide-specific post-training adds 1.6 points overall, with the largest generation gains in content faithfulness; the remaining gap to proprietary models is smallest in content faithfulness and largest in aesthetic quality. Built on InfoVis, our document-to-slide workflow achieves the second-highest Aesthetics score on the external SlidesGen-Bench. We will release the model, code, data, and benchmark.

AI.title_translation: InfoVis：统一的幻灯片图像生成与编辑

title: A Deterministic $0.401$-Approximation for Non-monotone Submodular Maximization under Matroid Constraints
summary:
Submodular maximization arises in a wide range of combinatorial optimization problems and has been extensively studied from the perspective of approximation algorithms. For maximizing nonnegative, non-monotone submodular functions subject to a matroid constraint, randomized algorithms achieve a $0.401$-approximation, whereas obtaining comparable deterministic guarantees remains challenging. In this paper, we present a deterministic $0.401$-approximation algorithm in the exact value and independence oracle model, improving upon the previous deterministic guarantee of $(0.385-\varepsilon)$ \cite{ChenGLSZ2026}.
  Our algorithm builds on the extended multilinear extension and provides a deterministic implementation of the recursive guided framework underlying the randomized $0.401$-approximation algorithm. The main technical ingredient is a direction oracle supported on at most two partitioned matroid bases. This oracle simultaneously satisfies the growth condition required by the extended-multilinear update and an approximate stationarity condition needed to construct the recursive guides. The resulting finite-support representation enables exact evaluation of the relevant expectations and marginal values without random sampling. The algorithm uses polynomially many value- and independence-oracle queries.

AI.title_translation: 非单调次模函数在拟阵约束下的确定性 $0.401$-近似算法
AI.tldr: 提出了一种确定性 $0.401$-近似算法，用于解决拟阵约束下的非单调次模函数最大化问题，超越了之前的确定性算法并与随机算法性能相当。
AI.motivation: 随机算法在非单调次模函数最大化问题上已达到 $0.401$-近似，但获得可比的确定性保证仍然具有挑战性。
AI.method: 算法基于扩展多线性扩展（extended multilinear extension），并提供了递归引导框架（recursive guided framework）的确定性实现。核心技术是一个方向预言机（direction oracle），它最多支持两个分区拟阵基，同时满足扩展多线性更新所需的增长条件和构建递归引导所需的近似平稳条件。这使得无需随机采样即可精确评估相关期望和边际值。算法使用多项式次数的值和独立性预言机查询。
AI.result: 提出了一种在精确值和独立性预言机模型中，确定性的 $0.401$-近似算法，改进了之前 $(0.385-\varepsilon)$ 的确定性保证。
AI.conclusion: 该论文成功地为拟阵约束下的非单调次模函数最大化问题提供了一个确定性的 $0.401$-近似算法，达到了与现有随机算法相当的近似比，并显著优于此前的确定性算法。
AI.translation: 次模函数最大化问题出现在广泛的组合优化问题中，并已从近似算法的角度进行了广泛研究。对于在拟阵约束下最大化非负、非单调次模函数，随机算法实现了 $0.401$-近似，而获得可比的确定性保证仍然具有挑战性。在本文中，我们提出了一个在精确值和独立性预言机模型中的确定性 $0.401$-近似算法，改进了之前 $(0.385-\varepsilon)$ 的确定性保证 \cite{ChenGLSZ2026}。我们的算法建立在扩展多线性扩展之上，并提供了作为随机 $0.401$-近似算法基础的递归引导框架的确定性实现。主要技术要素是一个方向预言机，它最多支持两个分区拟阵基。该预言机同时满足扩展多线性更新所需的增长条件和构建递归引导所需的近似平稳条件。由此产生的有限支持表示使得无需随机采样即可精确评估相关期望和边际值。该算法使用多项式次数的值和独立性预言机查询。
AI.summary: 本文针对拟阵约束下的非单调次模函数最大化问题，提出了一种确定性 $0.401$-近似算法。该算法基于扩展多线性扩展和递归引导框架的确定性实现，通过引入一个创新的方向预言机，成功地将确定性近似比提升至与随机算法相当的水平，并超越了以往的确定性结果。
AI.keywords: 次模函数最大化, 拟阵约束, 确定性近似, 非单调, 组合优化
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于首次为非单调次模函数在拟阵约束下的最大化问题提供了一个确定性的 $0.401$-近似算法，其近似比与现有最佳随机算法相当。这解决了长期以来确定性算法性能不足的挑战，并通过巧妙地设计方向预言机，避免了随机采样，在理论和实践上都具有重要意义。

title: Improved Massively Parallel Shortest Path Computation
summary:
We present new algorithms for approximate shortest path computation in weighted undirected graphs within the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. Specifically, we construct an $a$-approximate Single-Source Shortest Path (SSSP) oracle: Given a query consisting of a source vertex $u \in V$, the oracle returns $a$-approximate distances $δ(u,v)$ for all $v \in V$.
  Fix an $n$-vertex weighted undirected graph. We consider two regimes of the MPC model: the near-linear regime, where each machine has $\tildeΘ(n)$ memory, and the heterogeneous regime, where all machines have $Θ(n^γ)$ memory for some constant $γ\in (0,1]$, except for a single machine with $\tildeΘ(n)$ memory. We develop randomised algorithms that construct $O(1)$-approximate SSSP oracles in $O(\log\log n)$ rounds in the near-linear regime and in $O(\log^2\log n)$ rounds in the heterogeneous regime. These oracles answer distance queries in $O(1)$ rounds. Our results improve upon the recent work of Dory and Matar (SPAA 2024) which, for the same total memory, requires $\left(\log\log n\right)^{2+O(1/γ)}$ rounds and applies only to unweighted graphs in the heterogeneous setting.
  We say that $\tilde N_k(u)$ is the approximate $k$-nearest neighbourhood of a vertex $u$ if there exists an approximate distance estimate $δ$ such that $\tilde N_k(u)$ consists of the $k$ vertices closest to $u$ according to $δ$, breaking ties by vertex ID. The main technical ingredient is a new method for efficiently computing approximate $n^{O(γ)}$-nearest neighbourhoods in the heterogeneous MPC model in $O(\log^2\log n)$ rounds.

AI.title_translation: 改进的大规模并行最短路径计算
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种在MPC模型下针对带权无向图的高效近似单源最短路径算法，分别在近线性与异构内存模式下实现了 $O(\log\log n)$ 与 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮的构建复杂度，大幅改进了现有成果。
AI.motivation: 在现代大规模并行计算（MPC）模型下，带权无向图的近似最短路径计算轮数复杂度仍然较高，且现有最先进成果（如 Dory 和 Matar 于 SPAA 2024 的工作）仅适用于异构设置下的无权图，且轮数依赖于 $1/\gamma$。
AI.method: 核心技术方法是提出了一种在异构MPC模型中用 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮高效计算近似 $n^{O(\gamma)}$-最近邻（approximate nearest neighbourhoods）的新机制，并基于此构建随机化近似SSSP预处理预言机。
AI.result: 在近线性内存模式下，以 $O(\log\log n)$ 轮构建 $O(1)$-近似SSSP预言机；在异构内存模式下，以 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮构建该预言机。预言机均可在 $O(1)$ 轮内响应任意距离查询，性能全面优于先前基于同等内存的 SPAA 2024 工作。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功提出了在MPC模型下针对带权无向图的高效近似SSSP预处理算法，显著降低了轮数复杂度，并在更弱的图假设（带权图）下取得了优于现有前沿算法的结果。
AI.translation: 我们在大规模并行计算（MPC）模型中提出了带权无向图近似最短路径计算的新算法。具体而言，我们构建了一个 $a$-近似单源最短路径（SSSP）预言机：给定由源顶点 $u \in V$ 组成的查询，该预言机针对所有 $v \in V$ 返回 $a$-近似距离 $δ(u,v)$。固定一个具有 $n$ 个顶点的带权无向图，我们考虑MPC模型的两种场景：近线性场景，其中每台机器具有 $\tildeΘ(n)$ 内存；异构场景，其中除了单台具有 $\tildeΘ(n)$ 内存的机器外，其余所有机器均具有 $Θ(n^γ)$ 内存（对于某个常数 $γ\in (0,1]$）。我们开发了随机化算法，在近线性场景中以 $O(\log\log n)$ 轮、在异构场景中以 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮构建 $O(1)$-近似SSSP预言机。这些预言机可在 $O(1)$ 轮内回答距离查询。我们的结果改进了 Dory 和 Matar 最近的工作（SPAA 2024），后者在相同的总内存下需要 $(\log\log n)^{2+O(1/γ)}$ 轮，且在异构场景下仅适用于无权图。我们称 $\tilde N_k(u)$ 为顶点 $u$ 的近似 $k$-最近邻域，如果存在一个近似距离估计 $δ$，使得 $\tilde N_k(u)$ 包含根据 $δ$ 距离 $u$ 最近的 $k$ 个顶点（以顶点ID打破平局）。主要的技术组成部分是一种在异构MPC模型中以 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮高效计算近似 $n^{O(γ)}$-最近邻域的新方法。
AI.summary: 本文研究了大规模并行计算（MPC）模型下带权无向图的近似单源最短路径（SSSP）问题。作者针对近线性内存与异构内存两种模式分别提出了随机化算法，能在 $O(\log\log n)$ 和 $O(\log^2\log n)$ 轮内构建 $O(1)$-近似SSSP预言机，并支持 $O(1)$ 轮距离查询。通过引入高效计算近似最近邻的核心技术，本研究显著改进了先前的算法轮数复杂度，并拓展至带权图。
AI.keywords: 大规模并行计算 (MPC), 单源最短路径 (SSSP), 近似算法, 带权无向图, 邻域计算
AI.comments: 该论文显著改进了先前在MPC模型下的近似单源最短路径（SSSP）算法，不仅将轮数复杂度从依赖于常数项梯度的 $(\log\log n)^{2+O(1/\gamma)}$ 降低到仅需 $O(\log^2\log n)$，还将适用范围从无权图扩展到了更具通用性的带权无向图，其提出的近邻计算新技术对大规模图并行计算具有重要参考价值。

title: Logit Leakage through Floating-Point Bias Addition
summary: Language model APIs can expose token-specific biases while withholding logits and token probabilities. Existing bias-based extraction recovers relative logits, leaving a common additive component undetermined in ideal arithmetic. We identify a numerical side channel in floating-point bias addition that exposes information about this component through token identities alone. The channel distinguishes score vectors with identical complete unperturbed log probabilities. Our method exploits changes in representable spacing at binary exponent boundaries. Under the stated binary32 arithmetic assumptions and a known reachable score interval, it recovers a logit pair and its unknown tie-breaking priority exactly in at most 52 token queries. Given complete relative logits, one recovered anchor determines the original logit vector. We evaluate recovery across 11 public checkpoints from seven model families and extend the local method with adaptive interval search and anchor selection. In end-to-end experiments with vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp, adaptive recovery succeeds on all 128 Qwen3-0.6B inputs per system, including 64 held-out inputs. A separate token-only experiment extracts a pretrained small model's complete output-head representation up to an invertible hidden-basis transformation. We also establish a sufficient condition for suppressing common-shift disclosure by subtracting the maximum before bias addition. In controlled experiments, this mitigation eliminates all observed distinctions between common-shift variants and preserves token decisions under the tested random biases.

AI.title_translation: 浮点偏差加法导致的 Logit 泄露
AI.tldr: 本文发现了一种利用浮点偏差加法中的数值侧信道来恢复语言模型中被隐藏的 logit 值的通用加法分量的方法，并在多种模型和系统上验证了其有效性，并提出了缓解措施。
AI.motivation: 语言模型 API 在隐藏 logit 和 token 概率的同时会暴露 token 特定的偏差。现有方法只能恢复相对 logit，而无法确定通用加法分量。本文旨在解决这一问题，揭示被隐藏的 logit 信息的泄露途径。
AI.method: 作者识别了浮点偏差加法中的一个数值侧信道，该侧信道仅通过 token 身份就能暴露通用加法分量的信息。该方法利用二进制指数边界处可表示间距的变化。通过自适应区间搜索和锚点选择扩展了局部方法，并在多种模型家族和系统上进行了评估。此外，还提出了通过在偏差加法前减去最大值来抑制通用偏移泄露的条件。
AI.result: 1. 该方法在最多 52 次 token 查询中，能精确恢复一个 logit 对及其未知的决胜优先级。2. 给定完整的相对 logit，一个恢复的锚点可以确定原始 logit 向量。3. 在 vLLM、SGLang 和 llama.cpp 的端到端实验中，自适应恢复在每个系统上所有 128 个 Qwen3-0.6B 输入（包括 64 个保留输入）上都成功。4. 一项独立的仅基于 token 的实验提取了预训练小型模型的完整输出头表示。5. 提出的缓解措施在受控实验中消除了所有观察到的通用偏移变体之间的区别，并在测试的随机偏差下保留了 token 决策。
AI.conclusion: 本文揭示了浮点偏差加法中存在的数值侧信道可以泄露语言模型中被隐藏的 logit 的通用加法分量，并提出了一种有效的恢复方法及相应的缓解策略，证明了其在实际系统中的有效性。
AI.translation: 语言模型 API 可以在隐藏 logit 和 token 概率的同时暴露 token 特定的偏差。现有基于偏差的提取方法可以恢复相对 logit，但在理想算术中，一个共同的加法分量仍然未确定。我们识别出浮点偏差加法中的一个数值侧信道，该侧信道仅通过 token 身份就能暴露有关此分量的信息。该通道可以区分具有相同完整未扰动对数概率的得分向量。我们的方法利用二进制指数边界处可表示间距的变化。在所述 binary32 算术假设和已知可达得分区间下，它在最多 52 次 token 查询中精确恢复一个 logit 对及其未知的决胜优先级。给定完整的相对 logit，一个恢复的锚点可以确定原始 logit 向量。我们评估了来自七个模型家族的 11 个公共检查点上的恢复情况，并使用自适应区间搜索和锚点选择扩展了局部方法。在与 vLLM、SGLang 和 llama.cpp 的端到端实验中，自适应恢复在每个系统上所有 128 个 Qwen3-0.6B 输入（包括 64 个保留输入）上都成功。一项独立的仅基于 token 的实验提取了预训练小型模型的完整输出头表示，直至一个可逆的隐藏基变换。我们还建立了一个充分条件，通过在偏差加法前减去最大值来抑制通用偏移泄露。在受控实验中，这种缓解措施消除了所有观察到的通用偏移变体之间的区别，并在测试的随机偏差下保留了 token 决策。
AI.summary: 本文揭示了语言模型 API 中浮点偏差加法存在的数值侧信道，该侧信道能够泄露通常被隐藏的 logit 的通用加法分量。研究人员提出了一种利用二进制指数边界处可表示间距变化的方法来恢复这些信息，该方法在多种模型和系统上表现出高效率和准确性，甚至可以恢复完整的输出头表示。此外，文章还提出了一种通过在偏差加法前减去最大值来抑制这种信息泄露的有效缓解策略。
AI.keywords: Logit 泄露, 浮点偏差, 侧信道攻击, 语言模型 API, 数值精度
AI.comments: 这篇论文揭示了一个重要的安全和隐私问题，即语言模型 API 即使不直接暴露 logits，也可能通过浮点运算的数值特性间接泄露敏感信息。其创新点在于识别并利用了浮点偏差加法中的“侧信道”，这是一种非常巧妙且隐蔽的攻击方式。该研究不仅提出了有效的攻击方法，还提供了实用的缓解措施，对于提高语言模型 API 的安全性具有重要意义。

title: Efficient Preconditioned Optimization Methods with Frequent Directions
summary: Adaptive optimization methods have received considerable attention in recent years due to their strong empirical performance. However, they generally require maintaining a preconditioning matrix, which incurs prohibitive computational overhead in large-scale applications. To address these limitations, we investigate the acceleration of preconditioned optimization methods through frequent directions (FD), a widely used matrix sketching technique. We first propose FTSL by integrating FD with adaptive subgradient methods under the primal-dual framework and adding back the cumulative information discarded by FD. FTSL obtains a tighter regret bound than existing state-of-the-art results. We then apply a doubling trick that further reduces the time complexity of FTSL, while maintaining the same regret guarantee. We also consider optimization over matrix-valued decision variables and exploit their structural properties to construct sketched preconditioners. We develop FTSL-Shampoo by adapting FD to Shampoo and give a novel analysis under the primal-dual framework. To further mitigate its computational complexity, we design one-sided variants of FTSL-Shampoo under both mirror descent and primal-dual frameworks. Our algorithms not only reduce the computational cost of FTSL-Shampoo, but also achieve tighter regret bounds. We extend our methods to offline stochastic convex optimization and exploit smoothness to achieve faster convergence rates. Finally, we introduce practical variants of our algorithms and empirically demonstrate their efficiency and effectiveness across a broad range of tasks.

AI.title_translation: 高效预处理优化方法结合频繁方向
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为FTSL的新型自适应优化方法，通过结合频繁方向（FD）矩阵稀疏技术和累积信息，在保持理论界限的同时显著降低了计算成本。同时，还提出了FTSL-Shampoo及其单边变体，进一步优化了矩阵优化问题，并扩展到离线随机凸优化问题，最终通过实际应用验证了其效率和有效性。
AI.motivation: 传统的自适应优化方法在实际应用中存在计算开销过大的问题，尤其是在大规模场景下，需要维护预处理矩阵，这带来了高昂的计算成本。本研究旨在解决这一局限性，通过引入频繁方向（FD）技术来加速预处理优化方法。
AI.method: 本研究提出了一种名为FTSL（Frequent Directions with Adaptive Subgradient Methods under the Primal-Dual Framework）的方法，该方法将FD技术与自适应子梯度方法结合，并在对偶框架下进行分析。为了进一步降低计算复杂度，研究人员还应用了“加倍技巧”和设计了FTSL-Shampoo及其单边变体，并将其扩展到离线随机凸优化问题，利用平滑性实现更快的收敛速度。
AI.result: FTSL方法获得了比现有最优方法更优的遗憾界限。通过加倍技巧，在保持相同遗憾保证的同时，进一步降低了时间复杂度。FTSL-Shampoo及其单边变体不仅降低了计算成本，而且在矩阵优化问题上实现了更优的遗憾界限。在离线随机凸优化问题上，研究提出的方法实现了更快的收敛速度。实际应用结果表明，这些算法在效率和有效性方面表现出色。
AI.conclusion: 本研究成功地通过频繁方向（FD）技术加速了预处理优化方法，显著降低了计算开销，同时在理论上获得了更优的遗憾界限，并在实践中得到了验证。提出的FTSL及其变体为大规模自适应优化问题提供了一种高效且有效的解决方案。
AI.translation: 近年来，自适应优化方法因其强大的经验性能而备受关注。然而，它们通常需要维护一个预处理矩阵，这在大型应用中会带来过高的计算开销。为了解决这些局限性，我们研究了通过频繁方向（FD）——一种广泛使用的矩阵稀疏技术——来加速预处理优化方法。我们首先提出FTSL，通过将FD与对偶框架下的自适应子梯度方法相结合，并加回FD所丢弃的累积信息。FTSL获得了比现有最先进结果更优的遗憾界限。然后，我们应用加倍技巧，在保持相同遗憾保证的同时，进一步降低了FTSL的时间复杂度。我们还考虑了在矩阵值决策变量上的优化，并利用它们的结构特性来构建稀疏预处理矩阵。我们开发了FTSL-Shampoo，将FD应用于Shampoo算法，并在对偶框架下进行了新颖的分析。为了进一步减轻其计算复杂度，我们在镜像下降和对偶框架下设计了FTSL-Shampoo的单边变体。我们的算法不仅降低了FTSL-Shampoo的计算成本，而且实现了更优的遗憾界限。我们将我们的方法扩展到离线随机凸优化，并利用平滑性来实现更快的收敛速度。最后，我们介绍了我们算法的实际变体，并通过广泛的任务对其效率和有效性进行了实证证明。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为FTSL的新型自适应优化方法，通过结合频繁方向（FD）矩阵稀疏技术和累积信息，在保持理论界限的同时显著降低了计算成本。同时，还提出了FTSL-Shampoo及其单边变体，进一步优化了矩阵优化问题，并扩展到离线随机凸优化问题，最终通过实际应用验证了其效率和有效性。
AI.keywords: 频繁方向, 自适应优化, 预处理矩阵, 遗憾界限, 矩阵稀疏
AI.comments: 这项研究在解决大规模自适应优化中的计算效率问题方面取得了重要进展。通过巧妙地结合频繁方向（FD）技术和累积信息，作者们不仅降低了计算开销，而且在理论上获得了更优的遗憾界限。FTSL-Shampoo及其变体的提出，进一步扩展了该方法在矩阵优化问题上的应用。该研究的理论分析和实证结果都非常有说服力，为该领域的研究提供了有价值的贡献。然而，对于FD技术在不同规模和类型的数据集上的鲁棒性以及与其他先进优化技术的比较，可以进行更深入的探讨。
