AI.summary: 本文系统探究了基因表达转图像（GE2I）的学习机制，揭示了低频空间平滑模式与基因级表达保真度之间的权衡关系，证明了一对一基因像素分配的重要性，并为在单细胞数据上有效利用视觉模型先验提供了理论和实践指导。
AI.keywords: 单细胞RNA测序, 基因表达转图像 (GE2I), 空间平滑度, 信息保真度, 视觉骨干网络
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地探讨了生物信息与计算机视觉跨模态转换（GE2I）的核心机制，提出了“空间平滑度与信息保真度”的权衡视角，成功解释了以往研究中随机映射与结构化映射性能相近的反直觉现象。其关于“一对一基因-像素分配至关重要”的结论，为未来设计基于视觉架构的单细胞数据分析算法提供了明确且实用的指导原则。

title: Semi-Lagrangian Approximation of Master Equations with Individual Noise on Finite Graphs
summary: We develop and analyze a fully discrete semi-Lagrangian method for vector master equations associated with mean field games (MFGs) with individual noise on finite graphs. The method discretizes both the characteristic evolution in time and the population variable on the probability simplex. A central challenge is the degeneracy of the transport coefficients near the boundary of the open simplex, where no boundary condition is prescribed. To overcome this difficulty in the analysis, we introduce an interior localization based on exact density characteristics, which keeps numerical arrivals within compact regions of uniform coefficient control. Combined with a closure argument for the coupled numerical recursion, this localization yields local solvability of the updates and quantitative error bounds on compact subsets of the open simplex. Under additional $C^2$-regularity of the exact solution and suitable space--time mesh coupling, these bounds imply first-order accuracy. Furthermore, the density and value trajectories generated by the numerical master feedback converge to the corresponding MFG characteristics at the same rate. In the potential setting, the associated reconstructed density--flux pair is admissible and asymptotically optimal for the planning problem, with an action gap quadratic in the feedback error. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates, feedback responses to population redistribution, and the effects of graph topology.

AI.title_translation: 有限图上具有个体噪声的主方程的半拉格朗日近似
AI.tldr: 该论文提出了一种处理具有个体噪声的平均场博弈（MFG）的数值方法。该方法通过离散化时间和状态空间来解决主方程。研究人员开发了一种新的技术来处理数值计算中的奇异性问题，并证明了该方法的收敛性和精度。数值实验验证了该方法的有效性。
AI.motivation: 解决具有个体噪声的平均场博弈（MFG）的主方程的数值计算问题，特别是处理概率单纯形边界附近的奇异性。
AI.method: 开发并分析了一种完全离散的半拉格朗日方法，该方法离散化了时间和概率单纯形上的种群变量。通过引入基于精确密度特征的内部局部化来处理边界奇异性，并结合闭合论证来处理耦合数值递归，从而得到局部可解性和误差界限。
AI.result: 在满足附加条件的情况下，该方法具有一阶精度。数值生成的密度和价值轨迹以相同的速率收敛于MFG特征。在势能情况下，重建的密度-通量对是可容许的且渐近最优，具有二次于反馈误差的作用间隙。数值实验展示了收敛速率、对种群重新分配的反馈响应以及图拓扑的影响。
AI.conclusion: 该论文提出的半拉格朗日方法能够有效地处理具有个体噪声的MFG主方程，并在数值计算中实现了收敛性和精度。所提出的内部局部化技术克服了边界奇异性问题，并通过数值实验得到了验证。
AI.translation: 我们开发并分析了一种用于处理有限图上具有个体噪声的平均场博弈（MFGs）的向量主方程的全离散半拉格朗日方法。该方法在时间和概率单纯形上的种群变量上离散化了特征演化。一个核心的挑战是开放单纯形边界附近的输运系数的退化，在这些区域没有规定边界条件。为了克服分析中的这一困难，我们引入了一种基于精确密度特征的内部局部化，该方法将数值到达保持在系数控制紧区域内。结合对耦合数值递归的闭合论证，这种局部化产生了更新的局部可解性和开放单纯形紧子集上的定量误差界限。在满足附加的精确解的$C^2$正则性以及合适的时空网格耦合下，这些界限意味着一阶精度。此外，数值主反馈生成的密度和价值轨迹以相同的速率收敛于相应的MFG特征。在势能设定下，相关的重构密度-通量对是可容许的，并且对于规划问题是渐近最优的，具有二次于反馈误差的作用间隙。数值实验说明了收敛速率、对种群重新分配的反馈响应以及图拓扑的影响。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种用于求解具有个体噪声的平均场博弈（MFG）主方程的半拉格朗日数值方法。该方法通过时间和概率单纯形上的离散化来处理MFG问题。为了解决边界奇异性问题，作者引入了一种基于精确密度特征的内部局部化技术，并结合闭合论证来保证数值解的稳定性和准确性。研究表明，该方法具有一阶精度，并且数值结果能够收敛到精确解。此外，研究还探讨了该方法在势能情况下的性质以及其在不同图拓扑下的表现。
AI.keywords: 半拉格朗日方法, 平均场博弈, 个体噪声, 主方程, 内部局部化
AI.comments: 这项工作在数值方法领域具有重要意义，特别是对于解决具有个体噪声的平均场博弈问题。内部局部化技术的引入是该研究的一个亮点，有效地解决了数值计算中的关键挑战。然而，对$C^2$正则性和网格耦合的附加条件的依赖性可能限制了其在更广泛实际问题中的应用。未来的研究可以探索放宽这些条件的方法，并将其应用于更复杂的MFG模型。

title: A Node Embedding Framework for Model-Centric Conformance Checking in Process Mining
summary: Evaluating the quality of process models discovered from event logs is a fundamental challenge in process mining. Traditional evaluation relies on conformance metrics such as fitness and precision, which are highly sensitive to noise and deviations in event logs and therefore often fail to give a consistent assessment of discovery algorithms. We introduce a model-centric evaluation framework that combines node embeddings with Procrustes alignment to enable cross-graph comparability, since embeddings derived from different graphs reside in distinct vector spaces. The proposed PetriNetGraph method transforms Petri net process models into graph representations compatible with embedding algorithms. Comparing the node embeddings of ground-truth and discovered models through a parameterized cosine distance yields a unified and bounded metric for evaluating process discovery across datasets and methods. We evaluate the framework under static and context-aware scenarios to examine how prior knowledge of activity existence influences the assessment of structural similarity. The framework also integrates a compliance checking mechanism that localizes deviations at the activity level and an entropy-regularized node distance aggregation function that quantifies global deviations across the model. Experiments on nine publicly available event logs show that the approach provides a reliable embedding-based conformance indicator that reflects the behavior of fitness and precision. Experiments on synthetic logs with controlled noise levels confirm that it is substantially more robust to log deviations than traditional conformance metrics, PetriNet2Vec, and its dynamic-window and Procrustes-aligned variants, while remaining sensitive to process model degradation. All implementation details and datasets are publicly available.

AI.title_translation: 一种用于流程挖掘中以模型为中心的合规性检查的节点嵌入框架
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于节点嵌入和Procrustes对齐的模型中心合规性检查框架，用于流程挖掘，相比传统指标对日志偏差更具鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: 评估从事件日志中发现的流程模型的质量是流程挖掘中的一个基本挑战。传统的评估方法依赖于适应度和精确度等合规性指标，但这些指标对事件日志中的噪声和偏差高度敏感，因此常常无法对发现算法给出一致的评估。
AI.method: 本文引入了一个以模型为中心的评估框架，该框架将节点嵌入与Procrustes对齐相结合，以实现跨图可比性。提出的PetriNetGraph方法将Petri网流程模型转换为与嵌入算法兼容的图表示。通过参数化余弦距离比较真实模型和发现模型的节点嵌入，得到一个统一且有界的指标，用于跨数据集和方法评估流程发现。该框架在静态和上下文感知场景下进行评估，并集成了在活动级别定位偏差的合规性检查机制，以及量化模型全局偏差的熵正则化节点距离聚合函数。
AI.result: 在九个公开可用的事件日志上的实验表明，该方法提供了一个可靠的基于嵌入的合规性指标，反映了适应度和精确度的行为。在具有受控噪声水平的合成日志上的实验证实，它比传统合规性指标、PetriNet2Vec及其动态窗口和Procrustes对齐变体对日志偏差具有更强的鲁棒性，同时对流程模型退化保持敏感。
AI.conclusion: 该框架提供了一个可靠的、基于嵌入的合规性指标，能够反映传统适应度和精确度指标的行为，并且对日志偏差具有显著的鲁棒性，同时对流程模型退化保持敏感，从而解决了传统指标的局限性并提供了一致的评估。
AI.translation: 从事件日志中发现的流程模型质量评估是流程挖掘中的一个基本挑战。传统的评估依赖于适应度和精确度等合规性指标，这些指标对事件日志中的噪声和偏差高度敏感，因此常常无法对发现算法给出一致的评估。我们引入了一个以模型为中心的评估框架，该框架将节点嵌入与Procrustes对齐相结合，以实现跨图可比性，因为来自不同图的嵌入位于不同的向量空间中。所提出的PetriNetGraph方法将Petri网流程模型转换为与嵌入算法兼容的图表示。通过参数化余弦距离比较真实模型和发现模型的节点嵌入，得到一个统一且有界的指标，用于跨数据集和方法评估流程发现。我们在静态和上下文感知场景下评估该框架，以检查活动存在先验知识如何影响结构相似性的评估。该框架还集成了在活动级别定位偏差的合规性检查机制，以及量化模型全局偏差的熵正则化节点距离聚合函数。在九个公开可用的事件日志上的实验表明，该方法提供了一个可靠的基于嵌入的合规性指标，反映了适应度和精确度的行为。在具有受控噪声水平的合成日志上的实验证实，它比传统合规性指标、PetriNet2Vec及其动态窗口和Procrustes对齐变体对日志偏差具有更强的鲁棒性，同时对流程模型退化保持敏感。所有实现细节和数据集均已公开。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种用于流程挖掘中以模型为中心的合规性检查的新框架，该框架结合了节点嵌入和Procrustes对齐，以提供一个鲁棒、统一且有界的评估指标。该方法将Petri网模型转换为图表示，通过参数化余弦距离比较真实模型和发现模型的节点嵌入。它还集成了活动级偏差定位机制和全局偏差量化函数。实验证明，该方法比传统合规性指标对日志偏差更具鲁棒性，同时能可靠地反映模型行为和降级。
AI.keywords: 节点嵌入, 合规性检查, 流程挖掘, Petri网, Procrustes对齐
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于利用节点嵌入和Procrustes对齐进行鲁棒的合规性检查，解决了传统方法对噪声敏感的问题。它提供了一种更稳定和一致的评估，这对于实际的流程挖掘应用至关重要，尤其是在处理真实世界中包含噪声和偏差的事件日志时。其对模型中心评估的关注以及对局部和全局偏差的量化能力，增强了其在实际应用中的实用性。

title: Pushback in a Haystack: Language Models Respond to Factual Errors Ambiguously and Ineffectively
summary: The sycophancy of language models, or their failure to push back against faulty user input, is now widely studied. However, if LMs do push back, is sycophancy solved? We show that LMs vary in how they present pushback, and thus vary in how effectively they correct user beliefs. We introduce a phrase-level, human-validated response labeling framework to uncover fine-grained insights into how LMs push against and/or affirm false inputs. We develop and apply our framework on model responses in five languages: English, German, Chinese, Hindi, and Yoruba. We find that when models do push back against users' false assertions, they tend to use indirect phrasing and mix in affirmation, with more indirectness in Hindi and Yoruba than in other languages considered. In a large-scale human study (n = 300), we find that the pushback ambiguity we identified may fail to correct and prevent users' factual misconceptions.

AI.title_translation: 在稻草堆里推诿：语言模型对事实错误的反应模糊且无效
AI.tldr: 语言模型在面对用户错误输入时，即使进行“推诿”（pushback），也常常因为表达方式含糊不清（如间接措辞和混合肯定）而无法有效纠正用户的错误认知，尤其是在印地语和约鲁巴语等语言中。
AI.motivation: 研究语言模型在推诿用户错误输入时的有效性，以及推诿方式对纠正用户错误认知的潜在影响，探究“推诿”是否能解决模型的“谄媚”问题。
AI.method: 开发并应用了一个短语级别的、经过人类验证的响应标注框架，用于分析模型在面对错误输入时，是推诿还是肯定。该框架应用于五种语言（英语、德语、中文、印地语、约鲁巴语）的模型响应。通过大规模人类研究（n=300）评估推诿的有效性。
AI.result: 语言模型在推诿用户错误断言时，倾向于使用间接措辞，并混合使用肯定性语句。印地语和约鲁巴语的间接性高于其他语言。研究发现，这种模糊的推诿方式可能无法纠正和阻止用户的事实误解。
AI.conclusion: 语言模型的“推诿”反应可能因其模糊和混合肯定的表达方式而效果不佳，无法有效纠正用户的错误认知。推诿方式的有效性因语言而异，需要进一步研究。
AI.translation: 语言模型的谄媚，或者说它们未能抵制错误的用戶輸入，現在已被廣泛研究。然而，如果語言模型確實進行了抵制，那麼谄媚問題是否就解決了？我們表明，語言模型在表達抵制的方式上有所不同，因此在糾正用戶信念方面的有效性也不同。我們引入了一個短語級別的、經過人類驗證的響應標籤框架，以揭示語言模型如何抵制和/或肯定錯誤輸入的細微差別。我們在五種語言的 النموذج 響應上開發並應用了我們的框架：英語、德語、中文、印地語和約魯巴語。我們發現，當模型確實抵制用戶的錯誤斷言時，它們傾向於使用間接措辭並混合肯定，在印地語和約魯巴語中的間接性高於所考慮的其他語言。在一項大規模的人類研究（n = 300）中，我們發現我們識別出的推诿模糊性可能無法糾正和阻止用戶的事實誤解。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了语言模型（LMs）在面对用户错误输入时的“推诿”（pushback）行为。研究人员开发了一个短语级别的标注框架，分析了五种语言的模型响应，发现模型在推诿时常使用间接措辞并夹杂肯定，尤其在印地语和约鲁巴语中更为明显。大规模人类研究（n=300）表明，这种模糊的推诿方式可能无法有效纠正用户的错误认知。因此，尽管模型能够“推诿”，但其表达方式的有效性仍有待提高。
AI.keywords: 语言模型, 推诿, 事实错误, 错误认知, 表达模糊性
AI.comments: 该研究揭示了语言模型在纠正用户错误信息方面的一个重要且常常被忽视的方面：推诿的有效性。通过引入细粒度的分析框架和进行大规模人类实验，研究强调了模型在表达推诿时的措辞选择和文化差异（语言差异）的重要性。研究结果表明，仅仅“推诿”是不够的，推诿的方式直接影响其纠错能力。这对于开发更可靠、更有帮助的AI助手具有重要意义。局限性在于，研究主要关注推诿的模糊性，未来可以进一步探索如何设计更有效的推诿策略。

title: A Differentiable 3D Scene Graph Metric via Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry
summary: 3D scene graph prediction is commonly supervised with local object and predicate classification losses. Although effective for slot-wise label prediction, this formulation does not provide a graph-level semantic distance between a predicted scene graph and its ground truth: semantically mild label errors and structurally disruptive relational errors can be treated similarly, and subject-predicate-object facts are not compared as scene-level units. We propose Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry, a graph-level supervision objective that measures the semantic and structural discrepancy between 3D scene graphs. Our key idea is to reinterpret the conventional classifier outputs of a 3D scene graph predictor as an aligned probabilistic scene graph field, where object and predicate predictions jointly define contextual subject-predicate-object facts. This formulation yields a differentiable metric-based training objective with an efficient factorized implementation and can be applied to existing 3D scene graph prediction architectures without modifying their network design. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate that our supervision improves downstream graph-conditioned 3D scene generation, while ablation studies confirm the complementary roles of the proposed graph-level terms and user studies show better graph descriptiveness, relation plausibility, and structural preservation.

AI.title_translation: 通过上下文海林格三元组几何的可微分3D场景图度量
AI.tldr: 提出了一种基于上下文海林格三元组几何的可微分3D场景图图级度量与监督方法，有效弥补了传统局部损失在图结构和语义度量上的不足。
AI.motivation: 现有的3D场景图预测通常采用局部对象和谓词分类损失进行监督，这种方法无法提供图级别的语义距离，无法区分轻微的语义标签错误和结构破坏性的关系错误，也没有将主谓宾事实作为场景级别的单元进行比较。
AI.method: 提出Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry，将3D场景图预测器的传统分类器输出重新解释为对齐的概率场景图场，其中对象和谓词预测共同定义了上下文主谓宾事实，从而形成一个具有高效因式分解实现的可微分度量训练目标。
AI.result: 在3DSSG数据集上的实验表明，该监督方法改善了下游基于图的3D场景生成，消融实验证实了图级别各项的互补作用，用户研究显示其具有更好的图描述性、关系合理性和结构保持能力。
AI.conclusion: Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry 能够有效作为3D场景图预测的可微分度量和监督目标，改善下游3D场景生成，并在图描述性、关系合理性和结构保持方面优于传统方法。
AI.translation: 3D场景图预测通常采用局部对象和谓词分类损失进行监督。尽管该公式对槽位标签预测有效，但它没有提供预测场景图与其真实值之间的图级语义距离：语义较轻的标签错误和结构破坏性的关系错误可能会受到相似对待，且主谓宾事实未作为场景级单元进行比较。我们提出了上下文海林格三元组几何（Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry），这是一个衡量3D场景图之间语义和结构差异的图级监督目标。我们的核心思想是将3D场景图预测器的传统分类器输出重新解释为一个对齐的概率场景图场，其中对象和谓词预测共同定义了上下文的主谓宾事实。该公式产生了一个可微分的基于度量的训练目标，具有高效的因式分解实现，并且可以应用于现有的3D场景图预测架构而无需修改其网络设计。在3DSSG上的实验表明，我们的监督改善了下游的图条件3D场景生成，而消融实验证实了所提出的图级项的互补作用，用户研究显示出更好的图描述性、关系合理性和结构保持性。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一种名为Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry的3D场景图可微分度量与监督目标，用于测量预测与真实3D场景图之间的语义和结构差异。该方法将分类器输出解释为概率场景图场，无需修改网络架构即可应用于现有模型，实验证明其能有效提升3D场景生成的质量和图的结构合理性。
AI.keywords: 3D Scene Graphs, Metric Learning, Graph-Level Supervision, Triplet Geometry, Probabilistic Fields
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的可微分3D场景图度量方法，通过Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry，解决了传统逐项分类损失无法有效度量图级别语义和结构差异的问题。创新点在于将分类器输出重新解释为概率场景图场，实现了无需修改网络架构的图级别监督，对3D场景生成等下游任务具有重要意义。

title: From Token Correction to Claim Admission: Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Large vision-language models often exhibit object hallucination, generating claims that are not supported by the input image. To mitigate this issue, we propose Evidence-Guided Visual Claim Admission (EGVCA), a training-free framework that admits a semantic claim only when it receives sufficient image-dependent support. EGVCA measures this support by comparing the claim likelihood under the observed image and a visual-null input. For captioning, it controls semantic expansion without altering token generation. For binary visual question answering, it combines atomic visual support with the image-induced change in the model's native Yes--No margin. Experiments on CHAIR, POPE, and MME across three LVLM backbones show that EGVCA substantially reduces object hallucination while preserving caption quality. It achieves the highest POPE F1 in eight of nine backbone--sampling settings and improves the native MME total score on all three backbones. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of claim-level admission as a simple alternative to token-level distribution correction.

AI.title_translation: 从令牌校正到声明接受：大型视觉语言模型中免训练幻觉缓解
AI.tldr: EGVCA是一个免训练框架，通过比较图像和视觉空输入下的声明可能性来减少大型视觉语言模型中的对象幻觉，同时保持字幕质量。
AI.motivation: 大型视觉语言模型经常表现出对象幻觉，即生成与输入图像不符的声明。本文旨在缓解这一问题。
AI.method: 本文提出了证据引导的视觉声明接受（EGVCA），一个免训练框架。EGVCA通过比较在观察图像和视觉空输入下声明的可能性来衡量图像对语义声明的支持度，只有当获得足够的图像依赖支持时才接受声明。对于字幕生成，它在不改变令牌生成的情况下控制语义扩展。对于二元视觉问答，它将原子视觉支持与模型原生是-否裕度的图像诱导变化相结合。
AI.result: 在CHAIR、POPE和MME数据集上，EGVCA在三个LVLM骨干模型上进行了实验，结果显示它显著减少了对象幻觉，同时保持了字幕质量。在九个骨干-采样设置中的八个中，EGVCA实现了最高的POPE F1分数，并改善了所有三个骨干模型上的原生MME总分。
AI.conclusion: 声明级别的接受作为令牌级别分布校正的简单替代方案，在缓解大型视觉语言模型中的对象幻觉方面是有效的。
AI.translation: 大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）经常表现出对象幻觉，即生成与输入图像不符的声明。为了缓解这个问题，我们提出了证据引导的视觉声明接受（EGVCA），这是一个免训练框架，只有当语义声明获得足够的图像依赖支持时才接受它。EGVCA通过比较在观察图像和视觉空输入下声明的可能性来衡量这种支持。对于字幕生成，它在不改变令牌生成的情况下控制语义扩展。对于二元视觉问答，它将原子视觉支持与模型原生是-否裕度的图像诱导变化相结合。在CHAIR、POPE和MME数据集上，对三个LVLM骨干模型进行的实验表明，EGVCA显著减少了对象幻觉，同时保持了字幕质量。它在九个骨干-采样设置中的八个中实现了最高的POPE F1分数，并改善了所有三个骨干模型上的原生MME总分。这些结果表明，声明级别的接受作为令牌级别分布校正的简单替代方案是有效的。
AI.summary: 本文提出了EGVCA，一个免训练框架，用于缓解大型视觉语言模型中的对象幻觉。它通过评估图像对语义声明的支持度来决定是否接受声明，该支持度通过比较声明在实际图像和视觉空输入下的可能性来衡量。实验证明，EGVCA能有效减少幻觉，同时保持字幕质量，并在多个基准测试中表现出色。
AI.keywords: 对象幻觉, 视觉语言模型, 免训练, 声明接受, EGVCA
AI.comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于提出了一个免训练的声明级别接受框架EGVCA，以替代传统的令牌级别校正方法来缓解LVLM中的对象幻觉。其重要性在于提供了一种简单而有效的方法来提高LVLM的可靠性，同时避免了耗时的再训练过程。通过比较声明在有图像和无图像支持下的可能性来判断其真实性，这是一个巧妙且可解释的机制。

title: Focus on What You Need: Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
summary: Multimodal sarcasm detection has attracted increasing attention due to the widespread use of images and text on social media platforms. Existing studies generally treat the semantic or emotional inconsistency between images and text as a key cue for identifying sarcastic expressions. However, images in real-world scenarios often contain multiple visual objects, many of which are irrelevant to sarcasm-related semantics. Such redundant visual information may introduce noise during cross-modal interaction, distracting models from focusing on critical sarcasm cues and potentially leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this issue, we propose GLDA (Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention), a multimodal sarcasm detection framework that models cross-modal interactions from a global-to-local perspective. Specifically, GLDA first employs a global multimodal fusion module to capture high-level semantic interactions between visual and textual modalities, enabling the model to identify coarse-grained cross-modal inconsistencies. To further reduce the influence of irrelevant objects, GLDA introduces a local gated cross-modal attention mechanism that dynamically filters redundant visual and textual features and refines multimodal representations at a finer granularity. In addition, a multi-branch learning objective is designed to jointly optimize unimodal and multimodal representations. Experimental results demonstrate that GLDA effectively improves sarcasm detection performance and achieves competitive results compared with existing approaches. The code will be available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GLDA-DBE6.

title: Where Small Mistakes Matter: Quantifying State Criticality for Imitation Learning
comments: Accepted to the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). 18 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables. Project website: https://sia-lab-git.github.io/SCRIM/
summary: Imitation learning typically treats every demonstration state as equally important, optimizing a behavior-cloning objective uniformly across the dataset. Yet not all states are created equal: in a small number of critical states, even a slight deviation from the expert action can lead to a failure, while in many other states such errors are recoverable and inconsequential. We formalize state criticality in imitation learning as the worst-case degradation in downstream value induced by a bounded perturbation of the expert action at a given state. We then propose SCRIM, a practical State CRIticality Measure that estimates this quantity by training an adversarial disturbance policy and a value critic around a fixed imitation policy. SCRIM assigns each demonstration state a score reflecting how vulnerable the task outcome is to small, policy-relevant action errors. We show that these scores can be used to reweight behavior-cloning losses, improving imitation at consequential states and increasing overall task performance. We further show that SCRIM enables data curation by selecting compact, high-value subsets of demonstrations that preserve performance while substantially reducing the amount of training data. We evaluate SCRIM across various simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, and demonstrate that SCRIM improves policy training, enables efficient data selection, and provides interpretable insights into which moments in a demonstration are most critical for task success. Project website: https://sia-lab-git.github.io/SCRIM/

title: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents
summary: Training graphical user interface (GUI) agents with reinforcement learning suffers from sparse outcome rewards, leading to inefficient learning. Process rewards offer a promising direction for credit assignment to intermediate actions; however, accurately evaluating an action requires identifying evidence across long-horizon GUI trajectories, as its value may depend on information beyond its immediate state and observation. In this paper, we propose an adaptive-group process reward framework that dynamically partitions a GUI trajectory into semantically coherent subgoal groups, enabling process reward estimation at both the action and group levels. At the action level, a critic evaluates each action based on the visual changes and subsequent actions within the group for action correctness and contribution to the subgoal. At the group level, the framework aggregates action-level evaluations to assess subgoal completion and contribution to the overall task, and further refines these assessments by leveraging the context of all groups in the trajectory. The process reward of each action is obtained by combining its action-level evaluation with the refined group-level evaluation. We further augment GRPO's outcome advantage with the proposed process rewards to provide finer-grained guidance for GUI agent training. Experiments on process reward benchmarks and downstream RL training demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing: Below Half Threshold Rate
summary:
We study the local leakage resilience of Shamir secret sharing, where an adversary leaks a bounded number of bits from every share. For $n$ parties and reconstruction threshold $k$ over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p>n$, we prove the following.
  (1) There is an absolute constant $c_{\mathrm{bh}}<1/2$ such that, for $k\ge c_{\mathrm{bh}}n$, Shamir sharing is resilient to arbitrary one-bit leakage from every share. The best previous threshold was $0.668n$.
  (2) For every fixed $0<δ<1/2$ and $k\ge(1/2+δ)n$, Shamir sharing is resilient to $\left\lfloor\fracδ{24}\log_2 n\right\rfloor$ bits of arbitrary local leakage per share. By a recent attack, this number of bits is optimal up to a constant factor depending on $δ$.
  (3) For every fixed threshold rate $c>0$ and $k\ge cn$, Shamir sharing is resilient to quadratic-residue leakage and to almost all local leakage functions of up to $η_c\log_2 p$ bits, for a constant $η_c>0$.
  All three results follow from one analytic framework, which we develop for generalized Reed--Solomon codes: local leakage from a uniform codeword is statistically close to the same leakage from independent uniform field elements. The framework expresses the leakage distance as the norm of a function on the leakage outputs. The Efron--Stein decomposition splits this function into orthogonal components indexed by supports of dual codewords. Two tools bound the components: list recovery of the dual code, which is ordinary list decoding for one-bit leakage, and a generalized von Neumann inequality for MDS systems of linear forms that retains linearly many Gowers norms. The first tool gives the result above half, the second gives the constant-rate result, and applying both to different ranges of supports in the same decomposition gives the result below half.

title: Fully Dynamic Random-Walk Quantities on Undirected Expanders and $κ$-Uniform Directed Graphs
summary:
We study fully dynamic data structures for random-walk quantities on undirected expanders and fast-mixing directed graphs. For an unweighted graph whose normalized Laplacian has spectral gap at least $γ$, we give a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ effective-resistance data structure with expected update time $O(γ^{-4}\varepsilon^{-2}\log n\log^4(n/\varepsilon))$ and expected $O(1)$ query time.
  For directed graphs, somewhat surprisingly, the OMv conjecture precludes a fast data structure based on rapid mixing conditions alone. To address this, we introduce the notion of $κ$-uniform directed graphs, which requires the stationary distribution to $κ$-approximate the uniform distribution, and show that in this setting, random walk based data structures with $\text{poly}(κ, \log{n}, \varepsilon^{-1})$ update/query times are possible.

title: Confine to the Task, Anchor the Rest: Concept-Guided Retention Regularizer for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been widely used, yet the adapted model suffers catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. While most existing work hardens the adapter by constraining where the weight update may lie, we note that constraining this weight channel does not constrain the activation channel. In this paper, we propose Concept-Guided Retention (CGR), a plug-and-play regularizer that constrains both for any PEFT base. CGR reads a frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) and treats two disjoint concept sets differently. It softly confines the update to the task-concept subspace (via weight channel), and anchors a selected set of general-purpose concepts to the frozen model (via activation channel). We also provide anchor value bounds based on weight updates to understand how they interact, and show that both terms are necessary. On a CLIP vision panel, CGR significantly improves retention at comparable accuracy for every base, and the same pattern holds for world-knowledge retention under Llama-3.1-8B instruction tuning. Because the protected directions are named SAE concepts, CGR remains inspectable and controllable.

title: MissPath-FM: Flow Matching with Structured Priors for Partially Observed Time Series
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 24 pages. Project page: https://zgp110.github.io/misspath-fm/ Code: https://github.com/zgp110/misspath-fm
summary: Flow matching has emerged as a powerful alternative to diffusion models for generative modeling, but standard conditional flow matching is fundamentally misaligned with partially observed time series: starting from an uninformed Gaussian source forces the model to transport even already-observed entries from noise to the target, wasting capacity on trivially known regions. We propose MissPath-FM, a partial-observation-aware flow matching framework that redesigns the source prior and probability path for incomplete time series. MissPath-FM employs structured source priors (interpolation priors and Gaussian process posterior priors) to initialize the flow close to the observed signal, paired with a missingness-aware smooth path that allocates transport asymmetrically between observed and missing regions. We evaluate systematically across four datasets, four missingness mechanisms (MCAR, block, MNAR, irregular), two missing ratios, and three sequence lengths (T in {24, 48, 96}), totaling 48 settings against eight baselines. MissPath-FM wins 29 of 32 settings at T=48 and 45 of 48 overall (93.8%). Our ablations reveal a regime-dependent design hierarchy in which no single component suffices: under random missingness the source prior yields a large initial gain, but under structured block missingness it can fail entirely and the learned flow becomes indispensable; the missingness-aware path contributes a further 12%-26% across all regimes. Mechanistically, structured priors shorten observed-region transport by up to 15x, concentrating the velocity field on genuinely uncertain entries. Project page: https://zgp110.github.io/misspath-fm/

title: Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning Based Voice Conversion for Electrolaryngeal Speech Enhancement
summary: Electrolaryngeal (EL) speech suffers from severe acoustic mismatches with normal speech, resulting in degraded naturalness and intelligibility. These mismatches also make sequence-to-sequence voice conversion struggle to learn robust intermediate representations, hindering EL-speech-to-normal-speech conversion (EL2SP) performance. To address this, we propose a novel multimodal contrastive representation learning framework to 1) achieve richer multimodal-representation learning, and 2) facilitate the transferability of multimodal representations to speech-only EL2SP. First, EL speech and text representations are fused to learn multimodal representations for target speech generation, during which cross-modal contrastive learning is employed to encourage a semantically consistent speech--text representation space. Next, the fused representations are treated as a fixed target to guide speech-only representation learning through cross-stage contrastive learning, enabling multimodal knowledge to be transferred to the EL2SP task while preserving architectural and inference simplicity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms both the speech-only and multimodal-based baselines.

title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.

title: Keep Your Receipts: Trustworthy Cleanup of Agent-Built Knowledge Graphs
comments: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development
summary: Agents build knowledge graphs as memory, and building them has become easy. Maintaining them has not. When a source is retracted, overruled, or erased, everything built on top of it (entity merges, entailed edges, community summaries) must be re-examined, and the maintainer must choose between deleting too much and too little. Deployed pipelines delete only the directly extracted facts: on our corpus that reduces contaminated queries from 32.2% to 28.0% under a real retraction and changes nothing under predicate revocation. Rebuilding is no repair for a constructor that samples: two builds of the same 300-document corpus differ in 29,475 artifacts, five times the 6,248 that removing the 61 retracted documents changes. PolyGraph instead asks the constructor for receipts: for every artifact, alternative bundles of source evidence, each claimed sufficient on its own, emitted in the call that creates it. Cleanup is then set arithmetic over the receipts, with no model calls. Because receipts are the model's own self-report, a re-derivation audit checks them by deleting the cited evidence and testing whether the constructor still produces the artifact. The audit finds that a receipt is trustworthy when it is shaped like the claim it backs. Merge receipts, each backing one narrow claim, agree with re-derivation 68% and 85% of the time. Summary receipts, elicited per sentence but stored as one flat list for the whole text, are wrong about two thirds of the time, almost always by keeping dead content. One receipt per sentence instead is 100% and 88% faithful and lets cleanup keep 33 of 35 touched summaries. The result holds under a second oracle model, a claim-blind prompt, ten further deletions, a second domain and a second constructor. Distrusting the summary layer cuts contaminated queries to 0.4% and 0.8% at 99.8 to 100% of the recall a perfect maintainer would return.

title: Upstream Influence, Downstream Re-Anchoring in LLM Agent Chains
summary: People act on evaluative judgments produced by LLM agents, and in multi-agent systems those judgments pass through several agents before reaching a person. We show that a workflow's information architecture---source access, handoff format, and which model reads the untrusted content---governs how much of a coordinated manipulation reaches the end. On 32 Taiwan~2025 recall cases, ten authentic Threads comments shown to one agent move its stance by $+0.171$ toward the injected position, and a mirrored set moves it the other way. Passing that judgment down a chain removes more than half of the shift by the third agent; keeping the comments in front of every agent sustains more of it. The reduction is not attrition in transit: each receiver discounts the inherited stance in proportion to how far it sits from its own reading of the evidence, returning to what that evidence implies for the case rather than to neutrality---consistent with partial re-anchoring. Handoff format is a second lever: a stance relayed without its reasoning is largely discounted. Susceptibility at the exposed seat varies fourfold across models, while the chain's arrangement does not matter at all. None of this is visible in the transcripts---the injected claims are almost never restated, so reasoning-trace audits miss the attack.

title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
summary: Long-horizon, semi-verifiable agentic tasks often rely on rubric-based evaluation, but the evidence needed to assess these tasks can be spread across the environment state and the execution trace. A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success. When rubric verdicts serve as reinforcement-learning rewards, such errors can reinforce undesirable behavior. We introduce Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier that investigates both state and trace and relies on a claim only after independently validating it against its source. Bounded queries and joint investigation of related criteria reduce context use and redundant work, and each verdict carries an auditable receipt of its supporting evidence. Across 2,586 human-labeled criteria from 100 personal-assistant episodes, Sauron achieves the highest F1 of five verifiers on all eight backbones tested while costing less than Gandalf, the strongest baseline. With GPT-5.6 Sol, it reaches 0.96 F1 versus Gandalf's 0.92 at 23% lower cost, with a wider margin on process criteria. On a paired fault-injection suite covering 13 families, several of which simulate reward hacking, Sauron detects 97% of injected failures while flagging only 2% of clean controls, outperforming baselines even when they are given the full trace. On TRAIL, a benchmark for detecting and localizing real agent errors, Sauron leads both Gandalf and TRAIL's own judge on all three quality metrics.

title: Beyond Model Scaling: Rethinking Sequence Construction for Transformer-based Network Intrusion Detection
summary: Transformer-based network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) have shown strong potential for detecting multi-stage cyberattacks, yet most methods construct input sequences using fixed temporalization schemes rather than treating sequence construction as a systems design decision. In flow-based intrusion detection, timestamp-based windowing often fragments related attack activities while merging unrelated communications, reducing the behavioral context available to transformers. We present a unified pipeline abstraction that decomposes transformer-based NIDS into four design dimensions (traffic representation, temporalization, transformer backbone, and prediction aggregation) and propose session-coherent temporalization, which constructs sequences from communication sessions instead of fixed time windows. Experiments on three complementary intrusion detection datasets show that temporalization is the dominant factor governing transformer performance: session-coherent temporalization more than doubles Macro-F1 over timestamp-based windowing, enabling lightweight transformers to achieve up to 0.95 Macro-F1 at substantially higher inference throughput than pretrained models. We further vary the transformer size from 0.65M to 3.38M parameters and find that larger transformer models provide no measurable accuracy improvement despite substantially higher computational cost, while zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation shows only modest gains under domain shift. These results indicate that preserving communication-session semantics, rather than scaling transformer capacity, is the key to accurate and efficient transformer-based intrusion detection.

title: TSRL: Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Continual Agent Training
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents excel at complex, multi-step tasks but suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual learning--acquiring new skills often degrades previously mastered capabilities. Existing post-training paradigms face a fundamental trade-off: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is sample-efficient but prone to severe forgetting, while Reinforcement Learning (RL) preserves prior capabilities but converges slowly without expert guidance. To bridge this gap, we introduce Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning (TSRL), a framework that integrates the strengths of both paradigms through an adaptive, state-dependent expert supervision mechanism. TSRL employs RL as the optimization backbone, activating SFT selectively on "hard states" where the policy fails. Theoretically, we show that restricting supervision to failure states derives an upper bound on the cumulative parameter updates, thereby reducing forgetting compared to full SFT. Empirically, TSRL achieves consistent gains across three agent benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop, and Deep Search) at both 7B and 32B scales. In continual learning scenarios, our method retains up to 9.6 points more capability on prior tasks than SFT->RL baselines, while matching or exceeding target-task performance.

title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models
summary: Agent skills turn natural-language instructions into actions, creating a security challenge: legitimate automation and malicious behaviour can look deceptively similar. A practical screen must catch nearly every attack while keeping the review load manageable. We present SkillScreen, a compact decision model trained to score skill maliciousness directly from SKILL.md in a single forward pass. On MaliciousSkillBench, SkillScreen flags 20-25% of benign skills at 99% recall on unseen attack families, substantially fewer than the word-level classifier and prompted LLM judges tested. Under the same training protocol, it also generalizes better than a fully fine-tuned encoder to unseen sources. Yet unfamiliar benign sources sharply increase false positives, showing that recognizing new attacks does not ensure reliable screening of new skill collections. Our results demonstrate the value of task-trained decision models for high-recall skill screening. Project page: https://jerroldh.github.io/SkillScreen-webpage/

title: Safety for Whom? Benchmarking Understanding Beyond Refusal in Egocentric Multimodal Assistants
summary: Egocentric multimodal assistants see through the user's eyes and guide what the user does next, so their outputs directly shape physical actions, including those that affect bystanders. Yet existing safety evaluations do not distinguish whom a response would harm, and score only whether a model refuses. Pooling all harms into one refusal rate hides two failures: a model may protect one target but not another, and it may refuse without understanding the risk, or understand it and comply anyway. We present STOU, a benchmark of 2,902 egocentric video-audio and video-text queries whose potential harm targets the user (Self), co-present individuals (The Others), or society at large (Others). Our evaluation decouples safety understanding from refusal behavior: beyond refusal, we score whether the model recognizes the user's intent, the presence and target of harm, and its downstream consequences. Across 10 open and closed source omnimodal and multimodal LLMs, we find that refusal varies systematically with the harm target, and that models often recognize a harm yet still assist with it. These results show that refusal rates alone cannot certify an assistant as safe, and that safety alignment must account for who would be harmed. Project page: https://onedayoneyeah.github.io/safety-for-whom

title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) often underperforms full fine-tuning. We investigate this performance gap through a tangent-space lens: factorized updates are confined to the tangent space of the current low-rank factors, leaving gradient components outside this space unexploited. An analysis of ten representative LoRA variants reveals that these residual components account for most of the gradient energy and exhibit strong spectral concentration. Motivated by this finding, we propose Dynamic Tangent LoRA (DT-LoRA), which partitions a fixed rank budget into a stable branch and a dynamic branch to capture the principal residual gradient directions. We show that these directions define the optimal update of a local quadratic model under orthogonal-complement and rank constraints. Matrix-free randomized SVD recovers them without materializing the residual gradient, while controlled write-back preserves accumulated updates and stabilizes training within the allocated rank. DT-LoRA adds no trainable parameters or inference cost over LoRA. Experiments across computer vision and natural language processing tasks demonstrate consistent improvements over LoRA and its variants. Moreover, despite being a general-purpose adaptation method, DT-LoRA outperforms task-specific approaches to open-vocabulary domain generalization for semantic segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art results. Code is available at https://github.com/Snipine/DT-LoRA.

title: Understanding Machine Taste: Aesthetic Agreement Across Foundation Models in K-pop
summary: As foundation models enter creative industries, understanding their aesthetic preferences becomes an important step toward AI-assisted creative decision making. In this work, we investigate how foundation models evaluate creative content and characterize their ``machine taste'' using K-pop songs and music videos as a testbed. We formulate aesthetic evaluation as a pairwise ranking problem and systematically examine pairwise inter-model agreement, group-level consensus, and cross-modal preference alignment. Our results reveal stronger pairwise inter-model agreement and group-level consensus in visual evaluation than in audio evaluation, while preferences across the two modalities remain weakly aligned. We further examine how visual consensus rankings relate to real-world popularity using historical YouTube viewership data, finding positive but varying correlations across artist groups. These findings provide initial insights into machine aesthetic preferences and lay the groundwork for future AI-assisted creative decision making that considers creative content, artist identity, audience preferences, and market dynamics.

title: CoCA: Criterion-Aware Credit Assignment for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) evaluates responses against explicit criteria to construct rewards, offering a viable way to train large language models on open-ended tasks. However, standard methods compress criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards and assign uniform token advantages, leaving structured rubric supervision underutilized. Recent work seeks finer-grained guidance by treating rubrics as privileged information to derive self-distillation targets, but the resulting learning signal is not grounded in criterion outcomes and can lead to reward degradation. This motivates us to reframe the problem as criterion-aware credit assignment, where privileged rubric information serves as a relevance cue for credit allocation rather than a source of imitation targets. Accordingly, we propose CoCA, which derives criterion-level credits from group-relative outcomes and allocates them across tokens based on criterion-induced distribution shifts, yielding both outcome-grounded and fine-grained learning signals. Empirically, CoCA achieves an average gain of +4.2% over standard rubric-based RL across medicine and science benchmarks, demonstrating more effective learning on open-ended tasks.

title: Explore with Memory, Learn without It: In-Context Exploration and Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
summary: Exploration bounds learning efficiency in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Current methods explore mostly through independent sampling, without fully using the information gathered along the way, such as known wrong answers and environment feedback. We propose LEAF, which injects a dynamic, problem-specific memory into the context before every rollout. The memory contains the most recent response, its reward, and other environment feedback. It is updated after every verifier call. We decouple policy updates from rollouts and update the policy through self-distillation. On four benchmarks and two open models, LEAF accelerates exploration by about 4x compared with a random sampling baseline. On unseen test sets, it improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by 1.59 and 1.83 percentage points on the two models, while using less compute than any RL baseline. These results highlight the potential of LEAF in improving both exploration and learning efficiency. Code is available at: https://github.com/on1262/LEAF

title: Train for Many, Update with One: Improving Multi-Sample Reasoning via Fenchel-Bregman Posterior Learning
summary: Multi-sample reasoning measures candidate coverage, the probability that at least one of $K$ candidates is correct. However, minimizing the average loss of individual attempts does not directly optimize candidate coverage. We therefore formulate finite-$K$ posterior learning, which trains a distribution over solver parameters to reduce the probability that all $K$ independently generated candidates fail. To optimize this objective efficiently, we propose a Fenchel-Bregman (FB) approach that requires only one posterior draw per update, rather than the $K$ used by direct Monte Carlo optimization. FB first uses an exact Fenchel reformulation to separate problem-specific weights from the posterior update, enabling one-draw posterior updates. It then applies a closed-form Bregman update to track these weights through an exponential running average of observed failures, reusing the same draw. We instantiate FB with IVON, a variational optimizer for Gaussian posteriors over solver parameters, yielding Fenchel-Bregman IVON (FBI). Across diverse recursive and autoregressive reasoning tasks, FBI improves candidate coverage. In a matched comparison, it achieves comparable Pass@10 using 12.3% of the direct Monte Carlo baseline's measured training time per update.

title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via Rényi Divergence
summary: We investigate whether Rényi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by Rényi divergence of order $0<α<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of Rényi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to Rényi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.

title: DuplexAct: How Interactive Are Frontier Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models?
summary: End-to-end (E2E) full-duplex spoken language models (FD-SLMs) enable simutanous listening and speaking continously, requiring models to take appropriate interaction actions as conversations unfold. However, existing benchmarks lack a structured action-level formulation, often evaluate action occurrence rather than success, and provide limited coverage of diverse real-world conversations. We introduce DuplexAct, a benchmark for evaluating interaction action taking in E2E FD-SLMs. DuplexAct defines a three-level action taxonomy spanning eight interaction actions and 24 corresponding interaction conditions. We further characterize successful action-taking through immediate execution and subsequent follow-through, and develop action-specific evaluation metrics for both. DuplexAct contains 4,691 test instances spanning casual conversation, meetings, customer service, and interviews, including 2,531 instances derived from real-world conversational recordings. Together, DuplexAct provides a structured and real-world-grounded framework for systematically assessing how E2E FD-SLMs participate in ongoing spoken interaction.

title: HiSTOR: Structured Treatment-outcome Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Longitudinal Data
summary: Estimating potential outcomes under alternative treatment sequences is essential for personalized decision-making, but remains challenging with high-dimensional covariates and time-varying confounding. In this study, we propose HiSTOR (High-dimensional Structured Treatment-Outcome Representation), an end-to-end framework that integrates nonlinear dimension reduction with longitudinal counterfactual prediction. The central idea is to learn structured low-dimensional representations of both current patient states and evolving histories, according to their shared and distinct relationships with treatment assignment and outcomes. This extends latent-space covariate adjustment to longitudinal settings, jointly addressing covariate dimensionality and historical complexity. The resulting framework supports one-step and multi-step outcome prediction under specified treatment sequences. Experiments on CVSim and CancerSim demonstrate the superiority of HiSTOR across varying covariate dimensions, confounding strengths, and prediction horizons compared to state-of-the-art methods. To sum up, HiSTOR offers a unified approach to connecting high-dimensional covariate adjustment with longitudinal potential-outcome prediction.

title: Coupled Harness--Model Evolution for Scientific Equation Discovery
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to discover scientific equations from experimental data. Such a discovery system has two parts that must work together: a library of executable computational tools and the model's tool-use policy. The tools supply the solving capability, from diagnosing structure in the data to fitting candidate equations; the policy plans and orchestrates their use. Yet existing systems adapt only one part, keeping either the toolset or the model fixed, which leaves the corresponding failures uncorrectable. We develop a coupled evolution framework that improves both parts from the same verifiable fit-error signal. In the tool-evolution phase, an agent grows an executable tool library from a small set of generic numerical operations by diagnosing its own failures: it authors a new tool when a capability is missing and revises its selection rules when the right tool went unused. In the policy-evolution phase, a small open model (roughly 3B active parameters) is fine-tuned on successful tool-use trajectories collected with the frozen library, on training formulas screened to be disjoint from all evaluation benchmarks. Ablations show the two phases are complementary: with no tool library at all the same model solves almost nothing, the tools account for most of the gain, and trajectory training adds a further gain that is largest on the most difficult problems. The full system solves 79.1/71.3\% of LSR-Synth problems at fit tolerances $10^{-2}$/$10^{-3}$, reaches 63.8\% pooled accuracy on the distributionally different SRSD-Feynman panel, and obtains a normalized CP3-28 aggregate of $-7.27$. These results suggest a broader recipe for scientific agents: let the model and its instruments improve each other under verifiable feedback.

title: Geometric Structure Predicts Per-Example Neighborhood Loss Under PCA Truncation
summary: Dimensionality reduction can preserve the average performance of text embeddings even when a substantial fraction of their dimensions is removed. Aggregate metrics, however, do not reveal whether degradation is distributed uniformly across examples. We study per-example neighborhood stability under PCA truncation across static word embeddings and modern sentence encoders. Per-item neighbor retention varies widely and is predictable from geometric properties of the representation and its alignment with the retained PCA subspace. The fraction of centered-vector energy retained by the truncated subspace is strongest for CBOW and RI, with neighborhood contrast leading on SkipGram and the modern/Matryoshka settings (GTE approximately tied), while local density is associated with retention in marginal analysis but adds little unique information once energy and contrast are controlled (R-squared increments 0.001 to 0.010). Local intrinsic dimensionality accounts for more variation than density on modern sentence encoders in pairwise comparison. On SciFact, query density predicts retrieval degradation under aggressive compression; on NFCorpus the primary 32d association does not replicate, and a direct variance-restriction test leaves that null unresolved. Average compression performance conceals systematic per-example variation that geometry makes visible.

title: AttenIR: Aligning Dense Visual Attention with Mesh Warping for Unsupervised Image Retargeting
summary: Image retargeting aims to resize images while preserving salient content free from distortion and stretching. Recent learning-based solutions reduce reliance on traditional hand-crafted features and optimization procedures, leading to more efficient and generalizable performance. Nevertheless, existing approaches still struggle to preserve global structure and content fidelity. To address these limitations, we propose AttenIR, an unsupervised image retargeting framework requiring no manual labels, based on content-aware mesh warping, which ef- fectively couples dense visual attention with sparse mesh constraints. We for- mulate the mesh deformation as a vertex displacement regression task. Guided by saliency priors, our method jointly optimizes scale, structure, and geometry preservation losses. By combining dense visual attention with semantic features, it achieves robust, unsupervised retargeting without manual annotations. Our primary contributions include (1) a lightweight unsupervised method for image retargeting that ensures content fidelity and preserves global structure, and (2) a coarse-to-fine projection strategy to align dense visual attention priors with sparse mesh constraints, enabling content-aware deformation at the pixel level. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive and superior performance compared with both traditional and state-of-the-art learning-based methods.

title: A Matroid Generalization of Weighted Popular Matching: Characterization and Algorithm
summary:
We study a problem that unifies two major generalizations of popular matchings in the one-sided preference model. In a bipartite graph in which each vertex, or applicant, on one side has preferences over the adjacent vertices, a matching is called popular if it does not lose a head-to-head election against any other matching. Since the seminal work of Abraham, Irving, Kavitha, and Mehlhorn, who gave the first polynomial-time algorithm for finding a popular matching, numerous generalizations of the popular matching problem have been investigated. Two prominent directions are weighted popular matchings, in which each applicant is assigned a voting weight, and popularity problems under matroid constraints. The former admits a polynomial-time algorithm due to Mestre, while the most general form of the latter is the popular common independent set problem, for which a polynomial-time algorithm is given by Kavitha, Makino, Schlotter, and Yokoi.
  In this paper, we introduce the weighted popular common independent set problem, which simultaneously generalizes weighted popular matchings and popular common independent sets. Our main result is the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem. A key ingredient of the algorithm is a solution-independent characterization of weighted popular common independent sets, which we establish in this paper. As consequences of our algorithmic result, we obtain polynomial-time algorithms for several previously unresolved problems, including weighted popular matchings with matroid constraints and weighted popular branchings.

title: The Human--VLA Communication Gap: What Humans Leave Implicit and What Policies Cannot Recover
summary: A robot may know how to perform a task yet fail when a human asks for it naturally. We study this human--VLA communication gap by separating an \emph{information gap}, where task semantics, grounding, or event structure remain unresolved, from a residual \emph{execution gap}, where even a fully specified task depends on how it is organized and invoked. To do this, we characterize how people naturally express demonstrated objectives and evaluate controlled variants of the same physical tasks, with detailed analysis on $π_{0.5}$ and consistent trends on $π_0$-FAST and Cosmos3-Edge. Our study reveals that humans increasingly compress instructions as tasks grow, relying more on contextual grounding and implicit execution structure. Current policies are misaligned with this behavior: they tolerate grounding dependence relatively well, but struggle when task semantics or event structure must be reconstructed. Even after the information gap is resolved, execution remains sensitive to command granularity and invocation state. These findings identify concrete targets for human-centered policy learning and interfaces that better bridge natural human objectives to robot behavior. Project website: https://commgap.github.io/.

title: Auditing Failure Attribution: Label Predictability and Judge Behavior
summary: Failure-attribution benchmarks ask an LLM judge which step or agent caused a failure. A high score should mean the judge checked the faulty step against the run (a cross-step check). However, spurious signals (surface cues) that predict the annotation can produce a high score. In this paper, we propose four tests to separate checking from cue use. Input restriction asks whether partial input predicts the annotation. Cue following checks whether moved cues change answers. Residual accuracy scores judges where cue-only predictors fail. Aggregation asks whether the failure mix or metric changes rankings. Real observations motivate these tests: on three benchmarks, simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1. In two Who&When Pro systems, a classifier reading one step's reasoning finds 95-100% of faulty steps, motivating input restriction. In one of them, error injection leaves no reasoning after the faulty step; judges fine-tuned on its labels beat GPT-4.1 by 41 points. Adding task-related reasoning after that step moves this cue: fine-tuned judges lose 31-99 points, but zero-shot judges lose at most 9, motivating cue following. On Aegis, blaming every agent matches GPT-4.1 on micro-F1 but trails by 19 points in exact-set accuracy, motivating aggregation. We recommend reporting these tests when developing failure-attribution benchmarks.

title: I3L: Iterative Interactive Imitation Learning for Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation
summary: Policies trained offline from teleoperated demonstrations can degrade outside their training distribution. This gap is particularly acute in long-horizon whole-body mobile manipulation, where long horizons amplify compounding errors and coordinated arm, torso, and base motion makes exhaustive demonstration coverage impractical. We introduce I3L, an integrated hardware and learning system that combines whole-body correction with iterative policy refinement to address this last-mile reliability gap. Its low-cost, open-source JoyLo+ interface uses policy-tracking leader arms and touch-triggered takeover to enable coordinated corrections across the body parts, while iterative deployment and retraining allow operators to target failures of the updated policy. We evaluate I3L across three robot embodiments and eight simulated and real-world tasks, including four long-horizon whole-body mobile manipulation tasks. Controlled simulation experiments show that four-round HG-DAgger achieves the highest final success on both tasks. Under this protocol, I3L improves autonomous success over the base policies by an average of 68.3 percentage points and achieves at least 90% success on every task, outperforming demonstration-only training by 35.6 percentage points on average with the same number of training trajectories. Averaged across tasks, takeover duration per episode decreases by 72% over four rounds. Together, these results show that I3L helps close the last-mile gap between offline training and reliable deployment and provides practical insights into collecting and using corrections for long-horizon whole-body mobile manipulation. Videos, visualizations, and appendix are at https://i-3l.github.io/.

title: Learning Robot Policies for Whole-Body Mobility Assistance via Dynamic Human Motion Generation
summary: Robotic assistance for human mobility could benefit care recipients and reduce caregiver burden during physically demanding tasks such as Sit-to-Stand (STS) and Lift-and-Transfer (L&T). Learning robot policies for these whole-body assistive tasks is challenging: real-world data collection for human-robot interaction is costly and safety-critical, making simulation an attractive alternative. Prior work, however, typically treats the human as static or minimally responsive and thus fails to capture the cooperative nature of mobility assistance. We present a simulation-based framework for learning whole-body assistive robot policies. At its core is a human policy trained with an adversarial motion prior that produces realistic care-recipient motion in response to the robot's actions. A human-adaptive scripted controller interacts with this policy to collect diverse robot demonstrations at scale. From these demonstrations, we train 3D diffusion policies that map segmented human point clouds and robot joint positions to whole-body actions for a mobile manipulator, without relying on privileged human state at deployment. The resulting robot policies successfully perform both STS and L&T assistance in simulation. Preliminary experiments further demonstrate sim-to-real transfer for STS after fine-tuning on a small amount of real-world data. Videos are available on our project page: https://rchi-lab.github.io/human-gen-mobility-assistance/

title: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes
summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are commonly organized around two coordination regimes. Centralized coordination provides explicit control but can create a bottleneck at a single coordination locus, whereas decentralized coordination offers local autonomy but must achieve effective collaboration through distributed decisions and experience. These trade-offs motivate a systematic study of the space between the two regimes. We introduce Degrees of Freedom (DoF), a continuous configuration framework that quantifies the size of the decision space delegated to downstream agents. DoF controls the granularity of delegated work and the target probability that each task unit is assigned to the branches. Its endpoints recover the two coordination regimes. Across multiple task domains, DoF reveals a hierarchy of organizational effects. Delegated granularity and within-regime routing produce structured but bounded profile reallocations, whereas task domain and retained experience are associated with stronger differences between the centralized- and decentralized-branch profiles. The resulting performance landscape is task-dependent: different domains favor different DoF configurations, while atomic-target conditions are more consistent across runs. In-domain retained experience brings the two branch profiles closer together. The same controlled sweep reveals a task-dependent coordination landscape: some domains exhibit higher-performing configurations, whereas others show flatter responses and no single configuration dominates across domains. In five of the six evaluated state, an intermediate DoF configuration achieves higher mean accuracy than both endpoints, demonstrating the value of exploring the coordination space between them. Together, these findings provide empirical guidance for studying and designing intermediate coordination regimes in LLM-based MAS.

title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents
summary: Large language model agents can follow complex human instructions to solve real-world tasks. In practice, however, initial instructions are often incomplete. In our analysis of 100 user-agent trajectories from SWE-chat, 56\% of initial instructions omit requirements that later emerge as necessary, and 52\% of the useful follow-up requirements could have been inferred from the project. A user states requirements from their own understanding of the task, and these \textbf{stated requirements} often differ from the \textbf{true requirements} that completing the task imposes. An agent should therefore treat the instruction as evidence rather than as the objective, inferring the true requirements from the instruction and the environment and satisfying them even when the user is not yet aware of all of them. We call this ability \textbf{outcome alignment}. In this work, we construct \textbf{TiGanEval}, a benchmark of software engineering and research tasks. In every task the user genuinely lacks part of the requirements, each requirement stays discoverable from the code and runtime behaviour of the environment, and requirements the agent infers are separated from those the user adds after observing delivered work. These properties together make outcome alignment measurable. Evaluating eight frontier models including GPT-5.6-Sol, we find outcome alignment broadly missing: the models lose 53 to 67 points of success rate when moving from the full specification to the partial instruction, and consequence feedback across four submissions does not close the gap. Furthermore, a plan-mode harness cannot compensate for the missing ability of the model itself, which places outcome alignment among the abilities the next generation of models should be developed for.

title: POD-accelerated high-order multiscale method with corrected-basis reconstruction for transient multi-continuum problems
summary: Multi-continuum models provide an effective macroscopic description of transient flow in fractured and highly heterogeneous porous media by introducing several interacting state variables at each macroscale location. Although high-order multiscale (HOMS) methods reduce the cost of resolving microscopic heterogeneities while recovering local oscillatory features, repeated solution of the coupled homogenized system and repeated high-order reconstruction remain expensive in long-time and large-scale three-dimensional simulations. This work develops a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) accelerated HOMS framework for transient multi-continuum problems. A vector-valued POD space is constructed from snapshots of the coupled homogenized solution, and the resulting block system is projected onto a low-dimensional space. Two recovery strategies are considered. The first reconstructs the reduced homogenized fields and performs full HOMS assembly at every output time. The second applies the spatial part of the multiscale recovery operator to retained POD modes offline and evaluates the online solution by direct linear combinations of corrected bases and time-derivative bases. An error estimate between the fully discrete homogenized solution and its POD-reduced approximation is established for the coupled system. A recovered POD-HOMS estimate is then obtained by combining the HOMS consistency error with POD truncation errors propagated through value, gradient, inter-continuum exchange, second-derivative, and time-derivative recovery terms. Numerical experiments for two- and three-dimensional heterogeneous configurations show that the reduced solutions retain the accuracy and local oscillatory behavior of the corresponding HOMS solution while substantially decreasing computational cost.

title: Gaussian Process Bandits for AI System Optimization with Selectively Verified Feedback
summary: Gaussian process bandits exploit similarities among configurations to optimize prompts, retrieval systems, and agent workflows. In these applications, however, inexpensive model-based evaluations can disagree with trusted task outcomes. We study selective verification when an action is chosen before a diagnostic is observed and trusted feedback is informative on an unknown set of diagnostic states. A finite reliability class and a finite RKHS signal dictionary describe these two sources of uncertainty. We construct a fixed audit design that combines reliability coverage with reward separation and establish a finite-time regret bound that accounts for a hard audit budget and the rounds needed to obtain informative observations. A safe adaptive extension mixes this robust design with predictable Chernoff allocations while preserving a uniform identification floor and exact expected acquisition-cost accounting. For signed-coordinate kernels, structured and diffuse reliability classes require different audit scales despite sharing the same reward geometry. Synthetic experiments distinguish these certified designs from an adaptive posterior heuristic and GP controls. Safe adaptive allocation reduces aggregate regret relative to the fixed design under the exact dictionary, but its finite-budget error certificate is numerically loose. Conditional-feedback errors can remove the heuristic's advantage and target perturbations can reverse it. Separate AI-task replays assess feedback correction and fitted-dictionary policies without establishing end-to-end validation of a learned selective-verification method.

title: Connecting the Dots: Enduring Performance Gaps in ASR Systems Between Standard and Minority English Varieties
comments: Accepted to IEEE SLT 2026. 11 pages including appendix, 1 figure, 6 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/smfsamir/longitudinal-asr-eval
summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system evaluations have consistently revealed performance disparities along lines of race, gender, socioeconomic status, and language variety. While these disparities are well-documented, they are often (implicitly or explicitly) treated as issues that subsequent, larger, and more universal models will correct. We challenge this assumption of steady progress in reducing accent-related performance disparities, conducting a longitudinal evaluation of 16 prominent systems released between 2021-2025 across 8 datasets representing diverse English accent varieties. We find that the performance disparity between Mainstream US English (MUSE) and minority accents is stubborn, not reliably declining as a function of time. Specifically, while systems are reliably performant on MUSE, minority accents are subject to risks of large performance degradations between generations of systems, sometimes worsening by 65% absolute Word Error Rate. We argue that standard ASR benchmarks enact an implicit language policy privileging Mainstream US English varieties. As such, these performance disparities reflect systemic failures of language technology development infrastructure that disproportionately affect underrepresented speaker populations.
comment: Accepted to IEEE SLT 2026. 11 pages including appendix, 1 figure, 6 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/smfsamir/longitudinal-asr-eval

title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms
comments: Accepted at the 2026 Asia-Pacific Solar Research Conference (APSRC 2026), Canberra, Australia, 1-3 December 2026
summary: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) inspection is dominated by aerial surveys, which are effective for identifying module-level hot cells but provide limited visibility of critical components located under the array, including connectors, cabling, fasteners and structural elements. These assets are difficult to inspect consistently at scale, and their defects are often spatially small, partially occluded and difficult to localise from isolated images. We present an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system (Tricorder) for under-panel PV asset inspection. The approach combines LiDAR-inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery and machine-learning-based object detection and segmentation. Detected assets are associated with the reconstructed 3D environment, allowing visual and thermal observations from multiple viewpoints to be spatially fused and localised. We demonstrate the approach on utility-scale PV data for MC4 connector detection and connection-state recognition, thermal anomaly identification, and detection of structural components including bolts, nuts and torque tubes. The results demonstrate a pathway from image-based inspection toward spatially grounded autonomous inspection, where defects are detected and linked to specific assets and their 3D locations within the solar farm.
comment: Accepted at the 2026 Asia-Pacific Solar Research Conference (APSRC 2026), Canberra, Australia, 1-3 December 2026

title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
summary: Long-term memory supports agents across sessions. Repeated retrieval and write-back can let one historical claim occupy multiple retrieval positions and influence current answers without independent evidence. Existing work examines retrieval, updating, and question answering, leaving same-source record accumulation and post-correction persistence underexplored. Motivated by research in social cognition and memory psychology on repeated exposure, retrieval, and revision, we define \emph{Memory Echo} as the excess retrieval exposure gained by historical information from the same source without additional independent evidence, and introduce MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and effect on answers. To address this phenomenon, we introduce the Family--Provenance--Authority framework (FPA). Specifically, FPA selects one representative per source family, conditions the eligibility of old records for the answer context on verified corrections, and constrains final answers with authoritative evidence. In paired replay on 190 fixed questions across four memory frameworks, FPA raises accuracy from 0.825 to 0.920 with DeepSeek V4 Flash and from 0.782 to 0.916 with Kimi K2.6; mean Decision Contamination Effect falls from 0.106 to 0.030 and from 0.109 to 0.038, respectively. These results show that agent memory can preserve traceable history without allowing repeated historical information to govern current decisions. The code is available at https://github.com/OrcasSam/memory-echo-benchmark.

title: PROTEAN: Beyond De Novo Generation - Can LLM Agents Perform Text-Guided Protein Structure Editing?
summary: Generative AI has achieved remarkable success in de novo protein design, yet protein engineering typically begins with existing, characterized proteins. The primary demand is targeted local editing, e.g., engineering a specific region to optimize affinity, alter immunogenicity, or improve stability, while strictly preserving core catalytic motifs and overall scaffold integrity. However, no standardized framework currently exists for carrying out and evaluating such edits. In current generative-design workflows, researchers often need to manually specify complex low-level parameters and rely on repetitive, trial-and-error sampling and evaluation across generative backends to search for viable conformations. While large language models (LLMs) offer an intuitive interface to express these goals using natural language, prevailing structure-generation models cannot directly interpret high-level human instructions. To bridge this gap, we introduce PROTEAN, a standardized benchmark for text-guided protein structural editing. PROTEAN comprises 380 sub-tasks spanning six intervention families and evaluates a two-stage pipeline in which an LLM translates natural-language goals into backend-specific geometric constraints and a generative model remodels the protein backbone. A two-tier evaluation separates geometric compliance, including target attainment and off-target scope fidelity, from biophysical realizability assessed by inverse folding and refolding consistency. Across five frontier LLMs paired with three backends, strict end-to-end biophysical success starts at just 7.0%. Ablation studies show that LLM constraint compilation is already highly accurate, whereas the main bottlenecks are backend-specific scope leakage and refolding failure. PROTEAN provides an open testbed for developing autonomous, multi-backend macromolecular design agents.

title: Efficiently Learning To Reason or Not to Reason: Root-token Policy Optimization for Adaptive Thinking
summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) achieve strong performance by externalizing explicit reasoning traces before producing the answer, yet suffer from overthinking challenge that allocates uniformly heavy computation to queries of varying difficulty. While proprietary models mitigate this via opaque routing, open-source LRMs still lack an efficient mechanism to internalize adaptive reasoning due to both expensive training cost and limited disclosure of training recipes. In response, we introduce RPO (Root-token Policy Optimization), a framework that enables LRMs to self-determine when to reason by training only the initial root token (e.g., whether to invoke the <think> tag) via group relative reward and group-wise advantages. By focusing on this pivotal branching point, RPO drastically reduces training overhead and VRAM usage. Across multiple model families and scales, RPO learns difficulty-aware adaptive thinking at just ~2% of the training compute of prior adaptive-reasoning methods.

title: More Reader Data or a Better Teacher? Updating a Model of Crowd Highlights in Late 2026
comments: 10 pages, 4 tables, 1 figure. Ancillary files include the pre-registration with its amendments, the results write-up, the aggregate artifacts every reported number is generated from, and the prompt, scoring, target and contrast code
summary: A model trained on readers' highlights can show a newcomer where earlier readers converged on a page, even on pages with few readers. A year of stronger language models suggests two upgrades: use them directly, or use them as teachers. We compare both with a third, more reader data, on one social highlighting platform, with the comparisons, the selection rules and a sealed set of fresh pages fixed in advance. On 215 development pages, seven language models released by October 2026 rank sentences zero-shot at an average precision of at most 0.3744 against the sentences half the readers marked most, and 0.3931 when fused with reading position, while a 3-billion-parameter model trained on reader highlights alone reaches 0.4346. Used as the teacher that breaks ties among readers' counts, the stronger fusion changes a trained model by +0.0013 [-0.0012, +0.0040], whereas going from half to all of its training pages adds +0.0242 [+0.0179, +0.0301]. A 27-billion-parameter backbone on the reader-only recipe adds +0.0225 on the development pages; on 131 fresh pages, read once and too few for a confirmatory comparison, its difference from the 3-billion model is unresolved, both score above the fusion, and in an exploratory split their lead over the previous model sits on pages from domains that their fresh training pages also cover. In this recipe, more reader data improves a trained model where a stronger tie-breaking teacher yields no material gain, and frontier models used as rankers still trail a small model trained on readers.
