title: Multimodal synthesis of MRI and tabular data with diffusion in a joint latent space via cross-attention
summary: We propose a multimodal latent diffusion model that jointly synthesizes volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tabular clinical data within a shared latent space via cross-attention. This approach enables coherent joint representation learning of MRI and tabular modalities for generative modeling. Our model utilizes a variational autoencoder to fuse the two modalities before diffusion-based synthesis, allowing modality-appropriate reconstruction with separate decoders for MRI and tabular data. We evaluated the framework on data from the German National Cohort (NAKO Gesundheitsstudie), comprising over 10,000 participants with MRI scans and clinical tabular features such as age, sex, body measurements, and ethnicity. The generated MRI volumes exhibited anatomical plausibility and body composition consistent with the synthesized tabular attributes. Quantitative evaluation using Fréchet distance and precision-recall metrics confirmed high-fidelity image generation. In the tabular modality, our model outperformed CTGAN across standard evaluation metrics and achieved results comparable to TVAE, demonstrating competitive performance relative to established unimodal baselines. This work is, to our knowledge, the first to demonstrate the feasibility of jointly modeling MRI and mixed-type tabular data in a single latent diffusion framework, offering a proof-of-concept for generating coherent synthetic multimodal patient data and aligning with the broader goal of developing digital twins in healthcare.

title: Transceiver-Integrated BD-RIS: Wave-Domain Signal Processing for Sustainable and Inclusive 6G
comments: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Author-accepted manuscript. Accepted for publication in IEEE Wireless Communications, 2026
summary: The shift toward sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications demands transceiver architectures that simultaneously support high-data-rate communications, pervasive sensing, and sub-meter-level localization. Beyond these performance targets, 6G systems are also expected to align with long-term societal goals, including sustainability and inclusiveness. Conventional radio designs, however, remain heavily reliant on digital baseband processing, whose cost, power consumption, and computational complexity scale unfavorably with increasing array size and carrier frequency, making them poorly aligned with these emerging requirements. Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) introduce a new paradigm by enabling direct manipulation of electromagnetic waves in the analog domain. This article presents BD-RIS as a wave-domain analog processing unit embedded within the transceiver aperture. By migrating linear signal processing functions from the digital baseband to the wave domain, BD-RISs significantly reduce computational load and energy consumption, enabling scalable and sustainable operation for extra-large antenna array systems. Owing to their ability to jointly provide high operational flexibility, modularity, and energy-efficient analog processing, transceiver-integrated BD-RISs offer a compelling architectural trade-off and emerge as a strong candidate for next-generation wireless transceivers.

title: Map2APS: A Physically Grounded Benchmark for Direct Angle Power Spectrum Prediction from Urban Geometry
summary: Angle power spectrum (APS) characterizes the directional distribution of received signal power and is directly relevant to beam management and MIMO processing. While environment-aware learning has been widely studied for radio maps and path loss, direct map-to-APS prediction still lacks a standardized large-scale benchmark. This paper presents Map2APS, a physically grounded benchmark constructed from intelligent ray-tracing (IRT) path-level propagation records. Map2APS covers 51 equal-height urban maps and approximately 2.55 million Tx--Rx samples, with a strict cross-map split for evaluating generalization to unseen urban layouts. We benchmark representative model families and introduce MS-AReg as a strong reference baseline. On the full held-out test set of 249{,}993 samples, MS-AReg achieves a cosine similarity of 0.948, a peak location error of 1.20$^\circ$, and an inference latency of 0.101 ms/sample. We further report dominant-direction metrics, including Top-1 dominant peak hit rate and dominant peak recall, to evaluate whether predicted spectra preserve decision-relevant arrival directions. The benchmark, code, and evaluation scripts are released at https://github.com/UNIC-Lab/aps-data.

title: MagCeptor: Encoding Broadcast-Addressable Logic into Magnetic Receptors
summary: Selectively operating multiple components while simplifying actuation and control hardware is a common challenge in multifunctional mechanical and fluidic systems. Here, we introduce MagCeptor, an addressable magnetic-cluster architecture in which a shared external field conveys commands and supplies actuation energy. Fixed stators establish local magnetic-field gradients, while field-induced mover reorientation modulates the resulting forces to select guide-constrained mechanical outputs. Field-dependent position-orientation energy profiles explain target actuation, non-target retention and passive reset after field removal. The evaluated configuration achieves a maximum normalized force output of 385 mN/mm3. By coupling finite, addressable strokes to mechanical transmissions, accumulators and locks, we demonstrate coordinated rotation and multistep manipulation with retained task states. Hierarchical node-and-channel addressing further enables selective model-fluid release from distributed receivers in ex vivo tissue. These results establish a receiver-side architecture that combines shared magnetic inputs with task-specific mechanisms to organize mechanical work, retain operation states and access spatially distributed functions.

title: Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers
summary: High-order isogeometric discretizations produce a small number of non-physical outlier modes at the top of the discrete spectrum. These modes can pollute the numerical solution in wave propagation and structural dynamics. Most existing remedies modify the spatial discretization through outlier-free bases, mass lumping, subspace projection, and related constructions. We introduce MIISO (Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers), a family of exponential Rosenbrock-Krylov methods of orders two through six that suppress the outliers in the time integrator and leave the spatial discretization unchanged. We construct a non-holomorphic amplification map by blending a Padé approximation that preserves physical oscillatory modes with a Pade approximation that damps high frequencies, with the blend placed at the known spectral location of the outliers. For orders three and higher the damping approximant is repaired so that the method is unconditionally A-stable. Physical modes receive no numerical dissipation and the outliers are driven to zero. The outlier handling and the method steps are fully matrix-free, and the method extends to nonlinear problems. Numerical experiments recover the predicted orders, match spatial outlier removal without changing the discretization, show lower cost than generalized-alpha at matched accuracy and in scaling, and demonstrate the method on nonlinear and three-dimensional problems.

title: Sign-switched antithetic coupling in gradient random-walk methods for convection-diffusion equations
comments: 23 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23055907; https://github.com/stephen122204/sac-grw
summary: We propose an antithetic coupling that reduces the computational cost of gradient random-walk methods for one-dimensional convection-diffusion equations. The methods represent the solution's spatial derivative by particles with positive or negative masses, whose cumulative sums reconstruct the solution, and model diffusion by Gaussian displacements. The particles reorder and, for a nonlinear flux, interact. Antithetic sampling negates the displacements of a second simulation, which positively correlates the contributions of particles matched by position when their masses have opposite signs. Our coupling instead gives matched particles of opposite sign identical displacements and retains opposite displacements for equal-sign pairs. We prove that each simulation keeps the distribution of an uncoupled run as the matching changes, so the averaged solution keeps the bias of one simulation. For fixed particle configurations and matching, the coupling minimizes each matched pair's conditional variance contribution after diffusion among all couplings with the same Gaussian marginal distributions. From the same configurations, its variance reduction over antithetic sampling at the final diffusion stage has a closed form for any flux. For the heat equation, a martingale decomposition extends both results to each step's contribution to the terminal variance. In a Burgers' equation test, the coupling meets a tolerance for the spatially integrated mean squared error with 4 simulations, against 34 for antithetic sampling and 65 for independent sampling. In a second test, it meets a common error tolerance in about 40% less time than pairing particles only within each sign.

title: Residual Minimisation for Transport-Based Optimal Control
summary:
We consider an optimal control problem governed by a stationary linear transport equation in two or three spatial dimensions, motivated by photon transport in radiotherapy treatment planning. The control is an inflow boundary source, and the observation operator may track either the angular flux or its angular integral, the latter serving as a simplified dose surrogate. The associated optimality system consists of a transport--adjoint pair with angular dependence, coupled through a boundary optimality condition.
  We formulate a residual least-squares functional whose minimisers coincide with solutions of the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker system and show that the functional controls the $L^2$ errors in the state and adjoint and the flux-weighted $L^2$ error in the control. This yields a continuum-level a posteriori estimate without recourse to discretisation. An additional unweighted optimality residual certifies the control in the norm of the objective. The estimate holds for every admissible approximation and accounts for the different boundary measures in the control penalty and transport traces, without a positive lower bound on $|ω\cdot n|$. We then parameterise the state, adjoint and control using neural networks and minimise over a neural network space using appropriate quadrature. The Monte Carlo formulation replaces each residual integral by a weighted sample mean, whose quadrature error enters the a posteriori estimate.
  We prove convergence under explicit assumptions on approximation, quadrature and optimisation and derive bounds on the total error in terms of approximation, quadrature and optimisation error. Numerical examples in two and three dimensions illustrate the residual--error relation and the flexibility of the residual framework for field- and dose-tracking control problems, including regular manufactured solutions.

title: Optimal Diagonal Preconditioning Beyond Worst-Case Conditioning: Theory and Practice of Omega Scaling
summary:
We study optimal diagonal preconditioning using the classical worst-case $κ$-condition number and the averaging-based $ω$-condition number.
  For the $κ$-optimal preconditioning problem, we derive an affine-based pseudoconvex reformulation with three key advantages: all stationary points are global minima, subgradients are inexpensive to compute, and the optimization variable is an $n$-dimensional vector rather than an $n\times n$ matrix as in semidefinite programming (SDP) approaches. We develop a simple and highly efficient subgradient method, with convergence guarantees, for solving this pseudoconvex formulation that is substantially more scalable and accurate than existing SDP-based methods.
  For the $ω$-condition number, we provide explicit characterizations of optimal diagonal and block diagonal preconditioners. In particular, we show that several classical preconditioners, including Jacobi and row/column normalization, are $ω$-optimal, and that matrix balancing schemes monotonically reduce $ω$ and converge to stationary points of the two-sided problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified and explicit characterization of optimality conditions for both $κ$ and $ω$-based preconditioning.
  Our numerical experiments further reveal a striking phenomenon: although $κ$-optimal preconditioners achieve stronger reductions in the worst-case condition number, $ω$-optimal preconditioners are substantially cheaper to compute and yield better performance for iterative methods such as preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) and least squares method (LSQR). Moreover, applying $ω$-optimal scaling to linear systems that are already $κ$-optimally preconditioned leads to further improvements in PCG iterations.

title: Simulating Clifford Circuits with Gaussian Elimination
summary: Quantum circuits are considered more powerful than classical circuits and require exponential resources to simulate classically. Clifford circuits are a special class of quantum circuits that can be simulated in polynomial time but still show important quantum effects such as entanglement. In this work, we present an algorithm that simulates Clifford circuits by performing Gaussian elimination on a modified adjacency matrix derived from the circuit structure. Our work builds on a ZX-calculus tensor network representation of Clifford circuits that reduces to quantum graph states. We give a concise formula of amplitudes of graph states based on the LDL decomposition of matrices over GF(2), and use it to get efficient algorithms for strong and weak simulation of Clifford circuits using a tree-decomposition-based sparse LDL algorithm. The complexity of our algorithm matches the state of the art for weak graph state simulation and improves the state of the art for strong graph state simulation by taking advantage of Strassen-like fast matrix multiplication. Our algorithm is also efficient when computing many amplitudes or samples of a Clifford circuit. Further, our amplitudes formula provides a new characterization of locally Clifford equivalent graph states as well as an efficient protocol to learn graph states with low-rank adjacency matrices.

title: Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework
summary: We present an algorithm for studying the sum $$ G_N(x,ρ) = \sum_{k=1}^N \left[ \{x+kρ\} - \frac{1}{2}\right],$$ which is closely related to the discrepancy of the irrational rotation. Computation of $ G_N $ and associated statistics is notoriously difficult due to numerical instability and the failure of sampling to capture the discontinuities. Our algorithm instead fully defines $G_N$ through its discontinuities, which allows computation of $ G_N (x,ρ)$ with errors on the order of $N$ times machine epsilon in $O(N)$ time for practical $N$. The associated probability density function can then be computed in $O(N \log N)$ time. Presented as a tool for experimental mathematics, the algorithm enables reliable plots of the descriptive statistics of $G_N$ over $N$, in particular the length of the support of the $\text{pdf}$ (the discrepancy), revealing extremal behavior related to the arithmetic properties of $ρ$. We also observe a new pattern: when $ρ$ is well approximated by a continued-fraction convergent $\frac{p_n}{q_n}$, the $\text{pdf}$ exhibits a predictable spiked-trapezoidal pattern when $N=kq_n$, eventually degrading at a rate that appears to depend on approximation quality.

title: Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Reservoir Seepage Equations
summary: Solving reservoir seepage partial differential equations (PDEs) is critical for hydrocarbon development optimization and production forecasting. Conventional numerical solvers suffer from mesh errors and high computational cost. Standard Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are limited by inefficient parameters. They also face weak high-dimensional representation and poor nonlinear fitting ability. We adapt the Discrete Variable (DV)-Circuit Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Network (QCPINN) to tackle these drawbacks. This work applies the method to four representative reservoir seepage models. The models cover heterogeneous single-phase pressure diffusion. They also include nonlinear Buckley-Leverett two-phase waterflooding. Another case is adsorption-coupled convection-diffusion compositional flow. The last one refers to fully coupled pressure-saturation two-phase flow with exponential permeability heterogeneity. The QCPINN combines classical preprocessing and postprocessing networks with a DV quantum core. It leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to boost high-dimensional feature mapping. Physical constraints are embedded within the framework to guarantee physically consistent solutions. We evaluate three quantum circuit topologies including Cascade, Cross-mesh and Alternate. Numerical tests prove QCPINNs outperform classical PINNs in prediction accuracy, and the circuit topologies show case-specific performance with clear applicable ranges. This work verifies QCPINN's practicability for reservoir engineering. It bridges quantum computing research with oilfield industrial applications.

title: A Level Set Method on Particle Flow Maps
summary: Accurate interface tracking is central to numerical simulations involving moving boundaries, including multiphase flows, free-surface dynamics, phase-change problems, and other interface-driven processes in computational mechanics. Although level set methods provide a flexible implicit representation of evolving interfaces, their grid-based advection and reinitialization procedures often introduce numerical diffusion, volume loss, and degradation of thin or highly curved structures. This paper introduces a Particle Flow Map Level Set (PFM-LS) method that addresses these limitations by transporting interface geometry through particle-carried bidirectional flow maps. In contrast to particle level set methods that use particles mainly as corrective markers, PFM-LS uses particles as primary carriers of level-set values, gradients, and Hessians within a narrow band around the interface. The method combines long-range flow-map transport, high-order particle-grid reconstruction, adaptive particle control, and a hybrid particle-grid redistancing scheme to preserve both signed-distance consistency and sub-grid geometric features. Numerical benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including topology-change tests, chamfer and Hausdorff shape-error metrics, and coupling to an incompressible free-surface flow solver, show that PFM-LS achieves strong volume preservation, high shape fidelity, and near fourth-order convergence, outperforming a broad range of existing level set and reference-map-based methods.

title: From Consensus-Based Optimization to Evolution Strategies: Proof of Global Convergence
summary:
Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is a powerful and versatile zero-order multi-particle method designed to provably solve high-dimensional global optimization problems, including those that are genuinely nonconvex or nonsmooth. The method relies on a balance between stochastic exploration and contraction toward a consensus point, which is defined via the Laplace principle as a proxy for the global minimizer.
  In this paper, we introduce new CBO variants that address practical and theoretical limitations of the original formulation of this novel optimization methodology. First, we propose a model called $δ$-CBO}, which incorporates nonvanishing diffusion to prevent premature collapse to suboptimal states. We also develop a numerically stable implementation, the Consensus Freezing scheme, that remains robust even for arbitrarily large time steps by freezing the consensus point over time intervals. We connect these models through appropriate asymptotic limits. Furthermore, we derive from the Consensus Freezing scheme by suitable time rescaling and asymptotics a further algorithm, the Consensus Hopping scheme, which can be interpreted as a form of $(1,λ)$-Evolution Strategy. For all these schemes, we characterize for the first time the invariant measures and establish global convergence results, including exponential convergence rates.

title: Risk Control of Traffic Flow Through Chance Constraints and Large Deviation Approximation
summary: We develop a rare chance-constrained optimal control framework for autonomous traffic management, with traffic dynamics governed by stochastic partial differential equations. To efficiently enforce these probabilistic safety specifications, we exploit a large deviation theory (LDT) based approximation method, which converts the original highly non-convex, sampling-heavy stochastic optimization problem into a tractable deterministic nonlinear programming problem. The proposed LDT-based reformulation exhibits superior computational scalability, as its computational cost remains approximately constant regardless of the target violation probability, as opposed to the scaling challenge of traditional sampling-based methods. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is illustrated through numerical experiments on a ring road with stochastic on-ramp inflow, and evaluated with two representative risk measures, namely, maximum traffic density and speed variation. The results show that the proposed method keeps the violation probability close to the target without parameter tuning and is more than ten times faster than a risk-averse baseline.

title: Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential Equations
summary:
We develop a rough-path framework for two-parameter rough differential equations on rectangular and simplicial domains, motivated by the signature kernel and Schwinger--Dyson kernel equations. The theory is formulated in spaces of jointly controlled rough paths and is based on a robust two-parameter rough integration framework. In particular, we introduce a notion of rough integration over two-dimensional simplices at low regularity extending previous results in the literature.
  Within this setting, we show that the signature kernel equation arises naturally as a two-parameter rough differential equation and establish well-posedness and stability. We also extend the Schwinger--Dyson kernel equation, previously formulated for bounded-variation paths, to rough driving signals, proving existence and uniqueness in appropriate controlled rough path spaces.
  In the smooth rough path regime, we relate the resulting equations to PDE and integro-differential formulations. Finally, we derive and analyse a numerical scheme for the rough Schwinger--Dyson equation, including runtime and memory complexity estimates, and illustrate its performance with numerical experiments.

title: On the Robustness of Sparse Randomized Sketching to FP16 Rounding on GPUs
summary:
Randomized sketching replaces large matrices with smaller surrogates that preserve geometry for downstream numerical linear algebra. Sparse sketches promise faster formation than dense projections, but irregular GPU atomic updates become costly when each input row contributes to several output rows, as in SparseStack. FP16 accumulation halves sketch storage and update traffic, relieving cache pressure. How much does this rounding affect sketch geometry and downstream accuracy?
  For SparseStack with four nonzeros per column, cuSPARSE's FP16 path is slower than its FP32 baseline. Our custom kernel instead pairs FP32 inputs and signed products with packed FP16 vector atomic accumulation, turning lower precision into substantial gains. On NVIDIA H200, it forms complete sketches up to $1.91\times$ faster than our FP32 baseline and up to $1.58\times$ faster than cuSPARSE FP32.
  Under stated independence and range assumptions, random sketch signs cancel round-to-nearest conversion-error cross terms, giving expected squared Frobenius error no greater than ideal stochastic rounding. We assess accumulation empirically. At a sketch dimension of twice the number of input columns, the least-squares pipeline is $1.44$-$1.47\times$ faster than FP32, with median paired residual increases below $0.4\%$. Rescaling exposes range limitations and cases where stochastic conversion degrades accuracy.

title: Preconditioning Magnetic Systems in Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory
summary: The convergence of the self-consistent field iterations in Kohn-Sham density functional theory can be significantly hindered by the presence of small eigenvalues in the dielectric matrix, which are often associated with electronic phase transitions in magnetic systems. In this work, we study this type of convergence issues and propose a new preconditioning scheme to mitigate them. Our preconditioning scheme is inspired by the Stoner model and based on a non-interacting susceptibility that neglects orbital variations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of ferromagnetic systems, showing that it can significantly reduce the number of iterations required to achieve convergence in the vicinity of magnetic phase transitions.

title: Error-Conditioned Neural Solvers
summary: Neural surrogate models offer fast approximate mappings from PDE parameters to solutions, but they typically treat solving as a purely statistical task: once trained, they struggle to correct their own constraint violations and extrapolate beyond the training distribution. Recent hybrid methods promote physical correctness by targeting the PDE residual via gradient descent or Gauss--Newton steps, but inherit the compute cost and instability of the underlying classical optimizers. We show, theoretically and empirically, that numerically minimizing the PDE residual can be an unreliable proxy for reconstruction accuracy in ill-conditioned systems, explaining why these methods often do not make accurate predictions despite achieving low residuals. We propose error-conditioned Neural Solvers (ENS), built on a different principle: rather than an optimization target, the PDE residual field is passed as a direct input to the network at each iteration, enabling it to read the spatial structure of its own errors and learn an update policy to iteratively correct its predictions. Across four PDE families, ENS attains the highest prediction accuracy in the large majority of settings, with gains reaching $10\times$ on turbulent Kolmogorov flow, while avoiding the expensive compute cost of hybrid methods. ENS's learned correction policy generalizes under distribution shift, including zero-shot parameter changes and cross-equation transfer, where its relative advantage is largest in the ill-conditioned regimes where residual minimization is least reliable. Project website: https://neuralsolver.github.io/.

title: A neural delta-$f$ particle-in-cell method: evolving the background with learned backward flows
summary: We present a novel δf particle-in-cell (PIC) method for the kinetic simulation of electrostatic plasmas in which the bulk density, acting as a control variate, is evolved using symplectic neural networks (SympNets). The SympNets are used as an approximation of the backward flow and trained using the particle trajectories. We introduce a periodic variant of the SympNet architecture that encodes the spatial periodicity of the problem into the network itself. We validate the approach with numerical results in 1D1V and 3D3V for the Vlasov-Poisson system.

title: Optimal Extrapolation Bounds for Sparse Fourier Sums
summary:
We prove a sharp extrapolation bound for $k$-sparse Fourier sums with arbitrary real frequencies and no separation assumption. For every $g(t)=\sum_{j=1}^k v_je^{iλ_jt}$ with $λ_j\in\mathbb{R}$ and every $x\geq 1$, \begin{align*}
  |g(x)|\le k\exp(O(k\operatorname{arcosh} x))\|g\|_{L^2[-1,1]}. \end{align*} Near the endpoint at $x=1+δ$, this gives an exponential factor of $\exp(O(k\sqrtδ))$, improving on the $\exp(O(k^2\log k\cdotδ))$ estimate of Chen and Price (ICALP 2019), and the exponent is optimal up to a constant factor. Our theorem has algorithmic applications to recovering gapless Fourier-sparse signals: it improves the resolution of cluster-location algorithms and the sample complexity of Fourier interpolation algorithms. In addition, it gives sharp bounds on the error transfer of sparse Fourier models just outside the training interval.

title: A Spectral-Domain Pseudo-Inverse Method for True 3D Gravity Inversion
summary: The main difficulty in 3D gravity inversion is that surface observations lack vertical wavenumber information, making the problem underdetermined and depth resolution poor. Building on the author's spectral-domain pseudo-inverse theory for unitary diagonalizable systems, this paper presents a true 3D inversion method. Surface data are analytically continued upward via Laplace's equation to form a 3D data volume, providing the vertical wavenumber sampling for the 3D Fourier transform. A general analytical expression for the half-space spectrum is derived, separating the horizontal spectrum from the vertical propagation kernel. The Green's function of the 3D Poisson equation is unitarily diagonalized, yielding the forward spectral response $λ(\kk) = -i 4πG k_z / K^2$, and a stable inverse filter $q_α(λ) = \barλ/(|λ|^2 + α)$ is constructed. This filter is proved to have bounded stability and consistency (reducing to the exact inverse as $α\to 0^+$). Validation with a homogeneous sphere model shows correct recovery of the anomaly location and singular behavior at the source. The contributions are twofold: (1) upward continuation constructs a 3D volume from 2D surface data, which does not add physical observations but unfolds the 3D spatial variation information (data innovation) derived through the governing physical equation; (2) the inversion is reduced to one forward 3D Fourier transform, one spectral scaling, and one inverse transform. The framework extends to any linear potential-field inverse problem with a translation-invariant forward operator, including magnetic inversion.

title: Fully discrete stochastic maximal regularity and $H^\infty$-calculus for second-order elliptic operators
comments: Added a section with applications. Also fixed a few typos
summary:
This paper establishes the fully discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-regularity and the accompanying sharp maximal estimate for numerical approximations of parabolic stochastic partial differential equations. We consider the spatial finite element discretization $A_h$ of a general second-order elliptic operator $A=-
abla \cdot a
abla +b\cdot 
abla +c$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a smooth, bounded, convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, coupled with a broad class of temporal schemes, including rational approximations and the exponential Euler method. To obtain these optimal discrete regularity results, we establish a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the discrete spatial operator $A_h$, uniformly in the mesh size $h$. As a direct byproduct, we also establish the discrete-in-space stochastic maximal regularity for the corresponding spatial semi-discretizations.
  As an application, we establish the pathwise uniform convergence of a fully discrete approximation of the three-dimensional stochastic Allen--Cahn equation with variable diffusion coefficients and multiplicative noise.
