AI.title_translation: 基于强化学习的水下AUV无线光通信3D波束自适应
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于深度强化学习的框架，用于解决水下AUV无线光通信中因水流引起的发射器-接收器失准导致的波束指向问题，并通过优化波束转向和发散角来保持通信链路，在真实海洋数据下有效降低了中断率。
AI.motivation: 水下无线光通信(UWOC)为自主水下航行器(AUV)提供高数据速率，但发射器-接收器失准严重影响连接可靠性。在未知洋流作用下移动的AUV的波束指向问题是关键挑战。
AI.method: 提出一个深度强化学习(DRL)框架来解决波束指向问题。开发了一个综合的3D UWOC信道模型，该模型包含深度依赖衰减、湍流和离散射线方法，以准确量化几何和失准损耗。DRL代理联合优化波束转向和发散角，学习以连续链路维护为优先的策略。
AI.result: 在无洋流跟踪条件下，所提出的方法将因指向错误导致的中断率限制在8.5%；在受洋流引起的漂移影响时，中断率限制在16.2%。
AI.conclusion: DRL驱动的波束控制能够实现在动态水下环境中的自适应跟踪和缓解链路中断。
AI.translation: 水下无线光通信 (UWOC) 为自主水下航行器 (AUV) 提供必要的高数据速率，但可靠的连接性受到发射器-接收器失准的严重影响。这项工作通过深度强化学习 (DRL) 框架解决了在未知洋流作用下移动 AUV 的波束指向问题。我们开发了一个综合的 3D UWOC 信道模型，其中包含深度依赖衰减、湍流和离散射线方法，以准确量化几何和失准损耗。由此产生的智能体联合优化波束转向和发散角，学习一种优先考虑连续链路维护的策略。使用真实海洋学数据进行评估，该框架的性能通过“超额中断”指标进行评估，该指标专门隔离了仅由于指向错误而发生的中断。相对于节点之间的完美对准，所提出的方法在无洋流跟踪条件下将此指标限制在 8.5%，在受到洋流引起的漂移影响时将其限制在 16.2%。这项工作中获得的结果证实，DRL 驱动的波束控制能够实现在动态水下环境中的自适应跟踪和缓解链路中断。
AI.summary: 本文针对水下AUV无线光通信中因未知洋流导致的收发端失准问题，提出了一种基于深度强化学习的3D波束自适应框架。该框架通过一个综合的3D UWOC信道模型，使智能体能联合优化波束转向和发散角，以优先维护连续链路。实验结果表明，在有无洋流影响下，该方法能有效降低因指向错误造成的中断率，证明了DRL在动态水下环境中实现自适应波束控制和减少链路中断的有效性。
AI.keywords: 水下无线光通信, 深度强化学习, 波束自适应, AUV, 信道模型
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于将深度强化学习应用于动态水下环境中的3D波束自适应，以应对AUV移动和未知洋流引起的精确指向挑战。其综合的3D信道模型和对“超额中断”指标的关注，使得评估更加精准。这项工作对于提高水下无线光通信的可靠性和实用性具有重要意义。

title: Estimating Closed-Loop Multiple-Input Single-Output Dynamic Systems using Gaussian Processes
summary: This paper extends complex Gaussian process regression-based transfer function (TF) estimation from the single-input single-output setting to closed-loop multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems. Accurate estimation of individual TFs in closed-loop MISO systems is challenging as feedback and correlation between measured signals can obscure the contributions of each input. We formulate a Gaussian process-based estimator for MISO systems, provide analytical conditions under which each system module can be separately identified, and show that the estimator converges to the true TFs in the zero noise limit. Moreover, we demonstrate how conventional closed-loop bias handling techniques relying on external excitation can be employed to construct appropriate regressors. Monte Carlo simulations support the analytical identifiability results and highlight the trade-off between closed-loop bias and error introduced by constructing exogenous regressors partly from endogenous signals. The presented work offers an expressive, nonparametric alternative to existing estimation approaches for MISO systems, while providing a probabilistic characterization of the estimation uncertainty.

AI.title_translation: 使用高斯过程估计闭环多输入单输出动态系统
AI.tldr: 该论文将基于高斯过程回归的传递函数估计从单输入单输出扩展到闭环多输入单输出系统，解决了信号反馈和相关性带来的挑战。
AI.motivation: 闭环多输入单输出系统中准确估计单个传递函数的挑战，因为反馈和测量信号之间的相关性可能掩盖每个输入的贡献。
AI.method: 提出了一种基于高斯过程的MISO系统估计器，提供了单独识别每个系统模块的解析条件，并证明了在零噪声极限下估计器收敛到真实传递函数。此外，还展示了如何利用依赖外部激励的传统闭环偏差处理技术来构建合适的回归量。
AI.result: 蒙特卡洛模拟支持了解析可辨识性结果，并突出了闭环偏差和通过将内源信号部分地用于构建外源回归量而引入的误差之间的权衡。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的方法为MISO系统的现有估计算法提供了一种富有表现力的非参数替代方案，同时对估计不确定性进行了概率表征。
AI.translation: 本文将复杂的基于高斯过程回归的传递函数（TF）估计从单输入单输出（SISO）设置扩展到闭环多输入单输出（MISO）系统。闭环MISO系统中各个TF的准确估计具有挑战性，因为反馈和测量信号之间的相关性会掩盖每个输入的贡献。我们为MISO系统构建了一个基于高斯过程的估计器，提供了可以单独识别每个系统模块的解析条件，并表明在零噪声极限下该估计器收敛到真实的TF。此外，我们证明了如何利用依赖外部激励的传统闭环偏差处理技术来构建合适的回归量。蒙特卡洛模拟支持了解析可辨识性结果，并突出了闭环偏差与通过将内源信号部分地用于构建外源回归量而引入的误差之间的权衡。本文提出的工作为MISO系统的现有估计算法提供了一种富有表现力的非参数替代方案，同时对估计不确定性进行了概率表征。
AI.summary: 本研究将高斯过程回归技术从单输入单输出系统扩展到闭环多输入单输出（MISO）系统，用于传递函数（TF）估计。研究解决了闭环MISO系统中由于信号反馈和相关性导致的TF估计挑战，提出了一种高斯过程估计器，并给出了单独识别系统模块的解析条件。研究证明了该估计器在零噪声下能收敛到真实TF，并提出结合外部激励的偏差处理技术构建回归量。仿真结果支持了解析结果，并揭示了闭环偏差和外源回归量误差之间的权衡。该方法为MISO系统提供了一种非参数的估计选择，并能进行不确定性量化。
AI.keywords: 高斯过程, 传递函数估计, 闭环MISO系统, 非参数估计, 不确定性量化
AI.comments: 该研究在将高斯过程回归应用于闭环MISO系统方面取得了重要进展，解决了现有方法的局限性。解析条件和收敛性证明增加了理论基础。然而，外源回归量中内源信号的使用以及由此产生的权衡是该方法的一个潜在限制，需要进一步研究。

title: Fast Diffusion-GAN Model for Generating Symbolic Music with Emotions
summary: Diffusion models have shown promising results for a wide range of generative tasks with continuous data, such as image and audio synthesis. However, little progress has been made on using diffusion models to generate symbolic music since this class of generative models struggles with discrete data while its iterative sampling process is computationally expensive. In this work, we propose a diffusion model integrated with a Generative Adversarial Network, aiming to mitigate the slow sampling drawback of diffusion models applied to symbolic music generation. We enable the use of diffusion model by representing symbolic music as image-like pianorolls with velocity values instead of discrete event tokens and then used a Variational Autoencoder to obtain their latent representations to train the proposed diffusion model. Our results demonstrate the successful control of our diffusion model to generate symbolic music with a desired emotion. Our model uses merely 15 denoising diffusion steps to produce high-quality music, while most diffusion models for symbolic music generation require hundreds or thousands of steps.

AI.title_translation: 用于生成具有情感的符号音乐的快速扩散-GAN模型
AI.tldr: 提出了一种结合扩散模型和GAN的Fast Diffusion-GAN模型，通过将符号音乐表示为钢琴卷帘图的潜在表示，解决了扩散模型处理离散数据和采样速度慢的问题，并成功生成了具有指定情感的符号音乐，仅需15步即可完成采样。
AI.motivation: 现有的扩散模型在处理连续数据方面表现良好，但在生成符号音乐等离散数据方面进展甚微，并且采样过程计算成本高昂。因此，需要一种能够克服这些限制并有效生成符号音乐的模型。
AI.method: 将符号音乐表示为带有速度值的图像式钢琴卷帘图，并使用变分自编码器获取其潜在表示。然后，将该潜在表示输入到结合了生成对抗网络的扩散模型中进行训练。
AI.result: 所提出的模型能够成功生成具有所需情感的符号音乐，并且采样速度远超现有模型，仅需15步即可生成高质量音乐，而大多数现有模型需要数百甚至数千步。
AI.conclusion: Fast Diffusion-GAN模型有效地解决了扩散模型在生成符号音乐时面临的离散数据处理和采样速度慢的问题，并实现了对生成音乐情感的控制。
AI.translation: 扩散模型在广泛的生成任务中取得了有希望的结果，例如图像和音频合成等连续数据的生成。然而，在利用扩散模型生成符号音乐方面进展甚微，因为这类生成模型在处理离散数据时存在困难，并且其迭代采样过程在计算上成本高昂。在本研究中，我们提出了一种与生成对抗网络相结合的扩散模型，旨在缓解扩散模型应用于符号音乐生成时的慢速采样缺点。我们通过将符号音乐表示为带有速度值的图像状钢琴卷帘图，而不是离散事件标记，从而实现了扩散模型的应用，然后使用变分自编码器获取它们的潜在表示来训练所提出的扩散模型。我们的结果证明了我们的扩散模型能够成功控制生成具有期望情感的符号音乐。我们的模型仅使用15次去噪扩散步骤即可生成高质量音乐，而大多数用于符号音乐生成的扩散模型需要数百或数千步。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种Fast Diffusion-GAN模型，用于生成具有情感的符号音乐。该模型通过将符号音乐表示为图像式钢琴卷帘图的潜在表征，并结合生成对抗网络，解决了扩散模型在处理离散数据和采样速度慢的问题。实验结果表明，该模型能够以极快的速度（15步）生成高质量且可控情感的符号音乐。
AI.keywords: 扩散模型, 生成对抗网络, 符号音乐生成, 情感控制, 钢琴卷帘图
AI.comments: 该研究巧妙地将扩散模型与GAN结合，并创新性地将符号音乐表示为图像，解决了扩散模型在处理离散数据和采样效率上的挑战。模型能够在15步内生成高质量音乐，这在符号音乐生成领域是一个显著的进步，尤其是在情感控制方面。未来的工作可以探索更广泛的情感类别和音乐风格，以及更深入地理解模型生成音乐的内在机制。

title: No Undesirable Equilibria, No Collisions: Combining Modulation and Control Barrier Functions for Liveness and Safety in Dynamic Collision Avoidance
summary: Control Barrier Function Quadratic Programs (CBF-QPs) provide formal safety guarantees for general control-affine systems and accommodate actuation constraints, but do not inherently guarantee liveness, i.e., sustained progress toward and convergence to a goal. They may admit undesirable equilibria or dysfunctional circulation that impede goal convergence. In contrast, Modulation of Dynamical Systems (Mod-DS) promotes liveness through geometric reshaping of nominal vector fields, but is primarily suited to fully actuated systems and does not directly accommodate general actuation constraints. We establish theoretical connections between these paradigms, showing that normal Mod-DS is a special case of CBF-QP and that reference Mod-DS is linked to CBF-QP through a shared formulation. These connections motivate the Modulated CBF-QP (MCBF-QP) framework, which incorporates geometric guidance from Mod-DS into CBF-QPs to enhance liveness while retaining formal safety and control-affine generality. We develop reference MCBF-QP, which reduces undesirable equilibria and dysfunctional circulation for star-shaped obstacles, and on-manifold MCBF-QP, which eliminates undesirable equilibria and reduces dysfunctional circulation for arbitrarily shaped concave obstacles. Although no Lyapunov function is explicitly constructed, we prove that the tangent guidance constraint introduced into the CBF-QP formulation implicitly enforces the decrease condition of a hybrid Lyapunov function, yielding asymptotic goal convergence and thus liveness under the stated assumptions. Extensive simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate safe and live obstacle avoidance with the proposed MCBF-QP framework in static and dynamic environments.

AI.title_translation: 无不良平衡点，无碰撞：结合调制和控制障碍函数以实现动态避障中的活性和安全性
AI.tldr: 控制障碍函数（CBF-QPs）和动态系统调制（Mod-DS）是两种用于控制的框架，但各有局限。CBF-QPs 保证安全但不保证活性，而 Mod-DS 保证活性但对系统和执行器有限制。本文提出了 MCBF-QP 框架，它结合了两者的优点，既能保证安全，又能促进活性，并能处理执行器约束。该框架通过将 Mod-DS 的几何引导纳入 CBF-QPs 来实现，从而减少了不良平衡点和无效循环，并证明了其能实现渐近目标收敛。仿真和实验证明了该框架在静态和动态环境中的有效性。
AI.motivation: 传统的控制障碍函数（CBF-QPs）虽然能保证系统的安全性，但可能存在不良的平衡点或无效的循环，阻碍系统向目标收敛。而动态系统调制（Mod-DS）虽然能促进系统活性，但通常只适用于完全驱动的系统，并且难以处理执行器约束。因此，需要一种能够结合两者的优点，既保证安全又保证活性的方法。
AI.method: 本文提出了一种名为 MCBF-QP 的新框架，它将 Mod-DS 的几何引导机制融入 CBF-QPs 中。具体而言，通过引入切线引导约束，MCBF-QP 在保留 CBF-QP 的安全性和控制仿射系统的通用性的同时，增强了系统的活性。文章还提出了两种具体形式：参考 MCBF-QP 用于星形障碍物，以及流形上 MCBF-QP 用于任意形状的凹形障碍物。理论上证明了该框架隐含地保证了混合李雅普诺夫函数的递减条件，从而实现了渐近目标收敛。
AI.result: MCBF-QP 框架成功地减少了不良平衡点和无效循环，特别是在处理星形和凹形障碍物时。理论证明了该框架能够实现渐近目标收敛，即保证了系统的活性。仿真和硬件实验结果表明，该框架在静态和动态环境中都能实现安全且有活性的避障。
AI.conclusion: MCBF-QP 框架是一种有效的方法，它结合了 CBF-QPs 的安全保证和 Mod-DS 的活性促进能力，并能处理执行器约束。该框架能够减少不良平衡点和无效循环，并保证渐近目标收敛。仿真和实验结果验证了其在动态避障方面的有效性。
AI.translation: 控制障碍函数二次规划（CBF-QPs）为一般的控制仿射系统提供了正式的安全保证，并能适应执行器约束，但不能固有地保证活性，即持续向目标迈进和收敛。它们可能产生阻碍目标收敛的不良平衡点或功能失调的循环。相比之下，动态系统调制（Mod-DS）通过对标称向量场进行几何重塑来促进活性，但主要适用于完全驱动的系统，并且不能直接适应一般的执行器约束。我们建立了这些范式之间的理论联系，表明正常的 Mod-DS 是 CBF-QP 的一个特例，并且参考 Mod-DS 通过共享的公式与 CBF-QP 相关联。这些联系促使了调制 CBF-QP (MCBF-QP) 框架的产生，该框架将 Mod-DS 的几何引导纳入 CBF-QPs 中，以增强活性，同时保留正式的安全性和控制仿射的通用性。我们开发了参考 MCBF-QP，它减少了星形障碍物的不良平衡点和功能失调的循环，以及流形上 MCBF-QP，它消除了不良平衡点并减少了任意形状的凹形障碍物的功能失调的循环。尽管没有显式构建李雅普诺夫函数，但我们证明了引入 CBF-QP 公式中的切线引导约束隐含地强制执行了混合李雅普诺夫函数的递减条件，从而在所述假设下实现了渐近目标收敛，因此实现了活性。大量的仿真和硬件实验证明了所提出的 MCBF-QP 框架在静态和动态环境中具有安全和活性的避障能力。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为 MCBF-QP 的新框架，该框架结合了控制障碍函数（CBF-QPs）的安全保证和动态系统调制（Mod-DS）的活性促进能力。MCBF-QP 通过将 Mod-DS 的几何引导纳入 CBF-QPs 来增强活性，同时保留了对控制仿射系统和执行器约束的通用性。该框架通过引入切线引导约束，有效减少了不良平衡点和无效循环，并理论上证明了其能够实现渐近目标收敛。仿真和实验结果证实了 MCBF-QP 在静态和动态环境下的安全有效避障能力。
AI.keywords: 控制障碍函数, 动态系统调制, 活性, 安全性, 避障
AI.comments: 该研究成功地将两种现有的控制方法（CBF-QPs 和 Mod-DS）结合起来，形成了一个更强大的框架（MCBF-QP），解决了各自的局限性。通过理论分析和实验验证，证明了该框架在保证安全性和活性的同时，还能处理执行器约束和复杂的障碍物形状，这在机器人和自主系统领域具有重要的应用价值。未来可以进一步探索该框架在更复杂动态环境或多智能体系统中的应用。

title: Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation
comments: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT). Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS
summary: Panoramic imaging enables capturing 360° images with an ultra-wide Field-of-View (FoV) for dense omnidirectional perception, which is critical to applications such as autonomous driving and augmented reality. However, current panoramic semantic segmentation methods fail to identify outliers, and pinhole out-of-distribution segmentation (pinhole-OoS) models perform unsatisfactorily in the panoramic domain due to pixel distortions and background clutter. To address these issues, we introduce a new task, Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation (PanOoS), with the aim of achieving comprehensive and safe scene understanding. Furthermore, we propose the first solution, POS, which adapts to the characteristics of panoramic images through text-guided prompt distribution learning. Specifically, POS integrates a disentanglement strategy designed to materialize the cross-domain generalization capability of CLIP. The proposed Prompt-based Restoration Attention (PRA) optimizes semantic decoding by prompt guidance and self-adaptive correction, while Bilevel Prompt Distribution Learning (BPDL) refines the manifold of per-pixel mask embeddings via semantic prototype supervision. Besides, to compensate for the scarcity of PanOoS datasets, we establish two benchmarks: DenseOoS, which features diverse outliers in complex environments, and QuadOoS, captured by a quadruped robot with a panoramic annular lens system. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of POS, with AuPRC increasing and FPR95 decreasing by 34.25 and 21.42 percentage points, respectively, compared with RbA on DenseOoS, outperforming state-of-the-art pinhole-OoS methods. Moreover, POS achieves leading closed-set segmentation capabilities and advances the development of panoramic understanding. Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS.
comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT). Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS

AI.tldr: 该研究提出了全景图分布外分割（PanOoS）新任务和首个解决方案POS，通过文本引导的提示词分布学习来处理全景图像的像素畸变和背景杂乱问题，并建立了两个新基准数据集DenseOoS和QuadOoS，实验证明POS在提高分割准确率和降低误检率方面效果显著。
AI.motivation: 现有全景图像分割方法无法识别异常值，且针对全景图像设计的分布外分割模型由于像素畸变和背景杂乱表现不佳，因此需要新的全景图分布外分割方法以实现全面安全的场景理解。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为POS的解决方案，该方案通过文本引导的提示词分布学习来适应全景图像的特性。具体而言，POS集成了旨在实现CLIP跨域泛化能力的解耦策略。提出的基于提示词的恢复注意力（PRA）通过提示词引导和自适应校正来优化语义解码，而双层提示词分布学习（BPDL）通过语义原型监督来精炼每像素掩码嵌入的流形。此外，为了弥补PanOoS数据集的稀缺性，研究者建立了两个基准数据集：DenseOoS和QuadOoS。
AI.result: POS在DenseOoS数据集上的AuPRC提高了34.25个百分点，FPR95降低了21.42个百分点，优于最先进的针孔分布外分割方法。POS在闭集分割能力方面也表现出色。
AI.conclusion: POS是首个解决全景图分布外分割问题的方案，它通过新颖的提示词引导学习方法，有效解决了全景图像的挑战，并在分割性能上取得了显著的改进，同时推动了全景理解的发展。
AI.translation: 全景成像能够捕捉具有超宽视场（FoV）的360°图像，实现密集的全方位感知，这对于自动驾驶和增强现实等应用至关重要。然而，当前的全景语义分割方法无法识别异常值，并且针孔分布外分割（pinhole-OoS）模型由于像素畸变和背景杂乱，在全景域中的表现不令人满意。为了解决这些问题，我们引入了一个名为全景图分布外分割（PanOoS）的新任务，旨在实现全面安全的场景理解。此外，我们提出了首个解决方案POS，它通过文本引导的提示词分布学习来适应全景图像的特性。具体而言，POS集成了旨在实现CLIP跨域泛化能力的解耦策略。我们提出的基于提示词的恢复注意力（PRA）通过提示词引导和自适应校正来优化语义解码，而双层提示词分布学习（BPDL）通过语义原型监督来精炼每像素掩码嵌入的流形。此外，为了弥补PanOoS数据集的稀缺性，我们建立了两个基准：DenseOoS，其特点是包含复杂环境中的多样化异常值；以及QuadOoS，由具有全景环形透镜系统的四足机器人捕捉。大量的实验证明了POS的有效性，与DenseOoS上的RbA相比，AuPRC提高了34.25个百分点，FPR95降低了21.42个百分点，其性能优于最先进的针孔分布外分割方法。此外，POS实现了领先的闭集分割能力，并推动了全景理解的发展。代码和数据集将在https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS提供。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了全景图分布外分割（PanOoS）新任务，并首次提出POS解决方案，以应对全景图像分割中的异常值识别问题。POS利用文本引导的提示词分布学习，解决了像素畸变和背景杂乱的挑战，并通过PRA和BPDL模块优化分割性能。同时，研究者构建了DenseOoS和QuadOoS两个新数据集。实验结果表明，POS在分割准确率和异常值检测方面均取得了显著优于现有方法的性能。
AI.keywords: 全景分割,分布外分割,提示词学习,计算机视觉,深度学习
AI.comments: 该研究在全景图像理解领域提出了一个重要的新任务（PanOoS），并提供了首个有效的解决方案POS。POS方法巧妙地结合了提示词学习和图像特性适应，解决了全景图像固有的挑战。新数据集的构建也为该领域的研究提供了宝贵的资源。然而，未来可以进一步探索POS在更复杂、动态场景下的鲁棒性和效率。

title: Teleoperated Driving: a New Challenge for 3D Object Detection in Compressed Point Clouds
comments: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
summary: In recent years, the development of interconnected devices has expanded in many fields, from infotainment to education and industrial applications. This trend has been accelerated by the increased number of low-cost sensors and accessibility to powerful hardware and software. One area that significantly benefits from these advancements is Teleoperated Driving. In this scenario, a remote controller (human or software) safely drives a vehicle using sensor data generated onboard the vehicle, and exchanged via Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications. In this work, we tackle the problem of detecting the presence of cars, pedestrians, and cyclists from point cloud data generated by LiDAR sensors to enable safe Teleoperated Driving operations. Specifically, we use the SELMA dataset, a multimodal, open-source, synthetic dataset for autonomous driving, that we expanded by including the ground-truth bounding boxes of 3D objects to support object detection. We analyze the performance of state-of-the-art compression algorithms and object detectors under several metrics, including compression efficiency, (de)compression and inference time, and detection accuracy. Finally, we measure the impact of compression and detection on a simulated V2X network in terms of data rate and latency with respect to the 3GPP requirements of Teleoperated Driving applications. Our results show that G-PCC outperforms its competitors in terms of both compression efficiency and accuracy, and consumes fewer channel resources for data transmissions. On the contrary, the two most conservative quantization modes of Draco, combined with SECOND or PointPillars for object detection, offer superior speed in both compression and decompression with comparable accuracy. Finally, we show that the choice of the detector depends on the class of objects to detect, specifically pedestrians or cyclists.

AI.title_translation: 远程驾驶：压缩点云中3D对象检测的新挑战
AI.tldr: 该研究解决了远程驾驶中的3D对象检测问题，重点是压缩点云数据。研究人员使用了SELMA数据集，并评估了压缩算法和对象检测器的性能，包括压缩效率、时间和检测准确性。结果表明，G-PCC在压缩效率和准确性方面表现优异，而Draco的保守量化模式则在速度方面表现更好。研究还强调了根据检测对象的不同（行人或自行车），选择合适的检测器的重要性。
AI.motivation: 远程驾驶（Teleoperated Driving）需要安全地使用车载传感器数据进行车辆驾驶，而这些数据通过V2X通信进行交换。为了实现安全的远程驾驶操作，需要从LiDAR传感器生成的点云数据中检测车辆、行人和自行车等物体。
AI.method: 研究人员使用了SELMA数据集，并对其进行了扩展，添加了3D对象边界框的地面真实数据，以支持对象检测。他们评估了最先进的压缩算法和对象检测器在压缩效率、（解）压缩和推理时间以及检测准确性等多个指标下的性能。此外，他们还在模拟的V2X网络中测量了压缩和检测对数据速率和延迟的影响，并与远程驾驶应用的3GPP要求进行了比较。
AI.result: 研究结果表明，G-PCC在压缩效率和准确性方面优于其他压缩算法，并且在数据传输中消耗的信道资源更少。然而，Draco的两种最保守的量化模式，结合SECOND或PointPillars进行对象检测，在压缩和解压缩速度方面表现更优，同时具有相当的准确性。研究还发现，检测器的选择取决于需要检测的对象的类别，特别是行人或自行车。
AI.conclusion: 该研究分析了在远程驾驶场景下，压缩点云数据进行3D对象检测的挑战。研究结果为在V2X通信的约束下，选择合适的压缩算法和对象检测器提供了指导，并强调了根据具体检测任务（如行人或自行车）来选择检测器的重要性。
AI.translation: 近年来，从信息娱乐到教育和工业应用，互联设备的发展在许多领域得到了扩展。低成本传感器的数量增加以及强大硬件和软件的可及性加速了这一趋势。远程驾驶（Teleoperated Driving）是显著受益于这些进步的领域之一。在此场景下，远程控制器（人为或软件）通过车辆上生成并通过车联网（V2X）通信交换的传感器数据安全地驾驶车辆。在这项工作中，我们解决了从激光雷达传感器生成的点云数据中检测汽车、行人、自行车等物体存在的问题，以实现安全的远程驾驶操作。具体来说，我们使用了SELMA数据集，这是一个多模态、开源的自动驾驶合成数据集，并通过包含3D对象地面真实边界框来扩展它，以支持对象检测。我们分析了最先进的压缩算法和对象检测器在压缩效率、（解）压缩和推理时间以及检测准确性等多个指标下的性能。最后，我们测量了压缩和检测对模拟V2X网络在数据速率和延迟方面相对于远程驾驶应用的3GPP要求的影响。我们的结果表明，G-PCC在压缩效率和准确性方面均优于竞争对手，并且在数据传输中消耗的信道资源更少。相反，Draco的两种最保守的量化模式，结合SECOND或PointPillars进行对象检测，在压缩和解压缩速度方面表现更优，同时具有相当的准确性。最后，我们表明检测器的选择取决于需要检测的对象类别，特别是行人或自行车。
AI.summary: 本研究旨在解决远程驾驶场景下的3D对象检测问题，特别关注压缩后的点云数据。研究人员利用SELMA数据集，评估了G-PCC和Draco等压缩算法以及SECOND和PointPillars等检测器在效率、速度和准确性方面的表现。结果显示，G-PCC在压缩效率和准确性方面表现突出，而Draco在速度方面具有优势。此外，研究还指出，检测器的选择应根据具体检测对象（如行人或自行车）进行调整，以满足远程驾驶应用对V2X通信的性能要求。
AI.keywords: 远程驾驶, 3D对象检测, 点云压缩, V2X通信, SELMA数据集
AI.comments: 这项研究对于在带宽受限和延迟敏感的远程驾驶应用中实现高效可靠的对象检测具有重要意义。通过量化不同压缩算法和检测器的权衡，该研究为实际部署提供了有价值的见解。未来工作可以探索更先进的联合压缩和检测方法，以进一步提高性能。

title: End-to-End Spoken Grammatical Error Correction
comments: Accepted for publication in Speech Communication
summary: Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) and feedback play a vital role in supporting second language (L2) learners, educators, and examiners. While written GEC is well-established, spoken GEC (SGEC), aiming to provide feedback based on learners' speech, poses additional challenges due to disfluencies, transcription errors, and the lack of structured input. SGEC systems typically follow a cascaded pipeline consisting of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), disfluency detection, and GEC, making them vulnerable to error propagation across modules. This work examines an End-to-End (E2E) framework for SGEC and feedback generation, highlighting challenges and possible solutions when developing these systems. Cascaded, partial-cascaded and E2E architectures are compared, all built on the Whisper foundation model. A challenge for E2E systems is the scarcity of GEC labeled spoken data. To address this, an automatic pseudo-labeling framework is examined, increasing the training data from 77 to over 2500 hours. To improve the accuracy of the SGEC system, additional contextual information, exploiting the ASR output, is investigated. Candidate feedback of their mistakes is an essential step to improving performance. In E2E systems the SGEC output must be compared with an estimate of the fluent transcription to obtain the feedback. To improve the precision of this feedback, a novel reference alignment process is proposed that aims to remove hypothesised edits that results from fluent transcription errors. Finally, these approaches are combined with an edit confidence estimation approach, to exclude low-confidence edits. Experiments on the in-house Linguaskill (LNG) corpora and the publicly available Speak & Improve (S&I) corpus show that the proposed approaches significantly boost E2E SGEC performance.

AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种端到端（E2E）框架用于口语语法纠错（SGEC），解决了传统级联方法中的错误累积问题。通过伪标签技术扩充了训练数据，并引入了利用ASR输出的上下文信息和改进的参考对齐过程来提高反馈的准确性。实验表明，该E2E方法在Linguaskill和Speak & Improve语料库上显著提升了SGEC性能。
AI.motivation: 支持二语学习者、教育者和考官，并解决了口语语法纠错（SGEC）相比书面语法纠错面临的额外挑战，如口语不流畅、转录错误和缺乏结构化输入。传统级联方法容易在模块间传播错误，因此需要端到端（E2E）框架。
AI.method: 提出并评估了一种端到端（E2E）的SGEC框架，与级联和部分级联架构进行了比较，所有架构均基于Whisper基础模型。为了解决E2E系统数据稀疏的问题，研究了一个自动伪标签框架，将训练数据从77小时增加到2500多小时。为了提高SGEC系统的准确性，研究了利用ASR输出的额外上下文信息。为了提高反馈的精确度，提出了一种新颖的参考对齐过程，以去除源于流畅转录错误的假设性编辑。最后，将这些方法与编辑置信度估计方法相结合，以排除低置信度的编辑。
AI.result: 所提出的方法显著提高了端到端SGEC的性能，并在Linguaskill和Speak & Improve语料库上进行了验证。
AI.conclusion: 端到端（E2E）框架结合伪标签、上下文信息利用、改进的参考对齐和编辑置信度估计，能够显著提升口语语法纠错（SGEC）的性能，克服了传统级联方法的局限性。
AI.translation: 语法错误纠正（GEC）和反馈在支持二语（L2）学习者、教育者和考官方面发挥着至关重要的作用。虽然书面GEC已经很成熟，但口语GEC（SGEC）旨在根据学习者的语音提供反馈，由于口语不流畅、转录错误和缺乏结构化输入，面临着额外的挑战。SGEC系统通常遵循由自动语音识别（ASR）、不流畅检测和GEC组成的级联流水线，这使得它们容易在模块间传播错误。这项工作考察了SGEC和反馈生成的端到端（E2E）框架，强调了开发这些系统时面临的挑战和可能的解决方案。比较了级联、部分级联和E2E架构，所有这些都建立在Whisper基础模型之上。E2E系统面临的一个挑战是GEC标记的口语数据稀缺。为了解决这个问题，研究了一个自动伪标签框架，将训练数据从77小时增加到2500多小时。为了提高SGEC系统的准确性，研究了利用ASR输出的额外上下文信息。候选错误的反馈是提高性能的重要一步。在E2E系统中，SGEC输出必须与流畅转录的估计值进行比较才能获得反馈。为了提高此反馈的精确度，提出了一种新颖的参考对齐过程，旨在去除源于流畅转录错误的假设性编辑。最后，将这些方法与编辑置信度估计方法相结合，以排除低置信度编辑。在内部Linguaskill（LNG）语料库和公开的Speak & Improve（S&I）语料库上的实验表明，所提出的方法显著提高了E2E SGEC的性能。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种用于口语语法纠错（SGEC）的端到端（E2E）框架，以克服传统级联方法中常见的错误累积问题。该框架基于Whisper模型，并通过自动伪标签技术有效解决了口语GEC数据稀缺的挑战，将训练数据量大幅增加。此外，研究还探索了利用ASR输出的上下文信息和一种新颖的参考对齐方法来提高反馈的准确性和精确度，并结合了编辑置信度估计来过滤低质量的编辑。实验结果表明，该E2E方法在Linguaskill和Speak & Improve语料库上取得了显著的性能提升。
AI.keywords: 口语语法纠错, 端到端学习, 伪标签, 参考对齐, Whisper模型
AI.comments: 这项工作解决了口语语法纠错（SGEC）领域的一个重要问题，即如何克服数据稀缺和级联系统中的错误累积。端到端（E2E）方法的提出和伪标签技术的应用是该研究的亮点，为未来SGEC系统的发展指明了方向。然而，对于新颖的参考对齐过程和编辑置信度估计的细节，以及它们在不同口音或语速下的鲁棒性，还需要更深入的分析和实验验证。此外，与现有先进的级联方法的比较也可能提供更全面的性能评估。

title: Cross-Subject and Cross-Montage EEG Transfer Learning via Individual Tangent Space Alignment and Spatial-Riemannian Feature Fusion
summary: Personalised music-based interventions offer a powerful means of supporting motor rehabilitation by dynamically tailoring auditory stimuli to provide external timekeeping cues, modulate affective states, and stabilise gait patterns. Generalisable Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) thus hold promise for adapting these interventions across individuals. However, inter-subject variability in EEG signals, further compounded by movement-induced artefacts and motor planning differences, hinders the generalisability of BCIs and results in lengthy calibration processes. We propose Individual Tangent Space Alignment (ITSA), a novel pre-alignment strategy incorporating subject-specific recentering, distribution matching, and supervised rotational alignment to enhance cross-subject generalisation. Our hybrid architecture fuses Regularised Common Spatial Patterns (RCSP) with Riemannian geometry in parallel and sequential configurations, improving class separability while maintaining the geometric structure of covariance matrices for robust statistical computation. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, `ITSA' demonstrates significant performance improvements across subjects and conditions. The parallel fusion approach shows the greatest enhancement over its sequential counterpart, with robust performance maintained across varying data conditions and electrode configurations. The code will be made publicly available at the time of publication.

AI.title_translation: 通过个体切线空间对齐和空间-黎曼特征融合实现的跨主体和跨蒙太奇脑电图迁移学习
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为ITSA的新型预对齐策略，结合了 sujeto-specific 重心调整、分布匹配和监督旋转对齐，以提高跨主体的通用性。同时，研究还提出了一种融合正则化公共空间模式（RCSP）和黎曼几何的混合架构，以提高类可分性。实验结果表明，该方法在跨主体和跨条件方面都有显著的性能提升，特别是并行融合方法效果最佳。
AI.motivation: 跨主体脑电图（EEG）信号的变异性，加上运动伪影和运动规划差异，阻碍了脑机接口（BCI）的通用性，并导致冗长的校准过程。为了解决这个问题，需要开发能够提高跨主体通用性的BCI。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为ITSA（Individual Tangent Space Alignment）的新型预对齐策略，该策略包括 sujeto-specific 重心调整、分布匹配和监督旋转对齐。此外，还提出了一种混合架构，将正则化公共空间模式（RCSP）与黎曼几何相结合，以并行和串行配置进行融合，以提高类可分性并保持协方差矩阵的几何结构。
AI.result: 使用留一主体交叉验证，ITSA在跨主体和跨条件方面都显示出显著的性能提升。并行融合方法比串行方法表现出更大的提升，并且在不同的数据条件和电极配置下都保持了稳健的性能。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的ITSA预对齐策略和混合融合架构能够有效提高跨主体和跨蒙太奇脑电图迁移学习的性能，克服了现有方法的局限性。
AI.translation: 个性化的音乐干预通过动态调整声音刺激以提供外部计时提示、调节情绪状态和稳定步态模式，为运动康复提供了强大的手段。因此，通用的脑机接口（BCI）有望实现跨个体适应这些干预。然而，脑电图信号的跨主体变异性，以及运动引起的伪影和运动规划差异，阻碍了BCI的通用性，并导致冗长的校准过程。我们提出了一种新颖的预对齐策略——个体切线空间对齐（ITSA），它结合了 soggetto-specific 的重置、分布匹配和监督旋转对齐，以增强跨主体的通用性。我们的混合架构将正则化公共空间模式（RCSP）与黎曼几何并行和串行配置融合，在保持协方差矩阵的几何结构以进行稳健的统计计算的同时，提高了类的可分性。通过留一主体交叉验证，ITSA在跨主体和跨条件方面都显示出显著的性能提升。并行融合方法显示出比其串行对应物最大的增强，并且在不同数据条件和电极配置下都保持了稳健的性能。代码将在出版时公开提供。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为ITSA的新型预对齐策略，用于提高跨主体脑电图（EEG）信号的通用性，克服了信号变异性和运动伪影等挑战。该策略结合了 soggetto-specific 的重置、分布匹配和监督旋转对齐。此外，研究人员还开发了一种混合架构，将正则化公共空间图（RCSP）与黎曼几何相结合，以提高分类器的性能。实验结果表明，该方法在跨主体和跨条件方面均取得了显著的性能提升，其中并行融合方法效果尤为突出。
AI.keywords: 脑电图迁移学习, 个体切线空间对齐, 黎曼几何, 脑机接口, 跨主体通用性
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的ITSA策略和混合架构，以解决脑电图迁移学习中的跨主体变异性问题，并在实验中取得了显著的性能提升。代码的公开也为后续研究提供了便利。然而，该研究可能未充分探讨在更复杂或更不理想的数据条件下（例如，噪声水平更高或数据量更少）的鲁棒性。

title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical gold standard for cardiovascular disease (CVD) assessment, yet continuous monitoring is constrained by the need for dedicated hardware and trained personnel. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearable devices and readily scalable, but it lacks electrophysiological specificity, limiting diagnostic reliability. While generative methods aim to translate PPG into clinically useful ECG signals, existing approaches are limited by the misalignment of physiological semantics in generative models and the complexity of modeling in high-dimensional signals. To address these limitations, we propose PPGFlowECG, a two-stage framework that aligns PPG and ECG in a shared latent space using the CardioAlign Encoder and then synthesizes ECGs with latent rectified flow. We further provide a formal analysis of this coupling, showing that the CardioAlign Encoder is necessary to guarantee stable and semantically consistent ECG synthesis under our formulation. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate improved synthesis fidelity and downstream diagnostic utility. These results indicate that PPGFlowECG supports scalable, wearable-first CVD screening when standard ECG acquisition is unavailable.

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Subspace Coefficients Search
summary: Real-world deployment often exposes vision models to distribution shifts, making test-time adaptation (TTA) important for reliable prediction. Existing TTA methods can be difficult to deploy on edge devices because they require backpropagation, activation storage, or test-time batches, which increase computation, memory, and state. We propose \textbf{ELaTTA} (\textit{Efficient Latent Test-Time Adaptation}), a forward-only, gradient-free framework for single-instance TTA. ELaTTA freezes the pretrained model and adapts each test input by searching a low-dimensional coefficient vector in a principal latent subspace computed offline from a source-domain cache. The basis is stored once and source data are discarded before deployment. At test time, CMA-ES performs covariance-adaptive Gaussian search, ranks candidate corrections by prediction entropy, and selects the best candidate within a fixed evaluation budget. On five visual benchmarks spanning corruption, natural, rendition, sketch, and cross-domain shifts, ELaTTA provides strong accuracy under strict and continual single-instance protocols. In the strict single-instance comparison, MEMO requires \emph{64.7$\times$} the computation and \emph{12.4$\times$} the peak memory of ELaTTA. A complementary keyword-spotting experiment shows that the same coefficient-search design transfers beyond vision. We further demonstrate ViT-Base adaptation on a Raspberry Pi 5, confirming the feasibility of deploying ELaTTA on an edge device.

title: Distributed Stochastic Proximal Algorithm on Riemannian Submanifolds for Weakly-convex Functions
summary: This paper aims to investigate the distributed stochastic optimization problems on compact embedded submanifolds (in the Euclidean space) where the local cost functions are weakly-convex. To address the manifold structure, we propose a distributed Riemannian stochastic proximal algorithm framework by utilizing the retraction and Riemannian consensus protocol, and analyze three specific algorithms: the distributed Riemannian stochastic subgradient, proximal point, and prox-linear algorithms. When the initial points satisfy certain conditions, we show that the iterates generated by this framework converge to a nearly stationary point in expectation while achieving consensus. We further establish the convergence rate of the algorithm framework as $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1+κ_g}{\sqrt{k}})$ where $k$ denotes the number of iterations and $κ_g$ shows the impact of manifold geometry on the algorithm performance. Finally, numerical experiments are implemented to demonstrate the theoretical results and show the empirical performance.

title: Joint Transmit Beamforming and Reflection Optimization for Beyond Diagonal RIS Aided Multi-Cell MIMO Communication
comments: This paper has been presented in ICASSP 2026
summary: The sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks will rely on ultra-dense multi-cell deployment to meet the high rate and connectivity demands. However, frequency reuse leads to severe inter-cell interference, particularly for cell-edge users, which limits the communication performance. To overcome this challenge, we investigate a beyond diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) aided multi-cell multi-user downlink MIMO communication system, where a BD-RIS is deployed to enhance desired signals and suppress both intra-cell and inter-cell interference. We formulate the joint optimization problem of the transmit beamforming matrices at the BSs and the BD-RIS reflection matrix to maximize the weighted sum rate of all users, subject to the challenging unitary constraint of the BD-RIS reflection matrix and transmit power constraints at the BSs. To tackle this non-convex and difficult problem, we apply the weighted minimum mean squared error (WMMSE) method to transform the problem into an equivalent tractable form, and propose an efficient alternating optimization (AO) based algorithm to iteratively update the transmit beamforming and BD-RIS reflection using Lagrange duality theory and manifold optimization. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed design over various benchmark schemes, and provide useful practical insights on the BD-RIS deployment strategy for multi-cell systems.

title: Naga: Vedic Encoding for Deep State Space Models
summary: This paper presents Naga, a deep State Space Model (SSM) encoding approach inspired by structural concepts from Vedic mathematics. The proposed method introduces a bidirectional representation for time series by jointly processing forward and time-reversed input sequences. These representations are then combined through an element-wise (Hadamard) interaction, resulting in a Vedic-inspired encoding that enhances the model's ability to capture temporal dependencies across distant time steps. We evaluate Naga on multiple long-term time series forecasting (LTSF) benchmarks, including ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Weather, Traffic, and ILI. The experimental results show that Naga outperforms 28 current state of the art models and demonstrates improved efficiency compared to existing deep SSM-based approaches. The findings suggest that incorporating structured, Vedic-inspired decomposition can provide an interpretable and computationally efficient alternative for long-range sequence modeling.

title: Time-Invariant Linear Quadratic Regulators: A New Look
summary: This paper demonstrates that linear ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients serve as the main building block for time-invariant linear quadratic regulators (LQRs). By applying the Euler-Lagrange equations to a flat output, i.e., to a basis of the free finitely-generated module over the commutative principal ideal ring of time-invariant linear differential operators with respect to the time derivation, this result emerges directly. In module-theoretic terms. The freeness of this structure corresponds to the classical Kalman controllability condition (M. Fliess, Some basic structural properties of generalized linear systems, Syst. Contr. Lett., 15 (1990) 391-396). Within this framework, the two-point boundary value problem, including the control variables, becomes analytically tractable, enabling the derivation of optimal time horizons, optimal parameter design, and rest-to-rest trajectories. Furthermore, a novel turnpike-like phenomenon is established via nonstandard analysis. The feedback loop is closed thanks to the HEOL approach (C. Join, E. Delaleau, M. Fliess, Flatness-based control revisited: The HEOL setting, C.R. Math., 362 (2024) 1693-1706), an extension of model-free control (MFC) that leverages intelligent controllers. Our viewpoint, which significantly simplifies the presentation by avoiding the conventional Kalman state-space representation, relies on foundational algebraic concepts that, while elementary, are rarely used in today's control theory. To aid intuition, some rudimentary examples are presented, most of which include computer simulations.

title: Lyapunov characterization of boundedness of reachability sets for infinite-dimensional systems
summary:
We prove a converse Lyapunov theorem for boundedness of reachability sets for a general class of control systems whose flow is Lipschitz continuous on compact intervals with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. We show that this condition is satisfied by broad classes of semilinear evolution equations.
  For ordinary differential equations, as a consequence of our results, we obtain a converse Lyapunov theorem for forward completeness, without a priori restrictions on the magnitude of inputs. As an example, we rederive Wintner's classical result using our Lyapunov approach.

title: Tutorial on Aided Inertial Navigation Systems: A Modern Treatment Using Lie-Group Theoretical Methods
comments: Accepted in IEEE Control Systems Magazine
summary:
Robots and autonomous vehicles rely on accurate estimates of their position, velocity, and orientation. Inertial sensors measure motion at high rates, but errors accumulate as these measurements are integrated. Satellite navigation, cameras, and other sensors help limit this drift. Combining these sources effectively requires estimation methods that account for the geometry of the navigation state.
  This tutorial presents a unified introduction to aided inertial navigation from a Lie-group perspective. It connects motion prediction, uncertainty propagation, and measurement updates within a common geometric framework. Particular attention is given to invariant filtering, which uses system symmetries to simplify the description and evolution of estimation errors. The tutorial explains how choices of state and error representations shape the filter equations. It connects theoretical principles with formulas suitable for implementation and discusses recent extensions addressing convergence and sensor biases. By organizing established and emerging methods around their shared geometric foundations, the presentation provides students, researchers, and engineers with a basis for understanding, implementing, and extending navigation algorithms.
comment: Accepted in IEEE Control Systems Magazine

title: Soft MPCritic: Value-Based Reinforcement Learning for Non-Differentiable Predictive Control
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) and model predictive control (MPC) offer complementary strengths, yet existing MPC-RL frameworks commonly rely on gradient-based optimization and therefore cannot handle the non-differentiable dynamics and objectives common in RL. We propose Soft MPCritic, an MPC-RL framework that learns a soft value function and uses sampling-based planning both for online control and for generating value targets. Specifically, Soft MPCritic instantiates MPC with model predictive path integral control (MPPI) and learns a terminal Q-function through fitted value iteration. Because the value targets are computed by the same planner used for control, the learned value function is aligned with the planner and implicitly extends its effective horizon. To keep target generation tractable, we introduce an amortized warm-start strategy that reuses the open-loop action sequences planned during online control to initialize batched MPPI computations of value targets, reducing computational cost without sacrificing solution quality. For robustness to model error, Soft MPCritic plans over scenarios drawn from an ensemble of dynamics models trained for next-step prediction. On both classical and constrained control tasks, Soft MPCritic learns effective policies with non-differentiable objectives, particularly where finite-horizon MPPI alone falls short. Soft MPCritic thus offers a practical blueprint for synthesizing MPC policies directly from black-box objectives, without differentiable surrogates.

title: High-Order Matrix Control Barrier Functions: Well-Posedness and Feasibility via Matrix Relative Degree
summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an effective framework for enforcing safety in dynamical systems with scalar constraints. However, many safety constraints are more naturally expressed as matrix-valued conditions, such as positive definiteness or eigenvalue bounds - scalar formulations introduce potential nonsmoothness that complicates analysis. Matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs) address this limitation by directly enforcing matrix-valued safety constraints. Yet for constraints where the control input does not appear in the first derivative, high-order formulations are required. While such extensions are well understood in the scalar case, they remain largely unexplored in the matrix case. This paper develops high-order matrix control barrier functions (HOMCBFs) and establishes conditions ensuring well-posedness and feasibility of the associated constraints, enabling enforcement of matrix-valued safety constraints for systems with high-order dynamics. We further show that, using an optimal-decay HOMCBF formulation, forward invariance can be ensured while requiring control only over the minimum eigenspace. The framework is demonstrated on a double-integrator localization problem by enforcing positive definiteness of the information matrix.

title: MosaicMRI: A Diverse Dataset and Benchmark for Raw Musculoskeletal MRI
comments: 10 pages, 4 figures, The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Deep learning underpins a wide range of applications in MRI, including reconstruction, artifact removal, and segmentation. However, progress has been driven largely by public datasets focused on brain and knee imaging, shaping how models are trained and evaluated. As a result, careful studies of the reliability of these models across diverse anatomical settings remain limited. In this work, we introduce MosaicMRI, a large and diverse collection of fully sampled raw musculoskeletal (MSK) MR measurements designed for training and evaluating machine-learning--based methods. MosaicMRI is the largest open-source raw MSK MRI dataset to date, comprising 3,150 volumes and 89,830 slices, including a 3,096-volume 1.5~T core dataset and a 54-volume 0.55~T low-field set. The dataset offers substantial diversity in volume orientation (e.g., axial, sagittal), imaging contrasts (e.g., PD, T1, T2), anatomies (e.g., spine, knee, hip, ankle, and others), numbers of acquisition coils, and field strengths. Using accelerated reconstruction as a testbed, we study scaling, robustness, and data selection under realistic MSK distribution shifts. Across E2E-VarNet, U-Net, and ViT baselines, mixed-anatomy training improves over anatomy-specific training, showing that the benefit of anatomical diversity is not architecture-specific. Zero-shot experiments on the 0.55~T low-field set highlight that using more training data improves average reconstruction under field-strength shift. Controlled subset experiments further suggest that these gains come from transferable cross-anatomy structure, rather than anatomy or contrast matching alone.
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems

title: L1 Regularization Paths in Linear Models by Parametric Gaussian Message Passing
summary: The paper proposes new algorithms for computing the regularization path of linear-model fitting (i) with L1 costs for the independent variables and L2 costs for the dependent variables, and (ii) with L2 costs for the independent variables and L1 costs for the dependent variables. Unlike previously proposed algorithms, the proposed algorithms for (i) and (ii) are exact duals of each other. The heart of the proposed algorithms is parametric Gaussian message passing (i.e., Kalman-type forward-backward recursions) in the pertinent factor graphs. We first develop such algorithms for linear models with general (but preferably low-dimensional) state space representations. We then specialize to specific state space representations of generic linear models; in this case, the structure of the factor graph allows to refine the proposed algorithms such that the computational complexity drops to linear scale.

title: Fourier-Curve Constellations under Tangential Perturbation: Covariance-Aware Soft Demapping on Coded Links
summary: A Fourier-curve constellation places $M$ points on a closed curve through $k$ complex slots. A Gaussian perturbation along the curve's tangent, whether injected as artificial noise or arising from first-order jitter of the curve parameter, gives every symbol an observation with a symbol-dependent rank-one covariance, and the maximum-likelihood symbol metric differs from the Euclidean rule by one rank-one correction per candidate. We realize this metric as a max-log soft demapper beside a Euclidean correlator bank at $2kM$ additional multiply--accumulate operations per symbol. On a regular $(3,6)$ LDPC-coded link at $(k,M){=}(20,64)$ it recovers $5.1$\,dB of the Euclidean mismatch at BLER${=}10^{-1}$ under natural labeling and $1.1$\,dB under Gray labeling, of which an average-covariance receiver recovers $0.7$\,dB and nothing measurable, respectively, and it makes the tangential perturbation $0.2$ to $1.0$\,dB cheaper than white noise of the same power on the same codebook. The per-tone phase orientation of the curve acts as an orthogonal rotation, so these results hold at every orientation, and the demapper decodes at the level of an exactly oriented receiver up to $0.2$\,rad of orientation error per component. A bit-interleaved coded-modulation achievable rate corroborates the ordering, a Woodbury extension keeps the rank-one structure under per-tone Rician fading, and $6$-bit lookup-table quantization costs no measurable degradation.

title: Reduced-Feedback Hybrid Precoding for Wideband mmWave MIMO-OFDM Systems via Hierarchical Interpolation
comments: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE GLOBECOM Workshops
summary: In this paper, we propose a feedback-efficient hybrid precoding framework for wideband millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. To reduce the hardware cost of radio-frequency (RF) chains and the feedback burden associated with frequency-selective digital precoding, frequency-flat analog precoders and combiners are first constructed from the dominant angle-of-arrival (AoA) and angle-of-departure (AoD) directions associated with the strongest propagation paths. For digital precoding, a shared quantized codebook is designed using the Lloyd algorithm, and a binary-search-based hierarchical interpolation method is developed to identify codeword switching locations between adjacent pilot subcarriers. By avoiding exhaustive codeword comparisons over all intermediate subcarriers, the proposed method reduces online search complexity and enables compact digital-precoder feedback. For the considered system configuration, the proposed method achieves a worst-case feedback reduction of approximately 98.34% relative to full-grid per-subcarrier feedback. Simulation results further demonstrate competitive spectral efficiency and bit error rate (BER) performance, low computational cost, and robustness under imperfect effective channel state information (CSI).
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE GLOBECOM Workshops

title: Learning from Real Stuttering: Synthetic Mandarin Stuttering Speech for Data Augmentation in Speech Recognition
summary: Mandarin stuttered speech remains under-resourced, limiting the development of robust speech processing systems. We present a Mandarin stuttering speech synthesis and data augmentation framework that adapts both autoregressive and non-autoregressive TTS models using naturally stuttered speech. Specifically, we adapt CosyVoice2 and MaskGCT to support controllable generation of specific stuttering events while also modeling broader utterance-level characteristics of stuttered speech. Using the adapted models, we construct synthetic data resources for downstream augmentation. Evaluations show that the generated speech closely approaches real stuttered speech. Extensive ASR experiments demonstrate consistent augmentation gains and further observe a domain-gap--diversity trade-off between synthetic and real data. These results demonstrate the value of learning synthetic stuttering data directly from real dysfluency for robust Mandarin speech processing.

title: CylindTrack: Depth-Aware Cylindrical Motion Modeling for Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking
comments: The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack
summary: Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) is essential for embodied perception, where panoramic cameras provide a 360° field of view to reduce blind spots and keep surrounding targets observable for longer durations. However, panoramic MOT requires motion estimates and association cues consistent with its imaging geometry. In videos represented in equirectangular projection (ERP), horizontal coordinates wrap at the image seam, while frame-wise relative-depth estimates may fluctuate over time. These inconsistencies can disrupt trajectory prediction and identity association. To address these challenges, we propose CylindTrack, a depth-aware cylindrical tracking-by-detection framework that integrates continuous angular motion modeling with temporally filtered relative-depth cues. Specifically, Depth-Temporal Trajectory Modeling (DTM) promotes instance depth from an isolated frame-wise cue into temporally filtered trajectory-level states. Spherical Spatio-Temporal Consistency Learning (SSTC) combines a Temporal Mixer and Spherical Geometry-aware Attention to enhance temporal coherence and panoramic geometric alignment in depth-aware representations. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Cylindrical Motion Model (TCMM) lifts horizontal motion into a continuous angular state space, enabling seam-consistent motion prediction and association. By jointly modeling trajectory-level depth consistency and panoramic topology, CylindTrack improves identity preservation and trajectory continuity in challenging panoramic scenes. Experiments on QuadTrack and JRDB demonstrate improvements in identity-oriented metrics with practical efficiency, achieving HOTA scores of 33.67 and 31.12, IDF1 scores of 40.45 and 34.33, and tracking speeds of 28.56 and 21.34 FPS, respectively. The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack.
comment: The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack

title: A Situational Speech Synthesizer for Yoruba: System Design, Phonological Rule Architecture, and Orthographic Extensions for Contour
comments: 18 pages. v4: updated citations to the companion paper (arXiv:2609.38627), which proposes the caron/circumflex convention as a revision of the standard Yoruba orthography; corrected rulebook entry numbers and the Adenike example in Section 5 to match the deposited rule specification; fixed missing characters (equivalence symbol, IPA and syllabic-nasal marks); improved table layout
summary:
We present TTSYoruba, a rule-based concatenative diphone speech synthesizer for Yoruba, deployed at online as part of the YorubaName.com open dictionary of Yoruba personal names. The system takes tone-marked Yoruba text as input and produces audio output by applying a hand-crafted phonological rule system to a recorded inventory of 651 diphone units spanning five tonal variants of every consonant-vowel combination in the language. We describe the phonological architecture of the system in detail, including our complete tonal file-selection logic, our treatment of the three-way nasal disambiguation problem (oral /n/, nasalized vowel, and syllabic nasal), and the derivation of contextual rising and falling tones from level-tone input. We also present, as an orthographic contribution, the adoption of the caron and circumflex, which are symbols with prior standing in Yoruba phonological transcription, as standard single-vowel contour tone markers, integrated into the TTS normalization pipeline and the WriteYoruba keyboard input tool. The system's performance was evaluated through a listener study (N=50), with detailed results on Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) presented in Section 6.
  Keywords: Yoruba, text-to-speech, low-resource languages, diphone synthesis, contour tones, African language NLP, rule-based synthesis

title: Mean-Field Oscillator Ising Machines: Gradient Flows and Classification of Limit Solutions
summary: Oscillator Ising Machines (OIMs) have emerged as promising computational architectures for approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems. We derive and analyze the mean-field limit of an OIM model and show that it inherits the gradient flow structure of the finite-dimensional dynamics. We identify conditions under which this mean-field evolution admits an Eulerian formulation as a gradient flow on the Wasserstein space of probability measures and contrast this with a Lagrangian formulation which is always available. This gradient flow structure strongly constrains the long-time dynamics and enables a complete classification of limit solutions and their stability in the totally symmetric case. In particular, all limit solutions are fixed points whose phases cluster into at most four groups, and for almost all parameter values, only binarized fixed points -- those with clusters at $0$ and/or $π$ -- can be stable. Since binarized states are exactly those for which a feasible solution to the original problem can be read out, this shows that feasible solutions can almost always be recovered. We provide tight bounds on the parameter thresholds for which fixed points in this binarized family are stable, thereby identifying the threshold for binarization in this model, and present numerical evidence that the mean-field model correctly predicts behavioral regimes in certain large random networks, including Erdős-Rényi networks. Moreover, this problem provides a case study in the application of mean-field models, gradient flows, and optimal transport to the study of large-scale systems, and we highlight a number of features of this problem which are informative in this respect.

title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization
summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have made rapid progress on standardized benchmarks, yet their deployment in practical media workflows, curation, archival indexing, and content distribution remains largely unrealized. We identify automated audio chapterization, the task of segmenting continuous audio streams into thematically coherent chapters, as a demanding and commercially consequential setting that exposes this gap. Chapterization is challenging because boundaries are defined less by objective acoustic events than by subjective editorial judgment, requiring models to reason sequentially over long acoustic contexts and approximate creator-authored boundary decisions. We present AudioChaps, a post-training framework for aligning end-to-end LALMs for this task via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) guided by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. To support training and evaluation, we curate three datasets: AudioChaps-Alignment, derived from creator-annotated chapter boundaries on YouTube; AudioChaps-CoT, which provides structured supervision for well-formatted, high-quality, and evidence-grounded boundary reasoning; and AudioChaps-Eval, a held-out benchmark for audio chapterization. Applying GRPO directly without a Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) cold start, AudioChaps-R1-Zero already improves average F1 by 33 points over the state-of-the-art LALM Audio-Flamingo-3-Think. The AudioChaps framework produces our final aligned LALM, AudioChaps-R1, which improves average F1 by 49 points. These results demonstrate that GRPO-trained LALMs can reliably transform unstructured auditory streams into navigable, structured media. Our code, models, and dataset resources will be released upon acceptance at https://github.com/ta012/AudioChaps.

title: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Annealing-Inspired UAV Path Planning for Smart Agriculture
summary: With the rapid advancement of smart agriculture, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become indispensable for efficient coverage and path planning in grid-mapped agricultural fields. However, optimizing UAV flight paths in large-scale environments remains a complex Nondeterministic Polynomial-time (NP)-hard problem. Traditional path planning methods are often constrained by local optima, limited scalability, and slow convergence, which significantly restrict their effectiveness in solving large-scale problems. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel optimization framework utilizing a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-parallelized Ising solver. Our method mimics the operational principles of quantum annealing on GPU hardware, enabling rapid search for the minimum-energy state of Ising models. Unlike physical quantum devices, which are often constrained by the number of qubits, our approach leverages the Fixstars Amplify (FA) platform to perform parallel annealing on highly parallelized GPUs. This enables the simultaneous evaluation of thousands of potential path candidates and vast state transitions. By leveraging large-scale parallel processing, this framework's core strength lies in minimizing computation time even as the problem scale increases. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method consistently identifies superior flight paths while maintaining stable computational performance compared with the genetic algorithm and simulated annealing method.

title: The De Cock--De Moor Conjecture: Proof, Normal Form, and Indefinite Angles
summary: De Cock and De Moor conjectured that two matrices built from the solutions of three coupled Lyapunov equations always share their eigenvalues, an identity linking principal angles between model subspaces with the canonical correlations between the past and future of a stochastic process. The conjecture was recorded as Problem 9.1 of \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}. We prove it under the natural nonresonance condition, without stability or diagonalizability, and show that the two matrices are similar. The proof exposes a Cauchy-matrix structure created by the rank-one perturbation and reduces the problem to rational interpolation, and the main theorem has also been verified in the Lean~4 proof assistant. The same structure gives a normal form that depends only on the poles and zeros of the model. Off the stable set the eigenvalues become squared cosines of angles in an indefinite metric. We prove an inertia theorem for them and show that reflecting a pole or a zero across the unit circle acts on the angles by a principal pivot transform. For several inputs and outputs, where the conjecture fails, we identify the subspaces whose angles do give the canonical correlations. We also relate our approach to the independent proof of Gillberg and Löfberg.

title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track
summary: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,056 expert submissions and 12,051 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench sep- arates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a consistent gap: while models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, Top-3 fine-grained issue-label identification remains below label-prior baselines and strict diagnosis alignment stays below 7%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench pro- vides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Permanent Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential equation carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at the separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

title: Riccati Stability Without Auxiliary Matrices
summary: In the 2004 collection \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}, Erik Verriest posed the problem of characterizing Riccati stability ``without invoking additional matrices.'' We give such a characterization through a scalar invariant of the resolvent family. The invariant is defined by covariance balances using at most $n^2+1$ frequency--direction pairs. A finite-dimensional separation argument shows that this covariance radius equals the optimal common ellipsoidal norm of the resolvent family. Combined with the strict bounded real lemma, this yields a necessary and sufficient condition for Riccati stability involving only the Hurwitz property of the first matrix and a single scalar inequality. The invariant reduces to the ordinary spectral radius for one matrix, lies between the pointwise spectral-radius and unscaled small-gain levels of the resolvent family, and coincides with the operator-space spectral radius of Shalit and Shamovich for the natural resolvent function space. The main results have been formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.

title: Why Learning Rediscovers the Closed-Form Diagonal Regularizer
summary: Recovering modal amplitudes from a few sensors requires regularization, and the shape of the penalty decides how strongly each mode is shrunk. The best shape depends on the truncation noise that discarded modes add to every measurement, which is unobserved and could be room-specific. We identify a diagonal saturation principle: for a single snapshot, isotropic truncation noise makes the Bayes-optimal Tikhonov shape a closed-form power law Gamma_k proportional to lambda_k^|s|, set by the prior alone and independent of the domain. The off-diagonal anisotropy equals the Herfindahl index H of the discarded-mode power exactly, Weyl's eigenvalue counting law fixes the number of discarded modes and hence H, and Berry's random-wave conjecture enters only through a diagonal term D, which we measure directly. Together they predict an approximately flat loss landscape over the penalty exponent, which leaves a learned diagonal regularizer little to gain from tuning the exponent per room. On simulated acoustic rooms the closed form stays within 5.83% of a per-room power-law oracle across observation windows, and three learned diagonal architectures track its error, the closest within a fraction of a point and none more than 3pp above it, while learning qualitatively different spectra. In the truncation regime no tested method consistently improves on the closed form, including Learned Iterative Ridge, which couples modes across layers. The framework extends to heat diffusion through a known Green's-function correction with no new free parameters.

title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
summary: Realtime spoken interaction demands deep reasoning, prompt responses, and fluid turn-taking. We present StepAudio 3 Realtime, an audio-language foundation model organized around a continuous listen-converse-think-act loop. Deep Perception captures rich acoustic cues to interpret user intent, while Seamless Duplex models synchronized audio streams to handle pauses, backchannels, and interruptions naturally. Crucially, we resolve the tension between deep deliberation and latency via Think-While-Speaking, executing private reasoning in parallel with spoken delivery. In reasoning mode, StepAudio 3 reaches a 73.0 macro average on StepAudioChat. With Think-While-Speaking, it achieves dialogue and reasoning performance comparable to dedicated reasoning models while speaking in real time. Furthermore, an integrated Voice Agent handles asynchronous tool execution without disrupting the dialogue flow. StepAudio 3 Realtime achieves top-tier performance across key dimensions: an exceptional 90.6 on the MMSU benchmark, 98.9 Overall on the Artificial Analysis Full-Duplex Bench, and a 56.0% macro task-success rate on $τ$-Voice.

title: Robust Cross-Domain Speech-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection via Iterative Adversarial Self-Training
summary: As Alzheimer's disease (AD) has increasingly become a major global public health issue, speech-based AD detection has attracted widespread attention. However, most existing methods are trained and evaluated on a single dataset, often leading to severe cross-domain performance degradation due to reliance on dataset-specific artifacts rather than disease-related speech cues. In real-world applications, reliable Alzheimer's disease detection requires models that are robust to variations in recording environments, speakers and data collection conditions. To address this challenge, this paper adopts unsupervised domain adaptation to learn robust, domain-invariant feature representations in the absence of target-domain diagnosis labels. On this basis, a novel unsupervised domain adaptation method, Iterative Adversarial Self-Training (IAST), is proposed. Results demonstrate that IAST significantly improves the generalization ability and robustness under various cross-domain settings.

title: MagNav: A Dual-Core Magnetic Track Guidance Framework for Lighting-Invariant Navigation in Two-Wheeled Robots
comments: 6 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT), organized by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Patna
summary: Two-Wheeled Inverted Pendulum (TWIP) robots are useful for studying how to control systems that are naturally unstable and have fewer actuators than degrees of freedom. Adding autonomous line-following to these robots is challenging because steering and balancing are closely linked. Most existing systems use infrared sensors, which can be affected by changes in lighting, such as sunlight or shadows, making them reliable only indoors. This paper presents a self-balancing robot that can follow a line using a magnetic track guidance system. By using a five-channel analog Hall-effect sensor array, the robot is not affected by optical interference. The control system uses a cascaded PID structure: the inner loop keeps the robot balanced using data from an inertial measurement unit with a complementary filter, while the outer loop adjusts steering based on the magnetic sensor readings. Stepper motors provide precise torque control without needing extra rotary encoders. For comparison, an optical sensor module was also included. Tests show that the magnetic guidance system keeps accurate tracking even in very bright lighting, over 10,000 Lux, while the optical system loses accuracy and sometimes fails. This design provides a reliable, lighting-independent solution for autonomous navigation in places like factories, warehouses, and outdoor paths.
comment: 6 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT), organized by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Patna

title: Rank-one variance inflation in polynomial estimation of signal parameters with a sign-preserving fractional-power basis
comments: 29 pages, 3 figures, 8 tables. v2: corrected Sections 1.2 and 5.5 (relation to arXiv:2606.11421 is a shared mechanism, not a special case). Code and stored results reproducing every number, table and figure: https://github.com/SZabolotnii/Ku-PMM-Rank-One-code-supplement
summary: The polynomial maximization method estimates signal parameters in non-Gaussian noise from a finite description of the noise by its moments and cumulants, without a density. Known accuracy results assume that these noise characteristics are known, or use a design in which estimating them jointly costs no accuracy. In practice they are estimated from the residuals of a preliminary fit, and the effect of this substitution on accuracy is unknown. We treat the feasible scheme as a two-step estimator and, for a general smooth signal model in a fixed design, find the increment of its asymptotic covariance in closed form: $Σ_{\rm fe}-Σ_{\rm or}=c_2(1-g_{\rm or}) Q^{-1}\bar{d}\bar{d}^{\top}Q^{-1}$, a positive semidefinite matrix of rank at most one. Here $c_2$ is the noise variance, $g_{\rm or}\le 1$ the oracle variance reduction factor, and $Q$ and $\bar{d}$ the second-moment matrix and mean of the signal gradient over the design. Estimating the fractional moments that form the weights costs no first-order accuracy, because that block is orthogonal; the whole increment comes from estimating the sign-preserving centering means. The increment lies along the single direction $Q^{-1}\bar{d}$, so linear combinations of the parameters orthogonal to it keep oracle accuracy. In the trace metric the variance reduction factor becomes $g_{\rm fe}=g_{\rm or}+(1-g_{\rm or})R_D$, where $R_D=\|Q^{-1}\bar{d}\|^2/{\rm tr} Q^{-1}$ depends on the design alone. We give four sufficient conditions for first-order oracle equivalence; noise symmetry is not among them. Monte Carlo experiments with a harmonic signal confirm the direction and size of the increment. A covariance estimate that ignores the increment undercovers where non-Gaussianity gives the largest gain, symmetric noise included.

title: Adaptive Gait Biofeedback With Participant-Held-Out Modeling and Participant-Specific Updating in Chronic Ankle Instability
comments: 28 pages (14-page main manuscript and 14-page supplementary material), 5 main figures
summary: Adaptive gait biofeedback may support repeated practice in chronic ankle instability, but its evaluation must address model performance and human response. We evaluated a temporal convolutional classifier on protocol-defined, angle-derived GOOD/BAD gait-cycle labels using participant-held-out leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation in 20 participants. Seven participants in the adaptive-intervention group completed nine sessions over three weeks, with one motion-capture recording analyzed per session. Models updated after failed sessions were compared offline with their parent models on the same-session validation subset used for candidate selection and the first subsequent adaptive-session recording. Frontal-plane ankle angle was compared between the adaptive group and 10 sequentially enrolled controls at Baseline, Post, and 7-day Retention. Across 20 held-out folds, mean fold-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.948, sensitivity for angle-threshold-exceeding BAD cycles was 0.941, and specificity for angle-threshold-meeting GOOD cycles was 0.366. Mean BAD-class F1 was higher in candidate models by 0.187 on the same-session subset and 0.118 on the first subsequent recording. At Post, the adaptive group had a baseline-adjusted frontal-plane ankle angle 5.168 degrees lower than controls (95% confidence interval, 1.766-8.569 degrees lower); the Retention contrast was uncertain. These findings characterize population-model discrimination and offline participant-specific updating during repeated biofeedback use, alongside a nonrandomized Post frontal-plane ankle angle association. They do not establish independent clinical gait classification or a causal benefit of updating.

title: Sparsity in control problems: Recent trends and open challenges
comments: Submitted to Annual Reviews in Control. FIx author name
summary: As in all fields of engineering, control engineers constantly face a dichotomy between achieving high performance and the limited availability of resources for sensing, actuation, and control. This tension often translates into formalizing design problems with sparsity constraints; that is, the design involves decision variables whose number, spatial reach, temporal spread, or other physical expressions are much smaller than in the ideal scenario of unconstrained optimization of a task-related performance metric. Even though this fundamental limitation underlines a plethora of methodological approaches and application domains, the control literature is fragmented into several lines of work tailored to specific scenarios. This survey fills the gap by bringing together several lines of work on handling sparsity in relevant control problems such as actuator scheduling, minimal-energy controllability, maximum hands-off control, and online convex optimization, and weaving a red thread through theoretical foundations and algorithms. Beyond establishing a coherent, structured narrative of problems and solutions for handling sparsity in control scenarios, we discuss open areas and relevant directions for future research, motivated by the growing complexity of control systems and their relations with key domains such as pervasive computing, distributed learning, cyberphysical security, and ecological footprint.
